title: SET: Stream-Event-Triggered Scheduling for Efficient CUDA Graph Pipelines
summary: Achieving peak GPU performance remains a significant challenge as the system throughput is constrained by host-device synchronization delays and kernel scheduling overheads, even with aggressive kernel optimizations and batch processing. Furthermore, existing approaches often underutilize hardware resources such as compute cores and copy engines due to scheduling overheads. To address these problems, we propose a CUDA runtime framework for task-parallel pipelines to minimize the synchronization overheads and the gap between kernel executions. The proposed solution combines two innovations: (1) a multi-stream task-parallel pipeline programming model that leverages event-chaining and work-stealing mechanisms to fully utilize available hardware resources; (2) a graph-based execution flow with per-stream buffers to ensure memory safety for multiple in-flight jobs running concurrently. Extensive evaluations on representative real-world workloads show 1.15--1.44X speedup and reduce scheduling overheads by 18--54% compared to state-of-the-art CUDA graph baselines.

AI.tldr: A CUDA runtime framework improves task-parallel GPU pipelines through multi-stream scheduling, event chaining, work stealing, and safe graph-based execution, delivering measurable speedups and lower scheduling overhead than CUDA graph baselines.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that peak GPU performance is often limited not by kernel efficiency alone, but by synchronization delays, scheduling overheads, and underutilization of hardware resources in existing CUDA execution approaches.
AI.method: The method introduces a CUDA runtime framework with two core components: a multi-stream task-parallel pipeline programming model using event chaining and work stealing, and a graph-based execution flow with per-stream buffers to maintain memory safety across multiple concurrent in-flight jobs.
AI.result: On representative real-world workloads, the proposed framework achieves 1.15x to 1.44x speedup and reduces scheduling overheads by 18% to 54% compared with strong CUDA graph baselines.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a CUDA runtime framework for task-parallel pipelines can substantially improve GPU throughput by reducing host-device synchronization and kernel scheduling overheads, while also improving utilization of compute and copy engines.

title: Full-Field Calibration of Coupled Thermomechanical Material Models at Finite Strain
summary:
Calibrating thermomechanical material models from experiments is challenging because deformation, temperature, and force responses are strongly coupled, while measurements are usually restricted to specimen surfaces. We present a full-field calibration framework for coupled finite-strain thermomechanical material models using boundary displacement, reaction-force data, and temperature. The forward model is formulated as a near-incompressible thermo-hyperelastic problem with thermomechanical coupling derived from a Helmholtz free energy, and the inverse problem is posed as a PDE-constrained optimization problem with weighted observation terms for the available data streams.
  Reduced gradients are computed with adjoint sensitivities that are obtained by automatic differentiation, enabling gradient-based calibration of nonlinear transient thermomechanical systems. The formulation is first verified on synthetic examples involving uniform thermal preconditioning and localized transient rod contact, where the ground-truth parameters are recovered from full-field measurements and force observations. The same workflow is then applied to experimental thermomechanical data by first calibrating a hyperelastic mechanical baseline from cyclic equibiaxial loading and subsequently identifying thermal expansion and directional shrinkage parameters from surface-temperature and boundary-force histories. The results demonstrate that coupled thermomechanical parameters can be inferred from experimentally accessible surface data without requiring volumetric observations.

AI.tldr: They build an adjoint-based full-field calibration method for coupled thermo-mechanical materials, showing that surface displacement, force, and temperature measurements are enough to estimate key material parameters accurately.
AI.motivation: Thermomechanical material model calibration is difficult because deformation, temperature, and force are strongly coupled, while experiments typically provide only limited surface measurements.
AI.method: The paper formulates the forward problem as a near-incompressible thermo-hyperelastic model with coupling derived from Helmholtz free energy, and solves the inverse problem as a PDE-constrained optimization with weighted observation terms. Reduced gradients are computed using adjoint sensitivities obtained via automatic differentiation for gradient-based calibration of nonlinear transient thermomechanical systems.
AI.result: The framework recovers ground-truth parameters on synthetic tests and successfully calibrates experimental data by first fitting a hyperelastic baseline under cyclic equibiaxial loading, then identifying thermal expansion and directional shrinkage parameters from surface-temperature and boundary-force histories.
AI.conclusion: A full-field PDE-constrained calibration framework can reliably identify coupled finite-strain thermomechanical material parameters from experimentally accessible surface displacement, force, and temperature data, without needing volumetric observations.

title: Leveraging MTG-FCI fire observations for event-based fire behavior monitoring from near-real-time operation to seasonal analysis
summary:
Wildfire monitoring and suppression require timely information on fire behavior, including fire energy release and rate of spread, to support operational decision-making and resource allocation. Active fire products from the Flexible Combined Imager (FCI) aboard the geostationary Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) satellites provide 10-min observations over Europe and Africa. Deriving fire behavior information from these observations requires associating individual hotspot detections into coherent fire events.
  We present a Fire Event Tracker (FET) algorithm that performs spatio-temporal clustering of hotspot detections from the LSA-SAF FCI active fire product. The algorithm assigns persistent identifiers to fire events and updates their geometry, fire radiative power, and rate of spread at each 10-min interval. The same parameterization is used for both near-real-time and retrospective processing.
  FET was applied retrospectively to the Mediterranean FCI hotspot archive of 2025 and operationally in two near-real-time contexts: wildfire monitoring in Portugal and support of the 2025 SILEX airborne campaign within the EUBURN project, where besides fire monitoring, FET products were also used to initialize coupled FOREFIRE-MesoNH simulations for plume forecasting.
  Results show that event-based clustering of FCI active fire detections provides a consistent description of fire evolution, enabling both tactical wildfire management and high-frequency seasonal fire analyses.

AI.tldr: A new FET algorithm groups 10-minute MTG/FCI fire hotspots into persistent fire events and tracks their growth, power, and spread, proving useful for real-time wildfire monitoring and retrospective seasonal analysis.
AI.motivation: FCI provides high-frequency active fire observations over Europe and Africa, but operational use for fire behavior assessment requires linking individual hotspot detections into coherent fire events so that fire energy release and spread can be tracked over time.
AI.method: The paper proposes a Fire Event Tracker (FET) that performs spatio-temporal clustering of FCI hotspot detections, assigns persistent fire-event IDs, and updates event geometry, fire radiative power, and rate of spread every 10 minutes for both near-real-time and retrospective processing.
AI.result: FET was successfully applied retrospectively to the 2025 Mediterranean FCI hotspot archive and operationally in Portugal and the 2025 SILEX/EUBURN campaign. It provided coherent fire evolution products and was also used to initialize coupled FOREFIRE-MesoNH plume forecasting simulations.
AI.conclusion: Event-based clustering of MTG/FCI active fire detections can consistently reconstruct wildfire evolution, supporting both operational wildfire management and seasonal-scale fire analysis.

title: VideoKR: Towards Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Understanding
summary: We introduce VideoKR, the first large-scale training corpus specifically designed to strengthen knowledge- and reasoning-intensive video understanding. It comprises 315K video reasoning examples over 145K newly collected, CC-licensed, expert-domain videos. We develop a human-in-the-loop, skill-oriented example generation pipeline that targets progressively deeper video reasoning capabilities while ensuring the difficulty, diversity, and reliability of both the examples and their CoT rationales. We also curate VideoKR-Eval, a new expert-annotated benchmark where questions require genuine video understanding and knowledge-intensive reasoning rather than textual shortcuts. Our experiments show that, under a standard SFT$\rightarrow$GRPO pipeline, models post-trained on VideoKR outperform prior post-training approaches on knowledge-intensive video reasoning while remaining competitive on general video reasoning, highlighting data design as a key driver of progress in video reasoning. We further conduct comprehensive ablations to isolate the contributions of VideoKR, providing actionable insights for future work.

AI.tldr: VideoKR is a large, carefully curated dataset and benchmark for training video models to do deeper knowledge-based reasoning; when used in standard post-training, it significantly improves knowledge-intensive video reasoning performance.
AI.motivation: Existing video understanding benchmarks and training data are insufficient for knowledge-intensive and reasoning-intensive video understanding, often allowing textual shortcuts rather than requiring genuine video comprehension and deeper reasoning. The work is motivated by the need for a large-scale, high-quality corpus specifically designed to strengthen these capabilities.
AI.method: The paper builds VideoKR, a 315K-example corpus over 145K newly collected CC-licensed expert-domain videos, using a human-in-the-loop, skill-oriented data generation pipeline that produces difficult, diverse, and reliable reasoning examples with chain-of-thought rationales. It also introduces VideoKR-Eval, an expert-annotated benchmark, and evaluates models under a standard SFT-to-GRPO post-training pipeline with ablation studies.
AI.result: Experiments show that post-training on VideoKR improves performance over previous post-training methods on knowledge-intensive video reasoning, while maintaining competitive results on general video reasoning. The ablation studies further clarify which aspects of the dataset design contribute to the gains.
AI.conclusion: VideoKR demonstrates that carefully designed, large-scale post-training data is a major driver for improving knowledge- and reasoning-intensive video understanding. Models trained on it outperform prior post-training approaches on knowledge-intensive video reasoning while staying competitive on general video reasoning.

title: Epidemiology of Model Collapse: Modeling Synthetic Data Contamination via Bilayer SIR Dynamics
summary: Training on synthetic data causes model collapse, but existing analyses treat this as single-chain degradation. In reality, the AI ecosystem involves cross-contamination: models ingest synthetic data from other models, produce new synthetic text, and contaminate shared corpora. We propose a bilayer coupled SIR/SIRS framework -- a phenomenological mean-field model treating data corpora and AI models as two interacting populations, each with susceptible, infected, and recovered compartments linked by cross-layer transmission. The SIRS variant (our primary recommendation) incorporates immunity waning, reflecting that filtered corpora and retrained models remain susceptible to re-contamination. We derive the basic reproduction number $R_0 = \sqrt{β_D β_M / [(γ_D+μ_D)(γ_M+μ_M)]}$ via the Next Generation Matrix and apply standard epidemic threshold results to the bilayer system. Illustrative scenario-based calibration from public AI text prevalence data yields supercritical dynamics ($R_0 > 1$) across three scenarios; Sobol sensitivity analysis identifies synthetic-text detection as the highest-leverage parameter. A bipartite-network agent-based model confirms mean-field consistency ($R^2 > 0.96$) for dense networks but degrades under heterogeneity. GPT-2 contamination chain experiments (192 runs across WikiText and Shakespeare) show dose-response degradation and diversity loss qualitatively consistent with the threshold picture. Matched-budget source-diversity experiments (1,088 runs) provide suggestive evidence that multi-source mixing modestly attenuates collapse, but the effect vanishes at lower contamination fractions. Intervention analysis identifies detection-based filtering and herd immunity as the highest-leverage strategies.

AI.tldr: Treat synthetic-data contamination as an epidemic spreading jointly between models and datasets. The paper proposes a coupled SIR/SIRS model, derives an R0 threshold, shows realistic scenarios are above threshold, and finds detection/filtering is the strongest control lever; source diversity helps only weakly.
AI.motivation: Prior work studies model collapse largely as a single sequential degradation process, but real-world AI systems are interconnected: models are trained on shared corpora that already contain synthetic text from multiple other models, and their outputs further contaminate future training data. The paper is motivated by the need for a system-level framework that captures this cross-contamination feedback loop and supports threshold analysis and intervention design.
AI.method: The authors build a bilayer mean-field epidemic model with two interacting layers: data corpora and AI models. Each layer is divided into susceptible, infected, and recovered compartments, with cross-layer transmission representing models contaminating corpora and corpora contaminating models. They emphasize an SIRS version with waning immunity, derive the basic reproduction number using the Next Generation Matrix, calibrate illustrative scenarios from public AI-text prevalence data, run Sobol sensitivity analysis, validate the mean-field behavior with a bipartite-network agent-based model, and conduct GPT-2 contamination-chain plus matched-budget source-diversity experiments.
AI.result: The paper derives a closed-form threshold, R0 = sqrt(beta_D beta_M / ((gamma_D+mu_D)(gamma_M+mu_M))), showing when contamination spreads or dies out in the coupled system. Scenario-based calibration indicates supercritical dynamics in all three tested scenarios. Sobol analysis finds synthetic-text detection to be the most influential parameter. Agent-based simulations match the mean-field model well on dense bipartite networks (R^2 > 0.96) but diverge under heterogeneous connectivity. GPT-2 experiments show dose-dependent degradation and diversity loss consistent with the epidemic threshold framing, and source-mixing experiments suggest only modest, fragile mitigation benefits.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that synthetic-data contamination in the AI ecosystem is better understood as a coupled epidemic process across data corpora and models rather than as a single-chain collapse. In the proposed bilayer SIR/SIRS framework, contamination becomes self-sustaining when the derived threshold exceeds one, and under realistic scenario-based calibration the system is supercritical. Detection-based filtering and population-level resistance are identified as the most effective intervention levers, while source diversity offers only limited and contamination-dependent mitigation.

title: Aggregating LLM-Based Weak Verifiers for Spatial Layout Generation
summary: We present a pipeline for building and aggregating task-specific, LLM-generated weak (imperfect) verifiers into a strong verifier for spatial layout domains. Given a task description, our pipeline asks an LLM to synthesize a collection of verifier programs using a layout verification DSL. Each individual LLM-generated verifier usually provides an imperfect check for a match between the layout and the corresponding task description. We show that by aggregating the responses of many such verifiers we can produce a stronger verifier. Moreover, by applying techniques from weak learning, our pipeline can learn how to aggregate the weak verifiers from a very sparse set of human labeled example layouts (about 10). We find that the strong verifiers produced by our pipeline outperform the status-quo approach of using a set of LLM judges to directly check whether a layout matches a task description, raising F1-scores by up to 7X across a variety of 3D room layout and 2D poster design tasks. We also demonstrate that verifier-guided layout generation using natural language feedback from our strong verifiers improves layout quality of a base layout generator by up to 66.2% according to a human evaluator.

AI.tldr: Use an LLM to write many imperfect layout-checking programs, then learn how to combine them from about 10 labeled examples; the combined verifier is much stronger than direct LLM judging and also improves layout generation.
AI.motivation: Direct LLM-based judging of whether a spatial layout satisfies a task description is unreliable. The authors aim to turn many imperfect, task-specific verifier signals into a more accurate and data-efficient verifier for layout domains.
AI.method: The paper proposes a pipeline that takes a task description, prompts an LLM to generate multiple task-specific verifier programs in a layout verification DSL, treats them as weak verifiers, and learns an aggregation rule from a very small set of human-labeled examples using weak learning techniques.
AI.result: The learned strong verifier improves F1 by up to 7x over status-quo LLM judges on 3D room layout and 2D poster design tasks, and verifier-guided generation improves layout quality by up to 66.2% in human evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Aggregating many LLM-generated weak verifier programs into a learned ensemble yields a strong verifier for spatial layout tasks, outperforming direct LLM judging and improving downstream layout generation via verifier-guided feedback.

title: The Evaluation Blind Spot: A Stereological Theory of Benchmark Coverage for Large Language Models
comment: 55 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables, extensive appendix with proofs
summary: We give a stereological theory of LLM benchmark coverage. For any suite with effective dimensionality d_eff, the visible Hausdorff distance between two convex capability profiles consistent with the same scores is bounded by epsilon + C R m^(-1/(d_eff-1)), with matching Lipschitz lower bound. Empirically, three independent leaderboards (Open LLM v2, an extended 12-benchmark suite, LiveBench) all have d_eff in [2.86, 4.80] on their competitive frontier; the structural blind spot exceeds the observed runner-up score gap by two orders of magnitude and dominates statistical noise by 52-127x. Under a chi-squared projection model, the isotropic prior is the optimistic case; across six hidden-capability priors and four ambient dimensions the simulated half-split swap rate of the top two models stays in [0.38, 0.49], and a 500-trial random visible/held-out split shows that 92% of trials swap the top-1 ranking with on average 2.83 of 5 top-5 models changing. A submodular greedy algorithm with the Nemhauser (1 - 1/e) guarantee finds a stable core of 4 benchmarks; 7 of 12 suffice for 90% coverage, and the trained subset transfers across temporal quarters with 93-97% retention. A counterfactual validation across 12 internal benchmarks and 27 Chatbot Arena categories confirms that the eigenstructure predicts which evaluations are irreplaceable (rho = -0.69, p = 0.013 for removal disruption) and which external evaluations bring new information (rho = +0.38). As a second, independent theoretical contribution, we resolve Gardner's Problem 1.5 (1995) for C^2 support functions, establishing the minimax rate Theta(R/(kappa m^(2/(D-1)))) in general dimension via optimal recovery theory on S^(D-1).

AI.tldr: The paper argues that LLM leaderboards are structurally underdetermined: a few visible benchmark scores cannot reliably pin down the true capability ranking because hidden dimensions are large enough to change winners. It provides both theory and experiments showing frequent rank swaps, then proposes a compact benchmark core that preserves most coverage. It also independently solves a classic convex-geometry problem with an optimal minimax rate.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that leaderboard scores from a limited set of benchmarks may substantially underrepresent the true capability space of LLMs. If benchmark coverage is incomplete, rankings can be unstable and misleading. The paper aims to quantify this blind spot theoretically and empirically, and to identify which benchmarks are essential versus redundant.
AI.method: The authors develop a stereological/geometric theory for benchmark coverage using convex capability profiles, effective dimensionality, Hausdorff-distance bounds, and matching lower bounds. They estimate effective dimensionality on multiple LLM leaderboards, simulate hidden-capability priors under a chi-squared projection model, test ranking instability with random visible/held-out splits, and use a submodular greedy selection algorithm with the Nemhauser guarantee to find a stable benchmark core. They also validate predictions against internal benchmarks and Chatbot Arena categories. In a second theory part, they use optimal recovery theory on the sphere to solve Gardner's Problem 1.5 for C^2 support functions.
AI.result: The main results are: (1) a visible Hausdorff upper bound of epsilon + C R m^(-1/(d_eff-1)) and a matching Lipschitz lower bound; (2) empirical effective dimensionality of about 2.86 to 4.80 on competitive frontiers of three leaderboard suites; (3) structural blind spots far larger than runner-up score gaps and statistical noise; (4) high ranking instability, with top-2 swap rates of 0.38 to 0.49 and 92% top-1 swaps under random visible/held-out splits; (5) a stable core of 4 benchmarks, with 7 of 12 giving 90% coverage and 93-97% temporal retention; (6) validation correlations showing eigenstructure predicts irreplaceable and novel evaluations; and (7) a proof of the minimax rate Theta(R/(kappa m^(2/(D-1)))) for Gardner's Problem 1.5.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that current LLM benchmark suites have low effective dimensionality and therefore large structural blind spots: observed leaderboard scores do not uniquely determine true capability profiles, and hidden capabilities can easily change rankings. A small, carefully selected benchmark core can recover most visible coverage and transfer well over time. Separately, the paper proves the optimal minimax rate for Gardner's Problem 1.5 for C^2 support functions.

title: How Far Did They Go? The Persuasive Tactics of Covert LLM Agents in a Discontinued Field Experiment
summary: This study analyzes a publicly released dataset from a discontinued field experiment on Reddit's r/ChangeMyView. The intervention, conducted by unknown, external researchers and halted following ethical backlash, involved undisclosed AI-generated accounts engaging users in live debate. After public disclosure, Reddit authorized moderators to release an archive of the AI-generated comments, creating a rare opportunity to examine how large language models operated in an identity-rich deliberative forum without disclosure. We conduct a structured content analysis of this corpus, evaluating identity performance, authority signaling, alignment strategies, and activation of cognitive heuristics. Identity targeting or adoption appears in over two-thirds of comments, alignment moves and authority claims in nearly all of them, and cognitive-bias triggers -- particularly confirmation bias, representativeness, and availability -- in the large majority. These patterns co-occur systematically, composing a rhetorical architecture calibrated for persuasive efficiency rather than authentic deliberative participation. Compared against human-authored CMV counter-arguments, the agents inverted the typical distribution on every dimension: denser authority use, more adversarial alignment, and heavier reliance on external citation over experiential grounding. In such environments, distinctions between authentic and synthetic epistemic standing grow increasingly opaque -- an asymmetry that disclosure mandates alone cannot address. The results point toward auditing frameworks capable of assessing how AI systems structure credibility, not merely whether they are present.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that covert AI debaters on Reddit were optimized for persuasion through identity cues, authority claims, and cognitive-bias triggers, not authentic deliberation, and argues for auditing frameworks that assess credibility construction rather than just AI disclosure.
AI.motivation: The release of archived AI-generated comments from an ethically controversial, undisclosed Reddit experiment created a rare empirical opportunity to study how large language models behave persuasively in a real, identity-rich deliberative environment without prior disclosure.
AI.method: The paper performs a structured content analysis on a publicly released corpus of AI-generated comments from a discontinued Reddit field experiment, and compares these comments against human-authored CMV counter-arguments across dimensions such as identity performance, authority signaling, alignment strategies, and cognitive heuristics.
AI.result: The study finds identity targeting/adoption in over two-thirds of AI comments, alignment moves and authority claims in nearly all comments, and frequent activation of cognitive heuristics such as confirmation bias, representativeness, and availability. These features co-occur systematically and differ sharply from human CMV arguments, which rely less on authority and external citation and more on experiential grounding.
AI.conclusion: AI-generated debaters in r/ChangeMyView systematically used identity performance, authority signaling, alignment tactics, and cognitive-bias triggers to maximize persuasion, making authentic and synthetic epistemic standing harder to distinguish; disclosure alone is insufficient, so auditing should evaluate how AI structures credibility.

title: Beyond Greedy Chunking: SLO-Aware Sliding-Window Scheduling for LLM Inference
summary: With the rapid growth of interactive applications in large language model (LLM) online services, maintaining high system throughput while ensuring user-perceived latency has become a key issue in inference scheduling. Existing LLM service systems rely on coarse-grained output constraints, making it difficult to effectively handle resource contention among multiple requests, resulting in low resource utilization efficiency and limited support for fine-grained quality of service (QoS) differentiation. We present SlidingServe, a sliding-window-driven SLO-Aware scheduling system for online LLM inference. SlidingServe designed a lightweight batch latency predictor to estimate the execution time of a batch. Based on this, SlidingServe uses SlidingChunker to combine information from the current iteration and the next iteration to achieve dynamic chunking and improve the overall system throughput while maintaining strict QoS guarantees. SlidingServe introduces Multi-Level Priority Sorter to sort candidate requests in order to balance fairness and efficiency. Additionally, when multiple requests within the same batch are at risk of SLO violating,SlidingServe introduces BatchConstructor, which uses dynamic programming to select the set of requests to execute in the current round, mitigating the SLO violation risk of critical requests.Our evaluation demonstrates that SlidingServe can improve service capacity by up to 30% compared to advanced scheduling systems under various load conditions, and further reduces the rate of SLO violation by 16%-53% under heavy-load inference mode.

AI.tldr: SlidingServe 通过滑动窗口预测、动态 chunking、优先级排序和动态规划批构造，在在线 LLM 推理中同时提升吞吐和 SLO 保证。 / SlidingServe boosts online LLM inference throughput and service capacity while cutting SLO violations through sliding-window-based prediction, dynamic chunking, priority sorting, and DP-based batch construction.
AI.motivation: 研究动机是：随着交互式 LLM 在线服务快速增长，系统必须在高吞吐与用户感知延迟之间取得更细粒度的平衡；现有系统依赖粗粒度输出约束，难以有效处理多请求资源竞争，导致资源利用率低、细粒度 QoS 区分能力不足。 / The motivation is that fast-growing interactive LLM services need to sustain high throughput without hurting user-perceived latency, while existing schedulers rely on coarse-grained output constraints and handle resource contention poorly, limiting utilization and fine-grained QoS differentiation.
AI.method: 方法上，论文设计了轻量级 batch 延迟预测器来估计批次执行时间；基于该预测器，SlidingChunker 结合当前迭代与下一迭代的信息进行动态 chunking；Multi-Level Priority Sorter 对候选请求排序以平衡公平性与效率；BatchConstructor 在同批多个请求存在 SLO 违约风险时，利用动态规划选择当前轮应执行的请求集合。 / Methodologically, the paper introduces a lightweight batch latency predictor, a SlidingChunker that jointly uses current- and next-iteration information for dynamic chunking, a Multi-Level Priority Sorter for balancing fairness and efficiency, and a dynamic-programming-based BatchConstructor to reduce SLO violation risk among critical requests.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，在不同负载条件下，SlidingServe 相比先进调度系统可将服务能力最高提升 30%；在重负载推理模式下，SLO 违约率进一步降低 16%–53%。 / Results show that SlidingServe improves service capacity by up to 30% over advanced baselines across various loads, and under heavy-load inference further reduces SLO violation rates by 16%–53%.
AI.conclusion: 提出了 SlidingServe，一个面向在线大语言模型推理的滑动窗口驱动、SLO 感知调度系统；它在保证严格 QoS/SLO 约束的同时显著提升吞吐与资源利用率。 / The paper concludes that SlidingServe, a sliding-window-driven and SLO-aware scheduling system for online LLM inference, can substantially improve throughput and resource efficiency while maintaining strict QoS/SLO guarantees.

title: VITO: Vascular Geometry and Blood Flow Estimation Using Inverse Topology Optimization
summary: Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) is widely used to reconstruct vascular geometry from projection measurements, with conventional approaches such as Filtered Back-Projection (FBP) and Iterative Reconstruction (IR) forming the clinical standard. Blood flow is subsequently estimated through Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations, which require vascular geometry and boundary conditions to be specified a priori. Since the geometry is fixed prior to flow estimation, the recovery of unknown anatomical features (e.g., missing branches or stenoses) is precluded. In this work, we present a fluid-physics-constrained reconstruction framework that leverages topology optimization (TO) to jointly recover vascular geometry and blood velocity directly from time-resolved CTA sinograms. The formulation couples a steady incompressible flow model with a transient advection-diffusion contrast transport model, mapped to sinogram space through a differentiable projection operator. The recovered velocity fields provide hemodynamic information and can support downstream estimation of wall shear stress and flow distribution, without requiring a separate CFD pipeline. The proposed method is demonstrated on synthetic phantoms under varying sparsity and noise levels, and on representative projection data.

AI.tldr: A differentiable physics-based topology-optimization method reconstructs vessel shape and blood flow together from CTA sinograms, enabling recovery of missing anatomy and flow estimates without a separate CFD pipeline.
AI.motivation: Conventional CTA reconstruction and downstream CFD are decoupled: vessel geometry is fixed before flow estimation, which prevents recovery of unknown anatomical structures such as missing branches or stenoses and requires separate boundary-condition-dependent CFD analysis.
AI.method: The method formulates a joint inverse problem combining topology optimization, a steady incompressible flow model, a transient advection-diffusion contrast transport model, and a differentiable projection operator that maps simulated fields into sinogram space for data-consistent reconstruction.
AI.result: The proposed framework is demonstrated on synthetic phantoms across different sparsity and noise settings, as well as representative projection data, showing feasibility for recovering both vascular structure and velocity fields while providing hemodynamic information for downstream metrics.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a fluid-physics-constrained topology-optimization framework can jointly reconstruct vascular geometry and blood velocity directly from time-resolved CTA sinograms, potentially recovering previously unknown anatomical features and reducing reliance on a separate CFD workflow.

title: NIV: Neural Axis Variations for Variable Font Generation
summary: Variable fonts enable continuous variation of glyph geometry along semantic design axes such as weight, width, slant, and optical size. However, constructing a variable font from a static font remains a labor-intensive process requiring expert typographic design and manual specification of glyph variation data. We introduce NIV (Neural Axis Variations), a method that automatically converts a static font into a fully functional variable font. Given glyph outlines and a set of desired design axes, NIV predicts per-point displacements. The model operates directly on vector glyph geometry and employs a novel Property Embedding mechanism that captures interactions between multiple axes, enabling consistent multi-axis variation within a unified framework. We train NIV on a newly constructed dataset derived from variable Google Fonts, comprising over one million variation tuples. The resulting model generalizes across unseen code points, unseen font styles, high-complexity CJK glyphs, and even out-of-distribution handwriting inputs. The generated outputs are standard variable font files supporting continuous interpolation via existing rendering engines. To facilitate research, we release the dataset, the complete training and inference implementation, and trained models at https://github.com/ndvbd/NIV. Beyond typography, our approach demonstrates how structured geometric objects with continuous parametric variation can be synthesized using neural deformations.

AI.tldr: NIV uses a neural deformation model on vector glyph outlines to turn a static font into a usable variable font automatically, handling multiple design axes jointly and generalizing well beyond the training set.
AI.motivation: Creating variable fonts from static fonts is currently labor-intensive, requires expert typographic knowledge, and depends on manually specifying glyph variation data. The paper is motivated by the need to automate this process while preserving continuous controllable variation along semantic axes such as weight, width, slant, and optical size.
AI.method: The paper proposes Neural Axis Variations (NIV), a model that operates directly on vector glyph geometry. Given glyph outlines and target design axes, it predicts per-point displacements. A key component is a Property Embedding mechanism that models interactions among multiple axes so that one unified model can generate consistent multi-axis variations. The model is trained on a large dataset built from variable Google Fonts with over one million variation tuples.
AI.result: NIV produces outputs as standard variable font files compatible with existing rendering engines and supports continuous interpolation. Experiments show strong generalization to unseen code points, unseen font styles, high-complexity CJK glyphs, and even out-of-distribution handwriting inputs. The authors also release the dataset, code, and trained models.
AI.conclusion: NIV can automatically convert a static font into a standard, fully functional variable font by predicting vector-outline point displacements across multiple semantic design axes, and it generalizes well across unseen glyphs, styles, complex CJK characters, and handwriting-like inputs.

title: Preparing for the Next Carrington: Spatiotemporal Agent-Based Modeling for Safeguarding Satellite Infrastructure Under Extreme Space Weather Disturbances
summary:
Extreme space weather poses an existential threat to modern satellite infrastructure, with a Carrington-class solar storm projected to cause economic losses of billions of dollars per day. Due to the rapid proliferation of satellites (with over 70,000 expected to be deployed in the next 5 years), understanding extreme space weather impacts has become essential for global economic stability and national security, and consequently, the lives of millions. However, our current vulnerability to such events remains largely unknown, and existing models rely primarily on statistical populations instead of individual satellite behavior.
  Through the development of a novel spatiotemporal agent-based model (ABM), this study addresses two critical research challenges: (1) predicting the impacts of extreme space weather disturbances and (2) enabling real-time maneuver guidance for satellites during such events. Utilizing 41,644 satellite records, historical records from 5 recent space weather events, and atmospheric density models, we built individual satellite agents with physics-driven behaviors that make independent decisions by dynamically responding to constraints such as propellant requirements and collision avoidance thresholds.
  Scenario analysis suggests that 95% of satellites in Low Earth Orbit altitudes would experience enhanced atmospheric drag of 8x baseline levels, increasing collision risks by 2-3x. Monte Carlo simulations also predict direct economic impact per affected satellite on the order of $40M. Furthermore, the model successfully uses real-time conditions to provide maneuver recommendations, with 92% accuracy. This study is thus the first to provide a prototype framework for real-time adaptive decision systems to safeguard satellites against the next Carrington-class disruption.

AI.tldr: This paper builds a satellite-by-satellite agent-based simulation for extreme space weather. It finds major increases in drag, collision risk, and economic loss during severe storms, and shows that the model can generate accurate real-time maneuver recommendations.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that extreme space weather may severely disrupt rapidly growing satellite infrastructure, yet current vulnerability remains poorly understood because most existing approaches rely on statistical populations rather than individual satellite behavior. A more granular and operationally useful model is needed to predict impacts and support real-time mitigation.
AI.method: The study develops a novel spatiotemporal agent-based model using 41,644 satellite records, historical data from five recent space weather events, and atmospheric density models. Each satellite is modeled as an individual physics-driven agent that makes decisions under operational constraints such as propellant limits and collision avoidance thresholds. Scenario analysis and Monte Carlo simulation are used to estimate physical and economic impacts, while real-time environmental inputs are used for maneuver recommendation.
AI.result: The results indicate that about 95% of satellites in low Earth orbit would face atmospheric drag around 8 times the baseline during extreme events, raising collision risk by 2 to 3 times. Monte Carlo simulations estimate direct economic losses of roughly $40M per affected satellite, and the real-time maneuver guidance component achieves 92% accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a spatiotemporal agent-based model can estimate satellite-level impacts of extreme space weather and provide effective real-time maneuver guidance. It suggests that Carrington-class events could sharply increase atmospheric drag and collision risk for most low Earth orbit satellites, with substantial economic losses per affected satellite.

title: Predict and Reconstruct: Joint Objectives for Self-Supervised Language Representation Learning
comment: 12 pages, 10 figures, 11 tables. Preprint. Code available at : https://github.com/aymen-000/predict-reconstruct-language-models
summary: Masked language modelling (MLM) has been the dominant pre-training objective for text encoders since BERT, yet it encourages representations that are strongly anchored to surface-form token identity rather than deeper semantic structure. Inspired by the success of Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) (LeCun, 2022) in vision and audio, we propose a hybrid pre-training objective that combines a JEPA-style latent-space prediction loss with a standard MLM objective over a single shared encoder. A learnable scalar parameter continuously balances the two objectives during training. We pre-train both a hybrid model and a pure-MLM baseline on English Wikipedia using identical architectures and compute budgets (NVIDIA H100). Extensive representation analysis across five GLUE benchmarks (SST-2, MRPC, MNLI, CoLA, STS-B) using four pooling strategies reveals that the hybrid encoder produces significantly more uniform embeddings (uniformity less than -0.16 vs -0.05 for MLM), exhibits richer spectral geometry under max pooling, encodes less surface-level lexical information, and achieves a better semantic-to-lexical balance. Despite similar linear-probe downstream accuracy, the geometric differences are consistent and significant, suggesting that the JEPA predictive objective reshapes the latent space in ways that standard accuracy metrics alone cannot capture.

AI.tldr: A JEPA+MLM hybrid objective for text encoders does not noticeably improve GLUE accuracy over MLM alone, but it consistently produces cleaner, more semantic, and less token-identity-driven representation geometry.
AI.motivation: Standard MLM has dominated text encoder pre-training but tends to anchor representations to token identity and surface form rather than deeper semantic structure; the work is motivated by adapting JEPA-style predictive learning, successful in vision and audio, to encourage more semantically structured text representations.
AI.method: The paper pre-trains a shared text encoder on English Wikipedia using a hybrid objective that combines a JEPA-style latent-space prediction loss with standard masked language modeling, balanced by a learnable scalar during training; it compares this model against an architecture- and compute-matched pure-MLM baseline and evaluates representations on five GLUE tasks with four pooling strategies.
AI.result: Compared with the pure MLM baseline, the hybrid encoder yields substantially more uniform embeddings, richer spectral geometry under max pooling, less surface-level lexical encoding, and a better semantic-to-lexical balance, while maintaining similar linear-probe performance on GLUE benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid JEPA+MLM pre-training objective meaningfully reshapes encoder representation geometry toward more semantic and less surface-form-biased embeddings, even when conventional downstream accuracy remains similar to a pure MLM baseline.

title: The Invisible Hand of Physics: When Video Diffusion Models Know More Than They Show
summary: Modern video diffusion models generate increasingly realistic and temporally coherent videos, motivating their use as candidate world simulators. Yet it remains unclear whether these models internally encode physical structure, or merely reproduce motion patterns seen during training. We study this question by probing video diffusion models along latent trajectories corresponding to real videos with known physical plausibility. To obtain such trajectories, we approximately invert the deterministic sampling process by integrating the learned velocity field backward from a clean video latent to noise, giving access to the model's intermediate states and attention maps. Using these recovered trajectories, we show that physical plausibility is linearly decodable from diffusion transformer states across IntPhys and InfLevel, reaching around 81.27% average accuracy and outperforming dedicated representation-learning baselines such as V-JEPA and VideoMAE. Surprisingly, this signal is absent from the VAE latent input and emerges inside the denoising transformer itself, despite the model not being trained with a self-supervised predictive objective. These findings suggest that physically meaningful representations can arise as a byproduct of generative denoising.

AI.tldr: By reconstructing and probing latent denoising trajectories in video diffusion models, the paper shows that their transformer internals encode physical plausibility, even without explicit predictive self-supervised training.
AI.motivation: Although modern video diffusion models produce realistic and temporally coherent videos, it is unclear whether they actually internalize physical structure or simply imitate motion statistics from training data. The work aims to test whether these models contain representations of physical plausibility.
AI.method: The paper approximately inverts the deterministic sampling trajectory of a video diffusion model by integrating the learned velocity field backward from a clean video latent to noise. It then probes intermediate transformer states and attention maps along recovered latent trajectories using linear decoding to test whether physical plausibility is represented.
AI.result: On IntPhys and InfLevel, physical plausibility is linearly decodable from diffusion transformer states with about 81.27% average accuracy, outperforming representation-learning baselines such as V-JEPA and VideoMAE. The signal is not present in the VAE latent input and instead emerges within the denoising transformer.
AI.conclusion: Physically meaningful representations can emerge inside video diffusion transformers as a byproduct of generative denoising, and these representations encode physical plausibility better than several dedicated video representation baselines.

title: ERRORQUAKE: Heavy-Tailed Error Severity Distributions in Open-Weight Large Language Models
summary: At matched accuracy, open-weight LLMs differ substantially in the shape of their error severity distribution -- a difference invisible to the scalar error rate. Hallucination benchmarks report a single error count and treat all errors as equivalent, yet a wrong date and a fabricated court ruling differ by orders of magnitude. We introduce Errorquake-10k, a 10,000-query benchmark scoring each response on a continuous 0-4 severity scale across 8 domains and 5 difficulty tiers, and we fit per-model severity distributions for 21 open-weight models. For each model we estimate a severity distribution index (b, the Gutenberg-Richter upper-tail slope) with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Headline: across the 210 model pairs, 85 have disjoint 95% b confidence intervals at matched accuracy (|Delta epsilon| < 0.05) on human-consensus scoring, e.g. deepseek-v3.2 vs. ministral-14b at epsilon = 0.586 and Delta b = 0.47. A 519-item three-rater human validation study confirms measurement reliability (ICC(2,k=3) = 0.85), validates the LLM-judge ranking (rho = 0.89), and confirms the dense-model scaling correlation on human data (rho_s = -0.86). We prove a Non-Reducibility Theorem showing that severity profile and error rate are informationally non-redundant (I(b; model | epsilon) = 1.56 bits; 64.5% of cross-model b variance is unexplained by epsilon). A severity mechanism taxonomy (kappa = 0.83) reveals that error type shifts categorically with severity: low-severity errors are retrievals (71%); high-severity errors are fabrications (39%) -- and this composition differs by model size (p < 0.0001). Severity distribution should be reported alongside accuracy; it carries discriminative information that the error rate cannot.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that two LLMs can have the same accuracy but very different kinds of mistakes. Using a new 10k-query benchmark and a continuous error-severity scale, the authors find severity patterns differ significantly across open models and contain information that plain error rate misses.
AI.motivation: Existing hallucination benchmarks collapse all errors into a single count and ignore that errors vary greatly in real-world impact, so scalar error rate hides important differences between models.
AI.method: The paper introduces Errorquake-10k, a 10,000-query benchmark with continuous 0-4 severity scoring across 8 domains and 5 difficulty tiers, evaluates 21 open-weight models, fits per-model severity distributions using the Gutenberg-Richter upper-tail slope b, and validates the measurements with bootstrap confidence intervals, human three-rater annotation, LLM-judge comparison, and a severity mechanism taxonomy.
AI.result: Among 210 model pairs, 85 have disjoint 95% confidence intervals for severity slope b at matched accuracy; human validation shows strong reliability (ICC=0.85), strong agreement with LLM-judge rankings (rho=0.89), and strong scaling correlation on human data (rho_s=-0.86). Severity profile is proven non-redundant with error rate, with 1.56 bits of conditional information and 64.5% of cross-model b variance unexplained by epsilon.
AI.conclusion: Severity distribution should be reported alongside accuracy because models with similar error rates can differ substantially in how severe their errors are, and severity provides non-redundant discriminative information beyond scalar accuracy.

title: What Should Agents Say? Action-state Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models are typically organized around roles, pipelines, and turn schedules, while the content that agents pass to one another is often left as unconstrained natural language. However, this free-form communication can rapidly inflate token usage, consume the shared context window, and ultimately affect both system performance and inference cost. We analyze five common inter-agent communication strategies across two MAS topologies, finding that no fixed strategy is universally optimal. Instead, effective inter-agent messages consistently preserve action-centered information needed by downstream agents. Building on this, we propose the PACT (Protocolized Action-state Communication and Transmission), which treats inter-agent communication as a public state-update problem and projects each raw agent output into a compact action-state record before it enters shared history. Across different MAS topologies, PACT consistently improves the performance-cost trade-off, achieving comparable or stronger task performance with substantially fewer tokens. The gains extend to production coding harnesses: PACT lifts OpenHands' resolve rate at -10% tokens-per-resolved, and is resolve-neutral on SWE-agent while halving input tokens. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/iNLP-Lab/PACT.

AI.tldr: LLM multi-agent teams waste tokens when agents talk in free-form text. This paper proposes PACT, which compresses agent outputs into structured action-state updates, improving or preserving task performance while significantly cutting token usage.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM-based multi-agent systems rely on unconstrained natural-language communication between agents, which increases token consumption, fills the shared context window, and can hurt both system performance and inference cost.
AI.method: The paper analyzes five common inter-agent communication strategies across two multi-agent system topologies, identifies that effective messages preserve downstream-relevant action-centered information, and then proposes PACT, which converts each raw agent output into a compact public action-state record before adding it to shared history.
AI.result: PACT achieves comparable or better task performance with substantially fewer tokens across multiple MAS topologies. In production coding settings, it improves OpenHands' resolve rate with 10% fewer tokens per resolved issue and remains resolve-neutral on SWE-agent while reducing input tokens by about half.
AI.conclusion: PACT, a protocolized action-state communication method for LLM-based multi-agent systems, consistently improves the performance-cost trade-off by preserving action-centered information while substantially reducing token usage across different MAS topologies and production coding harnesses.

title: Demystifying NVSHMEM: A System-Level Analysis on Symmetric Memory and Device-Initiated Operations in GPU Communication
summary: NVSHMEM is NVIDIA's OpenSHMEM-based PGAS communication library for GPU clusters, enabling GPU-initiated, one-sided communication through symmetric memory. Despite its growing adoption, a system-level understanding of its design and behavior remains scattered across documentation, source code, and application experience. This paper presents a concise study of NVSHMEM's programming model, implementation, and performance characteristics, focusing on symmetric memory, one-sided operations, and device-side collectives. We also examine DeepEP as a case study of NVSHMEM in performance-critical sparse deep learning workloads. Our analysis shows that NVSHMEM pioneered a device-side symmetric-memory programming model that enables fine-grained GPU-driven communication and is important for approaching the hardware performance limit. Overall, this work defines NVSHMEM's role as a systems building block, highlights its design tradeoffs, and identifies opportunities for improving GPU communication runtimes.

AI.tldr: A focused systems analysis of NVSHMEM: how its symmetric-memory, GPU-initiated one-sided communication model works, why it matters for high-performance GPU clusters, and what tradeoffs and optimization opportunities remain.
AI.motivation: Although NVSHMEM is increasingly used in GPU clusters, knowledge about how it works at the system level is fragmented across documentation, source code, and application practice; the paper aims to consolidate and clarify this understanding.
AI.method: The paper conducts a concise system-level study of NVSHMEM by analyzing its programming model, implementation details, and performance behavior, with emphasis on symmetric memory, one-sided operations, and device-side collectives, and uses DeepEP as a case study in sparse deep learning workloads.
AI.result: The study shows that NVSHMEM pioneered a practical device-side symmetric-memory programming model, supports fine-grained GPU-driven communication effectively, and serves as an important systems primitive for high-performance GPU communication, especially in performance-critical workloads such as sparse deep learning.
AI.conclusion: NVSHMEM establishes a device-side symmetric-memory PGAS model for GPU clusters that enables fine-grained, GPU-initiated one-sided communication and helps applications approach hardware communication limits, while still exposing clear systems tradeoffs and runtime improvement opportunities.

title: AGI and the Limits of Value Production
summary: This paper develops a political-economy model of artificial general intelligence (AGI) as a technology that progressively substitutes living labor with machine-based productive systems. The model studies the transition from the first moment at which AGI becomes economically capable of replacing labor to the later moment at which AGI becomes technically and actually capable of near-complete replacement. The central distinction is between technical substitutability and actual adoption. Technical substitutability is the feasible replacement ceiling implied by the state of AGI capability, whereas actual adoption is the realized replacement share chosen under cost, profitability, and adoption frictions. Under the strict value-theoretic assumption that AGI transfers value but does not itself create new value, deeper AGI adoption raises the organic composition of capital, reduces the quantity of living labor when adoption outpaces the creation of new labor fields, compresses the source of surplus value, and places downward pressure on the social rate of profit. In the limiting case in which actual AGI adoption approaches complete substitution and new labor fields fail to compensate for displaced labor, living labor tends to zero, surplus value tends to zero, and the profit rate tends to zero. The model therefore identifies near-complete AGI substitution not merely as an efficiency transition, but as a boundary case for value production under a strict political-economy theory of value.
