title: Personal AI Agent for Camera Roll VQA
comment: Project page, code, and demo: https://thaoshibe.github.io/camroll
summary: We study the personal camera roll visual question answering setting. In this setting, a conversational AI assistant can access a user's personal camera roll and retrieve relevant photos to answer queries, ranging from simple factual questions (e.g., ``Name of the food I tried yesterday?'') to more open-ended ones (e.g., ``Recommend some dishes I have never eaten before''). Given the vast nature of the personal camera roll (i.e., multiple years, hundreds to thousands of photos), a successful AI assistant needs to understand a long-horizon, highly personalized visual content stream in order to navigate and locate the correct and/or relevant information. To support this, we collect and manually annotate questions that mimic real-world usage. The final dataset, camroll, contains 50 users, 31,476 images, and 2,500 QA pairs. We further design camroll-agent, a conversational AI agent equipped with hierarchical memory and a minimal set of tools for efficient navigation over large, personalized visual memory. Experimental results show that camroll-agent outperforms numerous baselines and methods for long-context understanding AI agents system. Together, the camroll dataset and camroll-agent highlight the gap in AI agents' long-context reasoning: personalized visual memory requires different approaches from standard long-context textual memory, especially when consistency, visual details, and user-specific context are present.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：这篇论文为“个人相册问答”提出了一个新数据集和一个分层记忆 agent，证明处理个性化视觉长期记忆不能直接照搬文本长上下文方法。 / TL;DR: This paper introduces a new dataset and a hierarchical-memory agent for personal camera-roll QA, showing that personalized long-term visual memory cannot be handled well by simply reusing standard long-context text approaches.
AI.motivation: 论文动机：个人相册包含多年、数百到数千张照片，用户问题既有事实型也有开放型，现有长上下文方法难以同时处理长期跨度、视觉细节、一致性与用户特定语境，因此需要新的数据与方法。 / Motivation: Personal camera rolls span years and contain hundreds to thousands of photos; user queries range from factual to open-ended, and existing long-context methods struggle with long time horizons, visual detail, consistency, and user-specific context, motivating new datasets and methods.
AI.method: 论文方法：作者构建了一个名为 camroll 的个人相册视觉问答数据集，并提出 camroll-agent，一个具备分层记忆和最小工具集的对话式 AI agent，用于在大规模、长期、个性化图像流中高效检索与推理。 / Method: The authors build a personal camera-roll VQA dataset called camroll and propose camroll-agent, a conversational AI agent with hierarchical memory and a minimal toolset for efficient retrieval and reasoning over large-scale, long-horizon, personalized image streams.
AI.result: 论文结果：camroll 数据集包含 50 位用户、31,476 张图像和 2,500 个问答对；实验表明 camroll-agent 优于多种基线以及长上下文理解 agent 系统。 / Result: The camroll dataset contains 50 users, 31,476 images, and 2,500 QA pairs; experiments show that camroll-agent outperforms numerous baselines and long-context understanding agent systems.
AI.conclusion: 论文结论：个性化视觉记忆与标准长文本记忆不同，面向个人相册的长上下文推理需要专门的方法；所提出的 camroll 数据集与 camroll-agent 能有效揭示并缩小这一差距。 / Conclusion: Personalized visual memory differs from standard long-context textual memory, and personal camera-roll reasoning requires specialized methods; the proposed camroll dataset and camroll-agent expose and help reduce this gap.

title: Multi-Condition Guided Diffusion Model for Controllable Elastic Parameter Synthesis
summary: Prestack elastic parameter inversion is important for reservoir characterization and quantitative seismic interpretation. Most existing deep-learning-based methods have achieved promising results, but they generally require sufficient labeled training data and have limited flexibility in integrating multi-source conditioning information. To address this issue, we propose a multi-condition guided diffusion model for controllable elastic parameter synthesis. Elastic parameter training datasets are first constructed based on well log statistics and geological characteristics of the target area and are used to train the diffusion model. A unified multi-condition guided diffusion framework is then developed to incorporate both implicit and explicit conditioning information. Specifically, iterative latent variable refinement, Adapter-based conditioning, and a diffusion posterior sampling (DPS)-projection guidance strategy are introduced for implicit model-domain constraints, implicit structural constraints, and explicit conditioning-operator constraints, respectively. Synthetic examples demonstrate that the proposed method can generate elastic parameter samples that are consistent with the prescribed conditions under both single-condition and multi-condition guidance. When seismic data are used as conditioning information, the framework can be further adapted to seismic elastic parameter inversion. Experiments show that the proposed method improves the prediction of representative elastic parameters, including P-wave velocity, S-wave velocity, and density, compared with baseline methods. The synthesized samples can also support downstream deep-learning-based inversion under limited labeled data, achieving competitive performance.

AI.tldr: A multi-condition guided diffusion model is proposed for controllable elastic-parameter synthesis and seismic inversion, combining several guidance mechanisms to use diverse constraints; it outperforms baselines and is especially useful when labeled training data are limited.
AI.motivation: Existing deep-learning methods for prestack elastic parameter inversion perform well but depend heavily on sufficient labeled data and offer limited flexibility for integrating multiple conditioning sources. The work is motivated by the need for controllable synthesis and inversion under limited labels and multi-source constraints.
AI.method: The method constructs elastic-parameter training datasets from well-log statistics and geological characteristics, trains a diffusion model, and introduces a unified multi-condition guidance framework combining iterative latent variable refinement, Adapter-based conditioning, and DPS-projection guidance to incorporate implicit model-domain, structural, and explicit operator-based constraints.
AI.result: Synthetic and inversion experiments show the method generates elastic parameter samples consistent with prescribed single or multiple conditions, adapts to seismic conditioning for inversion, improves predictions of P-wave velocity, S-wave velocity, and density compared with baselines, and helps downstream deep-learning inversion achieve competitive performance with limited labeled data.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a unified multi-condition guided diffusion framework can controllably synthesize elastic parameter models and can be adapted for seismic elastic parameter inversion, improving prediction of P-wave velocity, S-wave velocity, and density over baseline methods while also supporting downstream inversion when labeled data are scarce.

title: Improving Heart-Focused Medical Question Answering in LLMs via Variance-Aware Rubric Rewards with GRPO
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong promise in healthcare applications. Yet deploying general-purpose models in real-world settings remains difficult due to data privacy constraints, inference costs, and limited suitability for edge or on-device use. These challenges motivate the development of smaller, more efficient models that require robust post-training strategies to ensure reliable medical reasoning. In this work, we investigate Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for post-training LLMs on heart-focused medical question answering with rubric-based supervision derived from RaR-Medicine. We propose a Variance-Aware Reward Framework that extends the Explicit Aggregation and Implicit Aggregation strategies of Rubrics as Rewards by replacing weighted binary criterion aggregation and single overall Likert-style scoring with continuous analytical reward functions derived from criterion-level rubric outcomes. This formulation provides richer optimization signals for feedback that is sparse, multi-criteria, and difficult to verify automatically, and enables more stable on-policy reinforcement learning. On a held-out heart-related subset of HealthBench, our best GRPO variant improves accuracy from 0.362 to 0.502 and F1 from 0.532 to 0.668 relative to the Qwen3-14B base model, while remaining competitive with GPT-OSS-120B (0.508 accuracy, 0.674 F1). Our findings show that carefully designed rubric-based rewards provide a practical strategy for improving heart-focused medical question answering in LLMs, with potential to extend to other rubric-based tasks.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that GRPO with a variance-aware, rubric-based reward design can significantly improve a 14B model on cardiology QA, bringing it close to a much larger 120B model while remaining more practical for healthcare deployment.
AI.motivation: General-purpose LLMs are hard to deploy in healthcare because of privacy constraints, inference cost, and weak suitability for edge or on-device use. Smaller models are more deployable, but they need effective post-training methods to achieve reliable medical reasoning.
AI.method: The paper post-trains a Qwen3-14B model for heart-focused medical QA using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with rubric-based supervision derived from RaR-Medicine. It introduces a Variance-Aware Reward Framework that converts criterion-level rubric outcomes into continuous analytical reward functions, extending both explicit and implicit rubric aggregation strategies.
AI.result: On a held-out heart-related subset of HealthBench, the best GRPO variant improves accuracy from 0.362 to 0.502 and F1 from 0.532 to 0.668 over the Qwen3-14B base model, approaching GPT-OSS-120B performance of 0.508 accuracy and 0.674 F1.
AI.conclusion: Carefully designed rubric-based rewards combined with GRPO can substantially improve heart-focused medical question answering in smaller LLMs, making them more practical for healthcare deployment and competitive with much larger models.

title: Monte Carlo Steklov Operators for Large-Scale Geometry Processing in the Wild
summary: Intrinsic methods fill the default toolbox for geometry processing on meshes. Intrinsic operators, in particular the Laplacian, underlie methods that require invariance to isometry and have hence been employed in many algorithms for shape analysis, learning, and editing. However, intrinsic methods are predicated on assumptions that quickly become brittle when working with in-the-wild geometry, where (i) mesh quality is not guaranteed, and (ii) many meshes are modeled with multiple connected components. In such settings, volumetric constructions are better-defined, since restrictions on surface topology can be relaxed. This paper presents a Monte Carlo method for estimating the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operator -- a boundary-to-boundary volumetric operator -- and its associated Steklov eigenmodes. We build on recent developments in Monte Carlo geometry processing by casting this boundary operator itself as the subject of estimation. The DtN operator, defined through a volumetric stochastic process, is then generalized to the exterior domain, where it couples disconnected components through the surrounding ambient space. We show that our method is orders of magnitude faster than existing boundary-element approaches for computing Steklov spectra while remaining robust to poor triangulations, high-resolution meshes, and multi-component geometry. To demonstrate this scalability, we compute interior and exterior Steklov eigenspectra for approximately 450,000 shapes from the uncurated Objaverse dataset. We incorporate these operators into Steklov-CLIP, a mesh-based neural network that uses volumetric spectral operators for large-scale contrastive 3D representation learning. The resulting network learns semantically meaningful global and dense shape representations, illustrating that geometrically-principled volumetric operators can be made practical at the scale of modern 3D datasets.

AI.tldr: 论文提出一种Monte Carlo体积谱方法来估计DtN算子和Steklov特征模态，既快又稳健，尤其适合劣质、多组件的大规模3D网格，并成功用于Objaverse级别的3D表示学习。 / The paper presents a Monte Carlo volumetric spectral method for estimating the DtN operator and Steklov eigenmodes that is fast, robust, and well suited to large-scale, poor-quality, multi-component 3D meshes, and it works effectively for Objaverse-scale representation learning.
AI.motivation: 动机在于传统内蕴网格处理方法依赖表面Laplacian等内蕴算子，但这些方法在真实世界几何数据上容易失效，因为网格质量差、分辨率高、且常含多个不连通组件；相比之下，体积方法对拓扑限制更少，更适合处理非理想数据。 / The motivation is that standard intrinsic mesh-processing methods, especially those based on the Laplacian, become brittle on in-the-wild geometry due to poor mesh quality, high resolution, and multiple disconnected components. Volumetric constructions are better defined in these cases and impose fewer topological restrictions.
AI.method: 方法上，作者将DtN这一边界到边界的体积算子本身作为Monte Carlo估计对象，通过体积随机过程来定义和估计该算子及其Steklov谱；同时将其推广到外部域，使环境空间能够耦合多个彼此断开的网格组件；最后将这些体积谱算子用于Steklov-CLIP网络进行对比学习。 / Methodologically, the authors directly estimate the boundary-to-boundary DtN operator via Monte Carlo geometry processing, using a volumetric stochastic process to define and compute the operator and its Steklov spectrum. They further generalize it to the exterior domain to couple disconnected components through ambient space, and integrate these volumetric spectral operators into a contrastive neural model, Steklov-CLIP.
AI.result: 结果表明，该方法在计算Steklov谱时比现有边界元方法快几个数量级，同时对差三角化、高分辨率网格和多组件几何保持鲁棒；作者还在约45万个Objaverse形状上计算了内外Steklov谱，并展示Steklov-CLIP能够学习具有语义意义的全局与稠密3D表示。 / Results show that the method is orders of magnitude faster than existing boundary-element approaches for Steklov spectra, while remaining robust to bad triangulations, high-resolution meshes, and multi-component geometry. The authors compute interior and exterior Steklov spectra for about 450,000 Objaverse shapes and demonstrate that Steklov-CLIP learns semantically meaningful global and dense 3D representations.
AI.conclusion: 该论文证明了基于Monte Carlo的Dirichlet-to-Neumann（DtN）算子与Steklov特征模态估计在实际大规模3D数据上是可行的；相比传统边界元方法更快、对劣质网格和多连通组件更稳健，并且能够有效支持大规模3D表示学习。 / The paper concludes that Monte Carlo estimation of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operator and Steklov eigenmodes is practical for large-scale 3D geometry, substantially faster than boundary-element methods, more robust to poor meshes and multi-component shapes, and useful for large-scale 3D representation learning.

title: Staged Factorial Screening for Budget-Constrained Micro-Pretraining
summary: Budget-constrained micro-pretraining often requires triaging many candidate recipes on a shared accelerator before larger search budgets are spent. We study whether a staged fractional-factorial workflow can recover stable early effect structure in this setting. On a fixed autoresearch-derived single-GPU training loop, we run 613 experiments across pilot and follow-up screens at 2, 5, and 10 minutes; full 16-condition seeded reruns at 5 and 10 minutes; targeted seeded anchor checks; same-host greedy and matched-cost random baselines; a 60-minute bridge package; and bounded Windows A100 and Linux L40S anchor continuations through 24 hours. Main penalties from total batch, depth, and width are largest at short budgets and relax as budget increases. Within the predeclared seeded full-screen families, D, A, B, and C retain non-zero estimates at 5 and 10 minutes after within-budget Benjamini-Hochberg correction, while E does not. Random search can reach strong incumbents in this 32-condition space, but repeatedly in the same low-penalty region and without factor attribution. The 60-minute bridge anchor has the lowest mean, although that package does not separate workflow refinement from the larger bridge model's capacity advantage. In bounded 12-hour and 24-hour three-anchor continuations on both hosts, the bridge has the lowest sample mean while the non-bridge ordering stays host-sensitive. We therefore present a bounded methods result: use short designed screens to identify high-penalty directions, confirm promising anchors under repeated runs, and refine locally inside the reduced space. The evidence supports a bridge-centered recommendation through 24 hours on two hosts, not hardware-invariant ranking or general hyperparameter-optimization superiority.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文证明：在超小预算预训练中，短时长的实验设计筛选比单纯随机试更适合先找出“明显差”的方向；再对少数候选做重复验证和局部细化，效率更高。到24小时为止，bridge方案在两种硬件上整体最稳，但作者没有声称它在所有硬件上排序都一致，也没有证明它普遍胜过所有超参数优化方法。
AI.motivation: 动机是解决预算受限的micro-pretraining场景：在真正投入更大搜索预算前，需要在共享加速器上快速筛查大量候选训练配方。作者关注的是，分阶段的分数因子设计能否在极短训练预算下恢复稳定的早期效应结构，并比单纯随机搜索提供更可解释的因素归因。
AI.method: 论文采用分阶段的分数因子设计工作流，在固定的单GPU训练循环上进行613次实验。实验包括2/5/10分钟的pilot与follow-up筛选、5/10分钟的16条件带种子重复全筛、定向带种子anchor检查、同主机greedy与匹配成本随机基线、60分钟bridge实验包，以及在Windows A100和Linux L40S上延续到24小时的有界anchor continuation。统计上使用预算内Benjamini-Hochberg校正评估因素效应。
AI.result: 结果表明，总batch、depth和width在短预算下带来的性能惩罚最大，且随着预算增加而减弱。在预先声明的带种子全筛家族中，D、A、B、C在5和10分钟下经Benjamini-Hochberg校正后仍保持非零估计，而E没有。随机搜索虽然能在32条件空间中找到较强候选，但反复落在相同的低惩罚区域，且无法提供因素归因。60分钟bridge anchor具有最低平均值；在12小时和24小时、两个主机上的三anchor延续实验中，bridge仍具有最低样本均值，但非bridge方案的相对排序对主机敏感。
AI.conclusion: 提出一种有界的方法学结论：先用短时长的设计化筛选识别高惩罚方向，再通过重复运行确认有前景的锚点，并在缩减后的空间内做局部细化。证据支持在两个主机上、最长到24小时的预算内优先采用bridge方案，但不支持硬件不变的排序结论，也不证明其普遍优于一般超参数优化。

title: I Know What You Meme, Even If it Emerged Today: Understanding Evolving Memes through Open-World Knowledge Acquisition
summary: Multimodal memes are dynamic and often require up to date background knowledge for interpretation. Existing methods often overlook such knowledge or rely on fixed parametric knowledge of pretrained models that may be incomplete, outdated, or unavailable for emerging memes. We introduce Query Retrieve Conclude, a zero shot framework that identifies missing knowledge, retrieves open web evidence, and synthesizes evidence grounded background knowledge for meme understanding and detection. We also introduce a curated meme understanding benchmark of recent memes from 2024 to 2026 with external background knowledge annotations. Experiments on three meme understanding datasets and five meme detection tasks show that our framework improves knowledge recovery, meme understanding and downstream detection over zero shot baselines.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that modern memes often need fresh external knowledge to understand. It presents a zero-shot system that detects what knowledge is missing, searches the web for evidence, and uses that evidence to explain and classify memes, achieving better performance than standard zero-shot methods.
AI.motivation: Multimodal memes are time-sensitive and often depend on current background knowledge. Existing approaches either ignore this need or depend on static parametric knowledge in pretrained models, which can be incomplete, outdated, or ineffective for emerging memes.
AI.method: The paper proposes Query Retrieve Conclude (QRC), a zero-shot pipeline that first identifies missing background knowledge in a multimodal meme, then retrieves relevant open-web evidence, and finally synthesizes grounded background knowledge for interpretation and detection. It also introduces a curated benchmark of recent memes from 2024 to 2026 with annotated external knowledge needs.
AI.result: Across three meme understanding datasets and five meme detection tasks, the framework outperforms zero-shot baselines in knowledge recovery, meme understanding, and downstream detection.
AI.conclusion: A zero-shot framework, Query Retrieve Conclude, can improve meme knowledge recovery, understanding, and downstream detection by retrieving up-to-date external evidence instead of relying only on fixed model knowledge.

title: LLM-Based Porting of Optimized C++ to CUDA Through Deoptimization and Reoptimization
summary: When porting high-performance computing (HPC) code from CPU to GPU, CPU-oriented optimizations may obstruct LLM-based CUDA translation. We design and evaluate a Deopt-Reopt workflow that first simplifies the input C++ code and then retranslates and reoptimizes it for CUDA, comparing it against direct translation (Direct) on twelve HPC kernels with two LLMs (gpt-oss-120b (O120) and qwen-3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507 (Q235)) in Single-shot (one pass) and Iterative (repeated refinement) settings. In Single-shot, among 18 testable cases Deopt-Reopt was significantly faster among successful trials (after BH-FDR correction) in five - most clearly for conv2d, where CPU- and GPU-oriented designs diverge - but Direct was faster in three, so removing CPU-specific optimizations is not universally beneficial. An exploratory Direct-3 control that equalizes the LLM-call count left Deopt-Reopt ahead in only four of nineteen testable cases, with Direct-3 ahead in four others. In Iterative, repeated generation and repair narrow the mode gap - markedly so for O120 - while Q235 retains large Deopt-Reopt advantages on conv2d, ddgemm, and bgemm. Deopt-Reopt's effect on feasibility is also mixed - sharply higher for some kernels Direct rarely compiles, lower for others. Because performance is conditioned on successful trials, the benefit is conditional rather than a guaranteed end-to-end gain. Overall, Deopt-Reopt is an effective but non-universal technique for LLM-based GPU porting, with gains that depend on the kernel, the model, the search budget, and the success rate.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：先“去除 CPU 优化”再让 LLM 生成 CUDA，有时明显优于直接翻译，特别是在 CPU/GPU 设计差异大的算子上；但这种优势并不稳定，经过多轮迭代或控制调用次数后差距会缩小，因此它更像是一种有条件有效的迁移策略，而非通用最佳实践。 / TL;DR: Stripping CPU-oriented optimizations before LLM-based CUDA generation can help, especially for kernels with strong CPU/GPU design mismatch, but the advantage is inconsistent. Once iteration or call-budget controls are introduced, the gap narrows, making Deopt-Reopt a conditionally useful strategy rather than a universal best practice.
AI.motivation: 动机：CPU 导向的手工优化在迁移到 GPU 时可能不再合适，甚至会阻碍 LLM 生成高质量 CUDA 代码。因此作者希望验证，先移除这些 CPU 特定优化、再针对 GPU 重新表达和优化，是否能提高 CUDA 迁移的性能与可行性。 / Motivation: CPU-oriented hand optimizations may become mismatched on GPUs and can obstruct LLM-based CUDA generation. The authors therefore investigate whether removing CPU-specific optimizations first and then re-expressing/reoptimizing for GPUs can improve translation quality, performance, and feasibility.
AI.method: 方法：论文提出 Deopt-Reopt 工作流，先对面向 CPU 优化的 C++ HPC 代码做简化/去优化，再让 LLM 重新翻译并针对 CUDA 进行重优化；并与直接翻译（Direct）对比。在 12 个 HPC kernels、两种 LLM（O120 与 Q235）上，分别评估 Single-shot 和 Iterative 两种设置，并加入 Direct-3 作为控制以平衡 LLM 调用次数。 / Method: The paper proposes a Deopt-Reopt workflow that first simplifies/de-optimizes CPU-oriented C++ HPC code, then asks an LLM to retranslate and reoptimize it for CUDA. It compares this workflow with direct translation (Direct) across 12 HPC kernels and two LLMs (O120 and Q235) under Single-shot and Iterative settings, with an exploratory Direct-3 control to equalize LLM-call count.
AI.result: 结果：Single-shot 下，在 18 个可测试案例中，Deopt-Reopt 在 5 个成功案例中显著更快，尤其是 conv2d；但 Direct 在 3 个案例中更快，说明收益并不普遍。加入平衡调用次数的 Direct-3 后，Deopt-Reopt 仅在 19 个可测试案例中的 4 个领先，而 Direct-3 也在 4 个领先。Iterative 下，多轮生成与修复缩小了两种方法的差距，O120 上尤为明显；但 Q235 在 conv2d、ddgemm 和 bgemm 上仍显示出显著的 Deopt-Reopt 优势。对编译/可行性的影响同样是混合的：某些 kernel 明显提升，另一些反而下降。 / Results: In Single-shot, among 18 testable cases, Deopt-Reopt was significantly faster in 5 successful cases, especially conv2d, while Direct was faster in 3, showing that the benefit is not universal. With Direct-3 controlling for LLM-call count, Deopt-Reopt led in only 4 of 19 testable cases, while Direct-3 also led in 4. In Iterative mode, repeated generation and repair reduced the gap substantially, especially for O120; however, Q235 still showed large Deopt-Reopt advantages on conv2d, ddgemm, and bgemm. Effects on feasibility/compilability were also mixed, improving some kernels but hurting others.
AI.conclusion: 结论：Deopt-Reopt 是一种对基于 LLM 的 GPU 迁移有效但并非普适的方法；其收益取决于具体 kernel、所用模型、搜索预算以及成功率，因此它带来的性能提升是有条件的，而不是稳定的端到端优势。 / Conclusion: Deopt-Reopt is effective but not universal for LLM-based GPU porting; its benefits depend on the kernel, model, search budget, and success rate, so the performance gains are conditional rather than guaranteed end-to-end improvements.

title: Do Models Share Safety Representations? Cross-Model Steering for Safe Visual Generation
summary: Recent progress in generative modeling has made safety control a central challenge, yet existing approaches remain largely model-specific, requiring retraining or tailored interventions for each new architecture. In this work, we ask whether safety can be represented as a portable latent direction, learned once and reused across heterogeneous generators. We introduce the first framework for cross-model safety steering, in which a safety direction is estimated in a source LLM from paired safe-unsafe prompts, transported to a target generator through a lightweight alignment fitted on benign data alone, and applied at inference time. Crucially, our pipeline never accesses unsafe data on the target side, isolating whether safety can be transferred through shared representation geometry. Beyond a single global direction, we also identify a multi-vector extension that captures category-specific safety behaviors, enabling more selective control. We evaluate our approach in text-to-image and text-to-video generation across diverse source-target model pairs. Across models, transferred safety directions achieve ASR reduction and CLIP-Score/FID trade-offs comparable to directions learned natively on the target model using unsafe data, while requiring no target-side unsafe data. This indicates that safety improvements do not come at the expense of generation quality. Our results point to a modular view of safety: safety-relevant behavior is not purely model-local, but can be controlled through latent directions that persist across models. This suggests a new path toward lightweight, reusable safety mechanisms that do not require target-side unsafe data.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes cross-model safety steering: learn a safety direction once in a source model, map it into another generator using only benign alignment data, and use it to improve safety at inference time. It works across modalities and performs close to native target-side safety training without requiring unsafe target data.
AI.motivation: Existing safety-control methods are usually model-specific and require retraining or architecture-tailored interventions. The paper is motivated by the need for a portable, reusable safety mechanism that can generalize across different generators while avoiding unsafe data on the target model.
AI.method: The paper learns a safety direction in a source LLM from paired safe/unsafe prompts, aligns source and target latent spaces using a lightweight mapping trained only on benign data, and applies the transferred direction at inference time. It also extends the approach from a single global direction to multiple category-specific vectors for finer control.
AI.result: On text-to-image and text-to-video tasks across diverse source-target model pairs, transferred safety directions reduce attack success rate and achieve CLIP-Score/FID trade-offs comparable to safety directions learned directly on the target model with unsafe data. This shows effective safety transfer with preserved generation quality.
AI.conclusion: Safety can be transferred across heterogeneous generative models as reusable latent directions, including both global and category-specific directions, without using unsafe target-side data and without materially harming generation quality.

title: Generic Triple-Latent Compression with Gated Associative Retrieval
summary: We study generic triple-latent sequence models that maintain a running token state and compressed pair-memory pathway to capture higher-order token interactions without benchmark-specific parsing. The triple-latent family improves a small Transformer baseline on byte-level WikiText-2 and on a tokenizer-based MiniMind language-model benchmark, while a recall-focused gated key-value retrieval extension improves associative recall but remains seed-sensitive and much slower in the current reference implementation.

AI.tldr: A generic triple-latent model beats a small Transformer on two language-model benchmarks; adding gated KV retrieval boosts recall but is slow and seed-sensitive.
AI.motivation: Standard small sequence models may miss higher-order token interactions or require benchmark-specific parsing. The work aims to build a more generic architecture that captures richer token dependencies and improves recall ability in a unified way.
AI.method: The paper studies a generic triple-latent architecture with three interacting latent pathways: a running token state, a compressed pair-memory pathway for higher-order token interactions, and an optional gated key-value retrieval extension focused on recall.
AI.result: Compared with a small Transformer baseline, the triple-latent family improves performance on byte-level WikiText-2 and a tokenizer-based MiniMind language-model benchmark. The recall-oriented retrieval extension further improves associative recall, but is much slower in the current implementation and unstable across seeds.
AI.conclusion: Triple-latent sequence models can improve language modeling over a small Transformer baseline without task-specific parsing, while the retrieval-augmented variant helps associative recall but currently suffers from high runtime cost and sensitivity to random seeds.

title: Function2Scene: 3D Indoor Scene Layout from Functional Specifications
summary: Most text-driven 3D indoor scene synthesis methods generate rooms from object-centric prompts, asking what furniture should be placed rather than how the space is used. Yet in real interior design, a layout is judged by how well it supports its occupants, e.g., their activities and physical needs. We introduce Function2Scene, a framework for generating 3D indoor layouts from functional specifications, i.e., natural-language design briefs describing who will use a room and what they need to do there. Given such a specification, our system parses occupant personas and activities, derives a customized set of functional design constraints from a taxonomy of 17 criteria spanning spatial, ergonomic, activity, and environmental considerations, and uses these constraints to guide layout generation. Rather than relying on an LLM to directly produce a final scene, Function2Scene performs iterative evaluation and refinement through a tool-augmented check-and-repair loop, combining geometric measurements, LLM-based contextual reasoning, and VLM-based visual assessment. Experiments on 30 professionally written interior-design cases show that Function2Scene produces layouts that better satisfy functional requirements than recent LLM-based scene synthesis baselines, with our results preferred in 94.3% of pairwise comparisons. Our work reframes text-driven indoor scene synthesis from placing plausible objects to designing spaces that support human use.

AI.tldr: Function2Scene generates 3D indoor layouts from user-function-oriented design briefs, using explicit functional constraints and iterative multimodal evaluation to produce more usable rooms than object-centric baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing text-driven 3D indoor scene synthesis methods are largely object-centric and focus on what furniture to place, but real interior design should prioritize how well a space supports occupants’ activities, ergonomics, and physical needs.
AI.method: The method takes natural-language functional design briefs, parses occupant personas and activities, maps them to a taxonomy of 17 functional design criteria, and generates layouts through an iterative check-and-repair loop using geometric analysis, LLM-based reasoning, and VLM-based visual assessment.
AI.result: On 30 professionally written interior-design cases, Function2Scene outperformed recent LLM-based scene synthesis baselines in satisfying functional requirements, and its outputs were preferred in 94.3% of pairwise comparisons.
AI.conclusion: Function2Scene reframes text-driven 3D indoor scene synthesis around human function rather than object placement, and it produces layouts that better satisfy user needs than prior LLM-based baselines.

title: PyCC.id: A package for hypothesis-driven equation discovery with structural identifiability
comment: The software package is available at: https://github.com/FedejGon/pyCC.id
summary: Data-driven equation discovery is fundamentally an inverse problem that seeks to infer the governing differential equations of a system directly from time-series measurements. A known issue is the ill-conditioned nature of the inverse problem, which frequently produces multiple mathematical models that fit the data similarly well. One path to address this issue is by incorporating known hypotheses and constraints into the training phase beforehand. While this approach effectively reduces the search space, it still results in multiple candidate models, forcing practitioners to rely on post-hoc manual filtering based on their own domain expertise. A recent approach incorporates structural `skeletons' inspired by characteristic curves (CCs), defining a hypothesis-driven methodology. In this methodology, practitioners define a skeleton, which is associated with a family of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and then add their hypotheses and priors based on their domain knowledge to refine the obtained model iteratively. An important advantage of this approach is that some skeletons have demonstrable structural identifiability properties, which are useful for checking whether the skeleton is correct or should be discarded. Furthermore, this formalism enables the use of multiple equation discovery paradigms due to its modularity (such as neural networks, symbolic regression, and sparse regression). In this work, we present the Python library PyCC, which condenses these efforts into a flexible tool that allows researchers and engineers to seamlessly define their skeletons and hypotheses to discover ODEs from time-dependent data.

AI.tldr: PyCC是一个把“结构骨架+领域先验+可辨识性检验”整合到数据驱动ODE发现中的Python库，目标是减少病态逆问题带来的多解性并降低人工筛选负担。 / PyCC is a Python library that integrates structural skeletons, domain priors, and identifiability checks into data-driven ODE discovery to reduce ambiguity from ill-conditioned inverse problems and lessen manual post-hoc filtering.
AI.motivation: 数据驱动方程发现本质上是病态的逆问题，常会产生多个对数据拟合同样良好的候选方程。仅靠预先加入约束虽能减少搜索空间，但仍需事后依赖专家手工筛选，因此需要一种更系统、可验证、可模块化地融入领域知识的方法。 / Data-driven equation discovery is an ill-conditioned inverse problem that often yields multiple equations fitting the data equally well. Although adding constraints beforehand reduces the search space, it still leaves practitioners with post-hoc expert filtering, motivating a more systematic, verifiable, and modular way to incorporate domain knowledge.
AI.method: 论文的方法是提出并实现PyCC库：用户先定义与一族常微分方程对应的结构骨架，再逐步加入领域假设与先验约束，以迭代方式缩小搜索空间并进行方程发现；该框架是模块化的，可对接神经网络、符号回归和稀疏回归等不同发现范式。 / The paper’s method is to introduce and implement the PyCC library: users define a structural skeleton associated with a family of ODEs, then iteratively add domain hypotheses and priors to narrow the search space for equation discovery; the framework is modular and can interface with neural networks, symbolic regression, and sparse regression.
AI.result: 结果上，作者给出了一个统一的软件工具PyCC，用于从时间序列数据中发现ODE；其主要价值在于支持骨架与假设的无缝定义、迭代建模，以及利用结构可辨识性判断某些骨架是否应被保留或丢弃，同时兼容多种方程发现技术路线。 / As a result, the authors provide a unified software tool, PyCC, for discovering ODEs from time-series data; its main value is seamless specification of skeletons and hypotheses, iterative model refinement, and the ability to use structural identifiability to retain or discard some skeletons, while remaining compatible with multiple equation-discovery paradigms.
AI.conclusion: PyCC将基于特征曲线(characteristic curves, CCs)的结构骨架(skeleton)方法封装为一个灵活的Python库，使研究者能够把先验假设与约束系统化地纳入ODE发现流程，并借助部分骨架可证明的结构可辨识性来更可靠地筛选候选模型。 / PyCC packages the characteristic-curve-inspired skeleton methodology into a flexible Python library, enabling researchers to systematically inject prior hypotheses and constraints into ODE discovery and to use structural identifiability of some skeletons to more reliably reject incorrect candidate models.

title: GITCO: Gated Inference-Time Context Optimization in TSFMs
comment: ICML 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Structured Data
summary: Patch-based Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) suffer from context poisoning: structurally anomalous patches capture disproportionate attention and silently degrade zero-shot forecast quality. We propose improving TSFM accuracy at inference time by optimizing the input context rather than modifying model weights. We present GITCO (Gated Inference-Time Context Optimization), a lightweight three-component framework: Gate, Router, and Critic that selectively identifies and suppresses harmful patches without any parameter updates. Evaluated on TimesFM 2.5 across 53 GIFT-Eval datasets under K-fold cross-validation, GITCO achieves an average +1.95% MASE reduction on TimesFM 2.5 while capturing 89.9% of the improvement upper bound. We introduce context sensitivity profiles as a new characterizable property of TSFMs: the mapping from time series meta-features to expected accuracy improvement under inference-time context intervention, shaped jointly by model architecture and the statistical structure of the data.

AI.tldr: GITCO improves TSFM zero-shot forecasts by filtering harmful input patches at inference time, yielding measurable gains without any weight updates and introducing context sensitivity profiles to predict when this helps.
AI.motivation: Patch-based TSFMs suffer from context poisoning, where structurally anomalous patches attract excessive attention and silently reduce forecast quality. The work is motivated by the need to fix this failure mode without retraining or fine-tuning the foundation model.
AI.method: The paper proposes GITCO, a lightweight inference-time framework with three components: Gate, Router, and Critic. It optimizes the input context by identifying and suppressing harmful anomalous patches instead of modifying model parameters.
AI.result: On TimesFM 2.5 evaluated over 53 GIFT-Eval datasets with K-fold cross-validation, GITCO achieves an average 1.95% reduction in MASE and captures 89.9% of the achievable improvement upper bound.
AI.conclusion: GITCO can improve zero-shot forecasting accuracy of patch-based TSFMs at inference time without updating model weights, and context sensitivity profiles reveal when such intervention is likely to help.

title: Discrete Incremental Voting: New Bounds for General Graphs and Expanders
summary:
We analyze the discrete incremental voting process (DIV) introduced by Cooper, Radzik, and Shiraga [OPODIS '23]. In this process, we consider a set $V$ of $n$ nodes connected in an undirected graph $G = (V, E)$ where each node has an integer opinion. In one step a randomly selected node interacts with its randomly selected neighbor and changes its opinion by $1$ in the direction of the neighbour's opinion. The process converges to a unique opinion that, in expectation, is the degree-weighted average of the initial opinions.
  We show that if the graph has conductance $Φ(G)$, the ratio of the average to smallest degree is $γ(G)$, and the maximal difference between initial opinions is $K$, then the expected convergence time is ${O}\left({n\left(K\log (Kn)+γ(G) n \right)}/{Φ(G)^2}\right)$. This bound is essentially optimal for a large class of graphs of bounded expansion. We also show that for regular graphs, if the second largest eigenvalue is $o(1/\log^2 n)$ and $K$ is $o\left({n}/{\log^2 n}\right)$, then w.h.p.\ DIV converges to the initial average opinion (rounded up or down).

AI.tldr: DIV reaches consensus in time controlled mainly by conductance, degree imbalance, and initial opinion range; on sufficiently well-mixing regular graphs, the consensus is almost surely the rounded initial average.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to understand how quickly and to what value the discrete incremental voting process converges on general graphs, extending prior work by relating convergence behavior to interpretable graph-mixing quantities and the spread of initial opinions.
AI.method: The analysis studies the stochastic opinion-update dynamics on graphs using structural graph parameters such as conductance, degree ratios, and spectral properties. It derives expected convergence-time bounds and then specializes the argument to regular graphs with small second eigenvalue to characterize the limiting consensus value with high probability.
AI.result: The main result is an expected convergence-time bound of O(n(K log(Kn) + gamma(G) n) / Phi(G)^2). This is essentially tight for a broad class of bounded-expansion graphs. In addition, for regular graphs with second largest eigenvalue o(1/log^2 n) and opinion range K = o(n/log^2 n), the process converges with high probability to either the floor or ceiling of the initial average opinion.
AI.conclusion: The paper proves near-optimal upper bounds on the convergence time of the discrete incremental voting process in terms of graph conductance, degree imbalance, and initial opinion spread, and shows that on sufficiently well-mixing regular graphs the final consensus is with high probability the rounded initial average opinion.

title: TopoPult-SSL: Gland-Mask-Free Cross-Device Meibomian Gland Segmentation via Self-Distilled Weak Clinical Priors
summary: Every new clinical imaging device creates a domain shift where dense gland masks are expensive yet cheap clinical signals -- eyelid outlines, Pult grades, morphometric ratios -- are routinely recorded. We present TopoPult-SSL, a two-stage framework for cross-device meibomian gland segmentation. Stage 1 adapts a source-trained model without target gland masks in the training loss, using four weak-prior anchors driven by target eyelid masks and clinical metadata only. Stage 2, when target gland masks are available, distils complementary Stage-1 teachers into a single compact student via supervised self-distillation. We develop and validate the technique on the public MGD-1k to CAMG research benchmark (1,000 to 100 images, different device), where the distilled model achieves Dice 0.716+/-0.006 (best 0.726), surpassing UA-MT (0.710) and the ensemble teacher (0.720) -- with a single pass. The gland-mask-free Stage-1 variant reaches Precision 0.694 vs. 0.30-0.34 for SAM/MedSAM (p<0.001), enabling deployment without dense gland contouring. Code and reproducibility scripts are released.

AI.tldr: TopoPult-SSL is a two-stage cross-device meibomian gland segmentation method that first adapts using only weak target priors like eyelid masks and clinical metadata, then distills the adapted teachers into one compact model when target masks are available. It beats prior baselines and remains useful even when no target gland masks are provided.
AI.motivation: Clinical imaging devices introduce domain shift, making source-trained segmentation models degrade on new devices. Dense meibomian gland annotations are expensive to obtain, while weak clinical signals like eyelid outlines, Pult grades, and morphometric ratios are cheap and routinely available. The work is motivated by the need to exploit these weak signals for practical cross-device adaptation.
AI.method: The paper proposes a two-stage framework called TopoPult-SSL. Stage 1 performs source-to-target adaptation without using target gland masks in the training loss, relying instead on four weak-prior anchors derived from target eyelid masks and clinical metadata such as Pult grades and morphometric ratios. Stage 2 uses available target gland masks to distill multiple complementary Stage-1 teacher models into one compact student through supervised self-distillation.
AI.result: On the MGD-1k to CAMG benchmark, the distilled model achieves Dice 0.716 ± 0.006 with best 0.726, outperforming UA-MT at 0.710 and even the ensemble teacher at 0.720 while requiring only a single inference pass. The gland-mask-free Stage-1 variant achieves Precision 0.694, far above SAM/MedSAM at 0.30–0.34 with p<0.001. Code and reproducibility scripts are released.
AI.conclusion: TopoPult-SSL can effectively handle cross-device meibomian gland segmentation. It works even without target-domain gland masks in Stage 1 and, when masks are later available, supervised self-distillation further improves performance into a compact single-pass model that outperforms strong baselines.

title: PEFT of SLM for Telecommunications Customer Support: A Comparative Study of LoRA Configurations with Energy Consumption Analysis
summary:
While large language models (LLMs) show strong performance in natural language understanding and generation, their evaluation and adaptation to domain-specific constraints in telecommunications customer support remain limited. In addition, data sovereignty, regulatory constraints, and the handling of sensitive customer and network information complicate the use of externally hosted foundation models in this domain.
  We present a systematic study of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) applied to Qwen2.5-3B to build a domain-specific conversational assistant. We introduce a combinatorial synthetic data generation approach based on a glossary of 52 industry-specific terms, producing approximately 30,000 training examples across 1,560 distinct problem scenarios via a generative pipeline powered by Gemini 2.0 Flash.
  We evaluate 16 LoRA configurations by varying hyperparameters and target modules. Our evaluation extends beyond standard metrics by incorporating energy consumption analysis and qualitative assessment using an LLM-as-a-judge framework with GPT-5.2 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet.
  Results show a clear divergence between quantitative and qualitative performance: models achieving the lowest validation loss do not necessarily obtain the best human-aligned rankings. The best validation loss (0.5024) ranks only 6th-7th in qualitative evaluation, while the worst loss (0.6807) ranks first according to both judges.
  This work contributes (1) a combinatorial method for synthetic dataset construction, (2) insights into the impact of target module selection for LoRA injection, (3) evidence that validation loss alone is insufficient for selecting fine-tuning configurations in conversational AI, and (4) an energy-performance trade-off analysis for sustainable LLM deployment.

AI.tldr: The paper builds a telecom-specific assistant by LoRA-tuning Qwen2.5-3B on a large synthetic dataset and shows that the lowest validation loss does not correspond to the best judged conversational quality, so deployment decisions should combine qualitative and energy-aware evaluation.
AI.motivation: Telecommunications customer support requires domain-specific adaptation of LLMs, but externally hosted foundation models are constrained by data sovereignty, regulation, and sensitive customer/network information. The study is motivated by the need for an efficient, deployable, domain-adapted assistant and more realistic evaluation criteria than standard loss metrics alone.
AI.method: The paper fine-tunes Qwen2.5-3B with parameter-efficient fine-tuning using LoRA, builds a synthetic telecom-support dataset via a combinatorial glossary-based generation pipeline using 52 industry terms and Gemini 2.0 Flash, and evaluates 16 LoRA configurations across different hyperparameters and target modules using validation loss, energy consumption, and LLM-as-a-judge qualitative assessment with GPT-5.2 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet.
AI.result: The authors generate about 30,000 training examples covering 1,560 problem scenarios and find a strong mismatch between quantitative and qualitative results: the model with the best validation loss of 0.5024 ranks only 6th-7th qualitatively, while the model with the worst loss of 0.6807 ranks first in both judge evaluations. They also provide findings on LoRA target-module choice and energy-performance trade-offs.
AI.conclusion: Validation loss alone is not a reliable criterion for selecting LoRA fine-tuning configurations for telecom customer-support conversational assistants; qualitative, human-aligned evaluation and energy-performance trade-offs are necessary for practical model selection.

title: Temporal Preference Concepts and their Functions in a Large Language Model
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed to make decisions that require trading off near-term gains against long-term consequences, yet little is known about how they internally represent or resolve these tradeoffs. In this work, we causally localize an underlying subgraph for temporal preference in a distilled LLM (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507), identifying mid-to-upper-layer nodes through converging evidence from gradient-based attribution and activation patching. We find that the geometry of time horizon is encoded in the residual stream at the expected localized layers. A behavioral analysis reveals that unintervened LLMs discount the future several times less steeply than humans, yet this preference is unstable across contexts, motivating explicit control rather than implicit reliance on training. Finally, we find suggestive evidence that steering vectors can shift temporal preference. Our work demonstrates how mechanistic interpretability can bring us closer to reliable control over how LLMs plan and reason

AI.tldr: 论文用机制可解释性方法在Qwen3-4B中定位了“时间偏好”电路，发现模型对未来的折扣比人类弱但不稳定，并初步证明可用steering vectors进行调控。 / The paper localizes a temporal-preference circuit in Qwen3-4B, shows the model discounts the future less than humans but inconsistently across contexts, and gives preliminary evidence that steering vectors can control this preference.
AI.motivation: LLM越来越多地被用于需要权衡短期收益与长期后果的决策任务，但我们仍不清楚它们内部如何表征和解决这种跨期权衡；同时，若模型的时间偏好不稳定，就需要显式控制而非依赖训练中隐含形成的偏好。 / LLMs are increasingly used for decisions that trade off short-term gains against long-term consequences, yet their internal representation and resolution of such tradeoffs are poorly understood; if temporal preferences are unstable, explicit control is needed rather than relying on implicit training effects.
AI.method: 作者在Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507上结合基于梯度的归因和activation patching，对时间偏好的内部子图进行因果定位；随后分析局部层残差流中的时间跨度几何表征，并通过行为实验评估模型的跨情境时间折扣特性，最后测试steering vectors的干预效果。 / The authors use gradient-based attribution and activation patching on Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 to causally localize a subgraph for temporal preference, analyze time-horizon geometry in the residual stream at localized layers, run behavioral analyses of intertemporal discounting across contexts, and test steering-vector interventions.
AI.result: 论文发现：时间偏好的相关节点主要位于模型中高层；时间跨度的几何信息确实编码在这些局部层的残差流中；未干预LLM对未来的折扣明显比人类更平缓，但这一偏好在不同语境下不稳定；此外，steering vectors显示出能够改变时间偏好的初步证据。 / The paper finds that temporal-preference-related nodes are mainly in mid-to-upper layers; time-horizon geometry is encoded in the residual stream at those layers; unintervened LLMs discount the future much less steeply than humans, but this preference is unstable across contexts; and steering vectors provide suggestive evidence of shifting temporal preference.
AI.conclusion: 该论文表明，可以用机制可解释性方法在蒸馏LLM中因果定位与时间偏好相关的内部子图，并初步展示通过steering vectors对模型时间偏好进行可控干预的可能性，从而为更可靠地控制LLM的规划与推理提供基础。 / The paper concludes that mechanistic interpretability can causally localize an internal subgraph related to temporal preference in a distilled LLM, and provides preliminary evidence that steering vectors may controllably shift that preference, moving toward more reliable control of LLM planning and reasoning.

title: Uncertainty Aware Functional Behavior Prediction and Material Fatigue Assessment for Circular Factory
comment: 27 pages, submitted to the Journal of Manufacturing Systems' special issue about circular factories, the manuscript is under review
summary: Returned products in circular factories re-enter production with heterogeneous degradation states, usage histories, and remaining capability. Reuse cannot be decided from the current inspection alone, because future function fulfillment and component integrity may evolve differently under the next service scenario. Existing PHM approaches support degradation prediction, but often target fixed operating conditions or isolated component benchmarks, while material-fatigue assessment is rarely linked to system-level functional prognosis. This paper addresses this gap for an angle grinder by combining uncertainty-aware functional prediction with component-level fatigue assessment in an instance-specific reliability workflow. The proposed framework combines the current tool state with recent force--torque usage windows. A convolutional encoder extracts loading patterns from spindle forces and shaft torque, and an LSTM backbone predicts nine functional variables as Gaussian mean and variance estimates. In parallel, the same loading history is translated into output-shaft fatigue information through finite-element-supported stress reconstruction, S--N/Miner damage evaluation with Haibach extension, and Paris-law crack-growth analysis. A streaming replay algorithm consolidates both branches into functional, material, and system reliability trajectories. Held-out tests show mean \(2\%\)-tolerance accuracy of 0.9652 across nine outputs. Thermal variables are predicted near-perfectly, while drive motor current and load speed remain the most demanding dynamic outputs, with \(R^2\) values of 0.9750 and 0.9924. Torque history is especially important for these variables, and the conventional LSTM outperforms GRU and xLSTM in the short-history setting. Reliability calibration is most informative for drive motor current, where predicted and observed exceedance probabilities ...

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid prognostics framework for reused angle grinders that jointly predicts future functional performance and component fatigue under uncertainty. By combining CNN-LSTM functional prediction with fatigue/crack-growth physics and fusing them into reliability trajectories, it supports more reliable reuse decisions and achieves strong predictive performance on held-out data.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that returned products in circular factories have heterogeneous degradation, usage histories, and remaining capability, so reuse decisions cannot rely only on current inspection. Existing PHM methods usually assume fixed operating conditions or isolated components, and they rarely connect material-fatigue assessment with system-level functional prognosis. The paper addresses this gap by creating an instance-specific reliability framework for reuse decisions.
AI.method: The method builds a dual-branch reliability workflow for an angle grinder. One branch uses the current tool state and recent force-torque history, with a convolutional encoder plus LSTM to predict nine functional variables as Gaussian mean/variance estimates. The other branch converts the same loading history into fatigue information using finite-element-supported stress reconstruction, S-N/Miner damage with Haibach extension, and Paris-law crack-growth analysis. A streaming replay algorithm then fuses functional, material, and system-level reliability trajectories.
AI.result: On held-out tests, the framework achieves a mean 2%-tolerance accuracy of 0.9652 across nine outputs. Thermal variables are predicted almost perfectly, while drive motor current and load speed are the hardest dynamic outputs, with R^2 values of 0.9750 and 0.9924. Torque history is especially influential for these variables, and the standard LSTM outperforms GRU and xLSTM in the short-history setting. Reliability calibration is particularly informative for drive motor current.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that integrating uncertainty-aware functional prognosis with component-level fatigue and crack-growth assessment enables instance-specific reliability evaluation for reused products in circular manufacturing. For the angle grinder case, the framework delivers high predictive accuracy, identifies torque history as a key driver for difficult dynamic variables, and shows that a conventional LSTM is better suited than GRU and xLSTM for short loading histories.

title: On GPU Implementation for Multi-Precision Integer Division
summary: This paper presents the issues arising in implementing a fast integer division algorithm on general purpose GPUs. The algorithm uses a Newton iteration based on the shifted inverse operation, keeping all arithmetic in the integer domain and relying on data-parallel operators. The principal contribution is an efficient GPU/CUDA implementation for integer precisions from $2^{15}$ to $2^{18}$ -- sizes not supported by \cgbn{} division. We propose algorithmic refinements, define a cost model in terms of multiplications, build on prefix sums and previous work on multi-precision multiplication, and present an evaluation showing near-optimal performance relative to the model for the target precision.

AI.tldr:
中文：这篇论文针对GPU上大整数除法难题，提出了一个基于shifted inverse和Newton迭代的纯整数并行实现，并在2^15到2^18位精度上做到了接近成本模型最优的性能，补足了现有库的能力缺口。
English: This paper tackles large-integer division on GPUs with a pure-integer, data-parallel method based on shifted inverse Newton iteration, and achieves near cost-model-optimal performance for 2^15 to 2^18-bit precisions, covering a gap in existing libraries.
AI.motivation:
中文：动机在于，多精度整数除法在GPU上实现困难，而现有方案尤其是\cgbn{}在2^15到2^18位精度范围内缺乏支持。作者希望设计一种适用于通用GPU、可并行、且在目标精度区间内高效的整数除法实现。
English: The motivation is that multi-precision integer division is difficult to implement efficiently on GPUs, and existing solutions, especially \cgbn{}, do not support the 2^15 to 2^18-bit range. The authors aim to design a GPU-friendly, parallel, and efficient division implementation for this target precision interval.
AI.method:
中文：方法上，作者采用基于shifted inverse operation的Newton迭代来实现整数除法，整个过程保持在整数域内，并依赖数据并行算子。实现层面结合GPU/CUDA、多精度乘法的既有工作、prefix sums，以及以乘法次数为核心的成本模型，并加入若干算法级改进。
English: Methodologically, the authors implement integer division via Newton iteration on a shifted inverse, keeping all arithmetic in the integer domain and using data-parallel operators. The GPU/CUDA design builds on prior multi-precision multiplication work, prefix sums, and a cost model centered on multiplication counts, with additional algorithmic refinements.
AI.result:
中文：结果显示，作者给出了一个面向2^15至2^18位整数精度的高效GPU/CUDA实现；通过成本模型与实验评估，性能在目标精度范围内接近理论最优，并证明所提算法改进是有效的。
English: The results show an efficient GPU/CUDA implementation for integer precisions from 2^15 to 2^18 bits. Experimental evaluation against the cost model indicates performance is near-optimal in the target range, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed refinements.
AI.conclusion:
中文：论文认为，基于移位逆元与Newton迭代的纯整数除法算法可以在通用GPU上高效实现，并在2^15到2^18位精度范围内达到接近成本模型上界的性能，填补了现有库在该区间的支持空白。
English: The paper concludes that a pure-integer division algorithm based on shifted inverse Newton iteration can be implemented efficiently on general-purpose GPUs, achieving near cost-model-optimal performance for 2^15 to 2^18-bit precisions and filling a gap left by existing libraries.

title: Data valuation model for non-monetary exchanges
summary: In the evolving landscape of data product exchange platforms, traditional economic valuation models fall short due to the non-rival nature of data and the prevalence of non-monetary data product exchanges. This paper introduces a normative, choice-based metric for valuing data products within intracompany exchanges, where conventional pricing mechanisms are absent. By modeling consumer attention and preferences, the proposed metric quantifies the value of data offerings based solely on user selection behavior, without relying on cost, demand, or competitive pricing data. We show that this metric can be formally cast as a cooperative game with a closed-form Shapley value, providing a principled and fairness-based allocation of value across offerings. The model rewards uniqueness and discriminative consumption, effectively addressing the limitations of popularity-based metrics and incentivizing the creation of high-value, long-tail data products. Through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, the metric is shown to align with economic principles, support equitable valuation, and contribute to a robust framework for measuring gross data product value. Future research directions include exploring bundling strategies and quantifying product complementarity.

title: LightVesselNet: An Ultra-Lightweight Sub-100K Parameter Network for Retinal Blood Vessel Segmentation
summary: Retinal blood vessel segmentation plays a vital role in the early detection of diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma. While recent deep learning models have achieved great segmentation accuracy, they typically require heavy computational resources, making real-world deployment on edge devices difficult. In this paper, we propose LightVesselNet, an efficient neural network designed for retinal vessel segmentation in a resource-constrained environment. Despite containing only 75K parameters, LightVesselNet performs competitively with much larger models. The network employs a compact encoder decoder architecture enhanced with channel and spatial attention mechanisms, a multi-scale feature aggregation module at the bottleneck, and a subpixel upsampling strategy in the decoder. A dedicated edge residual connection preserves fine vessel detail throughout decoding. Extensive experiments on five publicly available datasets: DRIVE, STARE, CHASEDB1, FIVES, and HRF, yield sensitivity scores of 0.8189, 0.8499, 0.8640, 0.8634, 0.8096, and Dice coefficients of 0.8070, 0.8072, 0.8181, 0.8649, and 0.7686, respectively. LightVesselNet shows improved efficiency (Performance vs Parameter or GFlops) compared to State-of-the-Art models. Cross-dataset evaluation confirms the model's generalisation capability. Overall, LightVesselNet is a strong candidate for deployment in low-resource clinical settings and mobile screening tools.
