title: MCBench: A Multicontext Safety Assessment Benchmark for Omni Large Language Models
summary: Existing multimodal safety benchmarks focus solely on visual inputs and cannot assess Omni Large Language Models (LLMs) that process vision, audio, and text. We introduce MCBench, a benchmark with 1196 scenarios spanning four safety categories that require integrating multiple modalities for accurate safety assessment. Each unsafe scenario is paired with a minimally different safe counterpart to assess model sensitivity. Our evaluations of state-of-the-art models reveal significant challenges. Omni LLMs struggle with subtle or non-physical risks but perform better when salient visual or acoustic cues are present. Analysis of reasoning traces shows that, although models can extract modality-specific information, they often fail to integrate these cues effectively for safety judgments. Our findings reveal that current Omni LLMs lack robust cross-modal reasoning in safety-critical settings, underscoring the need for improved architectures and training strategies for multimodal safety.

AI.tldr: MCBench is a new benchmark for testing multimodal safety reasoning in Omni LLMs. Results show current models can detect cues from individual modalities but still struggle to combine them reliably for safety-critical decisions.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal safety benchmarks focus only on visual inputs and therefore cannot properly evaluate Omni LLMs that jointly process vision, audio, and text. A benchmark requiring cross-modal integration is needed.
AI.method: The paper introduces MCBench, a multimodal safety benchmark with 1,196 scenarios across four safety categories. Each unsafe scenario is paired with a minimally different safe counterpart to test model sensitivity, and state-of-the-art Omni LLMs are evaluated on these scenarios with analysis of their reasoning traces.
AI.result: Evaluations show that Omni LLMs face substantial difficulty on multimodal safety assessment, especially for subtle or non-physical risks. They perform better when strong visual or acoustic cues are present, but reasoning-trace analysis shows they often fail to integrate modality-specific cues into correct safety judgments.
AI.conclusion: Current Omni LLMs lack robust cross-modal reasoning for safety-critical multimodal assessment, indicating the need for better architectures and training strategies.

title: KV-Control: Parameter-Efficient K/V Injection for Trajectory-Controlled Text-to-Motion
summary: Text-conditioned 3D human motion models now synthesize plausible motions from prompts, but practical animation and embodied-agent workflows rarely stop at text: a character may need to follow a sketched root path, hit an end-effector target, or satisfy a multi-joint trajectory while still preserving the gait, style, and intent described by language. This exposes a control trade-off. A trajectory controller should be precise without overwriting the pretrained text-conditioned motion prior, yet existing solutions either duplicate large portions of the generator to regain per-layer control access or move much of the cost to test-time optimization. We introduce KV-Control, a compact attention-side control interface for frozen masked text-to-motion transformers. The key idea is to make geometric constraints available as memory inside self-attention rather than injecting them through a global pose token or enforcing them only at the output side. To support this interface, we co-design a part-tokenized motion substrate and controller: \textbf{PartVQ} learns anatomy-aligned part codebooks, T-Concat exposes each frame--part token as an attention-addressable site, and KV-Control injects control-conditioned key/value memories at every self-attention layer while preserving the pretrained query stream, text cross-attention, FFN, and all backbone weights. The resulting adapter adds only trainable injection parameters atop a shared trajectory encoder, yet tracks root and multi-joint constraints with sub-centimeter accuracy under the inherited refinement protocol while retaining text-conditioned motion quality. KV-Control reframes trajectory conditioning as lightweight memory retrieval, providing a small, precise, and transparent control interface for text-to-motion generation.

AI.tldr: A small adapter called KV-Control turns trajectory constraints into attention memory for frozen text-to-motion transformers, giving highly accurate root/multi-joint control without retraining the full model or sacrificing language-driven motion quality.
AI.motivation: Existing controllable text-to-motion methods face a trade-off between precise trajectory control and preservation of the pretrained text-conditioned motion prior; they often either duplicate large parts of the generator for layerwise access or rely heavily on expensive test-time optimization.
AI.method: The paper co-designs three components: PartVQ for anatomy-aligned part codebooks, T-Concat for exposing frame-part tokens as attention-addressable units, and KV-Control for injecting control-conditioned key/value memories into every self-attention layer while keeping the query stream, text cross-attention, FFN, and backbone weights frozen.
AI.result: The proposed adapter adds only small trainable injection parameters plus a shared trajectory encoder, yet achieves sub-centimeter tracking accuracy for root and multi-joint constraints while maintaining text-conditioned motion quality under the inherited refinement protocol.
AI.conclusion: KV-Control provides a lightweight and precise control interface for frozen text-to-motion transformers by treating trajectory constraints as attention memory, enabling accurate controllable motion generation without disturbing the pretrained motion prior.

title: State commitment learning: training language models to distinguish computation from memory
summary: Reasoning language models do not distinguish tokens used for computation from tokens that constitute persistent state: once generated, all hidden thoughts remain in context and influence future predictions. As a result, downstream reasoning may depend on failed attempts, dead ends, and private scratch work that should not be safely relied on later. We recast this phenomenon as a new training objective, state commitment learning: training models to explicitly distinguish information that should be committed as persistent state from temporary computation that can be discarded. We define a counterfactual criterion, persistent-state sufficiency, which makes it trainable and measurable whether an answer remains usable after hidden thoughts are erased. We then propose Counterfactual Erasure RL (CERL), which evaluates, under the same prefix, both a path that keeps hidden thoughts and a path that erases them, and gives reward only when the erasure path remains correct. We also introduce the Erasure Dependence Protocol and show across mathematics, long-chain logic, scientific QA, and multi-turn tool-use evaluation that CERL substantially reduces answer dependence on hidden thoughts without sacrificing accuracy, consistently outperforming correctness-only RL and long-answer SFT baselines.

AI.tldr: The paper teaches reasoning models what to remember versus what to forget. By training with counterfactual erasure of hidden thoughts, CERL makes answers stay correct even when scratch work is removed, improving robustness without hurting accuracy.
AI.motivation: Current reasoning language models treat all generated tokens as part of ongoing context, without distinguishing disposable intermediate computation from information that should persist. This causes future reasoning to depend on failed attempts, dead ends, and private scratch work, which is unsafe and brittle. The paper aims to train models to explicitly commit only useful persistent state.
AI.method: The authors formulate state commitment learning, define a counterfactual training target called persistent-state sufficiency, and propose Counterfactual Erasure RL (CERL). CERL compares two trajectories under the same prefix: one retains hidden thoughts and one erases them, and rewards the model only if the erased-thought trajectory still produces the correct answer. They also introduce the Erasure Dependence Protocol for evaluation.
AI.result: Across mathematics, long-chain logic, scientific question answering, and multi-turn tool-use benchmarks, CERL substantially reduces answer dependence on hidden thoughts without sacrificing accuracy. It consistently outperforms reinforcement learning that optimizes only correctness and supervised fine-tuning with long reasoning traces.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that explicitly training reasoning models to separate persistent state from temporary hidden computation is both feasible and effective. Its CERL method reduces reliance on hidden thoughts while preserving answer accuracy, outperforming correctness-only RL and long-answer SFT baselines across multiple reasoning and tool-use tasks.

title: SentinelBench: A Benchmark for Long-Running Monitoring Agents
summary:
AI agents are increasingly asked to carry out work that spans minutes, hours, or longer. Yet the default model of agent behavior is continuous action: issuing tool calls, refreshing pages, searching for alternatives, or otherwise trying to force progress. This is the wrong approach for many long-running tasks, which are better served by a strategy of sustained attention. Instead, agents should monitor an environment, notice when an external event makes progress possible, then respond promptly without wasting resources while waiting. To measure progress on this class of tasks, we introduce SentinelBench, an open-source benchmark for time-evolving monitoring tasks.
  SentinelBench contains 100 tasks across 10 synthetic web environments, including email, calendars, finance, professional networking, and entertainment. Each environment exposes a live web interface and replays a scripted sequence of events, requiring agents to navigate and reason about web pages whose state shifts underfoot. SentinelBench measures task completion, reaction time, and resource use, exposing the tradeoff between responsiveness and cost. We report results across three models and two browser-agent harnesses, establishing performance baselines for future comparison and demonstrating how agent design choices can dramatically impact key metrics. Together, these results show that SentinelBench distinguishes meaningful differences in agent behavior.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that long-horizon agents should wait and monitor, not constantly act, and introduces SentinelBench to measure how well agents handle such event-driven web tasks.
AI.motivation: Current agent defaults emphasize nonstop tool use and searching, which is inefficient and often inappropriate for tasks that require waiting for external events before acting.
AI.method: Create SentinelBench, an open-source benchmark with 100 tasks across 10 synthetic web environments (email, calendars, finance, professional networking, entertainment) that replay scripted events in live web interfaces; evaluate three models and two browser-agent harnesses using task completion, reaction time, and resource use.
AI.result: The benchmark exposes tradeoffs between responsiveness and cost, establishes baseline results across models and harnesses, and shows that agent design choices can substantially change performance metrics.
AI.conclusion: Long-running AI agents should use sustained attention rather than continuous action, and SentinelBench provides a benchmark to evaluate that behavior on time-evolving monitoring tasks.

title: CarbonSim: A Lifecycle-Aware Framework for Evaluating Carbon Tradeoffs in Hardware Upgrade Decisions
summary: As the demand for information and communication technologies (ICT) continues to rise, the environmental impact of computing systems is becoming an increasingly critical concern. Although newer hardware often improves performance and energy efficiency, these gains do not always offset the carbon cost of premature replacement, particularly under low-utilization workloads or low-carbon electricity grids. We present CarbonSim, a lifecycle-aware simulation framework for evaluating carbon tradeoffs in hardware upgrade decisions. CarbonSim combines workload execution profiles, machine-level power characteristics, embodied carbon inventories, scheduling policies, and time-varying grid carbon intensity to estimate total emissions under alternative deployment scenarios. The framework supports multiple embodied-carbon accounting strategies, including uniform amortization and front-loaded lifecycle attribution, enabling analysis under different hardware lifespan assumptions. Using heterogeneous CPU generations as calibration platforms, we demonstrate that newer machines do not always minimize total emissions: under lightly loaded workloads or cleaner electricity mixes, extending the useful life of existing hardware can reduce lifecycle carbon despite lower operational efficiency. These results highlight that hardware refresh decisions should be workload-aware, location-aware, and lifecycle-aware.

AI.tldr: CarbonSim is a simulation framework for comparing lifecycle carbon emissions of hardware upgrade choices. It shows that replacing old machines with newer, more efficient ones is not always the greenest option; under some workloads and grid conditions, using existing hardware longer emits less carbon overall.
AI.motivation: Rising ICT demand is increasing the environmental impact of computing. Although new hardware is often faster and more energy efficient, those gains may not compensate for the embodied carbon of early replacement, especially for low-utilization workloads or in low-carbon electricity regions. A better evaluation framework is therefore needed.
AI.method: The paper presents CarbonSim, a lifecycle-aware simulation framework that estimates total carbon emissions for hardware upgrade scenarios by combining workload execution profiles, machine-level power models, embodied carbon inventories, scheduling policies, and time-varying grid carbon intensity. It also supports different embodied-carbon accounting strategies such as uniform amortization and front-loaded attribution.
AI.result: Using heterogeneous CPU generations as calibration platforms, the study shows that newer machines do not always produce the lowest total emissions. Under lightly loaded workloads or cleaner electricity mixes, extending the service life of existing hardware can reduce lifecycle carbon despite worse operational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Hardware refresh decisions should not rely only on better device energy efficiency; they should be workload-aware, location-aware, and lifecycle-aware because keeping older machines longer can sometimes lower total lifecycle carbon emissions.

title: Bridging CAD and Data-Driven Design: Attributed Feature Graphs for Engineering Design
summary: Engineering design is an iterative, simulation-driven process where traditional workflows rely heavily on computationally expensive analyses such as finite element and computational fluid dynamics. Although data-driven methods have accelerated design evaluation and optimization, most existing geometric representations discard parametric and feature-level semantics, limiting their integration with CAD-driven design workflows and reducing model interpretability. To address this gap, this work introduces Attributed Feature Graphs (AFGs), a feature-based representation that encodes design features, such as extrusions, ribs, and pockets, as nodes and their geometric or dependency relations as directed edges. AFGs preserve design intent and parametric structure while remaining compatible with standard graph-based learning methods, enabling end-to-end learning directly on CAD-derived feature graphs. The paper demonstrates the proposed representation through a surrogate-modeling case study on the CarHoods10K automotive hood frame dataset, where a Graph Neural Network (GNN) is trained as an evaluation engine to predict performance metrics from AFG inputs. The learned model achieves competitive surrogate performance compared with traditional data-driven approaches, but with the added benefit that engineers can map predictions back to specific CAD features and interpret how individual design elements influence system behavior. Furthermore, because AFGs are built from native CAD features, engineers can directly edit the underlying geometry in the CAD environment and reevaluate the design through the same learned model.

AI.tldr: AFGs turn native CAD features into graphs for GNNs, giving competitive performance prediction with much better CAD integration and feature-level interpretability.
AI.motivation: Traditional simulation-driven engineering design is computationally expensive, and most existing data-driven geometric representations lose parametric and feature-level semantics. This weakens integration with CAD workflows and reduces interpretability, creating the need for a representation that preserves design intent and supports learning directly from CAD features.
AI.method: The paper proposes Attributed Feature Graphs (AFGs), where CAD features such as extrusions, ribs, and pockets are modeled as graph nodes and geometric/dependency relations are modeled as directed edges. A Graph Neural Network is then trained on AFGs from the CarHoods10K dataset to predict design performance metrics as a surrogate evaluation model.
AI.result: On the CarHoods10K automotive hood frame case study, the GNN trained on AFGs achieves competitive surrogate-model performance relative to traditional data-driven methods, while additionally allowing engineers to trace predictions back to specific CAD features and iteratively edit and reevaluate designs in CAD.
AI.conclusion: AFGs provide a CAD-native, feature-semantic graph representation that enables accurate and interpretable surrogate modeling while preserving direct editability in standard CAD workflows.

title: Recovering Physically Plausible Human-Object Interactions from Monocular Videos
summary: In this paper, we propose RePHO, a method to reconstruct physically plausible human-object interactions (HOI) from monocular videos. While existing kinematic-based approaches produce visually plausible motion, they often result in physically implausible artifacts such as interpenetration and object floating. To overcome these issues, we introduce a physics-guided reconstruction framework. We begin with a kinematic estimate and then refine it by training a policy with reinforcement learning (RL). This policy is optimized to reproduce the interaction in a physics simulator. Because kinematic estimates are typically noisy, naive RL training can fail. Therefore, we propose an adaptive sampling strategy with a dual self-updating mechanism that can identify the frames with the most informative and reliable kinematic reconstruction. Our process progressively improves reconstruction quality and yields physically consistent HOI sequences. We demonstrate our approach on two standard HOI benchmarks and achieve clear improvements in physical plausibility metrics over state-of-the-art methods. Project Page: https://dingbang777.github.io/RePHO/

AI.tldr: RePHO turns monocular HOI reconstruction into a physics-guided refinement problem: start from a noisy kinematic estimate, optimize it with RL in simulation, and use adaptive frame sampling to avoid bad supervision. This reduces interpenetration and object floating and improves benchmark physical plausibility.
AI.motivation: Existing monocular HOI reconstruction methods are largely kinematic and may look visually reasonable but often violate physics, producing artifacts such as body-object interpenetration and floating objects. The paper aims to improve physical realism and consistency.
AI.method: The method first obtains a kinematic HOI estimate from monocular video, then refines it in a physics simulator by training a reinforcement learning policy. To stabilize learning under noisy kinematic inputs, it uses an adaptive sampling strategy with a dual self-updating mechanism to select informative and reliable frames for training.
AI.result: On two standard HOI benchmarks, RePHO achieves clear improvements over state-of-the-art methods on physical plausibility metrics and produces more physically consistent HOI sequences.
AI.conclusion: RePHO can reconstruct human-object interactions from monocular video with higher physical plausibility than prior kinematic methods by refining kinematic estimates through physics-guided RL and adaptive frame sampling.

title: Efficient Punctuation Restoration via Weighted Lookahead Scoring Method for Streaming ASR Systems
comment: Accepted for presentation at The International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN) 2026
summary: Punctuation restoration improves ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) readability. However streaming ASR requires online decisions with limited future context. In streaming ASR, the system predicts punctuation incrementally, which makes generation-based approaches prone to latency and alignment failures under boundary-wise evaluation. This paper proposes a non-autoregressive scoring method (no free-form generation) that preserves the input transcript and makes a decision at each word boundary. Our method compares punctuation insertion hypotheses against a no-insertion baseline under a bounded K-subword-token lookahead, and calibrates decisions using a weight α and a validation-calibrated threshold τ (no parameter updates during inference). On IWSLT 2017, our scoring method achieves a 4-class macro F1 of 0.893 in the no fine-tuning setting (validation-calibrated, K=2) and 0.937 after fine-tuning (K=2), outperforming the prompt-based baseline (0.566) and a fine-tuned ELECTRA baseline (0.913) under the same lookahead budget. We analyze the impact of the lookahead budget through ablation studies on K.

AI.tldr: A streaming punctuation model that scores insert-vs-no-insert at each word boundary, instead of generating punctuation autoregressively, improves alignment and achieves the best macro F1 with only small lookahead.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that punctuation restoration is important for ASR readability, but in streaming ASR the model must decide online with only limited future context. Under this setting, generation-based methods often introduce latency and alignment errors, especially when evaluated boundary-wise, so a more stable boundary-preserving approach is needed.
AI.method: The method performs punctuation restoration as hypothesis scoring at each word boundary rather than free-form generation. For every boundary, it compares punctuation-insertion hypotheses against a no-insertion baseline using a bounded K-subword-token lookahead, then makes the final decision with calibration parameters: a weight alpha and a validation-tuned threshold tau. No parameter updates are required during inference.
AI.result: On IWSLT 2017, the proposed method reaches 0.893 4-class macro F1 without fine-tuning using validation calibration and K=2, and 0.937 after fine-tuning with K=2. It outperforms a prompt-based baseline at 0.566 and a fine-tuned ELECTRA baseline at 0.913 under the same lookahead budget. The paper also studies how performance changes with different lookahead budgets K.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a non-autoregressive boundary-wise scoring method is better suited for streaming punctuation restoration than generation-based approaches, because it preserves transcript alignment, works with limited lookahead, and achieves stronger boundary-wise macro F1 under the same online constraints.

title: FontFusion: Enhancing Generative Text in Diffusion Models with Typographic Conditioning
summary: Typography generation in diffusion models faces a persistent trade-off: enabling precise font control typically degrades text legibility, while maintaining readability often sacrifices typographic fidelity. We present FontFusion, a plug-and-play conditioning framework for Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architectures that resolves this dilemma through three core innovations: (1) a hierarchical token representation establishing explicit text-font relationships at multiple granularities, (2) position-aware embeddings creating spatial bindings between typography and image content, and (3) a multi-level token dropping strategy improving both computational efficiency and generalization to unseen fonts. Our systematic evaluation of font embedding spaces reveals that a dual encoder combining DeepFont and DINOv2 outperforms any single encoder for typography tasks. FontFusion demonstrates 76% relative improvement on challenging decorative fonts over single-encoder baselines and font consistency gains exceeding approximately 68-76% over unconditioned models, while integrating into existing DiT architectures without retraining.

AI.tldr: FontFusion adds hierarchical font-text conditioning, spatially aware embeddings, and token dropping to DiT-based diffusion models, substantially improving readable and style-faithful typography generation without retraining.
AI.motivation: Existing typography generation methods in diffusion models face a trade-off between accurate font control and readable text. The work aims to resolve this conflict while remaining compatible with existing DiT systems.
AI.method: The paper introduces three main components: a hierarchical token representation to model text-font relations at multiple granularities, position-aware embeddings to bind typography to spatial image context, and a multi-level token dropping strategy to improve efficiency and generalization. It also uses a dual font encoder that combines DeepFont and DINOv2 embeddings.
AI.result: FontFusion achieves a 76% relative improvement on difficult decorative fonts compared with single-encoder baselines, and improves font consistency by about 68-76% over unconditioned models. The dual DeepFont+DINOv2 encoder performs better than any single encoder for typography generation tasks.
AI.conclusion: FontFusion is a plug-and-play conditioning framework for Diffusion Transformer architectures that improves both font controllability and text legibility without requiring retraining, outperforming unconditioned and single-encoder baselines.

title: Gradient Descent with Large Step Size Restores Symmetry in Deep Linear Networks with Multi-Pathway
summary: Recent analyses of multi-pathway Deep Linear Networks use Gradient Flow to predict a "winner-takes-all" specialization in which path symmetry breaks and each feature concentrates in a single pathway. In this work, we show that discrete Gradient Descent (GD) with a large step size tells a different story. We prove that single-path solutions are sharp minima, whereas distributing signals across pathways reduces sharpness by a factor that decreases with both the number of pathways and depth. Consequently, while early training reproduces the depth-driven symmetry breaking predicted by GF, oscillations at the Edge of Stability subsequently override this tendency and drive the network into a re-balancing phase, where signals redistribute across pathways. Together, these results clarify how depth shapes pathway competition and explain why large-step GD favors shared representations rather than persistent single-pathway dominance.

AI.tldr: Large-step discrete GD changes the story from winner-takes-all to share-across-pathways: depth initially breaks symmetry, but edge-of-stability dynamics later push features to spread across pathways because distributed solutions are flatter than single-path minima.
AI.motivation: Prior work based on gradient flow predicts winner-takes-all specialization, where each feature collapses into a single pathway after symmetry breaking. The authors aim to explain whether this prediction still holds under practical discrete gradient descent with large learning rates, and how depth and pathway competition interact in that setting.
AI.method: The paper studies multi-pathway Deep Linear Networks under discrete gradient descent rather than continuous-time gradient flow. It provides theoretical analysis comparing the sharpness of single-path versus distributed-path solutions, and links training dynamics to oscillations at the edge of stability, considering the effects of pathway count and network depth.
AI.result: The authors prove that single-path solutions are sharp minima, while distributing signals across multiple pathways yields flatter minima, with sharpness reduced more strongly as depth and pathway number increase. Empirically or theoretically, training first shows gradient-flow-like symmetry breaking, but later edge-of-stability oscillations induce a re-balancing phase that redistributes signals.
AI.conclusion: Discrete gradient descent with a large step size does not sustain winner-takes-all specialization in multi-pathway deep linear networks. Instead, after an initial symmetry-breaking phase, edge-of-stability oscillations promote redistribution of features across pathways, making shared representations preferable because they correspond to flatter minima.

title: An interpretable and trustworthy AI framework for large-scale longitudinal structure-pain association studies using data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI)
summary: Purpose: To develop an interpretable and trustworthy AI framework that combines deep learning based MRI Osteoarthritis Knee Score (MOAKS) prediction with interpretable statistical modeling to study structure-pain relationships at scale using data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI). Materials and Methods: We first developed a deep learning framework to predict MOAKS features directly from knee MRIs and incorporated conformal prediction to provide prediction uncertainty quantification. This uncertainty-aware strategy enables explicit filtering of model outputs, retaining only high-confidence MOAKS predictions at the knee level. Second, we applied a longitudinal latent class mixed model (LCMM) to examine associations between key structural abnormalities and four complementary knee pain measurements. Results: Among the three MRI-defined abnormalities (i.e., bone marrow lesions (BML), cartilage loss (CART), and meniscal extrusion (ME)), our framework substantially improved the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and some other metrics. For example, MCC increased from 0.69 to 0.91 for BML, from 0.45 to 0.80 for CART, and from 0.59 to 0.89 for ME. Using these high-confidence predictions, we expanded the sample size to 2,175 knees for the LCMM analysis. Two distinct pain trajectories were identified (rapid and stable pain progression). The estimated odds ratios (95% CI) for the rapid progression group were 1.62 (1.12-2.35) for BML, 1.83 (1.24-2.70) for CART loss, and 2.50 (1.75-3.57) for ME. Conclusion: These results highlight the importance of these structural abnormalities as risk factors for pain and functional progression in osteoarthritis.

AI.tldr: An uncertainty-aware AI model predicted key knee MRI osteoarthritis features more accurately, then enabled large-scale longitudinal analysis showing that bone marrow lesions, cartilage loss, and especially meniscal extrusion are linked to faster pain progression.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to build an interpretable and trustworthy AI pipeline that can scale MRI-based structural assessment in osteoarthritis, overcome the limited availability of expert MOAKS readings, quantify model uncertainty, and clarify large-scale structure-pain relationships.
AI.method: The authors developed a deep learning framework to predict MRI Osteoarthritis Knee Score (MOAKS) features directly from knee MRIs, integrated conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification, filtered for high-confidence knee-level predictions, and then used a longitudinal latent class mixed model (LCMM) to analyze associations between MRI-derived structural abnormalities and four pain measurements in OAI data.
AI.result: The framework substantially improved classification performance for three MRI abnormalities: MCC rose from 0.69 to 0.91 for bone marrow lesions, 0.45 to 0.80 for cartilage loss, and 0.59 to 0.89 for meniscal extrusion. With high-confidence predictions, the sample expanded to 2,175 knees for LCMM analysis, which identified two pain trajectories: rapid and stable progression. Odds ratios for rapid progression were 1.62 for bone marrow lesions, 1.83 for cartilage loss, and 2.50 for meniscal extrusion.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that bone marrow lesions, cartilage loss, and meniscal extrusion are important structural risk factors associated with faster pain and functional progression in knee osteoarthritis, and that combining uncertainty-aware deep learning with interpretable longitudinal modeling enables scalable and trustworthy structure-pain analysis.

title: Biomazon: A Multimodal Dataset for 3D Forest Structure and Biomass Modeling in the Amazon Basin
summary: Accurate, spatially explicit characterization of tropical forest structure is essential for carbon accounting and ecosystem monitoring, yet most ML pipelines predict canopy-top height proxies (e.g., RH95/RH98) or AGBD as separate scalar targets, rather than learning the forest vertical structure as an ordered profile. The community lacks a ML-ready multimodal benchmark for predicting the entire GEDI RH profile jointly with AGBD, or for evaluating methods that enforce physically consistent ordering across RH percentiles. We address this with Biomazon, a 20 m multimodal benchmark dataset over the Amazon Basin that pairs GEDI RH and AGBD targets with multi-sensor predictors (Sentinel-1/2, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2, Copernicus DEM, Dynamic World LULC, and AlphaEarth embeddings) under standardized spatial splits and evaluation protocols. Using a shared encoder-decoder with task-specific heads as a baseline framework, we conduct a comprehensive ablation study of (i) backbone/model scale, (ii) modality contributions, and (iii) the use of auxiliary embeddings under standalone and fusion settings, and we report both single-target and joint-target results to quantify tradeoffs under a unified training protocol. Finally, we contextualize baseline performance through regionally aligned comparisons against existing gridded products, including GEDI L4D RH10-RH98 and AGBD, at matching temporal scale. Biomazon, together with the accompanying protocols and baseline results, establishes a reference benchmark for future work on structurally consistent RH-profile prediction and structure-biomass modeling in tropical forests.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Biomazon, a multimodal Amazon benchmark for learning the full GEDI canopy-height profile together with biomass, and supplies standardized protocols plus baseline experiments to support future structure-consistent forest modeling.
AI.motivation: Existing ML approaches usually predict canopy height proxies or AGBD as separate scalar targets, rather than modeling the ordered vertical forest structure profile. There is also no ML-ready benchmark for jointly predicting the full GEDI RH profile with AGBD while evaluating physically consistent ordering across RH percentiles.
AI.method: The paper builds a 20 m multimodal dataset combining GEDI RH and AGBD targets with predictors from Sentinel-1/2, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2, Copernicus DEM, Dynamic World LULC, and AlphaEarth embeddings. It uses a shared encoder-decoder with task-specific heads as a baseline and performs ablation studies on backbone/model scale, modality contribution, and auxiliary embeddings under standalone and fusion settings.
AI.result: The work provides standardized spatial splits, evaluation protocols, baseline single-target and joint-target results, modality/backbone ablations, and regionally aligned comparisons with existing gridded products such as GEDI L4D RH10-RH98 and AGBD.
AI.conclusion: Biomazon establishes a standardized multimodal benchmark over the Amazon Basin for jointly predicting the full GEDI RH vertical profile and AGBD, providing reference protocols and baselines for physically consistent tropical forest structure and biomass modeling.

title: From Scoring to Explanations: Evaluating SHAP and LLM Rationales for Rubric-based Teaching Quality Assessment
summary: Automated scoring models are increasingly used to assign rubric-based quality ratings to complex language performances, including classroom transcripts, yet they typically provide little insight into why a particular score is produced. We propose a general framework for sentence-level interpretability of rubric-based scoring that combines model-agnostic Shapley-value attributions with rationales generated by large language models (LLMs). Instantiated on the Quality of Feedback dimension of the CLASS framework using the NCTE corpus, the framework enables systematic comparison of fine-tuned pretrained language models (PLMs) and prompted LLMs on both scoring performance and explanation faithfulness. Across 6k annotated transcript segments, fine-tuned PLMs outperform LLMs in prediction accuracy but exhibit label compression toward mid-scale scores. Deletion-based tests show that SHAP identifies sentences that reliably drive model predictions, producing typically larger and more coherent prediction shifts than LLM-generated rationales. Cross-model analyses further reveal that SHAP attributions transfer robustly across architectures, whereas LLM rationales exert limited and inconsistent influence. Overall, the findings demonstrate that SHAP provides more faithful and transferable explanations for rubric-based scoring, and that the proposed framework offers a principled basis for evaluating both scoring models and their explanations in high-stakes educational settings and other rubric-based language assessment tasks.

AI.tldr: The paper builds and tests a sentence-level explanation framework for rubric-based scoring and finds that SHAP explanations are more faithful and transferable than LLM rationales, while fine-tuned PLMs score more accurately than prompted LLMs.
AI.motivation: Automated rubric-based scoring is widely used for complex language tasks, but existing systems usually give little explanation for why a score was assigned, which is problematic in high-stakes educational settings.
AI.method: The paper proposes a general interpretability framework for rubric-based scoring that combines model-agnostic SHAP sentence-level attributions with LLM-generated rationales, and evaluates fine-tuned pretrained language models versus prompted LLMs on 6k annotated classroom transcript segments from the NCTE corpus under the CLASS Quality of Feedback rubric using deletion tests and cross-model transfer analyses.
AI.result: Fine-tuned PLMs achieve higher scoring accuracy than prompted LLMs but tend to compress predictions toward middle scores. SHAP-selected sentences cause larger and more coherent prediction changes in deletion tests and transfer more robustly across model architectures than LLM-generated rationales, whose influence is limited and inconsistent.
AI.conclusion: SHAP-based sentence-level attributions are more faithful, coherent, and transferable than LLM-generated rationales for rubric-based automated scoring, providing a principled way to evaluate explanations in high-stakes assessment.

title: SC-MFJ: A Simple Haptic Quality Metric for Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Standard segmentation metrics such as Dice and Hausdorff distance measure geometric overlap but say nothing about whether a segmented surface is suitable for haptic rendering in surgical simulation. We propose SC-MFJ (Surface-Constrained Mean Force Jerk), a simple, inexpensive metric that samples a segmented organ surface with many short virtual stylus walks and measures how jerky the resulting contact forces are. The metric is computed from existing segmentation outputs and uses roughly one minute of CPU time per case. We evaluate three pancreas CT segmentation approaches-binary nnU-Net output, Gaussian-smoothed output, and learned signed distance function (SDF) regression-across 80 cases in five-fold cross-validation. SC-MFJ reveals a 147x gap in haptic quality between the raw binary baseline and simple Gaussian post-processing, a difference entirely invisible to Dice and HD95. It also shows that learned SDF regression, despite requiring full model retraining, produces more variable haptic quality than Gaussian smoothing, with a case-level standard deviation of 168 N/s2 compared with 22 N/s2 for Gaussian. A second evaluation on the LiTS liver dataset (131 cases) confirms the generality of these findings: the binary-to-Gaussian gap widens to 189x, and Gaussian smoothing again produces consistently low force jerk across all folds. Our results suggest that for haptic simulation applications, a one-line post-processing step may be sufficient, and that a cheap metric like SC-MFJ can flag problems that geometric metrics miss.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces SC-MFJ, a fast metric for judging whether segmentation surfaces are good for haptic rendering rather than just geometric accuracy. It shows that a simple Gaussian smoothing post-process dramatically improves haptic quality over raw binary masks and is more consistent than a retrained SDF model, while standard metrics like Dice and HD95 miss these differences.
AI.motivation: Dice and Hausdorff distance quantify geometric overlap but do not reflect whether a segmented surface yields stable, smooth force feedback during haptic rendering in surgical simulation. The work aims to provide a cheap, practical metric that captures this missing dimension of quality.
AI.method: The paper proposes SC-MFJ (Surface-Constrained Mean Force Jerk), a low-cost metric that evaluates segmentation suitability for haptic rendering by performing many short virtual stylus walks along the segmented organ surface and measuring the jerk of resulting contact forces. It is applied to outputs from binary nnU-Net, Gaussian-smoothed segmentations, and learned SDF regression on pancreas CT and validated again on LiTS liver data.
AI.result: Across 80 pancreas CT cases, SC-MFJ detected a 147x haptic-quality gap between raw binary output and Gaussian smoothing, which Dice and HD95 failed to show. Learned SDF regression had higher variability than Gaussian smoothing, with case-level standard deviation 168 N/s^2 versus 22 N/s^2. On 131 LiTS liver cases, the binary-to-Gaussian gap increased to 189x, and Gaussian smoothing again gave consistently low force jerk.
AI.conclusion: For haptic simulation, conventional geometric segmentation metrics are insufficient; SC-MFJ can expose clinically relevant surface-quality differences, and simple Gaussian smoothing may be a more reliable and cost-effective choice than retraining a learned SDF model.

title: Differentiable Efficient Operator Search
summary: Efficient multimodal foundation models often rely on manually designed token-reduction operators, such as pruning, merging, pooling, and adaptive reweighting. Although these operators appear different, we show that they can be interpreted as distinct regimes of a shared operator space. Based on this view, we introduce Efficient Operator Search, a differentiable framework that jointly searches where to reduce tokens, how many tokens to retain, and how reduced token information should be processed. The proposed search space parameterizes layer activation, retention budget, and operator behavior, while the search policy optimizes task performance under one-sided budget and cost constraints. This formulation recovers representative hand-designed baselines as special cases and further discovers hybrid operators beyond isolated manual designs. Experiments on multimodal benchmarks show that the searched operators achieve competitive accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, especially under aggressive visual-token reduction. These results suggest that efficient multimodal inference can be reframed from manual operator design to differentiable operator search.

AI.tldr: The paper unifies common token-reduction methods into one operator space and proposes a differentiable search framework that automatically finds better multimodal token-reduction strategies under efficiency constraints.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that efficient multimodal models currently depend heavily on hand-crafted token-reduction operators such as pruning, merging, pooling, and adaptive reweighting. These designs are fragmented and manually specified, so the paper aims to unify them and replace manual design with automated differentiable search.
AI.method: The method is Efficient Operator Search, a differentiable framework that jointly searches three aspects: where token reduction should happen, how many tokens to keep, and how the reduced token information should be processed. The search space parameterizes layer activation, retention budget, and operator behavior, while the policy is optimized under one-sided budget and cost constraints.
AI.result: Experiments on multimodal benchmarks show that the searched operators provide competitive accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, especially when visual-token reduction is aggressive. The framework also recovers representative manual baselines as special cases and finds hybrid operators beyond existing isolated designs.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that many manually designed token-reduction methods in multimodal foundation models can be unified within a shared operator space, and that a differentiable search framework can automatically discover more effective reduction strategies with strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

title: Synthetic Contrastive Reasoning for Multi-Table Q&A
summary: Multi-table question answering requires models to retrieve relevant evidence, link schemas, and perform compositional reasoning across relational tables. Existing multi-table Q&A resources typically provide questions and final answers but lack reasoning supervision that explains how answers are derived. To address this gap, we construct a synthetic contrastive reasoning-trace dataset for MMQA by generating validated positive traces and plausible negative traces with heterogeneous LLMs. We then use the resulting preference pairs to fine-tune open-weight LLMs with Contrastive Preference Optimization (CPO). Across Qwen3-14B, Mistral-8B, and Llama-3.1-8B, CPO achieves absolute average improvements over Q&A supervised fine-tuning ranging from 9.7%-16.3%, with gains up to 21 percentage points on MMQA. Ablations show that heterogeneous positive and negative trace generators strengthen the contrastive signal, and automated as well as human evaluations indicate that the generated pairs are largely faithful, coherent, and meaningfully contrastive.

AI.tldr: The paper improves multi-table QA by training LLMs on synthetic good-vs-bad reasoning traces; this significantly outperforms answer-only fine-tuning and works best when positive and negative traces are generated by different LLMs.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-table QA datasets usually contain only questions and final answers, lacking explicit reasoning supervision for evidence retrieval, schema linking, and compositional reasoning across relational tables.
AI.method: The paper builds a synthetic contrastive reasoning-trace dataset for MMQA by generating validated positive traces and plausible negative traces using heterogeneous LLMs, then fine-tunes open-weight LLMs such as Qwen3-14B, Mistral-8B, and Llama-3.1-8B with Contrastive Preference Optimization.
AI.result: Across three open-weight LLMs, the proposed CPO training gives absolute average gains of 9.7% to 16.3% over Q&A supervised fine-tuning, with improvements up to 21 percentage points on MMQA. Ablation and evaluation results show the generated preference pairs are faithful, coherent, and meaningfully contrastive.
AI.conclusion: Contrastive Preference Optimization on synthetic reasoning-trace preference pairs substantially improves multi-table question answering over standard Q&A supervised fine-tuning, and heterogeneous trace generators further enhance the learning signal.

title: Three-Dimensional Retinal Microvasculature Restoration in OCT Angiography
summary: Optical coherence tomographic angiography (OCTA) is a powerful technique for imaging retinal microvasculature. However, acquiring reliable quantification of retinal blood flow and areas of retinal nonperfusion is challenging because of imaging artifacts. Existing methods primarily focus on noise suppression, projection artifact removal, or signal enhancement to improve the image quality of OCTA in cross-sectional or two-dimensional (2D) en face projections, while neglecting the intrinsic three-dimensional vascular architecture. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based algorithm for restoring capillary anatomical vasculature from a single OCTA volume. The network consists of an EfficientNet-B5 encoder and a decoder incorporating concurrent spatial and channel squeeze-and-excitation modules, connected via skip connections to preserve spatial resolution. Three adjacent B-frames are used as input to predict the restored middle B-frame. We evaluated the performance of the model using the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) against ground truth generated from averaging multiple scans. The results show that the proposed model significantly (both p < 0.001) improved image quality compared with the original single OCTA volume, with a PSNR of 26.16 +/- 1.26 vs. 22.23 +/- 0.78 and an SSIM of 0.91 +/- 0.02 vs. 0.72 +/- 0.03. The proposed model also significantly (p < 0.001) improved microvascular fidelity, measured by the Dice coefficient overlap between the model output and ground truth, in both 2D and 3D by at least 3.8% and 51.2%, respectively, across several different vascular slabs.

AI.tldr: 该论文提出一种利用相邻B-frame恢复单次OCTA三维毛细血管结构的深度学习模型，显著优于原始单次扫描，在图像质量和血管结构一致性上都有明显提升。 / This paper presents a deep learning model that restores 3D capillary structure in single OCTA using adjacent B-frames, clearly outperforming raw single scans in both image quality and vascular structural consistency.
AI.motivation: 单次OCTA在定量视网膜血流和无灌注区域时容易受伪影影响，现有方法多关注2D或横截面图像增强，忽视了血管的内在三维结构，因此需要一种面向3D血管解剖恢复的方法。 / Single-scan OCTA quantification is unreliable due to artifacts, and prior methods mainly enhance 2D or cross-sectional images while neglecting intrinsic 3D vascular architecture, motivating a method for 3D anatomical vascular restoration.
AI.method: 作者构建了一个基于EfficientNet-B5编码器和带并行空间/通道SE模块解码器的网络，通过跳跃连接保留空间分辨率，并以相邻3个B-frame作为输入来预测中间B-frame的恢复结果。 / The authors built a network with an EfficientNet-B5 encoder and a decoder using concurrent spatial and channel squeeze-and-excitation modules, linked by skip connections; three adjacent B-frames are used to predict the restored middle B-frame.
AI.result: 与原始单次OCTA体数据相比，模型在PSNR和SSIM上均显著提升（26.16±1.26 vs 22.23±0.78；0.91±0.02 vs 0.72±0.03，均p<0.001），并且在多个血管层面上将2D和3D Dice重叠度至少分别提高3.8%和51.2%。 / Compared with the original single OCTA volume, the model significantly improved PSNR and SSIM (26.16±1.26 vs 22.23±0.78; 0.91±0.02 vs 0.72±0.03, both p<0.001) and increased 2D and 3D Dice overlap by at least 3.8% and 51.2%, respectively, across several vascular slabs.
AI.conclusion: 提出的深度学习方法能够从单次OCTA体数据中恢复更接近真实毛细血管解剖结构的血管图像，显著提升图像质量与2D/3D微血管保真度。 / The proposed deep learning method can restore capillary anatomy from a single OCTA volume and significantly improve both image quality and 2D/3D microvascular fidelity.

title: Multi-Granularity Reasoning for Natural Language Inference
summary: Natural Language Inference (NLI) is a fundamental task in natural language understanding that requires determining the logical relationship between a premise and a hypothesis. Despite the remarkable success of transformer-based pre-trained models, most existing approaches primarily rely on the final-layer token representations, which are often insufficient for capturing the complex and hierarchical semantic interactions required for effective reasoning. In particular, fine-grained lexical cues, phrasal compositions, and higher-level contextual semantics are typically entangled or diluted in a single representation space. To address these limitations, we propose a novel \emph{Multi-Granularity Reasoning Network} (MGRN) that explicitly leverages hierarchical semantic features within an interactive reasoning space. The proposed framework mimics the human cognitive process of language understanding, which naturally progresses from shallow lexical matching to deeper semantic abstraction and logical reasoning. By integrating semantic information across multiple granularities in a progressive and structured manner, MGRN is able to uncover intricate semantic relationships underlying natural language expressions. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks demonstrate that MGRN consistently outperforms strong baseline models, validating the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach.

AI.tldr: MGRN针对传统NLI模型只看最终层表示的问题，显式做多粒度层次语义推理，因此在多个NLI数据集上表现更好。 / MGRN addresses the limitation of using only final-layer representations in NLI by explicitly performing multi-granularity hierarchical reasoning, leading to better results across multiple NLI benchmarks.
AI.motivation: 现有基于Transformer的NLI方法大多依赖最终层token表示，这种单一表示空间难以充分捕捉复杂、层次化的语义交互，导致细粒度词汇线索、短语组合及高层上下文语义被纠缠或稀释。 / Existing transformer-based NLI methods mainly rely on final-layer token representations, and this single representation space is often insufficient for capturing complex hierarchical semantic interactions, causing fine-grained lexical cues, phrasal compositions, and higher-level contextual semantics to be entangled or diluted.
AI.method: 提出Multi-Granularity Reasoning Network (MGRN)，以渐进、结构化的方式融合词汇级、短语级和上下文级等多层次语义信息，模拟人类从浅层词汇匹配到深层语义抽象与逻辑推理的理解过程。 / The paper proposes a Multi-Granularity Reasoning Network (MGRN) that progressively and structurally integrates lexical-, phrasal-, and contextual-level semantic information, mimicking human understanding from shallow lexical matching to deeper semantic abstraction and logical reasoning.
AI.result: 在多个公开基准上的大量实验表明，MGRN持续优于强基线模型，显示出较强的有效性与鲁棒性。摘要未给出具体数值。 / Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks show that MGRN consistently outperforms strong baseline models, indicating strong effectiveness and robustness, although the abstract does not provide exact numerical gains.
AI.conclusion: MGRN通过在交互式推理空间中显式整合多粒度层次语义特征，能够更有效地建模前提与假设之间的复杂语义关系，并在多个公开NLI基准上稳定优于强基线，证明了其有效性与鲁棒性。 / MGRN explicitly integrates hierarchical semantic features in an interactive reasoning space, enabling more effective modeling of complex semantic relations between premise and hypothesis, and it consistently outperforms strong baselines on multiple public NLI benchmarks, demonstrating effectiveness and robustness.

title: DiffSlack: Learning under Nonlinear Inequality Constraints via Learnable Slack Variables
summary: Enforcing nonlinear inequality constraints in neural networks remains challenging, especially when the output is subject to many coupled constraints. Existing hard constraint methods often impose structural restrictions on the constraint set or introduce substantial computational overhead for large-scale nonlinear problems. Here, we propose DiffSlack, a differentiable projection layer for nonlinear inequality-constrained neural prediction. DiffSlack reformulates inequalities as equalities with learnable slack variables, which are predicted as part of the augmented network output and provide a data-driven warm start for damped Gauss-Newton projection. The projection layer maps raw predictions onto the augmented feasible manifold while preserving end-to-end differentiability. A two-stage curriculum further stabilizes training and improves constraint satisfaction. We evaluate DiffSlack on vehicle path planning with 200 nonlinear inequality constraints from collision avoidance, curvature limits, and waypoint spacing. Compared with existing learning-based baselines, DiffSlack achieves a higher planning success rate and stronger geometric constraint satisfaction under a comparable inference budget. Ablation studies further show that the hard projection layer reduces sensitivity to supervision quality. Closed-loop tracking in CARLA and real-world vehicle experiments confirms the executability of the generated trajectories. These results demonstrate that DiffSlack provides a practical and scalable approach to embedding hard inequality constraints into neural networks for engineering applications.

AI.tldr: DiffSlack adds learnable slack variables and a differentiable projection step so neural networks can satisfy many nonlinear inequality constraints more reliably and efficiently, with strong results in constrained vehicle path planning.
AI.motivation: Existing hard-constraint approaches for neural networks struggle with many coupled nonlinear inequality constraints because they either require restrictive constraint structure or incur high computational cost at scale. The authors aim to provide a more practical and scalable method.
AI.method: The paper proposes DiffSlack, which converts nonlinear inequality constraints into equalities using learnable slack variables, predicts these slacks jointly with the original outputs, and then applies a differentiable damped Gauss-Newton projection onto the augmented feasible manifold. A two-stage curriculum is used to stabilize training and improve feasibility.
AI.result: On vehicle path planning with 200 nonlinear inequality constraints, DiffSlack outperforms learning-based baselines in planning success rate and geometric constraint satisfaction under similar inference cost. Ablation studies show reduced sensitivity to supervision quality, and CARLA plus real-world experiments confirm executable trajectories.
AI.conclusion: DiffSlack is a practical, scalable, and differentiable hard-constraint layer that effectively embeds nonlinear inequality constraints into neural networks for engineering tasks such as vehicle trajectory generation.

title: Stability vs. Manipulability: Evaluating Robustness Under Post-Decision Interaction in LLM Judges
comment: Accepted at ACL 2026 GEM (Generation, Evaluation and Metrics) Workshop
summary: LLM-as-judge evaluation is widely used in benchmarking pipelines, where model outputs are compared and ranked using automated evaluators. These pipelines typically assume that judgments are stable properties of fixed inputs. We show that this assumption does not hold under interaction. We study post-decision manipulability: the extent to which an evaluation outcome can be altered through subsequent conversation with the judge after an initial decision has been made. Across controlled experiments on MT-Bench and AlpacaEval, we find that LLM judges are highly stable under repeated and neutral reevaluation, yet become substantially reversible under targeted post-decision challenge. An anti-baseline challenge protocol shows that stable judgments can be overturned through motivated interaction, while a counterbalanced target-validation protocol separates this reversibility from net target-directed steering. These reversals have practical consequences: they can degrade agreement with human preferences, shift benchmark rankings, and produce harmful evaluation changes despite high self-reported confidence. Authority framing is especially destabilizing, and revised judgments are often accompanied by low-overlap justifications, suggesting post hoc rationalization rather than reliable error correction. We introduce the Evaluation Robustness Score (ERS) to quantify interactional robustness by combining reversal susceptibility with counterbalanced directional effects. Our findings identify post-decision interaction as a distinct failure mode for LLM-as-judge evaluation and motivate evaluation protocols that measure not only static agreement, but robustness under challenge.

AI.tldr: LLM judges look stable if you simply ask again, but their decisions can often be flipped after targeted follow-up arguments. This makes benchmark results manipulable, motivates stronger evaluation protocols, and leads the authors to propose ERS as a robustness metric.
AI.motivation: Current LLM-as-judge benchmarking pipelines assume that judgments are stable for fixed inputs. The paper questions this assumption by asking whether a judge's decision can be changed after the decision has already been made through subsequent interaction.
AI.method: The paper conducts controlled experiments on MT-Bench and AlpacaEval to test post-decision manipulability. It compares repeated/neutral reevaluation against targeted post-decision challenge, uses an anti-baseline challenge protocol to test whether stable decisions can be overturned, introduces a counterbalanced target-validation protocol to separate pure reversibility from directional steering, and proposes the Evaluation Robustness Score (ERS) to quantify robustness.
AI.result: LLM judges remain mostly stable under repeated or neutral reevaluation, but become substantially reversible under targeted challenge. These reversals can reduce agreement with human preferences, alter benchmark rankings, and create harmful evaluation changes despite high judge confidence. Authority framing is particularly destabilizing, and changed justifications often have low overlap with original ones, indicating post hoc rationalization.
AI.conclusion: Post-decision interaction is a distinct and important failure mode in LLM-as-judge systems: even initially stable judgments can be reversed through targeted challenge, so evaluation should measure robustness under interaction, not only static agreement.

title: Deep Learning-assisted AMD Staging based on OCT and OCT Angiography
summary: To develop and evaluate deep learning models for automated grading of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) severity using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA) data. Two hundred seventy-one participants aged >= 50 years with varying AMD severities. Central macular 6 x 6 mm OCT/OCTA volumes were acquired using a swept-source OCTA system (SOLIX; Visionix/Optovue Inc., CA). AMD severity was graded into four stages (No AMD, Early AMD, Intermediate AMD, and Advanced AMD) according to the AREDS simplified severity scale. Three deep learning models were developed using different input modalities: (1) biomarker maps derived from segmented pathological features, including retinal fluid, drusen, geographic atrophy (GA), and macular neovascularization (MNV); (2) two-dimensional (2D) en face OCT and OCTA projections; and (3) three-dimensional (3D) OCT/OCTA volumes. EfficientNet-based architectures were trained using normalized inputs, data augmentation, and five-fold cross-validation. A total of 2,030 OCT/OCTA volumes from 351 eyes of 271 participants were analyzed. All models demonstrated strong AMD staging performance with substantial agreement with the reference standard (QWK >= 0.83). The biomarker-based model achieved the highest overall performance (QWK = 0.85 +/- 0.03, mean +/- standard deviation) and the best detection of early AMD (F1-score = 0.59 +/- 0.14). The 3D model achieved performance comparable to the 2D OCT/OCTA model (QWK = 0.83 +/- 0.04 vs. 0.83 +/- 0.09), while the 2D OCT/OCTA model showed the highest precision (0.79 +/- 0.06) and most accurately identified eyes without AMD. Deep learning models using OCT/OCTA data can accurately and automatically grade AMD severity. Among the evaluated approaches, the biomarker-based model provided the most balanced performance and showed particular value for early AMD detection.

AI.tldr: 研究比较了3种基于OCT/OCTA的AMD自动分期深度学习方案。三者都有效，但基于病灶生物标志物图谱的模型总体最好，尤其更适合早期AMD检出。 / This study compared three OCT/OCTA-based deep learning strategies for automated AMD staging. All worked well, but the biomarker-map model was the strongest overall, especially for detecting early AMD.
AI.motivation: AMD分期依赖专业判读，自动化、可扩展且准确的分级工具可提升临床筛查与随访效率；同时需要比较不同OCT/OCTA输入形式的价值，明确哪种表示最适合AMD严重度分级。 / AMD staging requires expert interpretation, so an automated, scalable, and accurate grading tool could improve screening and follow-up efficiency. The study also aims to compare different OCT/OCTA input modalities to determine which representation is most useful for AMD severity grading.
AI.method: 研究纳入271名50岁及以上、不同AMD严重程度的受试者，对其中央黄斑6×6 mm区域进行扫频源OCT/OCTA成像。依据AREDS简化严重度量表分为4期。构建3类EfficientNet模型：基于分割病灶生成的生物标志物图谱、2D en face OCT/OCTA投影、以及3D OCT/OCTA体数据；采用标准化、数据增强和五折交叉验证训练评估。 / The study enrolled 271 participants aged 50+ with varying AMD severities and acquired 6×6 mm central macular swept-source OCT/OCTA scans. AMD was graded into four AREDS-based stages. Three EfficientNet-based models were developed using segmented biomarker maps, 2D en face OCT/OCTA projections, and 3D OCT/OCTA volumes, with normalization, augmentation, and five-fold cross-validation.
AI.result: 共分析271名受试者351只眼的2030个OCT/OCTA体数据。所有模型均表现良好，与参考标准具有较强一致性（QWK≥0.83）。生物标志物模型最佳（QWK=0.85±0.03），且早期AMD检测F1最高（0.59±0.14）。3D模型与2D OCT/OCTA模型总体相当（QWK 0.83±0.04 vs 0.83±0.09），而2D模型精度最高（0.79±0.06），且最善于识别无AMD眼。 / A total of 2,030 OCT/OCTA volumes from 351 eyes of 271 participants were analyzed. All models showed strong agreement with the reference standard (QWK≥0.83). The biomarker-based model performed best overall (QWK=0.85±0.03) and achieved the highest F1 for early AMD detection (0.59±0.14). The 3D model performed comparably to the 2D OCT/OCTA model (QWK 0.83±0.04 vs 0.83±0.09), while the 2D model had the highest precision (0.79±0.06) and best identified non-AMD eyes.
AI.conclusion: 基于OCT/OCTA的深度学习模型能够准确自动分级AMD严重程度，其中基于生物标志物图谱的模型整体表现最均衡，尤其在早期AMD检出上最有价值。 / Deep learning models using OCT/OCTA can accurately and automatically grade AMD severity, with the biomarker-based model providing the most balanced overall performance and particular value for early AMD detection.

title: LANTERN: Layered Archival and Temporal Episodic Retrieval Network for Long-Context LLM Conversations
summary: Large language models discard critical details when conversation history is compacted to fit within finite context windows. We present LANTERN (Layered Archival aNd Temporal Episodic Retrieval Network), a lightweight memory layer that proactively archives every conversation turn and restores relevant details after compaction via hybrid retrieval -- requiring zero LLM calls and adding fewer than 25ms of latency per turn. On 94 real multi-turn conversations (1,894 ground-truth facts, human-validated at kappa=0.81), LANTERN-Rerank recovers 78.3% of verifiable facts lost to compaction, significantly outperforming a faithful reimplementation of MemGPT's LLM-driven extraction and multi-query search pipeline (72.4%; Wilcoxon p<0.0001, 95% CI [+3.1, +8.6] pp, d=0.43) at a fraction of the inference cost. Even without the reranker, base LANTERN matches or exceeds this LLM-driven baseline (p=0.005) using zero LLM calls. When four production LLMs answer fact-bearing questions using LANTERN-restored context, accuracy improves by 8.4 percentage points on average (Wilcoxon p<0.05 for each model individually), demonstrating that the recovered context is useful across diverse model architectures. We release the full evaluation framework -- paired significance tests, failure analysis, fact-type stratification, and compaction robustness analysis -- to support reproducibility and future work.

AI.tldr: LANTERN adds a fast external memory layer for chat systems: it stores all turns, retrieves lost facts after context compression, beats an LLM-based memory baseline, costs less, and improves downstream question answering.
AI.motivation: Current large language models lose important details when long conversation histories are compacted to fit limited context windows. The work aims to recover those lost details efficiently, accurately, and cheaply, without adding expensive LLM-based memory processing.
AI.method: The paper proposes LANTERN, which archives every conversation turn and later retrieves relevant information after compaction using a hybrid retrieval pipeline; the stronger variant, LANTERN-Rerank, adds a reranking stage while still avoiding LLM calls and keeping latency below 25 ms per turn.
AI.result: On 94 real multi-turn conversations containing 1,894 human-validated facts, LANTERN-Rerank recovered 78.3% of facts lost to compaction versus 72.4% for a MemGPT-style LLM-driven baseline, with statistically significant gains. Base LANTERN also matched or surpassed the baseline using zero LLM calls. Restored context improved answer accuracy of four production LLMs by 8.4 percentage points on average.
AI.conclusion: LANTERN is a lightweight memory layer that restores conversation details lost during context compaction without requiring any LLM calls, achieving better factual recovery and lower cost than an LLM-driven memory baseline, and improving downstream QA accuracy across multiple production LLMs.

title: Alpha-RTL: Test-Time Training for RTL Hardware Optimization
summary:
Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in generating
  functionally correct register-transfer-level (RTL) hardware designs.
  Recent systems improve further through EDA-integrated reinforcement
  learning with syntax, simulation, and PPA rewards, but train a general
  RTL generator before deployment while test-time approaches search with
  a frozen policy. We instead perform reinforcement learning at test time,
  allowing the LLM policy to adapt to executable EDA feedback for the
  specific RTL problem at hand. We propose TTT-RTL, to our knowledge the
  first per-design test-time training framework that closes the loop
  between an LLM policy and an EDA pipeline for RTL optimization. TTT-RTL
  samples candidate implementations, verifies them through syntax checking
  and simulation, scores valid designs using synthesis-derived PPA product,
  reuses high-reward variants through a PUCT-indexed design-state pool,
  and updates the policy with an entropic policy-gradient objective. To
  stabilize policy updates under sparse or plateaued rewards, we introduce
  an adaptive KL-budget controller that adjusts the entropy constraint
  using reference KL, effective sample size, and reward saturation signals.
  On RTLLM v2.0 under Nangate 45nm, TTT-RTL reduces the geometric-mean
  PPA product by 65.1% over the reference, outperforming the strongest
  published frozen-policy agent baseline at 26.1%. On an industrial
  XuanTie C910 FPU leading-zero-anticipation unit under Sky130, TTT-RTL
  achieves a 59.4% ADP reduction, and ablations confirm that policy
  adaptation, state reuse, and KL-budget control each contribute. These
  results suggest that test-time training with executable EDA feedback can
  move LLM-based RTL generation beyond functional correctness toward
  physically optimized hardware.

AI.tldr: TTT-RTL is a per-design test-time RL framework that lets an LLM adapt to real EDA feedback while generating RTL, significantly improving hardware physical metrics over frozen-policy methods.
AI.motivation: Prior RTL-generation systems either train a general policy before deployment or perform test-time search with a frozen policy, which limits adaptation to the specific RTL instance. The paper aims to let the LLM adapt online to executable EDA feedback for each design problem, improving not just correctness but physical optimization.
AI.method: The paper proposes TTT-RTL, a test-time training framework for RTL generation that samples candidate designs, filters them with syntax and simulation checks, evaluates valid candidates using synthesis-derived PPA product, reuses promising variants via a PUCT-indexed design-state pool, and updates the LLM policy using an entropic policy-gradient objective. It also introduces an adaptive KL-budget controller to stabilize updates under sparse or plateaued rewards.
AI.result: On RTLLM v2.0 under Nangate 45nm, TTT-RTL reduces geometric-mean PPA product by 65.1% over the reference and surpasses the strongest published frozen-policy baseline at 26.1%. On the industrial XuanTie C910 FPU leading-zero-anticipation unit under Sky130, it achieves a 59.4% ADP reduction. Ablation studies show that policy adaptation, state reuse, and KL-budget control each matter.
AI.conclusion: TTT-RTL demonstrates that per-design test-time reinforcement learning with executable EDA feedback can substantially improve RTL physical quality beyond functional correctness, yielding strong PPA/ADP gains on both benchmark and industrial cases.

title: Residual Modeling for High-Fidelity Learned Compression of Scientific Data
summary:
Lossy compression is essential for massive spatiotemporal data from scientific simulations. Learned compressors can achieve high compression ratios at moderate accuracy targets, but their aggregate reconstruction losses do not guarantee accuracy for each block. Existing Guaranteed Autoencoder (GAE) methods add a per-block residual correction by retaining SVD/PCA-style coefficients until the target is met. This works at moderate tolerances, but in the high-fidelity regime with block-level NRMSE from 10^-6 to 10^-4, the number of retained coefficients grows quickly and the correction stream dominates the total rate.
  We propose a residual-centric view: the learned residual is structurally different from the original scientific field and should be coded with a representation designed for that residual. We introduce two residual coders. LBRC is a deterministic, training-free pipeline that adaptively quantizes the learned residual to the target NRMSE and losslessly encodes the resulting integer residual using 3D Lorenzo differencing, zigzag mapping, bit-plane coding, and entropy coding. NGLR adds a causal neural predictor that outputs a normalized bias for an integer-rounded Lorenzo prediction in the same deterministic integer pipeline, reducing the entropy of the remaining residual code while preserving deterministic decoding. The predictor weights are serialized and counted in the bitstream.
  Across E3SM, JHTDB, and ERA5 at block-level NRMSE targets from 10^-6 to 10^-4, LBRC improves compression ratio over GAE by 30-60% and is broadly competitive with SZ. NGLR adds a further 10-40% over LBRC and outperforms SZ in the evaluated high-fidelity regime. These results show that residual representations tailored to learned-compressor residuals can preserve the advantage of learned compression when global residual correction becomes rate-dominant.

AI.tldr: For ultra-high-fidelity scientific data compression, replacing coefficient-based residual correction with residual-specific coding works better: a deterministic residual coder beats prior guaranteed autoencoders, and adding a causal neural predictor beats SZ in the tested regime.
AI.motivation: Existing guaranteed autoencoder methods ensure per-block accuracy by storing residual correction coefficients, but at very high fidelity targets (block-level NRMSE 10^-6 to 10^-4) the number of retained coefficients grows rapidly and the correction stream becomes the dominant bitrate. The authors argue that learned residuals have different structure from the original scientific field and therefore require a residual-specific representation.
AI.method: The paper proposes two residual coders for blockwise error-guaranteed learned compression. LBRC is a deterministic, training-free pipeline that adaptively quantizes learned residuals to a target block-level NRMSE and then losslessly compresses the integer residuals using 3D Lorenzo differencing, zigzag mapping, bit-plane coding, and entropy coding. NGLR extends this with a causal neural predictor that provides a normalized bias for integer-rounded Lorenzo prediction while keeping deterministic integer decoding; predictor weights are serialized into the bitstream.
AI.result: On E3SM, JHTDB, and ERA5 with block-level NRMSE targets from 10^-6 to 10^-4, LBRC improves compression ratio by 30-60% over prior GAE methods and is generally competitive with SZ. NGLR further improves compression ratio by 10-40% over LBRC and outperforms SZ in the tested high-fidelity setting.
AI.conclusion: Tailoring the residual coding stage to the structure of learned-compressor residuals is more effective than using generic SVD/PCA-style guaranteed correction in the high-fidelity regime. Residual-centric coding preserves the benefits of learned compression when correction bitrate would otherwise dominate.

title: UniPixie: Unified and Probabilistic 3D Physics Learning via Flow Matching
comment: Published at CVPR 2026 as a Highlight. Project page: https://unipixie.github.io/
summary: Existing feed-forward networks excel at predicting a single set of physical properties from visual appearance, but this point-estimate paradigm fundamentally fails to capture the real world's inherent physical ambiguity. We address this by reframing physics prediction as a task of learning a controllable, continuous distribution of material properties. We introduce UNIPIXIE, a framework trained to predict a continuous and parameterized path of physically plausible material properties from a single visual input. By learning a direct mapping along an object's softest-to-stiffest spectrum on our PIXIEMULTIVERSE dataset, UNIPIXIE allows for controllable generation of diverse, physically valid material fields via a single intuitive parameter. Crucially, UNIPIXIE introduces a novel unified architecture to produce simulation-ready parameters for diverse physics solvers, including continuum-based Material Point Method (MPM), reduced-order deformation based on Linear Blend Skinning (LBS), and anchor-based Spring-Mass systems, addressing a key portability issue in prior work. Experiments show our approach not only generates a rich variety of plausible dynamics but also reduces Young's Modulus prediction error by over 50% against the strongest deterministic baseline, bridging the gap between static point estimates and the continuous nature of physical reality. Project page: https://unipixie.github.io/
