We address this limitation with a phase-aware large language model (LLM) agent that conditions each proposal on its full optimization history, navigating the coupled parameter space across phase-partitioned exploration, exploitation, and fine-tuning stages. Evaluated on the HICO-DET human-object interaction retrieval benchmark using Intel VDMS (Visual Data Management System), our agent outperforms Optuna TPE by +33.3% and VDTuner by +34.2% under SIEVE (Safeguarded Index Evaluation of Vector-search Efficiency, a quality-constrained throughput metric), delivering a 15.3x throughput gain over UniIR. Validation across three benchmarks confirms that the agent's advantage grows with the degree of parameter coupling: +33.3% on HICO-DET (high coupling), methods converge within 1% on GLDv2 (moderate coupling) and within 3.6% on SIFT1M (near-independent control). Cross-system validation on Milvus confirms the optimizer ranks first on all three datasets without modification, demonstrating transferability across vector database management system (VDBMS) platforms.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that an LLM-based, history-aware, phase-structured hyperparameter optimizer works especially well for retrieval systems with strongly interacting parameters, outperforming standard HPO baselines and generalizing across databases.
AI.motivation: Traditional HPO methods such as TPE and Gaussian Process Bayesian Optimization assume parameter independence, which makes them weak for retrieval systems with highly coupled configuration spaces.
AI.method: The paper proposes a phase-aware LLM optimization agent that conditions each hyperparameter proposal on the full optimization history and organizes search into phase-partitioned exploration, exploitation, and fine-tuning stages.
AI.result: On HICO-DET with Intel VDMS, the agent beats Optuna TPE by 33.3% and VDTuner by 34.2% under SIEVE, and achieves 15.3x throughput over UniIR. Its advantage shrinks as parameter coupling decreases: 33.3% on HICO-DET, about 1% on GLDv2, and 3.6% on SIFT1M. It also ranks first on all three datasets on Milvus without modification.
AI.conclusion: A phase-aware LLM agent is more effective than traditional HPO methods for multi-stage retrieval systems when parameters are strongly coupled, and it transfers across VDBMS platforms.

title: Executable Schema Contracts: From Automatic Ingestion to Multi-Source Retrieval
summary: Real-world data spans tables, documents, and semi-structured files with implicit semantics. Querying this data requires integrating evidence across inconsistent schemas and formats, yet existing approaches either demand costly manual engineering or bypass structure entirely. We present a system that automatically discovers an executable schema from raw multi-source data and uses it as a shared contract for knowledge graph construction and query-time retrieval. A closed-world field catalog constrains LLM-based schema discovery to attested fields; deterministic structural analysis infers identity keys, foreign keys, and source hierarchy; and the resulting schema drives extraction, deduplication, and cross-source linking into a provenance-aware knowledge graph. At query time the schema -- optionally extended via a monotonic protocol -- conditions a multi-tool agent routing retrieval across structured lookup, graph traversal, and vector search, returning grounded answers with traceable citations. In controlled zero-shot comparisons using the same LLM, data, and evaluation harness, the system improves over retrieval-only and decomposition-based baselines across four QA benchmarks, with ablations showing that schema-conditioned routing, structural intelligence, and schema-guided construction each contribute to the gains.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a system that automatically discovers an executable schema from heterogeneous raw data and uses it to build a provenance-aware knowledge graph and guide multi-tool retrieval, yielding better zero-shot QA than strong retrieval-based baselines.
AI.motivation: Real-world enterprise data is spread across tables, documents, and semi-structured files with inconsistent schemas and implicit semantics. Existing solutions either require expensive manual schema engineering or ignore structure, making reliable cross-source querying and grounded QA difficult.
AI.method: The method first performs constrained LLM-based schema discovery using a closed-world field catalog, then applies deterministic structural analysis to infer identity keys, foreign keys, and source hierarchy. This executable schema drives extraction, deduplication, provenance-aware KG construction, and query-time multi-tool retrieval over structured lookup, graph traversal, and vector search; the schema can also be extended through a monotonic protocol.
AI.result: In controlled zero-shot experiments using the same LLM, data, and evaluation harness, the system outperforms retrieval-only and decomposition-based baselines on four QA benchmarks. Ablation studies show that schema-conditioned routing, structural intelligence, and schema-guided construction each contribute to the observed gains.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that automatically induced executable schemas can serve as a reliable shared contract across heterogeneous real-world data, improving both knowledge graph construction and query-time retrieval. Schema-conditioned routing and structural analysis materially improve grounded QA over retrieval-only and decomposition-based baselines.

title: Anomaly Detection for Electro-Hydrostatic Actuators using LSTM Autoencoder
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables, ESREL 2026 -European Safety and Reliability Conference, accepted paper to be published
summary: Electro-Hydrostatic Actuators (EHAs) are widely used in aerospace and industrial systems, where timely detection of sensor anomalies is essential to ensure safe and reliable operation. However, the large volume and high sampling frequency of EHA sensor data pose challenges for accurate and efficient anomaly detection. Conventional statistical and classical machine-learning methods such as Z-score, Interquartile Range (IQR), Median Absolute Deviation (MAD), Isolation Forest, Gaussian Mixture, and k-means often fail to capture the temporal dependencies inherent in EHA signals, resulting in limited detection accuracy and elevated false-alarm rates. Furthermore, systematic evaluations of data-driven anomaly detection approaches for EHA systems remain scarce, particularly under varying operational conditions. This study presents an offline anomaly-detection framework for univariate EHA sensor signals, focusing on temperature and pressure data collected from a controlled test bench. The method employs a reconstruction-based Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) autoencoder, calibrated and evaluated using validation-set reconstruction-error distributions. Performance is assessed across multiple fault-injection scenarios using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, complemented by sensitivity analyses under varying operating conditions. The LSTM autoencoder achieved an average accuracy of 99.0\%, precision up to 100\%, recall between 90.2\% and 99.6\%, and F1-scores from 93.1\% to 99.8\%, demonstrating high detection sensitivity and a very low false-alarm rate across all evaluated sensors. These results highlight the feasibility of data-driven offline anomaly detection for EHAs. Future work will focus on adapting the developed framework for an online (real-time) environment.

AI.tldr: 该文针对EHA温度和压力传感器提出离线LSTM自编码异常检测方法，利用重构误差识别异常；相比传统方法更适合捕捉时序依赖，在多故障注入与不同工况下取得接近99%准确率和极低误报。 / The paper presents an offline LSTM-autoencoder-based anomaly detector for EHA temperature and pressure sensors, using reconstruction error to flag anomalies; it better captures temporal dependencies than traditional methods and achieves near-99% accuracy with very low false alarms across injected faults and operating conditions.
AI.motivation: EHA广泛应用于航空航天和工业系统，传感器异常若不能及时发现会影响安全与可靠性；但EHA数据量大、采样频率高且具有明显时序依赖，传统统计方法和经典机器学习方法难以有效建模，导致检测精度有限、误报率偏高，同时针对不同工况下数据驱动方法的系统性评估仍然不足。 / EHAs are widely used in aerospace and industrial systems, and delayed sensor anomaly detection can compromise safety and reliability; however, EHA data are high-volume, high-frequency, and strongly temporal, making conventional statistical and classical ML methods inadequate, with limited accuracy, higher false alarms, and a lack of systematic evaluation of data-driven methods across operating conditions.
AI.method: 本文提出一个面向EHA温度与压力单变量传感器信号的离线异常检测框架，使用重构式LSTM自编码器建模正常时序模式，并基于验证集重构误差分布进行阈值校准与评估；在多种故障注入场景和不同工况下，用accuracy、precision、recall和F1-score进行测试。 / The paper proposes an offline anomaly-detection framework for univariate EHA temperature and pressure signals, using a reconstruction-based LSTM autoencoder to learn normal temporal patterns and calibrating thresholds via validation-set reconstruction-error distributions; it is evaluated under multiple fault-injection scenarios and operating conditions using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.
AI.result: LSTM自编码器平均准确率达到99.0%，精确率最高100%，召回率为90.2%到99.6%，F1分数为93.1%到99.8%，在所有评估传感器和多种工况下都表现出较高检测灵敏度与极低误报。 / The LSTM autoencoder achieved 99.0% average accuracy, precision up to 100%, recall from 90.2% to 99.6%, and F1-scores from 93.1% to 99.8%, showing high detection sensitivity and very low false-alarm rates across all evaluated sensors and conditions.
AI.conclusion: 基于重构的LSTM自编码器可对EHA单变量传感器信号进行高精度离线异常检测，在不同工况下保持高灵敏度和极低误报率，并具备向在线实时检测扩展的可行性。 / A reconstruction-based LSTM autoencoder enables high-accuracy offline anomaly detection for univariate EHA sensor signals, maintaining high sensitivity and very low false-alarm rates across varying operating conditions, with clear potential for future online deployment.

title: Zero knowledge verification for frontier AI training is possible
summary: Frontier AI governance frameworks increasingly use cumulative training compute as the primary criterion for designating high-impact models, but enforcement rests on self-reporting because no technical verification primitive for training exists. Any future international agreement on frontier AI faces the same problem at higher stakes: coordinated regulation of technologies with significant externalities has historically rested on technical verification, without which agreements are declaratory. Recent governance analyses judge zero-knowledge proofs a promising candidate but currently impractical at frontier scale [26, 4]. We argue the impracticality is paradigm-bound rather than fundamental, and propose a verification architecture for frontier dense pre-training combining a pre-committed training specification, inter-node network observations, and on-the-fly Merkle commitments of intermediate computation, verified through a zero-knowledge Virtual Machine (zkVM) with native BF16/FP32 precompiles. The proof checks the actual floating-point computation the GPU performed rather than a fixed-point approximation, and preserves model-architecture confidentiality through a private training specification. The protocol produces three proof types: a genesis proof at initialisation, in-training step proofs across the run, and ex-ante attestations enforcing policy-relevant claims as running invariants, turning the training record into a governance-enforceable artefact. We estimate a deployable proof of concept within approximately 36 months at single-digit-percent training-side overhead, against a six-to-ten-year cycle for verification-grade custom silicon. Thirteen open research and engineering problems are catalogued as a research agenda for external contribution

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a practical path to cryptographically verify large-scale AI pre-training runs, using zkVMs plus runtime commitments and network observations, so compute-based AI regulation can be enforced without exposing model architecture details.
AI.motivation: Current frontier AI governance often relies on cumulative training compute thresholds, but enforcement depends on self-reporting because there is no practical technical primitive to verify training. Since international governance of high-externality technologies usually depends on technical verification, the lack of such a mechanism makes AI agreements weak or merely declaratory.
AI.method: The method proposes a verification architecture for dense frontier-model pre-training. It includes: a pre-committed but privacy-preserving training specification, inter-node network observations, online Merkle commitments of intermediate computation, and zkVM verification with native BF16/FP32 precompiles. The system generates three proof classes: genesis proofs, in-training step proofs, and ex-ante attestations for policy-relevant invariants.
AI.result: The paper argues that the current impracticality of zero-knowledge verification for frontier training is not fundamental but due to the present paradigm. It estimates that a proof-of-concept could be deployable within about 36 months with single-digit-percent training overhead, and it identifies thirteen open research and engineering challenges.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that verifiable frontier AI training is technically plausible without waiting for custom verification hardware. By combining a committed training specification, network-side observations, Merkle commitments during execution, and zkVM-based verification of native floating-point computation, training runs can be turned into enforceable governance artifacts with manageable overhead.

title: Unpaired RGB-Thermal Gaussian-Splatting Using Visual Geometric Transformers
comment: Accepted at ICRA 2026's Workshop MM-SpatialAI: Multi-Modal Spatial AI for Robust Navigation and Open-World Understanding
summary: Multi-modal novel view synthesis (NVS) combining RGB and thermal imagery enables precise 3D scene reconstruction with visual and thermal information. However, existing methods typically rely on precisely calibrated RGB-thermal image pairs or stereo setups, limiting scalability and practical deployment. To address this, we introduce a framework for unpaired RGB-thermal NVS that leverages VGGT, a 3D feed-forward transformer architecture, to independently estimate camera poses for each modality. The pose sets are then aligned using the Procrustes algorithm with a cross-modal feature matcher, enabling joint registration without paired calibration. Building on this alignment, we further propose a multi-modal 3D Gaussian Splatting approach that learns directly from unpaired RGB and thermal images. Experiments on diverse scenes demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance in thermal view synthesis while maintaining RGB fidelity. Moreover, we show that existing reconstruction approaches can produce modality-specific reconstructions that lack cross-modal consistency. We thus introduce a benchmarking framework to rigorously evaluate both per-modality image synthesis and the multi-modal coherence of reconstructed scenes.

AI.tldr: 提出一种面向非配对RGB-热成像数据的多模态新视角合成框架：独立估计位姿、跨模态对齐、再用多模态3DGS联合重建，并新增跨模态一致性评测基准。 / A framework for unpaired RGB-thermal NVS: estimate poses independently, align them across modalities, train a multi-modal 3DGS model, and benchmark cross-modal consistency.
AI.motivation: 现有RGB-热成像NVS通常依赖严格配准的图像对或双目硬件，这限制了数据采集规模与实际部署，因此需要一种能够从非配对数据学习的跨模态重建方法。 / Existing RGB-thermal NVS methods usually require precisely calibrated paired images or stereo hardware, which limits scalability and deployment, so a method that can learn from unpaired cross-modal data is needed.
AI.method: 方法上，先利用VGGT分别估计RGB与热成像各自的相机位姿，再通过结合跨模态特征匹配的Procrustes算法对两组位姿进行对齐，最后基于对齐结果训练多模态3D Gaussian Splatting进行联合重建与合成。 / The method first uses VGGT to estimate camera poses independently for RGB and thermal images, then aligns the two pose sets with Procrustes analysis guided by cross-modal feature matching, and finally trains a multi-modal 3D Gaussian Splatting model for joint reconstruction and synthesis.
AI.result: 实验表明，该方法在保持RGB重建质量的同时，可实现具有竞争力的热成像视角合成；同时作者发现已有方法往往只能得到模态内质量较好、但跨模态不一致的重建结果。 / Experiments show the method achieves competitive thermal view synthesis while preserving RGB fidelity; the authors also show that existing methods often yield modality-specific reconstructions with poor cross-modal consistency.
AI.conclusion: 该工作证明了无需成对标定的RGB-热成像新视角合成是可行的，并提出了评测跨模态一致性的基准。 / This work shows that unpaired RGB-thermal novel view synthesis is feasible and introduces a benchmark for evaluating cross-modal consistency.

title: ComplexityMT: Benchmarking the Interaction Between Text Complexity and Machine Translation
summary: When a text is translated, does the translation retain the complexity of the original? We introduce ComplexityMT, a new challenge for assessing how text complexity and machine translation interact with and influence each other, using the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) levels as the measure of text complexity. Across six languages, including Arabic, Dutch, English, French, Hindi, and Russian, we evaluate three open-weight models, one closed model, and a commercial machine translation system on two tasks: i) correlation of CEFR with translation difficulty, and ii) shifts in CEFR levels of the source texts. Our experiments show that higher CEFR levels make texts more difficult to translate, and that machine translation shifts the CEFR level of the target text compared to the original source, for most languages. These findings provide new insights for researchers and practitioners working on multilingual pedagogical content generation and machine translation difficulty estimation.

AI.tldr: ComplexityMT is a new multilingual benchmark showing that harder texts are harder to translate and that translation often changes the complexity level of the text.
AI.motivation: The study is motivated by the need to understand whether translations preserve the linguistic complexity of original texts and how text complexity affects machine translation quality and behavior.
AI.method: The paper introduces ComplexityMT, a benchmark for studying interactions between text complexity and machine translation using CEFR levels. It evaluates three open-weight models, one closed model, and one commercial MT system across six languages on two tasks: correlating CEFR with translation difficulty and measuring CEFR shifts between source and target texts.
AI.result: Across Arabic, Dutch, English, French, Hindi, and Russian, the experiments show that texts with higher CEFR levels are generally harder to translate, and translated outputs frequently differ in CEFR level from their source texts.
AI.conclusion: Higher CEFR levels are associated with greater machine translation difficulty, and machine translation often alters the CEFR complexity level of the translated text relative to the source across most tested languages.

title: Agentic Monte Carlo: Simulating Reinforcement Learning for Black-Box Agents
summary: LLM agents operate in two distinct regimes: open-weight agents amenable to reinforcement learning (RL) and black-box agents whose behaviour must be controlled purely at test time. Although black-box agents are often backed by state-of-the-art proprietary LLMs, API-only access precludes parameter-level optimization, rendering most RL methods inapplicable. To address this limitation, we turn to a known equivalence between RL and Bayesian inference. We propose Agentic Monte Carlo (AMC) to directly sample from the optimal policy of a black-box agent rather than training it through RL. The optimal policy is a posterior over trajectories whose prior we define as the fixed black-box LLM agent. We employ Sequential Monte Carlo to sample from this posterior by learning a value function to steer the agent while leaving the underlying black-box model unchanged. We validate AMC on three diverse environments from the AgentGym benchmark, demonstrating significant improvements over prompting baselines and even outperforming Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) as we scale the test-time compute of our method. AMC demonstrates the feasibility of performing principled RL-style optimization of black-box LLM agents. Code is available at https://github.com/layer6ai-labs/Agentic-Monte-Carlo

AI.tldr: AMC optimizes black-box LLM agents at inference time by sampling better action trajectories with Sequential Monte Carlo, improving performance without any model fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM agents fall into open-weight agents that can be optimized with RL and black-box API-only agents that cannot be updated at the parameter level. The paper aims to bring RL-style optimization to black-box agents where standard RL methods are inapplicable.
AI.method: The paper proposes Agentic Monte Carlo (AMC), which leverages the RL-as-Bayesian-inference equivalence. It treats the fixed black-box LLM agent as a trajectory prior and uses Sequential Monte Carlo guided by a learned value function to sample from the posterior over optimal trajectories.
AI.result: On three AgentGym environments, AMC significantly outperforms prompting baselines and can surpass GRPO when given more test-time compute.
AI.conclusion: AMC shows that principled RL-style optimization is feasible for black-box LLM agents by sampling from an optimal-policy posterior at test time, without changing model parameters.

title: Ten Headache Specialists versus Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Literature Summarization: A Critical Evaluation and Comparison
summary: Summarizing the latest medical literature to guide clinical decision-making is essential for evidence-based medicine and high-quality patient care. Yet clinicians face increasing challenges due to limited time with patients and a rapidly growing volume of published articles. Although retrieval-augmented large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in clinical summarization, human evaluations of their effectiveness in synthesizing broader scientific literature and direct comparisons to expert-written syntheses remain scarce. We constructed a RAG-based agentic AI framework using three state-of-the-art LLMs: Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Llama 3.1. A headache specialist created 13 questions, three for prompt optimization and ten for evaluation. Ten headache specialists across the United States and Canada each wrote a summary for one question, yielding four summaries per question (expert, Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Llama). The experts, blinded to authorship, critically evaluated the summaries, excluding the topic for which they wrote a summary, based on correctness, completeness, conciseness, and clinical utility, scoring each from 1 to 10 using standardized rubrics. They also ranked the summaries by preference and indicated whether they believed each summary was written by an expert or an LLM. Our study, comparing LLM- and expert-written literature summaries evaluated by headache specialists, showed that expert-written summaries were preferred, although experts sometimes found it challenging to distinguish between human- and AI-generated summaries. We also identified key expert-valued features beyond standard evaluation metrics that can guide future refinement of both human and AI literature summarization pipelines.

AI.tldr: This paper compares expert-written headache literature summaries against RAG-based summaries from Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Llama 3.1 using blinded specialist evaluation. Experts still preferred human summaries overall, but AI summaries were sometimes convincing enough to be hard to distinguish. The work highlights practical quality criteria that should shape future clinical summarization systems.
AI.motivation: Clinicians need reliable summaries of fast-growing medical literature for evidence-based care, but they face time constraints and an overwhelming number of publications. While RAG-based LLMs appear promising for clinical summarization, there is limited human evaluation of their ability to synthesize broader scientific literature and limited direct comparison against expert-written summaries.
AI.method: The study built a retrieval-augmented generation agentic framework using Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Llama 3.1. A headache specialist created 13 clinical literature questions, with 3 used for prompt optimization and 10 for evaluation. Ten headache specialists each wrote one expert summary, producing four summaries per evaluation question: expert, Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Llama. Blinded specialists then scored summaries on correctness, completeness, conciseness, and clinical utility from 1 to 10, ranked them by preference, and judged whether each was expert- or LLM-written.
AI.result: Across the evaluated headache-literature questions, expert-written summaries were preferred overall. However, specialists were not always able to reliably tell human and AI summaries apart. The evaluation also surfaced expert-valued characteristics beyond standard quantitative metrics, indicating areas where both AI-generated and human summarization processes can be improved.
AI.conclusion: Expert-written literature summaries were generally preferred over summaries generated by RAG-based LLM systems, although specialists sometimes had difficulty distinguishing human-authored from AI-generated summaries. The study also identified qualitative features valued by experts that are not fully captured by standard scoring metrics and should inform future summarization workflows.

title: Robust Scene Transfer for PointGoal Navigation via Privileged Sensor Guided Contrastive Learning
summary:
We propose a sensor-guided adaptive contrastive learning framework for visual representation learning in PointGoal navigation. During training, privileged LiDAR sensing guides the contrastive objective through a geometry-aware similarity metric and adaptive temperature scaling, encouraging visual embeddings to capture navigation-relevant structure rather than scene-specific appearance. The resulting encoder is pretrained independently, frozen, and used as the perceptual backbone for reinforcement learning, decoupling representation learning from policy optimization. We further introduce a cross-stage domain mismatch between representation pretraining and policy learning to suppress environment-specific shortcuts and promote reliance on task-relevant features.
  Extensive experiments in high-fidelity simulation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves policy-level scene transfer across diverse indoor and outdoor environments. At deployment, the agent relies only on monocular RGB observations together with standard task-related inputs such as goal position and proprioceptive signals, without access to LiDAR or other privileged sensors. Our method outperforms large pretrained vision models and standard contrastive baselines under severe appearance and semantic shifts. We also release a multimodal dataset to support future research on privileged-guided visual representation learning for navigation. The code is available at:

AI.tldr: TL;DR：用训练时的LiDAR去“教”RGB编码器学习与导航几何结构相关的表征，再把该编码器冻结后用于RL，可明显提升PointGoal导航在新场景中的泛化，而且测试时不需要LiDAR。 / TL;DR: Use LiDAR during training to teach an RGB encoder geometry-aware, navigation-relevant representations, freeze it for RL, and achieve markedly better PointGoal generalization to unseen scenes without needing LiDAR at test time.
AI.motivation: 动机是现有视觉导航表征容易过度依赖外观和环境特定线索，导致在场景变化、外观变化和语义偏移下泛化较差；作者希望借助训练时可用的特权传感器信息，学习真正服务导航任务的视觉特征。 / The motivation is that existing visual navigation representations often overfit to appearance and environment-specific cues, resulting in poor generalization under scene, appearance, and semantic shifts; the paper aims to use privileged sensors available during training to learn features that are genuinely useful for navigation.
AI.method: 方法上，作者在表征预训练阶段使用特权LiDAR信号来指导对比学习：通过几何感知相似度度量与自适应温度缩放，约束RGB视觉嵌入聚焦于与导航相关的结构信息；随后将预训练得到的编码器冻结，作为强化学习策略的感知骨干，并引入预训练与策略学习之间的跨阶段域不匹配以抑制环境捷径。 / Methodologically, the authors use privileged LiDAR during representation pretraining to guide contrastive learning via a geometry-aware similarity metric and adaptive temperature scaling, then freeze the pretrained encoder as the perceptual backbone for RL, while introducing cross-stage domain mismatch to reduce environment-specific shortcuts.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，该方法在高保真仿真中的多种室内外环境下，显著提升了策略级场景迁移性能；在严重外观与语义分布偏移下优于大型预训练视觉模型和标准对比学习基线。部署时仅需单目RGB、目标位置和本体感觉信号。作者还发布了一个多模态数据集。 / Results show significant improvements in policy-level scene transfer across diverse indoor and outdoor simulated environments, outperforming large pretrained vision models and standard contrastive baselines under severe appearance and semantic shifts. At deployment, only monocular RGB, goal position, and proprioceptive inputs are needed. The authors also release a multimodal dataset.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出的传感器引导自适应对比学习框架，能在不依赖部署时LiDAR的前提下，学习更具导航相关性的视觉表征，并显著提升PointGoal导航中的跨场景泛化与迁移能力。 / The paper concludes that sensor-guided adaptive contrastive learning can learn navigation-relevant visual representations without requiring LiDAR at deployment, substantially improving cross-scene generalization and transfer in PointGoal navigation.

title: Multilingual Coreference Resolution via Cycle-Consistent Machine Translation
summary: Coreference resolution is a core NLP task, having a broad range of downstream applications, e.g.~machine translation, question answering, document summarization, etc. While the task is well-studied in English, comparatively less attention is dedicated to coreference resolution in other languages, especially low-resource ones. To mitigate this gap, we propose a novel coreference resolution pipeline that harnesses machine translation (MT) from English to a target low-resource language, to generate or expand training data. To automatically validate the quality of the translated samples, we back-translate the samples and assess the similarity with the original English samples via cosine similarity in the latent space of a BERT model. The resulting similarity scores are integrated into the loss function to weight training samples according to their MT cycle consistency. Extensive experiments on four low-resource languages show that our pipeline brings significant performance gains in coreference resolution. Moreover, our pipeline enables accurate coreference resolution in languages where no previous corpora were available.

AI.tldr: Use English-to-target MT plus back-translation consistency scoring to create and weight training data, yielding strong coreference resolution gains in low-resource languages.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that coreference resolution is important for many NLP applications, but low-resource languages lack sufficient annotated data and have received much less attention than English.
AI.method: The method translates English coreference data into target low-resource languages, back-translates the generated samples into English, measures source–back-translation similarity using BERT latent-space cosine similarity, and uses these similarity scores to weight training instances in the loss function.
AI.result: Experiments on four low-resource languages show significant performance gains, and the approach also enables accurate coreference resolution for languages without previously available corpora.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a machine-translation-based data augmentation and validation pipeline can substantially improve coreference resolution for low-resource languages, including settings with no existing coreference corpora.

title: Statistically Reliable LLM-Based Ranking Evaluation via Prediction-Powered Inference
summary: With PRECISE, we extended Prediction-Powered Inference to produce bias-corrected estimates of ranking evaluation metrics by combining a small human-labeled set with a large LLM-judged set. PPI is provably unbiased regardless of the LLM judge's error profile. We make it applicable to hierarchical metrics like Precision@K, where annotations are per-document but the metric is per-query, by reducing the output-space computation from O(2^|C|) to O(2^K). On the ESCI benchmark, augmenting 30 human annotations with Claude 3 Sonnet judgments reduces the standard error of Precision@4 estimates from 4.45 to 3.50 (a 21% relative reduction). In a production system, our framework correctly identified the best of three system variants from 100 human labels and 2 hours of domain-expert annotation; A/B testing confirmed this ranking with +407 bps in daily sales.

AI.tldr: PRECISE uses a few human labels plus many LLM judgments to estimate ranking metrics like Precision@K with unbiased correction. It makes PPI practical for hierarchical ranking metrics and improves estimation efficiency, showing lower standard error on ESCI and successful system selection in production.
AI.motivation: Human labeling for ranking evaluation is expensive and slow, while LLM judgments are cheap but biased. The work aims to leverage large-scale LLM judgments without sacrificing statistical validity in estimating ranking metrics.
AI.method: The paper extends Prediction-Powered Inference (PPI) to ranking evaluation. It combines limited human annotations with many LLM judgments, preserves unbiasedness regardless of the LLM judge's error profile, and reduces hierarchical output-space computation for query-level metrics from O(2^|C|) to O(2^K).
AI.result: On ESCI, adding Claude 3 Sonnet judgments to 30 human annotations reduced the standard error of Precision@4 from 4.45 to 3.50, a 21% relative reduction. In production, the method selected the best of three variants using 100 human labels and 2 hours of expert annotation, and A/B testing later confirmed the ranking with a +407 bps daily sales lift.
AI.conclusion: PRECISE enables unbiased, bias-corrected estimation of ranking metrics by combining a small human-labeled set with a large LLM-judged set, and it is practical for hierarchical metrics like Precision@K.

title: Brick-Composer: Using MLLMs for Assembly with Diverse Bricks
summary: We dream of AI agents that can read arbitrary designs and construct real-world objects from reusable building blocks. As a first step toward this vision, we study whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) possess the visual grounding and spatial reasoning capabilities required for brick assembly. We formulate brick assembly as a sequential decision-making problem, where each step involves two subtasks: brick selection, identifying the target brick from candidate components, and brick pose estimation, predicting where and how the selected brick should be placed. To support this study, we introduce BC-Bench (Brick Construction Benchmark), the first benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on assembly with diverse bricks. Experiments show that current state-of-the-art MLLMs remain far from reliable builders, struggling with fine-grained brick selection and failing at precise pose estimation. To bridge this gap, we propose Brick-Composer, a learning framework that equips MLLMs with assembly skills through three complementary signals: Human Design Sparks, which provide affordance-rich construction demonstrations; World Feedback, which grounds predicted actions in visual and physical consequences; and Synthetic Experience, which scales learning beyond existing object designs. Brick-Composer improves brick selection accuracy by over three times, substantially reduces pose estimation errors, and raises strict step-level assembly success from less than 1% to around 15%. After training, a Qwen-3-8B can correctly compose up to 42% of the steps for a complete object, suggesting that MLLMs can acquire assembly capabilities through targeted, physically grounded learning.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether MLLMs can assemble brick-based objects from designs. It introduces BC-Bench to evaluate brick selection and pose prediction, finds current models unreliable, and proposes Brick-Composer to train them with demonstrations, physical/world feedback, and synthetic data. The approach yields large gains, showing MLLMs can learn assembly skills with grounded supervision.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to assess and improve whether multimodal large language models have the visual grounding and spatial reasoning needed for assembling real-world objects from reusable building blocks, as an initial step toward general-purpose AI agents that can read designs and build physical objects.
AI.method: The paper formulates brick assembly as a sequential decision-making problem with two subtasks at each step: brick selection and brick pose estimation. It introduces BC-Bench, a benchmark for diverse brick assembly evaluation, and proposes Brick-Composer, a training framework using three signals: Human Design Sparks, World Feedback, and Synthetic Experience.
AI.result: Experiments show that existing state-of-the-art MLLMs perform poorly on assembly tasks. Brick-Composer improves brick selection accuracy by more than 3x, significantly reduces pose estimation errors, and increases strict step-level assembly success from below 1% to about 15%. A trained Qwen-3-8B can correctly complete up to 42% of the steps for a full object.
AI.conclusion: Current state-of-the-art multimodal large language models are not yet reliable for real-world brick assembly, especially in fine-grained brick selection and precise pose estimation. However, with targeted, physically grounded training, they can acquire meaningful assembly capabilities and substantially improve step-level construction performance.

title: BRepCLIP: Contrastive Multimodal Pretraining on BRep Primitives for CAD Understanding
summary: Learning representations of CAD models is a largely open problem. While 3D representation learning has flourished around point clouds and meshes, the native format of CAD - boundary representations BReps, which encodes exact parametric surfaces, curves, and their topology, has received little attention as a representation learning substrate. We introduce BRepCLIP, the first framework to align BRep geometry with language and image embeddings through contrastive pretraining. We model each CAD object as a sequence of face and edge tokens with separate discrete vocabularies for surface and curve geometry, augmented with spatial and semantic descriptors that capture surface types (e.g., cylindrical, torus, NURBS) and curve primitives (e.g., line, arc, B-spline). A transformer encoder aggregates these tokens into a global BRep embedding, aligned with CLIP's text and image encoders via a joint contrastive objective. BRepCLIP generates more discriminative and semantically grounded embeddings than existing point-based alternatives, improving Top-1 retrieval over OpenShape by 40.4%, 22.0%, and 23.9% on ABC, CADParser, and Automate, respectively, and improving zero-shot classification on FabWave by 15% in Top-1 score. We further demonstrate its utility as a CAD-aware similarity metric for evaluating text and image-conditioned CAD generation, establishing the importance of structure-aware pretraining for multimodal CAD understanding. Project page is available at https://muhammadusama100.github.io/BrepClip2026/

AI.tldr: BRepCLIP is the first framework to align CAD BRep geometry with language and image embeddings. By tokenizing BRep faces and edges and training a transformer with CLIP-style contrastive learning, it outperforms point-based baselines on retrieval and zero-shot classification, showing that structure-aware CAD-native pretraining is valuable.
AI.motivation: Most 3D representation learning focuses on point clouds and meshes, while native CAD BReps contain exact geometric and topological information but remain underexplored. The work aims to exploit this richer CAD-native format for stronger multimodal understanding and retrieval.
AI.method: The paper represents each CAD model as a sequence of BRep face and edge tokens, with separate discrete vocabularies for surfaces and curves plus spatial and semantic descriptors. A transformer encoder aggregates these tokens into a global embedding, which is jointly aligned with CLIP text and image embeddings using a contrastive learning objective.
AI.result: BRepCLIP improves Top-1 retrieval over OpenShape by 40.4% on ABC, 22.0% on CADParser, and 23.9% on Automate, and improves zero-shot Top-1 classification on FabWave by 15%. It also serves as a CAD-aware similarity metric for evaluating text- and image-conditioned CAD generation.
AI.conclusion: BRepCLIP shows that native CAD boundary representations can be effectively aligned with language and image spaces through contrastive pretraining, producing more semantically meaningful and discriminative embeddings than point-based methods for multimodal CAD understanding.

title: Localizing Prompt Ambiguity in Large Language Models with Probe-Targeted Attribution
summary: Prompt ambiguity is a common source of failure in large language models, but is difficult to localize because it is a latent property of the prompt, while existing attribution methods are designed to explain observable outputs such as logits or generated tokens. We introduce PRIG, a gradient attribution method that uses a probe logit to attribute latent ambiguity to token positions. Specifically, PRIG trains a linear probe to distinguish clear prompts from ambiguous prompts and attributes the probe score to earlier token representations in the residual stream. To enable token-level evaluation, we construct synthetic ambiguity datasets across coding, math, and writing by rewriting one task-critical sentence per prompt, and complement them with a human-written gold benchmark. In this setting, PRIG localizes ambiguous spans substantially better than gradient attribution baselines, achieving 0.840 AUROC on the combined synthetic benchmark and 0.891 AUROC on the gold set. It also outperforms GPT-5.4 on sentence-level ambiguity identification and retains useful signal out-of-domain. These results establish PRIG as a practical tool for identifying which parts of a prompt are ambiguous. More broadly, they suggest that latent prompt properties can be localized through intermediate representations, rather than through output-level attribution.

AI.tldr: PRIG trains a linear probe for prompt ambiguity and uses gradient attribution over intermediate token representations to find ambiguous spans. It localizes ambiguity much better than standard baselines and even outperforms GPT-5.4 on sentence-level detection.
AI.motivation: Existing attribution methods explain observable outputs such as logits or generated tokens, but prompt ambiguity is a latent property of the input and therefore hard to localize. The work is motivated by the need for a practical method that can identify which parts of a prompt are ambiguous and causing model failures.
AI.method: The paper proposes PRIG, a gradient-based attribution method for latent prompt ambiguity. It trains a linear probe to classify prompts as clear vs. ambiguous, then attributes the probe score back to earlier token positions in the model residual stream to identify which tokens/spans cause ambiguity. The authors evaluate it on synthetic ambiguity datasets created by rewriting one task-critical sentence per prompt across coding, math, and writing, plus a human-written gold benchmark.
AI.result: PRIG substantially improves ambiguity localization, reaching 0.840 AUROC on the combined synthetic benchmark and 0.891 AUROC on the human gold set. It also beats gradient attribution baselines, outperforms GPT-5.4 on sentence-level ambiguity identification, and retains useful out-of-domain signal.
AI.conclusion: PRIG can effectively localize ambiguous spans in prompts by attributing a probe logit over intermediate residual-stream representations, outperforming gradient baselines and even GPT-5.4 on sentence-level ambiguity identification. More broadly, the paper shows that latent prompt properties can be localized through intermediate representations rather than only output-level attribution.

title: Multimarginal flow matching with optimal transport potentials
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables, and a 27 page appendix. Accepted to the Forty-Third International Conference on Machine Learning
summary: Flow matching (FM) has emerged as a powerful framework for learning dynamic transport maps between two empirical distributions. However, less explored is the setting with intermediate observed marginals that can help constrain the flows between the endpoints. This "multimarginal" regime is central to modeling temporal evolution in dynamical systems in many scientific domains that can sample sequential distributions. We tackle this problem with a novel approach that leverages the connection between FM and dynamic optimal transport (OT), softly steering the flow towards the intermediate marginals through potential terms in the dynamic OT action. By extending the conditional FM learning target to incorporate these potentials, we derive an efficient, simulation-free algorithm for multimarginal FM that offers considerable flexibility in the spatiotemporal dynamics of the learned flows. We demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and training efficiency of OT-potential FM (OTP-FM) on diverse single-cell RNA sequencing, oceanographic, and meteorological datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/Bexorg-Inc/OTP-FM.

AI.tldr: OTP-FM adds optimal-transport-based potential guidance to Flow Matching so it can learn trajectories consistent with intermediate timepoint distributions, and it works well and efficiently on several scientific multimarginal datasets.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that standard Flow Matching mainly models transport between two endpoint distributions, while many real scientific problems provide sequential intermediate marginals that contain important temporal constraints. The paper aims to exploit these additional observations to better model realistic dynamical evolution.
AI.method: The method extends standard Flow Matching by connecting it to dynamic optimal transport and adding potential terms to the OT action that softly enforce consistency with intermediate marginals. It then derives a conditional FM training target with these potentials, resulting in a simulation-free algorithm for multimarginal flow learning.
AI.result: The paper reports state-of-the-art predictive performance and improved training efficiency on diverse datasets, including single-cell RNA sequencing, oceanographic, and meteorological data.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that OT-potential Flow Matching (OTP-FM) is an efficient and flexible multimarginal flow-learning method that incorporates intermediate observed marginals via optimal-transport-inspired potential terms, achieving state-of-the-art performance and strong training efficiency across scientific datasets.

title: Insurance of Agentic AI
summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are transforming the risk landscape by extending beyond information generation to autonomous planning, tool invocation, decision execution, and persistent modification of digital and physical environments. These capabilities introduce novel exposures that do not fit neatly within traditional insurance categories such as cyber, professional liability, product liability, or directors and officers coverage. This paper examines the emerging insurance market for agentic AI and develops a framework for understanding its underwriting, pricing, reinsurance, and product-design implications. We characterize agentic AI as a continuum of autonomy and delegated authority, emphasizing the distinction between informational outputs and systems capable of independently generating insured events through external actions. We analyze major risk pathways, including hallucinations, prompt-injection attacks, autonomous decision errors, model drift, dependency failures, and cyber-physical harms, and evaluate how existing insurance products are adapting to address these exposures. The paper further proposes an actuarial framework based on exposure assessment, scenario analysis, dependency mapping, and accumulation-risk management, drawing parallels to the evolution of cyber insurance. Finally, we present a coordinated insurance architecture that integrates cyber, technology errors and omissions, product liability, performance-warranty, and affirmative AI-liability coverages through explicit allocation mechanisms and dedicated AI aggregates. The analysis suggests that the future of agentic-AI insurance lies not in a single monoline product but in a layered ecosystem of complementary coverages supported by improved governance, transparency, telemetry, and regulatory clarity.

AI.tldr: Agentic AI changes insurance because it can act autonomously and cause real-world losses, not just produce bad information. The paper argues insurers should underwrite it through layered, coordinated coverages and new actuarial tools rather than trying to force it into one standalone policy.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that agentic AI systems no longer only generate information; they can autonomously plan, invoke tools, execute decisions, and modify digital or physical environments. These capabilities create new insured events and liabilities that do not fit neatly within existing insurance products such as cyber, professional liability, product liability, or D&O coverage.
AI.method: The paper uses a conceptual and market-oriented analytical method. It defines agentic AI as a continuum of autonomy and delegated authority, examines major risk pathways, compares these exposures against existing insurance categories, and proposes an actuarial and insurance-architecture framework based on exposure assessment, scenario analysis, dependency mapping, and accumulation-risk management.
AI.result: The paper identifies core risk pathways for agentic AI, including hallucinations, prompt injection, autonomous decision errors, model drift, dependency failures, and cyber-physical harms. It finds that existing insurance products are adapting but remain incomplete, and it proposes both an actuarial framework and a coordinated coverage architecture integrating cyber, tech E&O, product liability, performance warranty, and affirmative AI liability.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that agentic AI creates insurance exposures that cannot be adequately handled by any single traditional insurance line. The most viable future approach is a layered insurance ecosystem that combines multiple coverages, explicit risk allocation, dedicated AI aggregates, and stronger governance, telemetry, transparency, and regulatory clarity.

title: Almieyar-Oryx-BloomBench: A Bilingual Multimodal Benchmark for Cognitively Informed Evaluation of Vision-Language Models
summary: Despite the rapid progress of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the field lacks benchmarks that rigorously diagnose their true reasoning abilities and chart meaningful progress toward human-like multimodal intelligence. Most existing evaluations focus on piecemeal or disconnected tasks, obscuring critical cognitive weaknesses and providing little insight for targeted improvement. To address this gap, we introduce BloomBench, part of the Almieyar benchmarking series, the first cognitively human-grounded, bilingual (English-Arabic) multimodal benchmark for VLMs. Grounded in Bloom's Taxonomy, BloomBench systematically evaluates six levels of cognition (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create) through carefully designed image-question-answer tasks. Built with a semi-automated pipeline and validated through a stratified hybrid quality assurance protocol, it ensures scalability, cultural inclusivity, and linguistic fidelity. Leveraging this framework, we conduct a comprehensive study of state-of-the-art VLMs to diagnose their cognitive profiles. Our analysis reveals a sharp cognitive asymmetry: while state-of-the-art models achieve strong performance ceilings in semantic understanding, they struggle substantially with factual recall and creative synthesis. This demonstrates that current general multimodal proficiency masks deeper limitations in specific cognitive layers. Furthermore, our study highlights a critical performance gap between Arabic and English, exposing limitations in current cross-lingual multimodal reasoning. These findings establish a foundation for developing more cognitively aligned and inclusive VLMs. The benchmark framework and dataset is available at: https://github.com/qcri/Almieyar-Oryx-BloomBench.

AI.tldr: BloomBench is the first Bloom’s-Taxonomy-based bilingual multimodal benchmark for VLMs. It reveals that modern VLMs look generally capable, but their reasoning is uneven: they understand well, yet struggle with recall, creativity, and Arabic-English transfer.
AI.motivation: Existing VLM benchmarks assess fragmented or disconnected abilities and do not rigorously diagnose true reasoning or cognitive depth. The authors aim to provide a human-grounded, cognitively structured, scalable, and inclusive benchmark that better measures progress toward human-like multimodal intelligence.
AI.method: The paper introduces BloomBench, a bilingual (English-Arabic) multimodal benchmark grounded in Bloom’s Taxonomy. It evaluates six cognitive levels through image-question-answer tasks, built via a semi-automated data pipeline and validated with a stratified hybrid quality-assurance protocol. The benchmark is then used to evaluate state-of-the-art VLMs and profile their cognitive strengths and weaknesses.
AI.result: The evaluation finds a clear cognitive asymmetry in state-of-the-art VLMs: high performance in semantic understanding, but substantial weakness in remembering factual details and generating creative outputs. It also uncovers a notable Arabic-English performance gap, indicating limitations in cross-lingual multimodal reasoning.
AI.conclusion: BloomBench shows that current VLMs are not uniformly strong reasoners: they perform relatively well on semantic understanding but remain weak in factual recall, creative synthesis, and cross-lingual multimodal reasoning, especially in Arabic compared with English.

title: MASF: A Multi-Model Adaptive Selection Framework for Abstractive Text summarization
summary: Automatic text summarization has become increasingly important due to the rapid growth of digital textual information. This paper presents a Multi-Model Adaptive Summarization Framework designed to improve the robustness and quality of abstractive text summarization. Relying on a single model often leads to inconsistent summarization quality across articles with varying structures and topics. To address this limitation, the proposed framework integrates multiple fine-tuned transformer-based summarization models and introduces an adaptive selection mechanism. In this framework, each model independently generates a candidate summary for the same input article. The generated summaries are then evaluated using automatic evaluation metrics that capture both lexical similarity and semantic relevance. Based on these scores, the framework selects the highest-quality summary as the final output. The models are fine-tuned and evaluated on the widely used CNN/DailyMail news summarization dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves the highest BERTScore among all compared methods with a score of 88.63%. It also outperforms several LLMs such as GPT3-D2, Falcon-7b, and Mpt-7b, highlighting its effectiveness and robustness. These findings highlight the effectiveness of leveraging multiple transformer-based models within an adaptive selection strategy to improve the quality and robustness of automatic text summarization systems.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文用多个微调后的Transformer摘要模型同时生成候选摘要，再通过自动评分机制挑选最佳结果，从而比单模型和若干LLM获得更稳健、更高质量的新闻摘要。English: This paper uses multiple fine-tuned transformer summarizers to generate candidate summaries and an automatic scoring mechanism to pick the best one, yielding more robust and higher-quality news summaries than single-model baselines and several LLMs.
AI.motivation: 中文：单一摘要模型在面对不同结构和主题的文章时，摘要质量往往不稳定，难以持续输出高质量结果。因此作者希望通过整合多个模型并引入自适应选择机制来提升系统稳健性与整体摘要效果。English: The motivation is that relying on a single summarization model often produces inconsistent quality across articles with different structures and topics. The authors therefore aim to improve robustness and overall summary quality by integrating multiple models with an adaptive selection strategy.
AI.method: 中文：论文提出一个多模型自适应摘要框架。多个经过微调的Transformer摘要模型分别对同一输入生成候选摘要；随后使用同时衡量词汇相似度与语义相关性的自动评价指标对候选摘要打分，并选择得分最高的摘要作为最终输出。模型在CNN/DailyMail数据集上进行微调与评估。English: The paper proposes a multi-model adaptive summarization framework. Multiple fine-tuned transformer-based summarization models independently generate candidate summaries for the same input, then automatic metrics capturing both lexical similarity and semantic relevance score the candidates, and the best-scoring summary is selected as the final output. The models are fine-tuned and evaluated on CNN/DailyMail.
AI.result: 中文：实验表明，该方法在对比方法中取得最高的BERTScore，达到88.63%，并优于GPT3-D2、Falcon-7b和Mpt-7b等若干LLM，说明该框架在效果和稳健性方面具有优势。English: Experiments show that the method achieves the best BERTScore among compared approaches, reaching 88.63%, and outperforms several LLMs such as GPT3-D2, Falcon-7b, and Mpt-7b, indicating strong effectiveness and robustness.
AI.conclusion: 中文：该论文认为，多模型与自适应选择相结合能够显著提升抽象式文本摘要的质量与鲁棒性，尤其在不同文章结构与主题下比单一模型更稳定。English: The paper concludes that combining multiple summarization models with an adaptive selection mechanism significantly improves the quality and robustness of abstractive summarization, especially across articles with varying structures and topics.

title: A prism hierarchy of learning regimes in large linear autoencoders
summary: Theoretical studies of machine learning models commonly consider different limiting regimes in which the learning dynamics of gradient descent becomes theoretically tractable. It is, however, desirable to have a systematically obtained picture of all qualitatively different extreme learning regimes for a particular type of models. In this paper we propose such a picture for large weight-tied linear autoencoders characterized by input and latent dimensions, initialization magnitude, and training set size. This model is nonlinear in the weights and its gradient flow does not have a general theoretical solution. We show that at the level of the formal loss-expansion hierarchy, its extreme regimes are naturally associated with faces of a triangular prism. In particular, there are five basic extreme regimes associated with the 2-faces of the prism: (1) large-data, (2) small-data, (3) mean-field, (4) narrow-latent, and (5) free. For regimes (1,2,3,4), we derive explicit expressions for both train and population limiting loss evolutions under gradient flow, obtaining very good agreement with experimental results.

AI.tldr: The paper builds a unified map of how large weight-tied linear autoencoders learn in different asymptotic limits. It identifies five core extreme regimes and analytically solves loss dynamics in four of them, with theory closely matching experiments.
AI.motivation: Prior theory often analyzes isolated limiting regimes where gradient descent becomes tractable, but lacks a systematic map of all qualitatively distinct extreme regimes for a given model class. The paper aims to build such a unified picture for a nonlinear-in-weights yet analytically structured autoencoder model.
AI.method: The authors study large weight-tied linear autoencoders through a formal loss-expansion hierarchy under gradient flow, parameterized by input dimension, latent dimension, initialization scale, and dataset size. They classify asymptotic learning regimes via the faces of a triangular prism and derive limiting loss dynamics analytically in the large-data, small-data, mean-field, and narrow-latent regimes.
AI.result: The main result is a geometric classification of extreme regimes into five basic cases: large-data, small-data, mean-field, narrow-latent, and free. The paper provides explicit train and population loss trajectories for the first four regimes under gradient flow, and these predictions show very good empirical agreement.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the extreme learning behaviors of large weight-tied linear autoencoders can be organized systematically by a triangular-prism geometry over model/data scalings, with five fundamental regimes. For four of these regimes, the authors obtain explicit gradient-flow predictions for train and population loss that match experiments well.

title: Output Type Before Quality: A Standards-Derived XAI Admissibility Rubric for Autonomous-Driving Safety
summary:
Safety standards for ML-based autonomous driving specify the kind of evidence an assurance case must contain (directed cause-and-effect chains, quantified interventional effects, named root-cause variables), yet the XAI literature is organised by output type and technique family (saliency maps, feature attribution, counterfactuals, causal graphs, language traces). SHAP, the most-recommended ADS XAI method, returns a ranked feature list that no implementation effort can convert into a directed chain (Fig.1). We name this mismatch the evidence-type gap.
  From AMLAS, ISO 26262, ISO21448, ISO/PAS 8800 we derive 19 testable evidentiary criteria across 7 lifecycle stages with representative clause-cited derivations and score six XAI method classes structurally.
  Causal XAI emerges as structurally required to satisfy the derived criteria at three stages: hazard identification (+62% rubric gap), incident investigation (+50%), and data management (+50%); the verdict set is stable across thresholds T in (0%, 50%]$ and survives a worst-case single-cell flip down to T = 25%. At the remaining four stages, correlational or language-based methods are comparable or sufficient. The rubric identifies structural admissibility (necessary but not sufficient for compliance): an admissible method's specific output content may still be wrong, and validating that fidelity (the edges a fitted SCM produces, the cause a trace names) is the open assurance challenge. A single-VLA proof of concept on 1,996 real-world driving clips (79,840 rows, ten splits) is consistent with each method's observed output type matching its rubric prediction. XAI method selection for ADS safety assurance should be driven by lifecycle-stage evidence demand, not by method popularity.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that popular XAI methods often fail to produce the exact evidence required by autonomous-driving safety standards. By deriving a standards-based rubric, it finds causal XAI is structurally required for some lifecycle stages, while simpler correlational or language-based methods suffice for others.
AI.motivation: Current ADS safety standards require evidence such as directed causal chains, quantified interventional effects, and named root-cause variables, but XAI research is organized by output format and technique family. This creates an evidence-type gap, where popular methods like SHAP cannot directly provide the evidence forms demanded by assurance cases.
AI.method: The paper derives 19 testable evidentiary criteria across 7 lifecycle stages from AMLAS, ISO 26262, ISO 21448, and ISO/PAS 8800, then structurally scores six classes of XAI methods against these clause-derived criteria, performs threshold and worst-case sensitivity analyses, and checks consistency with a single-VLA proof of concept on 1,996 driving clips.
AI.result: Causal XAI shows the largest structural advantage at hazard identification (+62% rubric gap), incident investigation (+50%), and data management (+50%), with results stable for thresholds in (0%, 50%] and robust to a worst-case single-cell flip down to T=25%. At the other four lifecycle stages, correlational or language-based XAI can be comparable or sufficient. The proof of concept matches observed output types to rubric predictions.
AI.conclusion: For ADS safety assurance, XAI methods should be selected by lifecycle-stage evidence requirements rather than popularity; causal XAI is structurally necessary at several key stages, while admissibility alone does not guarantee faithful or correct explanations.

title: Noise-Aware Visual Representation Learning for Medical Visual Question Answering
summary: Medical visual question answering (Med-VQA) has strong potential for clinical decision support by enabling AI models to interpret medical images and answer clinically relevant queries. Recent approaches typically connect off-the-shelf vision encoders with large language models (LLMs) through lightweight mapping networks to reduce computational cost. However, these methods often overlook the importance of handling noise and small irrelevant changes in visual representations. To address these challenges, we propose a noise-aware Med-VQA framework that incorporates a denoising autoencoder before visual embeddings are mapped into the input space of an LLM. The denoising autoencoder is pretrained to reconstruct clean visual embeddings from corrupted inputs, encouraging the model to learn robust visual representations that are less sensitive to noise. The resulting embeddings are then projected into the language model embedding space using a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), forming visual prefix tokens that provide image information to the LLM. To enable efficient adaptation without full retraining, we employ parameter-efficient fine-tuning using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The proposed method is evaluated on the SLAKE and PathVQA benchmarks. Experimental results show improved robustness to noisy input embeddings while maintaining competitive clean performance across multiple evaluation criteria. These findings suggest that learning more robust visual representations can enhance Med-VQA performance and robustness.

AI.tldr: 通过在视觉嵌入进入LLM前加入去噪自编码器，并结合MLP映射与LoRA微调，论文提升了Med-VQA对噪声的鲁棒性，且不明显牺牲正常输入下的性能。 / By adding a denoising autoencoder before feeding visual embeddings into an LLM, together with MLP projection and LoRA tuning, the paper improves Med-VQA robustness to noise without clearly sacrificing performance on clean inputs.
AI.motivation: 现有Med-VQA方法通常将现成视觉编码器与LLM通过轻量映射连接，虽然计算高效，但往往忽视视觉表示中的噪声与微小无关变化，导致鲁棒性不足。 / Existing Med-VQA approaches efficiently connect off-the-shelf vision encoders to LLMs with lightweight mapping, but often ignore noise and small irrelevant perturbations in visual representations, limiting robustness.
AI.method: 提出一种noise-aware Med-VQA框架：先用预训练去噪自编码器从受扰动的视觉嵌入中恢复干净表示，再用MLP将其投影到LLM嵌入空间形成visual prefix tokens，并通过LoRA进行参数高效微调。 / The paper proposes a noise-aware Med-VQA framework: a pretrained denoising autoencoder first reconstructs clean visual embeddings from corrupted ones, then an MLP projects them into the LLM embedding space as visual prefix tokens, with LoRA used for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
AI.result: 在SLAKE和PathVQA基准上，方法在多项评估指标下表现出更强的噪声鲁棒性，同时保持了具有竞争力的clean performance。 / On SLAKE and PathVQA, the method achieves improved robustness to noisy input embeddings across multiple metrics while preserving competitive clean performance.
AI.conclusion: 在Med-VQA中，在视觉嵌入映射到LLM之前加入去噪自编码器，可以提升对噪声输入的鲁棒性，并在干净数据上保持有竞争力的性能。 / In Med-VQA, inserting a denoising autoencoder before mapping visual embeddings into an LLM improves robustness to noisy inputs while maintaining competitive performance on clean data.

title: CHASE: Adversarial Red-Blue Teaming for Improving LLM Safety using Reinforcement Learning
summary: Despite advances in safety alignment, prompt-rewriting attacks such as persona modulation, fictional framing and persuasion-based reformulation, can bypass safety filters even on frontier models. Existing defenses either rely on non-scalable human curation or white-box optimisation that overfits to specific model internals, leaving aligned models brittle against the very class of adaptive black-box adversaries they will face in deployment. To address this gap, we introduce CHASE (Co-evolutionary Hardening through Adversarial Safety-Escalation), a closed-loop red-blue teaming framework in which a black-box attacker and a safety-aligned defender co-evolve. The attacker is trained via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) under a multiplicative reward that jointly enforces bypass effectiveness and intent fidelity, while the defender is hardened on the harvested adversarial rewrites through a two-stage GRPO + rejection-sampled SFT pipeline balanced with benign data. Evaluated on BeaverTails and JailbreakBench against five held-out attack families (PAIR, TAP, AutoDAN, PAP, Translation), CHASE cuts mean StrongREJECT score by 43.2\% with 0\% false-refusal on benign prompts. Beyond the headline result, CHASE shows that template-free RL exploration recovers latent attack primitives that transfer across mechanistically distinct attack families, suggesting a path toward LLM safety hardening that generalises beyond the narrow distributions achieved thus far in adversarial training.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文用黑盒攻防共进化训练安全模型，让模型不只记住固定模板，而是学会抵抗可迁移的提示改写攻击。 English: This paper hardens safety-aligned LLMs through black-box co-evolution, helping them resist transferable prompt-rewriting jailbreaks rather than memorizing fixed attack templates.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有防御要么依赖难以扩展的人工整理，要么依赖对白盒模型内部的优化，容易过拟合，难以应对真实部署中自适应、黑盒、提示重写型攻击者。 English: Existing defenses are either unscalable due to human curation or overly tied to white-box model internals, making them brittle against adaptive black-box prompt-rewriting adversaries encountered in deployment.
AI.method: 中文：论文提出 CHASE，一个闭环红蓝对抗框架。攻击者使用 GRPO 在乘性奖励下训练，奖励同时约束绕过成功率与意图保真度；防御者则用收集到的对抗改写样本，经由两阶段 GRPO + 拒绝采样监督微调，并与良性数据混合进行加固。 English: The paper introduces CHASE, a closed-loop red-blue co-evolution framework. The attacker is trained with GRPO under a multiplicative reward that jointly optimizes bypass success and intent fidelity; the defender is hardened on harvested adversarial rewrites using a two-stage GRPO plus rejection-sampled SFT pipeline balanced with benign data.
AI.result: 中文：在 BeaverTails 和 JailbreakBench 上，面对五种留出的攻击家族（PAIR、TAP、AutoDAN、PAP、Translation），CHASE 将平均 StrongREJECT 分数降低 43.2%，并在良性提示上保持 0% 误拒。 English: On BeaverTails and JailbreakBench against five held-out attack families (PAIR, TAP, AutoDAN, PAP, Translation), CHASE reduces the mean StrongREJECT score by 43.2% while maintaining 0% false refusal on benign prompts.
AI.conclusion: 中文：CHASE 通过黑盒红蓝对抗共进化，显著提升了对提示重写型越狱攻击的鲁棒性，并且在保持良性请求零误拒的同时，获得了跨攻击家族的泛化防御能力。 English: CHASE significantly improves robustness against prompt-rewriting jailbreaks via black-box co-evolutionary red-blue teaming, while preserving zero false refusals on benign prompts and achieving cross-family defensive generalization.

title: PJ-RoPE: A Fourier-Jet-Affine Position Space for Relative Attention
comment: 26 pages, 6 figures, 10 tables. Code available at https://github.com/ybzhang-nxu/Poincare_Rope
summary:
We unify RoPE's Fourier phase, Jordan-RoPE's finite jets, and ALiBi's affine recency into a single learnable relative-position space, and study which regions of this space are selected by different tasks. PJ-RoPE is a Fourier-Jet-Affine formulation for relative attention, with an optional Poincare-type reading as the affine completion of a homogeneous Fourier-jet positional representation. Algebraically, the same primitives form a finite constant-coefficient difference module: simple roots of the lag-shift operator give Fourier/RoPE characters, repeated nonzero roots give Jordan/Fourier jets, and the repeated unit root gives ALiBi-like affine recency.
  The framework separates scalar PJ-bias kernels from exact PJ-rotary feature transforms, introduces adaptive sector diagnostics, and uses LC/rapidity coordinates to stabilize high-order jets. Controlled probes verify sector containment and selection; small language runs expose an affine/recency boundary; music-token streams provide the clearest case where LC/affine variants remain strong while carrying measurable high-order corrections; and LC diagnostics show a scale-stability gain coupled to phase-resolution loss.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文提出 PJ-RoPE，把 RoPE 的旋转相位、Jordan-RoPE 的高阶 jet 结构和 ALiBi 的线性近期偏置统一成一个可学习的相对位置表示空间，并用代数工具解释三者其实是同一类差分结构的不同根形态。实验表明，不同任务会偏好这个空间中的不同“sector”；LC/affine 形式在音乐等序列上尤其有效，而且更稳定，但会牺牲一部分相位分辨率。 / The paper introduces PJ-RoPE, a learnable relative-position framework that unifies RoPE’s rotational phase, Jordan-RoPE’s higher-order jet structure, and ALiBi’s linear recency bias, showing that all three arise from different root patterns of the same difference-operator view. Experiments suggest that different tasks prefer different sectors of this space; LC/affine variants are especially effective and stable on music-like sequences, though they sacrifice some phase resolution.
AI.motivation: 现有相对位置编码方法如 RoPE、Jordan-RoPE 和 ALiBi 各自捕捉了相位、有限阶导数结构和近期性偏置，但彼此分散，缺少统一的代数与几何视角，也不清楚不同任务实际偏好哪类位置结构。 / Existing relative-position schemes such as RoPE, Jordan-RoPE, and ALiBi capture phase, finite-jet structure, and recency bias separately, but lack a unified algebraic/geometric view, and it is unclear which positional structures different tasks actually prefer.
AI.method: 作者提出 Fourier-Jet-Affine 的 PJ-RoPE 框架，把标量位置偏置核与精确 PJ-rotary 特征变换分离，并用有限常系数差分模来统一解释 Fourier 字符、Jordan jets 与 affine recency；同时引入自适应 sector 诊断以及 LC/rapidity 坐标来稳定高阶 jets。 / The paper proposes PJ-RoPE, a Fourier-Jet-Affine framework that separates scalar positional bias kernels from exact PJ-rotary feature transforms, and gives a unified finite constant-coefficient difference-module interpretation of Fourier characters, Jordan jets, and affine recency; it also introduces adaptive sector diagnostics and LC/rapidity coordinates to stabilize higher-order jets.
AI.result: 受控探针验证了 sector containment 与 selection；小规模语言建模显示 affine/recency 存在清晰边界；音乐 token 流最明显地表明 LC/affine 变体在保留可测高阶修正时仍然强劲；LC 诊断显示更好的尺度稳定性，但伴随相位分辨率下降。 / Controlled probes verify sector containment and selection; small language-model runs expose an affine/recency boundary; music-token streams most clearly show that LC/affine variants stay strong while carrying measurable higher-order corrections; LC diagnostics indicate improved scale stability at the cost of phase resolution.
AI.conclusion: PJ-RoPE 将 RoPE、Jordan-RoPE 和 ALiBi 统一到一个可学习的相对位置空间中，不同任务会选择该空间中的不同区域；其中 LC/affine 变体在某些序列任务上表现稳定，并揭示了尺度稳定性与相位分辨率之间的权衡。 / PJ-RoPE unifies RoPE, Jordan-RoPE, and ALiBi into a learnable relative-position space, and different tasks select different regions of that space; LC/affine variants remain competitive on some sequence tasks and reveal a tradeoff between scale stability and phase resolution.

title: PSEBench: A Controllable and Verifiable Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Patient Safety Event Triage
summary: Patient safety event triage, determining whether a clinical event is reportable under jurisdiction-specific policy, is a high-stakes task typically performed manually by patient safety experts. Although LLMs may support this workflow, reliable evaluation is limited by the lack of benchmarks to capture evidence-grounded policy reasoning, proactive information seeking for incomplete reports, and principled abstention in irreducibly ambiguous cases. We address this gap with a policy-grounded construction methodology centered on the clause card, a structured representation that factorizes regulatory text into auditable decision specifications. Combining clause cards with anchor-driven instantiation and closed-loop verification, our scalable pipeline produces narratives with by-construction ground truth and naturally supports generating missing information and uncertain variants. We instantiate this method on Minnesota's 29 Reportable Adverse Health Events, producing PSEBench, a 5,074-case benchmark with an agentic evaluation environment. Evaluation on 15 representative LLMs reveals consistent capability trends, demonstrates the benchmark's utility, and identifies actionable gaps toward reliable LLM-based patient safety event triage.

AI.tldr: 作者提出一种基于法规条款结构化表示（clause card）的基准构建方法，创建了患者安全事件分诊基准 PSEBench，并发现当前LLM虽呈现稳定能力分层，但在证据驱动推理、缺失信息处理和不确定性弃答方面仍存在明显短板。 / The paper presents a clause-card-based method for building policy-grounded benchmarks, creates PSEBench for patient safety event triage, and shows that current LLMs still have clear weaknesses in evidence-based reasoning, missing-information handling, and abstention under uncertainty.
AI.motivation: 论文动机在于：患者安全事件分诊高度重要但通常依赖人工专家，而现有对LLM辅助该任务的评测不足，缺乏能够系统检验模型是否基于政策证据推理、是否会主动索取缺失信息、以及在无法判定时是否能够合理弃答的基准。 / The motivation is that patient safety event triage is a high-stakes, expert-driven task, yet reliable evaluation of LLMs for this setting is lacking. Existing benchmarks do not adequately test whether models can reason from policy evidence, seek missing information proactively, and abstain appropriately in genuinely ambiguous cases.
AI.method: 方法上，作者提出一种以 clause card 为核心的政策落地构建流程：先将法规条款分解为可审计的决策规范，再结合 anchor-driven instantiation 与 closed-loop verification，生成具有构造性真值标注的事件叙事；该流程还自然支持生成缺失信息版本和不确定版本，并最终在明尼苏达州29类可报告不良健康事件上实例化为包含5,074个案例、带有 agentic evaluation environment 的 PSEBench。 / Methodologically, the authors introduce a policy-grounded benchmark construction pipeline centered on clause cards, which factorize regulatory text into auditable decision specifications. They combine this with anchor-driven instantiation and closed-loop verification to generate narratives with by-construction ground truth, including variants with missing information and irreducible uncertainty, and instantiate the framework on Minnesota’s 29 reportable adverse health events to build the 5,074-case PSEBench with an agentic evaluation environment.
AI.result: 结果上，论文成功发布了 PSEBench，共5,074个案例，覆盖明尼苏达州29类可报告事件，并在15个代表性LLM上完成评测。实验显示该基准可以稳定地区分模型能力、验证评测环境的实用性，并明确指出当前模型在可靠落地到患者安全分诊中的若干可改进方向。 / As a result, the paper delivers PSEBench, a 5,074-case benchmark covering Minnesota’s 29 reportable event categories, and evaluates 15 representative LLMs on it. The results show consistent capability trends across models, demonstrate the benchmark’s practical utility, and identify actionable gaps that must be addressed for reliable deployment in patient safety event triage.
AI.conclusion: 该论文构建了一个面向患者安全事件分诊的高质量基准 PSEBench，并通过对15个代表性大语言模型的评测表明：该基准能够稳定揭示模型能力差异，同时暴露出在证据约束推理、主动补全信息和不确定情形下审慎弃答方面的关键不足。 / The paper concludes that PSEBench is an effective benchmark for patient safety event triage, capable of exposing consistent performance trends across 15 representative LLMs while highlighting important shortcomings in evidence-grounded reasoning, proactive information seeking, and principled abstention under ambiguity.

title: Dual Feature Decoupling for Fine-Grained OOD Detection
summary: Out-of-distribution detection (OOD) is an indispensable technique when applying machine learning models to real-world scenarios. Most existing OOD detection methods have been developed under the idealized assumption of large inter-class distributional differences, while largely overlooking fine-grained tasks characterized by subtle variations, such as medical image classification and vehicle recognition. The high visual similarity among fine-grained subcategories, together with the interference of background factors, makes OOD detection extremely challenging. To tackle this problem, we propose a novel Dual Feature Decoupling Network (DFDNet), which addresses fine-grained OOD detection from the perspective of feature disentanglement. The proposed DFDNet comprises two key components: a spatial-frequency decoupling module and a reconstruction-guided decoupling module. The spatial-frequency decoupling module is designed to preserve content features that are discriminative for classification while suppressing task-irrelevant style information.
