On the other hand, the reconstruction-guided decoupling module introduces a novel pixel-level adversarial reconstruction task to further remove low-level, non-discriminative information and enhance category-specific high-level semantic representations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance improvements on multiple datasets.

AI.tldr: DFDNet improves fine-grained OOD detection by disentangling useful class content from background/style and low-level noise using spatial-frequency decoupling plus reconstruction-guided adversarial learning.
AI.motivation: Existing OOD detection methods usually assume large inter-class differences and therefore perform poorly on fine-grained tasks, where classes are visually similar and background/style factors interfere strongly. The paper is motivated by the need for OOD detection methods tailored to subtle fine-grained distinctions.
AI.method: The paper proposes Dual Feature Decoupling Network (DFDNet) with two modules: (1) a spatial-frequency decoupling module to retain class-discriminative content while suppressing irrelevant style/background information, and (2) a reconstruction-guided decoupling module with a pixel-level adversarial reconstruction task to remove low-level non-discriminative cues and strengthen high-level category semantics.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple datasets show that DFDNet delivers competitive performance improvements for fine-grained OOD detection.
AI.conclusion: DFDNet effectively improves fine-grained OOD detection by disentangling discriminative content features from task-irrelevant style and low-level information, achieving competitive gains across multiple datasets.

title: Multilingual Detection of Alzheimer's Disease from Speech: A Cross-Linguistic Transfer Learning Approach
summary: The development of multilingual Alzheimer's Disease Dementia (AD) detection models presents significant challenges due to the resource-intensive and time-consuming nature of language-specific model training. We propose a novel solution using cross-language training to detect AD in languages beyond those used for model training. This study investigates multilingual deep learning models for detecting AD across different languages and cognitive impairment levels. Using datasets in English, Chinese, Arabic, and Hindi, we developed transformer-based models for binary AD classification. Our approach achieved F1 scores of 82\% across all languages, demonstrating strong cross-linguistic generalization. The rapid inference time (0.5 seconds) supports potential real-time screening applications, while consistent performance across languages indicates feasibility for global deployment.

AI.tldr: A multilingual transformer model trained across four languages detects AD with 82% F1 and 0.5s inference, showing cross-language generalization for scalable real-time screening.
AI.motivation: Language-specific AD detection models are costly and slow to build, so the work aims to reduce this burden by enabling detection in languages not seen during training through multilingual cross-language modeling.
AI.method: The paper trains multilingual transformer-based deep learning models for binary AD classification using speech/language datasets in English, Chinese, Arabic, and Hindi, evaluating cross-language training across different cognitive impairment levels.
AI.result: The approach achieves an F1 score of 82% across all languages and an inference time of 0.5 seconds, with consistent performance indicating feasibility for real-time and global deployment.
AI.conclusion: Cross-language transformer-based training can detect Alzheimer's Disease Dementia across English, Chinese, Arabic, and Hindi with strong generalization, supporting scalable multilingual screening.

title: Mamba-Assisted Non-Markovian Closure for Reduced-Order Modeling
comment: Code will be released upon acceptance
summary: Reduced-order modeling of high-dimensional dynamical systems is often hindered by the non-Markovian closure term that represents the effect of unresolved variables on the resolved dynamics. Inspired by the Mori--Zwanzig formalism, in which the closure takes the form of a memory functional of the resolved trajectory, we recast closure modeling as a sequence modeling problem and propose the Mamba-Assisted Closure (MAC) framework: a Mamba-based sequence model, trained to predict the closure from the resolved trajectory, is coupled with the reduced-order governing equations through a numerical integrator to advance the resolved variables in time. A key feature of the framework is its exploitation of the dual representation of state-space models -- the model is trained in a sequence-to-sequence fashion via the convolutional form, and deployed for step-by-step autoregressive rollout via the recurrent form, yielding both efficient long-trajectory training and constant per-step inference cost. On the viscous Burgers' equation and the chaotic two-scale Lorenz '96 system, the MAC model substantially outperforms the Markovian reduced-order model, the GRU-based sequence model, and the Wilks method in predictive accuracy and long-time rollout stability.

AI.tldr: The paper uses Mamba to learn memory-dependent closure terms for reduced-order dynamics, enabling efficient training and stable step-by-step simulation, and shows better accuracy and long-horizon stability than standard ROM and GRU/Wilks baselines.
AI.motivation: Reduced-order models for high-dimensional dynamical systems are limited by difficult non-Markovian closure terms that capture unresolved-variable effects. Inspired by the Mori-Zwanzig memory formulation, the authors seek a data-driven model that can represent history-dependent closure efficiently and stably.
AI.method: The paper formulates closure modeling as a sequence modeling task and proposes Mamba-Assisted Closure (MAC), where a Mamba-based state-space sequence model predicts the closure term from the resolved trajectory and is coupled with reduced-order equations through a numerical integrator. Training uses the convolutional form for efficient sequence-to-sequence learning, while inference uses the recurrent form for autoregressive rollout with constant per-step cost.
AI.result: On the viscous Burgers' equation and chaotic two-scale Lorenz '96 system, MAC substantially outperforms a Markovian reduced-order model, a GRU-based sequence model, and the Wilks method in predictive accuracy and long-time rollout stability.
AI.conclusion: MAC effectively models non-Markovian closure in reduced-order dynamical systems and delivers more accurate and stable long-term predictions than existing reduced-order and sequence-model baselines.

title: Step-by-Step Optimization-like Reasoning in LLMs over Expanding Search Spaces
summary: Verifiable reward training has improved mathematical and coding reasoning, but these domains capture only part of step-by-step decision making. Many real-world tasks require finding a high-value feasible plan among many valid alternatives. We introduce OPT*, a scalable family of optimization-style tasks for training and evaluating LLM step-by-step optimization-like reasoning along a complexity axis: each task provides a feasibility checker and evaluator, while a complexity parameter expands the search space without requiring new human labels. This motivates studying these tasks in two regimes: (i) solver-guided online policy optimization, which uses a solver as a value oracle for partial states and applies rank-based reward shaping to reinforce better next steps, and (ii) search-based offline RL when such solvers are unavailable. Theoretically, we relate success in large search spaces to the information a reasoner extracts per unit of search budget. Empirically, we ablate the ingredients that make search efficient on OPT* and show that training on OPT* improves step-by-step optimization-like reasoning.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes OPT*, a scalable benchmark for training and evaluating LLM optimization-style reasoning, combines solver-guided online RL and search-based offline RL, and shows both theoretically and empirically that OPT* training improves efficient step-by-step planning in large search spaces.
AI.motivation: Existing verifiable reward training has mainly advanced math and coding reasoning, but many real-world problems require selecting a high-value feasible plan from many valid alternatives. The authors aim to create scalable tasks that better capture optimization-like, step-by-step decision making without requiring new human labels as complexity grows.
AI.method: The paper introduces OPT*, a family of optimization-style tasks with feasibility checkers, evaluators, and a tunable complexity parameter. It studies two regimes: solver-guided online policy optimization using a solver as a value oracle with rank-based reward shaping, and search-based offline reinforcement learning when solvers are unavailable. It also analyzes the relation between success and information extracted per unit search budget, and performs ablations on search efficiency.
AI.result: Empirically, the study shows which ingredients make search efficient on OPT* and demonstrates that training on OPT* improves step-by-step optimization-like reasoning. Theoretically, it connects performance in large search spaces to the amount of useful information extracted under a fixed search budget.
AI.conclusion: OPT* provides a scalable benchmark and training framework for optimization-like step-by-step reasoning in LLMs, and training on OPT* improves such reasoning efficiency and performance.

title: UltraVR: A Diagnostic Ultra-Resolution Image-VQA Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Reasoning
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) excel on visual question answering and multimodal reasoning benchmarks. Yet their capability on ultra-resolution images - where critical evidence is tiny, subtle, spatially distant, or distributed - remains unclear. Existing evaluations largely report final-answer accuracy, offering limited insight into whether models acquire and integrate the necessary visual evidence. We introduce UltraVR, a diagnostic benchmark for evidence-grounded visual reasoning over ultra-resolution images. UltraVR spans four high-value scenarios: CCTV surveillance, remote sensing (RS), whole-slide image (WSI) pathology, and industrial anomaly detection (AD). These domains pose complementary challenges: fine-grained object grounding in crowded CCTV scenes, long-range spatial comparison in RS, multi-scale evidence navigation in WSI, and subtle irregularity detection in repetitive industrial layouts. Beyond standard QA triples, each instance includes a structured ground-truth chain of thought with step-level questions, intermediate answers, and reasoning labels. These labels decompose reasoning into evidence grounding, local perception, quantification, evidence integration, and decision inference, enabling process-level diagnosis over black-box scoring. Using UltraVR, we evaluate frontier VLMs and show that current models remain far from reliable on ultra-resolution reasoning. Importantly, the structured annotations allow us to localize failures across the visual-to-decision pipeline: errors concentrate in evidence grounding and local perception, while downstream inference often recovers when intermediate visual facts are supplied. These findings demonstrate UltraVR as a diagnostic testbed for measuring not only whether VLMs answer correctly, but where their ultra-resolution reasoning process breaks.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文提出UltraVR，一个面向超高分辨率图像的VLM诊断基准，不只评估答对没有，还评估推理在哪一步出错；结果发现当前模型最薄弱的是先找到并看清关键证据。English: This paper presents UltraVR, a diagnostic benchmark for VLM reasoning on ultra-resolution images that evaluates not just correctness but where the reasoning process breaks; current models are weakest at finding and perceiving the right evidence.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有VLM在VQA和多模态推理上表现强，但其处理超高分辨率图像时，是否真正获取并整合关键视觉证据并不清楚；传统只看最终答案准确率，无法定位推理链路中的失败点。English: Although VLMs perform well on VQA and multimodal reasoning, it is unclear whether they truly acquire and integrate critical evidence in ultra-resolution images. Existing evaluations focus on final-answer accuracy and cannot localize where reasoning fails.
AI.method: 中文：论文提出UltraVR诊断基准，覆盖CCTV、遥感、WSI病理和工业异常检测四类场景；除标准QA外，还为每个样本标注结构化真实推理链，包括分步问题、中间答案与推理标签，用于过程级诊断。English: The paper introduces UltraVR, a diagnostic benchmark spanning CCTV, remote sensing, WSI pathology, and industrial anomaly detection. Beyond standard QA, each sample includes a structured ground-truth reasoning chain with step questions, intermediate answers, and reasoning labels for process-level diagnosis.
AI.result: 中文：基于UltraVR的评测表明，当前模型在超高分辨率推理上距离可靠性仍有明显差距；错误主要集中在证据定位和局部视觉感知阶段，而非纯粹的后续推理阶段。English: Evaluations on UltraVR indicate that current models remain far from reliable for ultra-resolution reasoning; failures are concentrated in evidence grounding and local visual perception rather than purely downstream inference.
AI.conclusion: 中文：UltraVR证明当前前沿VLM在超高分辨率图像上的证据驱动推理仍不可靠，主要瓶颈在证据定位与局部感知；若提供中间视觉事实，下游推理常可恢复。English: UltraVR shows that state-of-the-art VLMs are still unreliable at evidence-grounded reasoning on ultra-resolution images, with major failures in evidence grounding and local perception; downstream inference often improves when intermediate visual facts are provided.

title: ArcANE: Do Role-Playing Language Agents Stay in Character at the Right Time?
summary: Role-playing language agents (RPLAs) should play characters whose values and behavior evolve as the story progresses, not maintain a fixed persona. Existing benchmarks measure factual recall at a given chapter, not whether responses align with the character's psychological trajectory, especially in scenarios the source text never explores. We introduce ArcANE (Arc-Aware Narrative Evaluation), an automatically constructed benchmark spanning 17 novels and 80 principal characters. A Character Arc segments the narrative into phases along a psychological axis, and each probe poses the same scenario across phases, spanning both situations within the source text and situations beyond it. Across six models and six context modes, conditioning on the Character Arc tops every other context strategy on every model, and the gap is largest on scenarios outside the source text where retrieval has nothing to find. We further fine-tune open-weight models on the same data to obtain ArcANE-8B/32B, which widen the Arc advantage even more on scenarios outside the source text.

AI.tldr: ArcANE is a benchmark for testing whether language agents follow a character’s evolving psychological arc rather than a fixed persona. Arc-aware context beats standard retrieval/context methods on every tested model, especially for unseen scenarios, and fine-tuning makes the advantage even stronger.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks mainly test chapter-level factual recall or static persona consistency, but they fail to assess whether a language agent tracks a character’s evolving psychology over time, especially in novel situations not explicitly covered by the source narrative.
AI.method: The paper introduces ArcANE, an automatically constructed benchmark built from 17 novels and 80 main characters. It models each character’s development as a Character Arc divided into psychological phases, then evaluates the same scenario across phases, including both in-text and extrapolative scenarios. The authors compare six models under six context-conditioning modes and additionally fine-tune open-weight models to create ArcANE-8B/32B.
AI.result: Across all six models and all six context modes, Character Arc conditioning outperforms every alternative context strategy. The improvement is largest on scenarios outside the source text. Fine-tuned open-weight models, ArcANE-8B and ArcANE-32B, further enlarge the performance gap in these out-of-text settings.
AI.conclusion: Character-arc-aware conditioning is consistently the most effective strategy for role-playing language agents, especially for out-of-text scenarios where simple retrieval is insufficient; fine-tuning on arc-aware data further strengthens this advantage.

title: Evidence-Guided Neural Architecture Selection under Uncertainty for Subject-Specific Blood Glucose Forecasting
summary: Reliable neural architecture selection is an open challenge in time-series forecasting under limited, noisy, and heterogeneous data, where standard heuristic architecture design and validation approaches fail to ensure accurate and reliable prediction and generalization. We propose EVIDENT (EVidence-based IDEntification of Neural archiTectures), a framework for architecture selection that integrates Bayesian training, evidence-based ranking, and task-specific validation under uncertainty. The framework explores the candidate architecture pool and identifies the lowest-capacity model that satisfies a prescribed validation criterion. We demonstrate this method using temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) for individualized blood glucose forecasting in type 1 diabetes patients. The results show that EVIDENT systematically rejects both under- and over-parameterized TCN architectures on population-level diabetes data, while identifying models that generalize reliably to unseen patients. When multiple architectures are competitive, the framework further supports plausibility-weighted ensemble predictions that enhance predictive performance. Compared with a random-search baseline, EVIDENT identified smaller architectures with more consistent forecasting performance on unseen patients. These findings establish EVIDENT as a strategy to neural architecture discovery, enabling reliable model selection for high-consequence forecasting in data-limited and heterogeneous settings.

AI.tldr: EVIDENT is a Bayesian evidence-based framework for selecting neural network architectures under uncertainty. In blood glucose forecasting, it finds smaller TCN models that generalize more reliably than random search and can improve accuracy further with weighted ensembles.
AI.motivation: Standard heuristic architecture design and validation are unreliable for time-series forecasting when data are limited, noisy, and heterogeneous. The work is motivated by the need for a principled architecture selection strategy that improves prediction reliability and generalization in high-consequence applications.
AI.method: The paper proposes EVIDENT, a framework that combines Bayesian training, evidence-based architecture ranking, and task-specific validation under uncertainty. It searches a candidate architecture pool and selects the lowest-capacity model that still satisfies a predefined validation criterion. The approach is demonstrated with temporal convolutional networks for individualized blood glucose forecasting.
AI.result: On population-level type 1 diabetes blood glucose forecasting, EVIDENT systematically rejected under- and over-parameterized TCNs, selected smaller architectures than random search, and achieved more consistent performance on unseen patients. When multiple architectures were similarly competitive, plausibility-weighted ensembles further improved forecasting accuracy.
AI.conclusion: EVIDENT provides a reliable strategy for neural architecture selection in data-limited, noisy, and heterogeneous time-series forecasting. It can identify compact architectures that generalize better to unseen patients and can also support plausibility-weighted ensembles when several models are competitive.

title: Severity-Aware Curriculum Learning with Multi-Model Response Selection for Medical Text Generation
summary: Telehealth systems have become increasingly important for delivering accessible and timely medical information. Existing large language models often struggle to provide consistent and contextually appropriate medical responses across varying levels of case severity. This limitation highlights the need for models that can effectively adapt to the progressive complexity in medical queries. To address this challenge, we introduce a severity-aware multi-model framework that integrates curriculum training strategy with relevance-based response selection. The proposed framework employs a three-stage curriculum learning strategy, where each model is trained sequentially on mild, moderate, and critical cases to progressively acquire domain knowledge. The approach utilizes five large language models, each independently trained under the same curriculum scheme. During inference, all models generate candidate responses, and the most appropriate response is selected as the final output. The framework is trained and evaluated on the MAQA dataset, which provides annotated medical question-answer pairs. Experimental results evaluated using BERTScore demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to both baseline and fine-tuned models, attaining 86.71% in the baseline setting and 90.30% after fine-tuning. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining curriculum learning with multi-model response selection in improving response quality and relevance in medical text generation.

AI.tldr: Train five LLMs with a mild-to-critical medical curriculum, then select the best answer among their outputs; this improves telehealth QA performance on MAQA.
AI.motivation: Existing LLMs in telehealth often fail to provide stable, context-appropriate responses across different levels of medical case severity. The work is motivated by the need for a system that adapts better to progressively more complex medical queries.
AI.method: The paper proposes a three-stage curriculum learning pipeline in which each of five large language models is trained sequentially on mild, moderate, and critical medical cases. At inference time, all five models generate candidate answers, and a relevance-based selector chooses the final response.
AI.result: On the MAQA dataset, the framework achieves better BERTScore performance than baseline and fine-tuned comparison models, reaching 86.71% in the baseline setting and 90.30% after fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: A severity-aware multi-model telehealth QA framework that combines curriculum learning with relevance-based response selection improves the quality and contextual appropriateness of medical text generation, outperforming baseline and fine-tuned single-model approaches.

title: BMCR: Adaptive Backbone Module Composition via Reinforcement Learning for Remote Sensing Object Detection
summary: In remote sensing object detection, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) excel at capturing local details while Vision Transformers (ViTs) are better at global context modeling. However, existing detectors typically rely on a single fixed backbone or a manually designed hybrid architecture, and thus fail to adaptively exploit these complementary strengths across inputs of diverse complexity. To address this limitation, we propose Backbone Module Composition via Reinforcement Learning (BMCR). BMCR dynamically assembles input-adaptive inference paths from reusable modules decomposed from off-the-shelf CNN and ViT backbones. To enable such cross-family composition, we first construct an extensible module toolbox. Specifically, we decompose representative CNN and ViT backbones into reusable functional modules and encapsulate each module with explicit structural, semantic, and computational metadata for compatibility-aware assembly. To bridge the gap between grid-based CNN features and token-based ViT representations, we design a lightweight Optimal Transport (OT) based transition interface that ensures distribution-aware alignment while respecting spatial consistency. The backbone composition process is then formulated as a sequential decision problem, in which a policy network progressively selects task-relevant modules according to intermediate multi-scale observations. To stabilize the joint optimization of reusable modules and the routing policy, we further develop an Adaptive Module Cooperative Optimization (AMCO) strategy that coordinates module updating, routing exploration, and reward assignment during training. On DOTA-v1.0, DOTA-v1.5 and DIOR-R, BMCR achieves 79.31\%, 73.41\% and 71.86\% mAP, respectively, surpassing strong static and dynamic baselines by up to 2.5 points while maintaining competitive efficiency.

AI.tldr: BMCR uses reinforcement learning to dynamically assemble CNN/ViT backbone modules for each image, improving remote sensing detection performance over fixed or manually hybrid backbones.
AI.motivation: Static single-backbone or manually designed hybrid detectors cannot adaptively leverage CNN local-detail modeling and ViT global-context modeling for inputs with different complexities in remote sensing object detection.
AI.method: The paper proposes BMCR, which decomposes off-the-shelf CNN and ViT backbones into reusable modules with metadata, connects cross-family features through a lightweight OT-based transition interface, formulates backbone composition as a sequential decision process optimized by reinforcement learning, and stabilizes training with AMCO.
AI.result: On DOTA-v1.0, DOTA-v1.5, and DIOR-R, BMCR achieves 79.31%, 73.41%, and 71.86% mAP, outperforming strong static and dynamic baselines by up to 2.5 points with competitive efficiency.
AI.conclusion: BMCR shows that dynamically composing CNN and ViT backbone modules per input improves remote sensing object detection accuracy while keeping efficiency competitive.

title: AURA: Intent-Directed Probing for Implicit-Need Surfacing in Situated LLM Agents
comment: Submitted to EMNLP 2026. Code, simulator, and benchmark: https://github.com/innovation64/AURA
summary: A situated query like "where is Lin Wei?" often encodes more than its literal content: the user may also want to know whether Lin Wei is free, in a good mood, or worth interrupting now. Standard tool-use agents answer the literal question and stop. AURA inserts an inference step between scene perception and tool use that produces an IntentFrame: a structured estimate of the implicit need with a scalar gap score that controls per-query probe budget and tool selection. On a 100-query four-scene implicit-intent benchmark, AURA improves implicit-need coverage over ReAct-style probing (Delta = +0.07, p < 10^-6); three of four scenes are individually significant, the gain reproduces on a second backbone, and a prompt ablation attributes the lift to gap calibration rather than answer memorisation. On factual lookup the controller trades raw accuracy for 82% fewer probes and zero forbidden-tool violations on a privacy-sensitive slice; scope conditions are detailed in Limitations. Code, simulator, and benchmark are released at https://github.com/innovation64/AURA.

AI.tldr: AURA adds an implicit-intent reasoning layer before tool use, improving hidden-need coverage and probe efficiency while reducing privacy violations, though with some factual accuracy tradeoff.
AI.motivation: Situated queries often carry implicit intents beyond their literal wording, such as checking availability, mood, or interruptibility. Standard tool-using agents typically answer only the explicit question, missing these latent needs and sometimes probing inefficiently or unsafely.
AI.method: The paper proposes AURA, an agent framework that adds an IntentFrame between scene perception and tool use. The IntentFrame estimates the user's implicit need and computes a scalar gap score, which then controls both the probe budget per query and the choice of tools.
AI.result: On a 100-query, four-scene benchmark for implicit intent, AURA improves implicit-need coverage over a ReAct-style probing baseline by +0.07 with p < 10^-6; three of the four scenes show individual significance. The result reproduces on a second backbone, and an ablation suggests the gain comes from gap calibration rather than memorization. On factual lookup, AURA uses 82% fewer probes and has zero forbidden-tool violations on a privacy-sensitive subset, at the cost of some raw accuracy.
AI.conclusion: AURA shows that inserting an explicit implicit-intent inference step before tool use can improve coverage of users' hidden needs while reducing unnecessary probing and preventing privacy-sensitive tool misuse, though it trades off some raw factual lookup accuracy and has stated scope limitations.

title: SHALA-LLM: Smartly Handling Ambiguous Labels in Aligning LLMs
summary: Many human-centered tasks, including natural language inference (NLI) and emotion recognition (ER), have multiple plausible interpretations, leading to label ambiguity and challenging disagreements across human annotators. As LLMs are increasingly deployed in real-world settings, faithfully modeling such ambiguity is essential to identify contested inputs, preserve variability in ambiguous cases, and capture the full distribution of human judgments. Yet, existing LLM alignment approaches have predominantly assumed a single correct label, excluding annotator disagreement during optimization. Instead of treating this ambiguity as noise, we show how to treat it as information that improves model behavior through a new algorithm called SMARTLY HANDLING AMBIGUOUS LABELS IN ALIGNING LLMS (SHALA-LLM). This reinforcement learning framework provides a new way for LLMs to learn directly from annotator distributions while dynamically prioritizing highly ambiguous samples during optimization. Experiments on ambiguity-sensitive NLI and ER benchmarks, including ChaosNLI, GoEmotions, and MSP-Podcast, demonstrate that SHALA-LLM improves agreement with annotator label distributions, e.g. on ChaosNLI, it reduces Jensen-Shannon Distance by up to 62.1%. At the same time, SHALA-LLM improves F1 by up to 16.7%, showing that modeling annotator disagreement can also strengthen classification performance.

AI.tldr: SHALA-LLM trains LLMs from annotator label distributions and emphasizes ambiguous examples, leading to better modeling of human disagreement and better classification results.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that many human-centered tasks such as natural language inference and emotion recognition are inherently ambiguous, and real human annotators often disagree. Existing alignment methods usually assume one correct label and ignore this disagreement, which prevents models from faithfully capturing uncertainty and the full range of human judgments.
AI.method: The method is SHALA-LLM, a reinforcement learning framework for aligning LLMs with annotator label distributions instead of a single gold label. It dynamically prioritizes highly ambiguous samples during optimization so the model can better learn from disagreement patterns.
AI.result: On ChaosNLI, GoEmotions, and MSP-Podcast, SHALA-LLM improves agreement with annotator distributions and also boosts task performance. For example, on ChaosNLI it reduces Jensen-Shannon Distance by up to 62.1%, and it improves F1 by up to 16.7%.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that explicitly modeling annotator disagreement during LLM alignment is beneficial rather than treating it as noise. Their SHALA-LLM framework improves both distributional agreement with human annotations and standard classification performance on ambiguity-sensitive tasks.

title: EpiEvolve: Self-Evolving Agents for Streaming Pandemic Forecasting under Regime Shifts
summary: Epidemic LLM forecasters are usually trained and evaluated as static supervised models, whereas operational pandemic forecasting is a streaming process in which labels arrive after predictions and disease regimes shift over time. We study this mismatch in weekly COVID-19 hospitalization trend forecasting across five variant regimes. We introduce EpiEvolve, a self-evolving agent that wraps an LLM forecaster trained on the warm-start period and keeps its weights fixed during streaming. EpiEvolve adapts by storing forecast outcomes in a hierarchical episodic memory, reflecting on delayed labels, retrieving cases relevant to the current regime, and distilling recurring errors into strategic rules. The resulting context lets the forecaster reuse its own past predictions and outcomes in later weeks while following a chronological protocol that prevents future leakage. On the streaming dataset, EpiEvolve reaches $0.629$ average accuracy, compared with $0.561$ for the static backbone and $0.325$ for the external CDC ensemble, and reduces recovery lag after regime shifts from $5$ to $2$ weeks. Ablations show that reflection, strategic memory, and regime-aware retrieval each contribute to the gains.

AI.tldr: EpiEvolve keeps the LLM weights fixed but lets the system learn during streaming through memory, reflection, and regime-aware retrieval. This significantly improves COVID-19 trend forecasting accuracy and adaptation speed across shifting variant regimes.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by a mismatch between how epidemic LLM forecasters are commonly developed and how real pandemic forecasting actually operates. Existing models are usually trained and evaluated as static supervised systems, but operational forecasting is a streaming setting with delayed labels and shifting disease regimes, so static evaluation can overstate practical usefulness.
AI.method: The paper proposes EpiEvolve, a self-evolving agent built around a warm-started LLM forecaster whose weights remain fixed during streaming deployment. It stores past forecasts and realized outcomes in hierarchical episodic memory, reflects when delayed labels arrive, retrieves historically relevant cases for the current disease regime, and distills repeated mistakes into reusable strategic rules that are injected back as context for future predictions.
AI.result: On weekly COVID-19 hospitalization trend forecasting across five variant regimes, EpiEvolve achieves 0.629 average accuracy versus 0.561 for the static backbone and 0.325 for the CDC ensemble. It also cuts recovery lag after regime shifts from 5 weeks to 2 weeks. Ablation studies indicate that reflection, strategic memory, and regime-aware retrieval each contribute to the improvement.
AI.conclusion: EpiEvolve shows that a fixed-weight LLM forecaster can substantially improve streaming epidemic forecasting by using chronological self-evolution mechanisms: episodic memory, delayed-label reflection, regime-aware retrieval, and strategic rule distillation. This design better handles regime shifts and avoids future leakage.

title: HDST-GNN: Heterogeneous Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Multi-Object Tracking in UAV Aerial Imagery
summary: Multi-object tracking (MOT) from UAV imagery presents unique challenges: altitude varies across sequences, objects are small and densely packed, and frequent occlusion causes identity switches. Existing graph-based trackers assume fixed spatial context and treat all objects uniformly, ignoring the heterogeneous lifecycle states of detections, active tracklets, and lost targets. We propose HDST-GNN, a Heterogeneous Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network with three novel contributions. First, Altitude-Adaptive Edge Construction estimates a camera-altitude proxy from mean object area and adjusts the graph connectivity radius accordingly. Second, Heterogeneous Node Representation models detections (Type-D), confirmed tracklets (Type-T), and lost tracklets (Type-L) as distinct node types with dedicated projections and typed edge relations. Third, Occlusion-Gated Temporal Aggregation gates each node's attention contribution by its occlusion confidence, preventing occluded nodes from corrupting neighbour embeddings. HDST-GNN is trained end-to-end with a differentiable Sinkhorn head using joint cross-entropy and triplet loss. On VisDrone2019-MOT with oracle detections, HDST-GNN achieves 94.51% MOTA and 97.24% IDF1, outperforming SORT by +5.0 MOTA points and reducing identity switches by 81%. With real YOLOv8n detections, HDST-GNN reduces identity switches by 49% vs. SORT. Ablation studies confirm the independent contribution of each component.

AI.tldr: HDST-GNN is a UAV tracking model that adapts graph connections to altitude, treats detections/tracklets/lost targets differently, and downweights occluded nodes; this substantially improves MOTA/IDF1 and sharply reduces identity switches on VisDrone2019-MOT.
AI.motivation: UAV-based MOT is difficult because viewpoint altitude changes across sequences, targets are small and crowded, and occlusions frequently cause identity switches. Existing graph-based trackers use fixed spatial assumptions and uniform object modeling, which fail to capture these UAV-specific dynamics and different target lifecycle states.
AI.method: The paper proposes HDST-GNN, a heterogeneous dynamic spatiotemporal graph neural network for UAV MOT. It introduces altitude-adaptive edge construction based on a camera-altitude proxy from mean object area, heterogeneous node representations for detections, confirmed tracklets, and lost tracklets with typed relations, and occlusion-gated temporal aggregation. The model is trained end-to-end with a differentiable Sinkhorn matching head using joint cross-entropy and triplet loss.
AI.result: On VisDrone2019-MOT with oracle detections, HDST-GNN reaches 94.51% MOTA and 97.24% IDF1, outperforming SORT by 5.0 MOTA points and reducing identity switches by 81%. With YOLOv8n detections, it reduces identity switches by 49% compared with SORT. Ablation studies show each proposed component contributes independently.
AI.conclusion: HDST-GNN effectively improves UAV multi-object tracking by adapting graph construction to altitude, modeling heterogeneous target states explicitly, and suppressing occlusion noise during temporal aggregation, leading to better association accuracy and far fewer identity switches than baseline trackers.

title: InfoShield: Privacy-Preserving Speech Representations for Mental Health Screening via Information-Theoretic Optimization
summary: Speech-based mental health screening offers scalable depression detection, yet clinical deployment faces a significant barrier: users' privacy concerns about demographic information exposure. Current techniques struggle to resolve this conflict. Adversarial training often fails against unseen threats, whereas Differential Privacy tends to compromise diagnostic performance by injecting noise across all features. This paper presents InfoShield, which minimizes mutual information between speech representations and sensitive attributes while preserving depression classification accuracy. We identify that standard MINE estimators struggle with sequential speech due to temporal-static misalignment, and introduce TimeAwareMINE with cross-modal attention to align acoustic frames with attribute embeddings. Experiments on the Androids Corpus show InfoShield reduces gender inference from 92.6\% to 55.5\% and age inference from 55.7\% to 30.3\% with limited utility loss (6\% F1 reduction), achieving F1=0.784 compared to prior SOTA's 0.723.

AI.tldr: InfoShield protects speaker demographics in depression-detection speech models by explicitly removing mutual information from representations, using a new TimeAwareMINE alignment module; it sharply lowers gender/age leakage while keeping strong diagnostic accuracy.
AI.motivation: Speech-based depression screening is scalable, but practical deployment is limited by privacy concerns because speech encodes sensitive demographic traits such as gender and age. Existing solutions either generalize poorly to unseen attacks, as in adversarial training, or degrade task performance by adding broad noise, as in Differential Privacy.
AI.method: The paper proposes InfoShield, a privacy-preserving speech-based depression detection framework that minimizes mutual information between learned speech representations and sensitive demographic attributes. To address the failure of standard MINE on sequential speech, it introduces TimeAwareMINE, which uses cross-modal attention to align temporal acoustic frames with static attribute embeddings.
AI.result: On the Androids Corpus, InfoShield reduces gender inference accuracy from 92.6% to 55.5% and age inference from 55.7% to 30.3%, while incurring only a 6% F1 reduction for depression classification. It still achieves F1=0.784, exceeding the prior state of the art at 0.723.
AI.conclusion: InfoShield can substantially reduce leakage of demographic information from speech representations while largely preserving depression screening performance, outperforming prior methods in the privacy-utility tradeoff.

title: Pattern Selectivity is Not Task-Causal Structure: A Cross-Architecture Mechanistic Study of Composed-Task Circuits in 1B-Class Language Models
summary:
We test whether a single screen-and-ablate recipe -- identify attention-head circuits by task-pattern selectivity, then verify by causal ablation against a matched-random null -- produces consistent mechanistic claims across model families. The recipe ports across pipelines; the specific circuit it identifies does not. Across four composed tasks (indirect-object identification, greater-than, successor sequences, variable binding) and three 1B-class language models from distinct training pipelines (Pythia 1B / Pile / dense; OLMo 1B / DCLM / dense; OLMoE 1B-7B / DCLM / mixture-of-experts), we run a unified protocol with the matched-random null sampled across ten seeds per cell. The resulting 12 (task, model) cells contain no two that share the same primary causal screen at comparable effect size: the same task, with the same behavioral capability, is implemented through different attention-pattern types across models.
  We introduce a five-category screen-outcome taxonomy -- primary cause, secondary cause, correlate, interferer, null -- with quantitative thresholds, and show that all five outcomes appear in the panel. We propose a falsifiable hypothesis: the MoE model in our panel builds composed-task circuits on top of a foundational previous-token positional substrate (the prev-token-circuit ablation is the strongest causal screen on 3 of 4 tasks for OLMoE 1B-7B), with the IOI exception consistent with IOI being a final-position name-copying task whose structure directly probes a different pattern. The hypothesis comes with explicit predictions for other MoE language models.
  We frame the methodology honestly: the spectral participation-ratio signal from the companion methodology paper is a general indicator of specialized computation; what makes a finding task-specific is the task-pattern screen plus a per-model causal verification.

AI.tldr: 同一种机制分析流程能跨模型使用，但不会找到同一种电路：不同模型会用不同注意力机制完成同一任务。作者还给出了一套更严格的因果结果分类，并提出MoE模型可能依赖“前一token”位置底座来实现组合任务。 / The same interpretability recipe works across models, but it does not recover the same circuit: different models use different attention mechanisms for the same task. The paper also provides a stricter causal taxonomy and proposes that the MoE model may rely on a previous-token positional substrate for composed tasks.
AI.motivation: 作者想检验一种常见机制解释流程是否能在不同模型家族上得出稳定、一致的机制性结论，从而区分“方法可迁移”与“机制本身可复现”这两个问题。 / The motivation is to test whether a standard mechanistic interpretability workflow yields stable, consistent claims across model families, separating portability of the method from reproducibility of the underlying mechanism.
AI.method: 作者在四个组合任务（IOI、greater-than、successor sequences、variable binding）和三个不同训练管线的1B级模型（Pythia 1B、OLMo 1B、OLMoE 1B-7B）上，采用统一协议：先用任务模式选择性筛查注意力头电路，再通过与匹配随机空基线比较的因果消融进行验证；每个(task, model)单元的空基线采样10个随机种子。 / The authors use a unified protocol over four composed tasks and three 1B-class models from distinct training pipelines: first screen attention-head circuits by task-pattern selectivity, then verify them via causal ablation against a matched-random null, with ten null seeds per (task, model) cell.
AI.result: 12个(task, model)单元中，没有任意两个在可比效应量下共享相同的主要因果筛查结果；作者提出了五类筛查结果分类法（primary cause、secondary cause、correlate、interferer、null），并观察到五类结果全部出现。另一个主要发现是：OLMoE在4个任务中的3个上最强的因果筛查都指向前一token位置性底座，支持其在此底座上构建组合任务电路的假设，IOI是例外。 / Across the 12 (task, model) cells, no two share the same primary causal screen at comparable effect size. The paper introduces a five-way taxonomy of screen outcomes and observes all five categories in the panel. It also finds that in OLMoE, the strongest causal screen for 3 of 4 tasks is the previous-token positional substrate, supporting a hypothesis that composed-task circuits are built on top of this substrate, with IOI as an exception.
AI.conclusion: 单一的“筛选+消融”机制分析流程可以跨模型家族复用，但它识别出的具体因果电路并不具有跨模型一致性；相同任务能力在不同1B级语言模型中由不同类型的注意力模式实现。 / A single screen-and-ablate mechanistic recipe transfers across model families, but the specific causal circuit it identifies does not; the same task capability is implemented by different attention-pattern types across 1B-class language models.

title: SciVisAgentSkills: Design and Evaluation of Agent Skills for Scientific Data Analysis and Visualization
summary: Recent advances in agentic visualization have enabled the translation of natural language into executable scientific visualization (SciVis) workflows. While general-purpose coding agents show strong capabilities, they often lack the tool-specific expertise required for SciVis tasks. In this work, we present SciVisAgentSkills, a collection of reusable agent skills that augment coding agents for scientific data analysis and visualization by encoding environment assumptions, tool usage patterns, and domain heuristics across scientific tools such as ParaView, napari, VMD, and TTK. We evaluate these skills on Codex and Claude Code using SciVisAgentBench, a benchmark of 108 expert-designed multi-step tasks. Results show that agent skills improve mean task scores across the evaluated suites, with token-efficiency benefits that depend on the agent harness and tool setting. These findings highlight the importance of structured procedural knowledge for enabling reliable, long-horizon SciVis workflows, while also showing that skills should be studied alongside the execution harness that loads and applies them. The skills are available at https://github.com/KuangshiAi/SciVisAgentSkills.

AI.tldr: CN: 论文给科学可视化代理加了一层可复用“技能包”，把工具经验和流程知识显式编码进去；在 108 个多步任务上，这些技能普遍提升了表现，并说明 SciVis 代理不仅要看模型能力，还要看 skill 设计和执行框架。 EN: The paper adds a reusable “skill layer” to SciVis agents by explicitly encoding tool expertise and workflow knowledge; on 108 multi-step tasks, these skills consistently improve performance and show that SciVis agent quality depends not just on the model, but also on skill design and the execution harness.
AI.motivation: CN: 通用编码代理虽能将自然语言转为可执行工作流，但在科学可视化任务中常缺乏工具级专业知识，导致多步骤 SciVis 分析与可视化不够稳定和高效。 EN: Although general-purpose coding agents can translate natural language into executable workflows, they often lack tool-specific expertise for scientific visualization, limiting reliability and efficiency on multi-step SciVis tasks.
AI.method: CN: 提出 SciVisAgentSkills，为编码代理封装环境假设、工具使用模式和领域启发式，覆盖 ParaView、napari、VMD、TTK 等工具；并在 SciVisAgentBench 的 108 个专家设计多步任务上，用 Codex 和 Claude Code 进行评测。 EN: The paper introduces SciVisAgentSkills, a reusable skill set encoding environment assumptions, tool-usage patterns, and domain heuristics for tools such as ParaView, napari, VMD, and TTK, and evaluates it on 108 expert-designed multi-step tasks in SciVisAgentBench using Codex and Claude Code.
AI.result: CN: 在所有评测套件上，agent skills 提升了平均任务分数；同时带来了 token 效率收益，但收益幅度取决于所用代理 harness 与具体工具设置。 EN: Across the evaluated suites, agent skills improved mean task scores and provided token-efficiency gains, although the magnitude of these gains varied with the agent harness and tool setting.
AI.conclusion: CN: 结构化、可复用的 SciVis agent skills 能显著提升科学可视化长流程任务的可靠性与平均任务表现，但其收益与执行 harness 及工具环境强相关，应联合研究。 EN: Structured, reusable SciVis agent skills significantly improve reliability and average performance on long-horizon scientific visualization tasks, but their benefits depend strongly on the execution harness and tool environment, so both should be studied together.

title: What's Under the Skin? Estimating Swine Body Condition
summary: Sow body condition is an important indicator for growers as it has a large impact on lactation performance and piglet survival. However, body condition measures used during production, such as visual scoring and calipers, correlate poorly with underlying tissue composition. Ultrasound scans can provide direct measurements of subcutaneous backfat thickness and loin muscle depth, but their operation is labor intensive and not scalable for production. We present PigFormer, an end-to-end two-stage system that takes raw depth frames from a ceiling-mounted RGB-D camera and predicts subcutaneous backfat thickness, loin muscle depth, and total tissue thickness at the last rib. Stage 1 is a geometric front-end that converts raw depth into a standardized height map via SAM3-to-MaskDINO segmentation distillation, ground-plane removal, and orientation normalization. Stage 2 is a Slice Attention Encoder that treats each height map as a sequence of cross-sectional slices and captures spatial relationships along the full dorsal surface. On a multi-site dataset of 319 sow and gilt instances from two facilities, PigFormer achieves 2.43 mm backfat MAE and 3.87 mm overall MAE. It outperforms strong single-stage ResNet-18 and ViT-small baselines. PigFormer offers a practical path toward continuous, automated, non-contact body condition monitoring in commercial swine production. Code is available at https://github.com/iambashar/Pigformer.

AI.tldr: PigFormer turns overhead RGB-D depth frames into standardized pig height maps and uses slice-based attention to predict tissue measurements more accurately than ResNet/ViT baselines, enabling scalable automated sow body-condition monitoring.
AI.motivation: Existing production measures such as visual scoring and calipers do not reliably reflect true tissue composition, while ultrasound gives direct measurements but is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. The work is motivated by the need for continuous, automated, non-contact, scalable body-condition monitoring in swine production.
AI.method: The paper proposes a two-stage end-to-end pipeline. Stage 1 geometrically standardizes raw depth frames into height maps using segmentation distillation (SAM3 to MaskDINO), ground-plane removal, and orientation normalization. Stage 2 uses a Slice Attention Encoder that models the height map as sequential dorsal cross-sections to predict backfat thickness, loin muscle depth, and total tissue thickness at the last rib.
AI.result: On a multi-site dataset of 319 sow and gilt instances from two facilities, PigFormer achieves 2.43 mm MAE for backfat and 3.87 mm overall MAE, outperforming single-stage ResNet-18 and ViT-small baselines.
AI.conclusion: PigFormer provides a practical and more accurate non-contact system for automated sow body-condition monitoring from ceiling-mounted RGB-D depth data, outperforming strong image-based baselines and showing deployment potential in commercial farms.

title: Using Large Language Models to Support High Volume Application Review for an Undergraduate Research Program
summary: Undergraduate research programs such as the Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) at Purdue University receive thousands of applications every year, requiring significant time and effort for program staff to evaluate each submission consistently and within tight timelines. This work-in-progress paper describes the development and initial deployment of a large language model (LLM)-based tool to assist in the evaluation of approximately 1,200 student Statements of Purpose (SoPs) for the SURF 2026 cycle at Purdue University. The workflow utilizes OpenAI GPT models (GPT-4o, GPT-5-mini, and GPT-5.2) and uses a structured rubric across six subcategories, each scored on a 0-3 scale. A few SoPs, graded by program staff, were used to tune the model responses. The model prompt was designed to generate both numerical scores, rationales (including positive and negative aspects) and short excerpts from each submission. Using GPT-5.2, the full batch of 1,200 SoPs was processed in approximately 4.6 hours of compute time, averaging roughly 14 seconds per SoP (with per-SoP timing varying with SoP length, which ranged from 500 to 2,000 words). Notable differences in rubric adherence were observed across model versions, with GPT-5.2 adhering most closely. Disagreement in model scores was more pronounced for lower-scoring submissions. The LLM outputs replicated the role previously played by distributed human graders, providing the program coordinator with scored and rationale-annotated outputs for the entire applicant pool. The program coordinator then reviewed these outputs alongside each applicant's SoP, applying the same downstream office criteria used in prior SURF cycles, to produce a shortlist of strong candidates. This coordinator review was completed in approximately 4 hours, compared to the multi-week coordination effort required in prior program cycles.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an LLM tool for scoring 1,200 undergraduate research application essays with a six-part rubric. Among several OpenAI models, GPT-5.2 performed best, producing rubric-aligned scores and rationales quickly enough to cut the review workflow from weeks to a few hours, while still keeping a human coordinator in the loop.
AI.motivation: Manual review of thousands of undergraduate research applications is labor-intensive, time-constrained, and difficult to keep fully consistent across distributed human graders. The work aims to reduce staff burden and accelerate evaluation while maintaining structured, rubric-based assessment.
AI.method: The authors built and deployed an LLM-assisted evaluation pipeline for about 1,200 SURF 2026 Statements of Purpose using OpenAI models (GPT-4o, GPT-5-mini, and GPT-5.2). They designed a structured prompt aligned to a six-category rubric scored from 0 to 3, tuned the prompts using a small set of staff-graded examples, and asked the model to produce scores, rationales with strengths and weaknesses, and short supporting excerpts. Outputs were then reviewed by the program coordinator using existing downstream criteria.
AI.result: GPT-5.2 processed the full batch in about 4.6 hours, averaging around 14 seconds per statement, and adhered to the rubric more closely than the other tested models. Score disagreement was greater on lower-scoring submissions. The generated outputs effectively replaced the prior distributed human-grader role, and coordinator review plus shortlist creation took about 4 hours instead of a multi-week coordination process.
AI.conclusion: LLM-based scoring can substantially streamline large-scale Statement of Purpose evaluation for undergraduate research applications, with GPT-5.2 showing the strongest rubric adherence and enabling major reductions in review time while preserving human oversight in final candidate selection.

title: Generalized TV--$\ell_p$ Structured Priors for Bayesian $T_1$ Mapping
comment: Accepted for publication at the Journal of Machine Learning for Biomedical Imaging (MELBA) https://melba-journal.org/2026:015
summary: We propose an extended family of structured spatial priors that incorporates the total variation (TV) function with $\ell_p$ norms. The prior is proven to be proper and incorporated into a Bayesian regression framework to enable uncertainty quantification in $T_1$ mapping, with posterior inference performed using the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS). This TV--$\ell_p$ construction is proven to constitute a well-defined family of prior distributions, and it naturally enforces spatial consistency and smooth variations in the estimated parameter maps. The method was evaluated in comparison to maximum-likelihood estimation and several Bayesian alternative priors based on the uniform, Gamma, and bounded TV priors. The evaluation includes experiments on synthetic brain and cardiac $T_1$ mapping datasets, as well as a real in-vivo breast $T_1$ mapping dataset. The results show that the TV--$\ell_p$ prior yields more concentrated posterior densities, indicating reduced uncertainty. It also consistently achieves lower variance and smaller (negative) bias, leading to more reliable estimates. Overall, embedding a TV-based structured penalty along with $\ell_p$ norms in a prior in a Bayesian model improves spatial coherence in $T_1$ maps and enhances uncertainty quantification, offering a robust approach for $T_1$ mapping with uncertainties.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a proper TV-ℓ_p prior for Bayesian T1 mapping and uses NUTS for inference. It improves spatial smoothness, reduces uncertainty, and outperforms MLE and several alternative priors in variance and bias on synthetic and real data.
AI.motivation: Conventional T1 mapping methods and simpler priors may not adequately model spatial structure or quantify uncertainty, which can lead to less stable estimates. The work aims to impose spatial consistency while preserving smooth variation and to provide stronger Bayesian uncertainty quantification.
AI.method: The paper defines an extended family of proper structured spatial priors that combines total variation with ℓ_p norms, embeds this prior in a Bayesian regression framework for T1 mapping, and performs posterior inference with the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS). The approach is evaluated on synthetic brain and cardiac datasets and a real in-vivo breast T1 mapping dataset against MLE and Bayesian baselines using uniform, Gamma, and bounded TV priors.
AI.result: Across synthetic and real datasets, the TV-ℓ_p prior produced more concentrated posterior densities, lower variance, and smaller negative bias than the comparison methods, indicating reduced uncertainty and more reliable T1 estimates.
AI.conclusion: A Bayesian T1 mapping model using a proper TV-ℓ_p structured spatial prior improves spatial coherence and uncertainty quantification, producing more reliable parameter estimates than maximum-likelihood and several alternative Bayesian priors.

title: When Should We Protect AI? A Precautionary Framework for Consciousness Uncertainty
summary: Existing frameworks assess whether AI systems might be conscious but provide no guidance on what to do with that assessment. We address this gap with a precautionary framework that maps consciousness evidence to graduated protective obligations. The framework comprises three components: (1) five welfare-relevant dimensions--phenomenal consciousness, affective valence, metacognitive awareness, self-narrative, and agency--each grounded in established consciousness science and linked to distinct moral concerns; (2) a threshold-plus-gradation hybrid specifying both binary triggers for new obligation categories and continuous scaling of protective weight; and (3) two complementary approaches to cross-dimensional aggregation, one hierarchical (drawing on Bach and Sorensen's Machine Consciousness Hypothesis) and one architecture-agnostic. We operationalize the framework through worked case studies of Replika and OpenClaw, demonstrating how systems occupying different regions of the dimensional space trigger different obligations, and derive design guidance for developers building systems near consciousness-relevant thresholds. The framework is architecture-agnostic, applying across neural, symbolic, and neurosymbolic systems, and aims to make consciousness science decision-relevant for organizations navigating uncertainty today.

AI.tldr: A practical framework for AI welfare: score systems on five consciousness-related dimensions, map the evidence to thresholds and graduated protections, aggregate across dimensions, and use the result to decide what obligations developers have.
AI.motivation: Current AI consciousness assessment frameworks can estimate whether systems may be conscious, but they do not say what actions should follow from that assessment. The paper aims to turn consciousness science into decision-relevant guidance.
AI.method: The paper proposes a precautionary framework with five welfare-relevant dimensions, a threshold-plus-gradation model for assigning obligations, and two cross-dimensional aggregation methods; it then applies the framework to case studies of Replika and OpenClaw.
AI.result: The result is an architecture-agnostic framework that maps evidence of consciousness-related properties to differentiated protective obligations, illustrated through case studies and translated into design guidance for systems near relevant thresholds.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that AI consciousness evaluations should be tied to practical, precautionary protections: evidence across multiple consciousness-related dimensions should trigger graduated obligations for developers and organizations, even under uncertainty.

title: Domain-Aware Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis Using Language-Specific Statistical Graphs
summary: Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis (MDD) has gained increasing importance in computer-assisted language learning and speech technology in recent years. In this paper, we propose a method for constructing statistical graphs that enable models to learn phoneme confusion patterns represented as directed graphs. Furthermore, we introduce a language-specific strategy to capture systematic pronunciation differences across various native language (L1) backgrounds. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on the L2-ARCTIC benchmark, where it achieves an F1-score of 59.52%, outperforming several competitive baselines.

AI.tldr: 该论文用统计有向图学习音素混淆，并结合母语相关策略建模系统性发音差异，在L2-ARCTIC上以59.52% F1超过多种基线。 / The paper learns phoneme confusion via statistical directed graphs and models L1-related pronunciation differences, reaching 59.52% F1 on L2-ARCTIC and outperforming multiple baselines.
AI.motivation: 误发音检测与诊断在计算机辅助语言学习和语音技术中日益重要，但现有方法对音素混淆关系及不同母语背景造成的系统性发音差异建模不足。 / Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis is increasingly important in computer-assisted language learning and speech technology, yet existing methods insufficiently model phoneme confusion relationships and systematic pronunciation differences caused by different native-language backgrounds.
AI.method: 提出一种统计图构建方法，将音素混淆模式表示为有向图供模型学习；同时设计语言特定策略，以捕获不同母语背景带来的系统性发音差异。 / The paper proposes a statistical graph construction method that represents phoneme confusion patterns as directed graphs for model learning, and introduces a language-specific strategy to capture systematic pronunciation differences from different native-language backgrounds.
AI.result: 在L2-ARCTIC基准上进行了广泛实验，方法取得59.52%的F1-score，优于多个具有竞争力的基线方法。 / Extensive experiments on the L2-ARCTIC benchmark show that the method achieves an F1-score of 59.52%, surpassing several competitive baselines.
AI.conclusion: 通过统计图建模音素混淆模式，并结合针对不同母语背景的语言特定策略，可以有效提升误发音检测与诊断性能，在L2-ARCTIC上优于多个强基线。 / Modeling phoneme confusion patterns with statistical directed graphs, combined with a language-specific strategy for different L1 backgrounds, effectively improves mispronunciation detection and diagnosis, outperforming several strong baselines on L2-ARCTIC.

title: Trust, but Don't Verify: Epistemic Blind Spots in LLM Source Evaluation
summary: Language models increasingly act as epistemic proxies, synthesizing evidence from multiple sources to inform decisions. Whether they evaluate the quality of that evidence, or merely aggregate it based on surface presentation, remains poorly understood. We show that models possess the capability to detect fabricated statistics (correct identification rates of 0.76-1.00 for methodology in isolation) but do not recruit this capability during multi-source synthesis, producing similar numeric estimates whether the statistics are fabricated or valid. Specifically, source influence is governed by a methodology-register gate that responds to the distributional register of analytical text but not to numeric validity: for example, statistically impossible confidence intervals receive the same weight as valid ones. The behavioral dissociation replicates across five models from three families (Claude, Qwen, OLMo) and three professional domains. Mechanistic analyses, including causal tracing, linear probes, and component-level attribution, converge on the same account: the model encodes and causally uses a methodology-register representation that transfers across domains (probe AUC 0.83-0.92), while numeric-validity signals, decodable in isolation, are suppressed to chance during multi-source synthesis. Prompting-based mitigations, even an oracle checklist naming the exact statistical checks, produce blanket skepticism rather than selective discernment, and the post-training pipelines we examine reinforce the stylistic shortcut without building numeric verification. Unlike sycophancy, which tracks user preference, this failure tracks whether a source presents as analytically credible, not whether its claims are internally consistent. We term this epistemic alignment: like preference and safety alignment, the question is not capability but deployment.

AI.tldr: 中文：模型会“看起来懂统计”，但在综合多来源证据时主要信方法学语气和文体，不认真核查数字是否真的成立。 English: Models can detect bad statistics alone, but when synthesizing sources they mainly trust methodological style rather than checking whether the numbers are actually valid.
AI.motivation: 中文：研究动机在于，语言模型正越来越多地充当“认知代理”来汇总多来源证据并支持决策，但我们并不清楚它们是在评估证据质量，还是仅仅被表面上专业、分析化的表达方式所影响。这个问题直接关系到模型在高风险决策场景中的可靠性。 English: The motivation is that language models increasingly serve as epistemic proxies that aggregate evidence for decisions, yet it remains unclear whether they actually assess evidence quality or merely respond to superficially professional analytical presentation. This matters directly for reliability in high-stakes decision contexts.
AI.method: 中文：作者结合行为实验与机制解释方法进行研究。行为上，他们比较模型在孤立条件下识别伪造统计与在多源综合任务中使用这些信号的表现；机制上，他们使用因果追踪、线性探针和组件级归因分析模型内部表征，并在多个模型家族与多个专业领域上复现结果。 English: The authors combine behavioral experiments with mechanistic interpretability. Behaviorally, they compare models’ ability to detect fabricated statistics in isolation versus their use of that signal during multi-source synthesis; mechanistically, they apply causal tracing, linear probes, and component-level attribution, and replicate the findings across multiple model families and professional domains.
AI.result: 中文：结果表明，模型在单独判断方法学文本时能够较高准确率识别伪造统计，但在多源综合时，伪造统计与有效统计对最终数值估计的影响几乎相同。模型真正依赖的是一种可跨领域迁移的“方法学文体表征”，而数值有效性信号虽可被解码，却在综合阶段被压制到接近随机。提示工程式缓解方法也未能实现有选择的甄别，只带来普遍怀疑。 English: The results show that models can identify fabricated statistics with high accuracy when methodology is evaluated in isolation, but during multi-source synthesis fabricated and valid statistics exert nearly the same influence on final numeric estimates. What models actually use is a cross-domain transferable methodology-register representation, while numeric-validity signals, though decodable in isolation, are suppressed to chance during synthesis. Prompt-based mitigations fail to induce selective discernment and instead produce blanket skepticism.
AI.conclusion: 中文：论文结论是，大语言模型并非在多源证据综合时真正核查数值是否有效，而是主要依据来源是否呈现出“方法学上看起来可信”的文体与分析风格来分配权重。这说明问题不在于模型缺乏识别伪造统计的能力，而在于该能力没有在综合阶段被调用。 English: The paper concludes that during multi-source evidence synthesis, language models do not genuinely verify numeric validity; instead, they mainly weight sources by whether they appear methodologically credible in style and analytical register. The issue is therefore not lack of capability to detect fabricated statistics, but failure to deploy that capability during synthesis.

title: Individual Gain, Collective Loss: Metacognitive Adaptation in AI-Assisted Creativity
summary: Recent studies reveal a paradox: AI enhances individual creative outputs while reducing collective diversity. Current explanations -- cognitive offloading and over-reliance -- identify symptoms but not mechanisms. We propose selective metacognitive adaptation: routine AI use redistributes rather than uniformly diminishes metacognitive effort. Some capacities are amplified (partner modeling, surface control), while others are systematically under-supported (originality evaluation, reflective integration). This redistribution explains both individual satisfaction and collective convergence. We present a taxonomy of six metacognitive capacities organized by temporal phase, characterize their tendencies under routine AI use, and show how individually rational adaptation produces emergent social costs. The framework generates specific predictions for researchers and design principles for practitioners seeking to preserve both individual creative satisfaction and collective creative diversity.

AI.tldr: AI helps people create better on their own, but repeated use shifts metacognitive effort toward easier, AI-compatible skills and away from deeper originality and reflection, which makes many individuals satisfied while making collective outputs more similar.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explain the paradox that AI improves individual creative output but reduces collective diversity. Existing explanations such as cognitive offloading and over-reliance describe the phenomenon but do not specify the mechanism producing it.
AI.method: The paper develops a conceptual framework and taxonomy of six metacognitive capacities organized by temporal phase. It analyzes how these capacities are differentially supported or weakened under routine AI use, and derives predictions and design principles from this framework.
AI.result: The main result is a taxonomy-based account showing that AI amplifies some metacognitive capacities, such as partner modeling and surface control, while under-supporting others, such as originality evaluation and reflective integration. This mechanism explains why individually beneficial AI use can lead to emergent social costs.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that routine AI use does not simply reduce metacognition; it selectively redistributes it across different capacities. This selective metacognitive adaptation can improve individual creative satisfaction while simultaneously driving collective convergence and lowering diversity.

title: ShotCrop$^3$: Cropping Human-Centric Images into Cinematic Triple-Shot Compositions
summary: Prior work on aesthetic composition typically produces a single aesthetically pleasing crop, overlooking the narrative value of composing multiple shots from one scene. In practice, multi-shot composition is critical for downstream creative workflows: commercial posters often require multiple crops with different emphases (e.g., context, subject, and emotion/product details) to present key story beats. Therefore, we propose \textbf{Triple-Shot Compositions (TSC)}, a composition task that generates a three-shot set -- establishing, medium, and close-up -- from a single human-centric image, each paired with a brief shot description to support visual narration. To learn TSC with limited expert annotations, we introduce \textbf{ShotCrop} which undergoes a three-stage training process: it first applies Chain-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning to establish basic reasoning and aesthetic shot-cropping skills, then performs semi-supervised fine-tuning with high-confidence pseudo labels to further enhance aesthetic capability, and is finally optimized with Group Relative Policy Optimization for \textbf{ShotCrop} (GRPO-S) using a composite reward tailored for it. Specifically, our pseudo-labeling strategy combines MLLM-based scoring, aesthetic assessment, and CLIP similarity to retain high-confidence training signals. In addition, we present TSC-Bench, a benchmark of 1.2k expert-annotated test cases. Notably, ShotCrop achieves an average improvement of \textbf{2.82} times over GPT-5 in shot localization accuracy.

AI.tldr: The paper defines a new task for turning one human-centric image into three narratively complementary crops with descriptions, and trains a model called ShotCrop with supervised, semi-supervised, and GRPO-based optimization to achieve large gains over GPT-5 on a new expert benchmark.
AI.motivation: Prior work usually outputs only one aesthetically pleasing crop and ignores the narrative value of composing multiple shots from the same scene. Real creative workflows such as posters need multiple crops with different emphases to convey context, subject, and detail, motivating a dedicated multi-shot composition task.
AI.method: The method introduces ShotCrop for Triple-Shot Compositions with a three-stage training pipeline: (1) Chain-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning for reasoning and aesthetic shot-cropping, (2) semi-supervised fine-tuning using high-confidence pseudo labels selected by MLLM-based scoring, aesthetic assessment, and CLIP similarity, and (3) GRPO-S optimization with a composite reward tailored to the task. The paper also constructs TSC-Bench with 1.2k expert-annotated test cases.
AI.result: The paper proposes the Triple-Shot Compositions task, releases the TSC-Bench benchmark, and shows that ShotCrop achieves strong performance, including an average 2.82x improvement over GPT-5 in shot localization accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that Triple-Shot Compositions is a useful new task for generating narratively coherent three-shot crop sets from a single human-centric image, and that the proposed ShotCrop training pipeline substantially improves multi-shot aesthetic composition quality and shot localization accuracy, outperforming GPT-5 by 2.82x on average on TSC-Bench.

title: TensorBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents on a Compiler-Based Tensor Framework
summary: Repository-level coding benchmarks face a trade-off between task difficulty and evaluation reliability: tasks that challenge frontier models often involve large codebases with incomplete test coverage, while human review does not scale. We introduce TensorBench, a benchmark of 199 feature-addition and refactoring tasks on an open-source compiler-based tensor framework that extends PyTorch with first-class support for dense and sparse tensors. Tasks cover new sparse formats, dense optimization passes, IR transformations, scheduler changes, runtime components, and high-level numerical operators. TensorBench grades each run by applying the agent's patch and running the framework's test suite, which includes the pre-existing randomized regression tests and any tests the agent adds. For feature-addition tasks, a pass means that the patched repository preserves the tested pre-existing behavior and satisfies the agent-added checks for the requested feature. We evaluate seven coding agents spanning three frontier model families and one open-weight model. Pass rates under this criterion range from $64.8\%$ for the strongest agent to $22.1\%$ for the weakest. Agents pass different subsets of tasks: pairwise Cohen's $κ$ ranges from $-0.07$ to $0.43$, with $κ= 0.05$ for the two strongest agents.

AI.tldr: TensorBench is a 199-task repo-level coding benchmark for a PyTorch-related tensor compiler framework, evaluated by patch application plus test-suite execution. It is challenging yet automatically gradable, and current coding agents vary widely in success and solve notably different tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing repository-level coding benchmarks must balance realistic difficulty against reliable evaluation. Hard tasks often live in large codebases with incomplete test coverage, while manual human review is not scalable. The paper aims to provide a benchmark that is both challenging and automatically evaluable.
AI.method: The paper introduces TensorBench, a benchmark of 199 repository-level feature-addition and refactoring tasks on an open-source compiler-based tensor framework extending PyTorch. Each agent run is graded by applying its patch and executing the framework’s existing randomized regression tests plus any tests added by the agent; feature tasks pass only if existing behavior is preserved and new feature checks succeed.
AI.result: Across seven coding agents from three frontier model families and one open-weight model, pass rates range from 64.8% for the best agent to 22.1% for the weakest. Different agents solve different subsets of tasks, with pairwise Cohen’s kappa from -0.07 to 0.43; even the two strongest agents have very low agreement (kappa = 0.05).
AI.conclusion: TensorBench offers a scalable, test-based way to evaluate repository-level coding agents on difficult compiler/tensor-framework tasks, and current agents show substantial but far from solved performance with strong complementarity across models.

title: CausalPOI: Spatio-Temporal Graph-Based Causal Modeling for Cold-Start POI Check-in Forecasting
summary: As urban environments continue to evolve rapidly, accurately modeling the dynamic behaviour of Points of Interest is essential for supporting data-driven urban planning and commercial decision-making. While recent advancements in spatio-temporal graph learning have improved POI forecasting, most methods rely on proximity-based graphs and correlation-driven modeling, which overlook the functional dependencies between POIs and fail to capture the causal effects of urban interventions. In this paper, we introduce a novel research problem -- cold-start POI check-in forecasting, which aims to predict the future check-in pattern of a newly introduced POI, by modeling its temporal evolution and functional interactions with nearby POIs in a structured urban spatial context. To address these challenges, we propose CausalPOI, a spatio-temporal graph-based causal representation learning framework. CausalPOI leverages Spatio-Temporal Functional Interaction Graph to model semantic and spatial relationships between POIs, and constructs structurally aligned treatment and control graphs to simulate factual and counterfactual scenarios. Extensive experiments on real-world SafeGraph datasets demonstrate that CausalPOI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across the board, validating its effectiveness in spatio-temporal forecasting, semantic interaction modeling, and causal effect estimation, providing a more interpretable and actionable foundation for urban intervention analysis. Source code is available at Github.

AI.tldr: The paper studies cold-start POI check-in forecasting and introduces CausalPOI, which uses functional spatio-temporal graphs plus causal treatment/control graph construction to predict new POI behavior more accurately and interpretably than prior methods.
AI.motivation: Existing POI forecasting methods mainly depend on proximity-based graphs and correlation-based learning, which miss functional dependencies between POIs and cannot properly model the causal impact of urban interventions. This is especially problematic for forecasting newly introduced POIs under cold-start conditions.
AI.method: The paper proposes CausalPOI, a spatio-temporal graph-based causal representation learning framework. It builds a Spatio-Temporal Functional Interaction Graph to capture semantic and spatial relations among POIs, and creates structurally aligned treatment and control graphs to model factual and counterfactual scenarios for causal effect estimation.
AI.result: Experiments on real-world SafeGraph datasets show that CausalPOI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in forecasting accuracy, semantic interaction modeling, and causal effect estimation.
AI.conclusion: CausalPOI provides an effective and interpretable framework for cold-start POI check-in forecasting by combining spatio-temporal graph learning with causal representation learning, and it consistently outperforms prior methods on real-world SafeGraph data.

title: SoCRATES: Towards Reliable Automated Evaluation of Proactive LLM Mediation across Domains and Socio-cognitive Variations
