AI.tldr: A deep unfolding model, PGU-Net, jointly estimates hyperspectral images and unknown sensor spectral degradation for blind cross-sensor SSR, outperforming prior methods on synthetic and real UAV data.
AI.motivation: Existing spectral super-resolution methods usually assume a fixed and known spectral response function, which restricts them to single-sensor settings. In practical cross-sensor UAV scenarios, the spectral degradation is unknown and varies across sensors and scenes, making hyperspectral reconstruction severely ill-posed.
AI.method: The paper proposes PGU-Net, a physics-guided deep unfolding network that unrolls an alternating optimization process into multiple trainable stages. In each stage, the model sequentially updates the hyperspectral image and a learnable spectral transformation function using learnable proximal networks together with differentiable closed-form solvers.
AI.result: Experiments on CAVE, NTIRE 2022, and a real UAV cross-sensor dataset show that PGU-Net accurately recovers the degradation operator and outperforms state-of-the-art SSR methods in reconstruction quality under blind conditions.
AI.conclusion: PGU-Net can effectively solve blind cross-sensor spectral super-resolution by jointly estimating hyperspectral images and the unknown spectral transformation function, achieving strong reconstruction accuracy and robustness in both benchmark and real UAV datasets.

title: PlanBench-V: A Spatial Planning Map Benchmark for Vision-Language Models
summary: Spatial planning maps are central to territorial governance, translating planning objectives, regulations, and spatial strategies into visual forms for decision-making, public communication, and institutional coordination. Their interpretation, however, requires fine-grained visual perception, spatial reasoning, and policy-informed professional judgment, creating major challenges for both human learners and AI systems. With the rapid progress of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), their use in urban planning analysis is gaining attention, yet existing multimodal benchmarks mainly target general visual understanding and overlook the domain-specific cognitive processes of planning practice. To address this gap, we introduce PlanBench-V, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs in spatial planning map interpretation. We first build the Spatial Planning Map Database (SPMD), an expert-annotated dataset of 223 planning maps and 1629 question-answer pairs curated by professional planners, covering diverse geographic regions and cartographic styles. We then propose a theory-informed evaluation framework assessing four progressive capabilities: Perception, Reasoning, Association, and Implementation, corresponding to the cognitive pipeline of planning map interpretation. Extensive experiments across two generations of VLMs show clear progress but persistent limitations. The best 2026 agentic reasoning model, Qwen3.6-Plus, substantially outperforms the best 2025 model, GPT-4o, by 27%. Nevertheless, all models still struggle with implementation-oriented tasks requiring evaluative judgment, policy sensitivity, and constraint-aware decision-making. These findings reveal fundamental limitations of current VLMs in professional planning contexts and highlight the need for domain-adaptive multimodal reasoning frameworks. Code and data are available at https://plangpt.github.io.

AI.tldr: PlanBench-V is the first benchmark for testing how well VLMs understand spatial planning maps. It introduces a new expert dataset and a four-level evaluation framework, showing that newer models are better but still not strong enough for professional planning decisions.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal benchmarks focus on general visual understanding and do not capture the domain-specific cognitive demands of spatial planning map interpretation, which requires visual perception, spatial reasoning, and policy-informed judgment. The paper aims to fill this evaluation gap for urban planning applications of VLMs.
AI.method: The paper constructs SPMD, an expert-annotated dataset of 223 spatial planning maps with 1629 QA pairs, and introduces PlanBench-V, a benchmark guided by planning cognition theory. It evaluates VLMs across four staged capabilities: Perception, Reasoning, Association, and Implementation, then compares two generations of VLMs through extensive experiments.
AI.result: The benchmark shows measurable progress across model generations: the best 2026 agentic reasoning model, Qwen3.6-Plus, outperforms the best 2025 model, GPT-4o, by 27%. However, all tested models remain weak on implementation-oriented questions involving evaluative judgment, policy sensitivity, and decision-making under constraints.
AI.conclusion: PlanBench-V exposes that although modern vision-language models have improved substantially on spatial planning map interpretation, they still fail on implementation-level tasks that require policy-sensitive, constraint-aware professional judgment. This indicates current VLMs are not yet reliable for real planning practice and need domain-adaptive multimodal reasoning frameworks.

title: Autoregressive Diffusion World Models for Off-Policy Evaluation of LLM Agents
summary: Evaluating large language model (LLM) agents in multi-turn interactive environments is expensive and risky, as it requires online environment interaction. We propose ADWM (Autoregressive Diffusion World Model), an evaluation framework that estimates the performance of a new LLM agent policy purely from pre-collected trajectories. The core idea is to learn a latent diffusion world model that simulates how the environment responds to the evaluation policy, without ever executing it in the real environment. Existing diffusion-based OPE methods guide full trajectories in a single pass by jointly diffusing states and actions, an assumption that breaks down for LLM agents whose actions are discrete text that must be sampled from the policy after observing the environment. Unlike autoregressive world models that suffer from compounding errors, ADWM models each transition as an independent denoising process, enabling reliable step-by-step rollouts where the world model and agent alternate in causal order. Crucially, the LLM agent under evaluation directly guides the diffusion generation at each step via a policy-conditioned score function, ensuring that simulated trajectories accurately reflect its decision-making patterns. Empirically, ADWM achieves accurate value estimates and evaluation reliability across diverse multi-turn agent tasks, demonstrating its promise as a practical framework for offline LLM agent evaluation.

AI.tldr: ADWM evaluates LLM agents offline by using a diffusion world model that simulates environment responses step by step under the target policy, avoiding risky online interaction and improving reliability over prior OPE/world-model approaches.
AI.motivation: Online evaluation of LLM agents in multi-turn interactive environments is costly and risky. Existing offline policy evaluation methods based on diffusion assume joint generation of continuous state-action trajectories, which does not fit LLM agents whose actions are discrete text sampled after observing the environment. Autoregressive world models also suffer from compounding rollout errors.
AI.method: The paper proposes ADWM, an Autoregressive Diffusion World Model that learns a latent diffusion-based environment model from offline trajectories. At each step, the world model generates the next transition through an independent denoising process, while the evaluated LLM policy conditions generation via a policy-guided score function, enabling causal step-by-step rollout without executing the policy online.
AI.result: Empirically, ADWM delivers accurate value estimates and reliable evaluation performance across diverse multi-turn agent tasks, indicating strong potential for practical offline evaluation of LLM agents.
AI.conclusion: ADWM provides a practical and reliable offline evaluation framework for LLM agents by estimating policy performance from pre-collected trajectories without online interaction, achieving accurate value estimation across diverse multi-turn tasks.

title: PerceptUI: LLM Agents as Human-Aligned Synthetic Users for UI/UX Evaluation
summary: User interface (UI) and user experience (UX) evaluation is central to product development, yet reliable feedback still relies on recruiting human participants or running online A/B tests, making early-stage iteration slow and costly. In light of this, recent work has explored Multimodal Large Language Models as proxy evaluators. However, existing approaches either produce surface-level critiques or a judgment that reflects the model's own biases rather than the genuine response of a particular user. We introduce PerceptUI, a framework for persona-conditioned UI/UX evaluation that predicts how a specific user would answer interface-related questions and produces natural-language rationales. PerceptUI is trained in two stages: (i) contrastive reflection fine-tuning distills teacher-generated rationales by extracting lessons from human decisions, and (ii) a reflective prompt-evolution step from the model's own failure traces. Across multiple domains and datasets, PerceptUI achieves human-level realism, generalizes to unseen questions and personas, and yields population-level response distributions.

AI.tldr: PerceptUI uses multimodal LLMs to simulate how specific users would evaluate interfaces, improving early UI/UX testing with more realistic, persona-aware predictions and explanations.
AI.motivation: Traditional UI/UX evaluation depends on human studies or A/B testing, which are slow and expensive in early product development. Prior multimodal LLM-based evaluators either give shallow feedback or reflect model bias rather than the perspective of a specific target user.
AI.method: The paper proposes PerceptUI, trained in two stages: first, contrastive reflection fine-tuning to distill teacher-generated rationales from human decisions; second, reflective prompt evolution using the model’s own failure traces to improve persona-conditioned prediction and explanation.
AI.result: Across multiple datasets and domains, PerceptUI reaches human-level realism, generalizes to unseen personas and questions, and can estimate population-level response distributions.
AI.conclusion: PerceptUI enables persona-conditioned UI/UX evaluation with human-level realism, producing both predicted user responses and natural-language rationales while generalizing across domains, questions, and unseen personas.

title: ExpSpeech-Net: Multimodal Fusion of Expression and Speech for Deepfake Detection
summary: Deepfake videos are increasingly challenging the credibility of online content. Many existing detection methodology relies on complex, resource-intensive models, which limit their practical use. The study introduces the ExpSpeech-Net deepfake detection (SqN-R-DFD) model, which utilizes SqueezeNet and RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) as its backbone, providing a lightweight and efficient deepfake detection framework that simultaneously analyzes facial expressions and speech patterns. The approach incorporates advanced feature extraction, such as ISLBT-based features for image and MPNCC for signals, along with a smart feature-selection strategy using SASMA (Sandpiper-Assisted Slime Mould Algorithm), ensuring optimal and balanced input to the detection models. By combining SqueezeNet and an RNN, subtle inconsistencies in deepfake videos are captured effectively. The framework achieves 94.5% accuracy, precision of 99.3%, and F-measure of 96.8%, outperforming conventional methods. This demonstrates that integrating multiple modalities with intelligent preprocessing and feature selection enables practical, real-time deepfake detection suitable for everyday applications.

AI.tldr: A lightweight deepfake detector combines face and speech cues using SqueezeNet, RNN, and optimized feature selection, achieving strong accuracy and improving practicality for real-time use.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that existing deepfake detection methods are often too complex and computationally expensive for practical deployment, so the authors aim to design a lighter and more efficient detector without sacrificing accuracy.
AI.method: The method uses a multimodal framework that analyzes facial expressions and speech patterns together. It extracts ISLBT-based image features and MPNCC-based audio features, applies SASMA for feature selection, and feeds the selected features into a SqueezeNet-RNN deepfake detection model.
AI.result: The reported results are 94.5% accuracy, 99.3% precision, and 96.8% F-measure, with performance better than conventional methods.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a lightweight multimodal deepfake detector built with SqueezeNet and RNN, combined with intelligent preprocessing and feature selection, can deliver strong performance and practical real-time usability.

title: MARDoc: A Memory-Aware Refinement Agent Framework for Multimodal Long Document QA
summary: Iterative retrieval-reasoning agents have recently shown promise for multimodal long-document question answering. However, most existing systems maintain a single growing context that mixes retrieval traces, observations, and intermediate reasoning. As interactions accumulate, key evidence becomes scattered and diluted, making multi-hop reasoning noisy. We propose MARDoc, a Memory-Aware Refinement Agent framework that decouples long-document QA into three specialized agents: an Explorer for multi-granularity multimodal retrieval, a Refiner for distilling interaction traces into structured evidence and reasoning memories, and a Reflector for checking evidence sufficiency and providing targeted feedback. Across iterations, the agents rely on a dynamically updated structured memory rather than a full accumulated interaction history. This design reduces context noise while preserving answer-critical facts and their logical dependencies. Experiments on MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench show that MARDoc achieves strong results, outperforming same-backbone baselines and demonstrating the effectiveness of structured memory for agentic document QA.

AI.tldr: MARDoc improves multimodal long-document QA by replacing a noisy accumulated history with structured memory managed by Explorer, Refiner, and Reflector agents, leading to better results on benchmark datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing iterative retrieval-reasoning agents usually keep a single ever-growing context that mixes retrieval traces, observations, and intermediate reasoning. Over time, important evidence becomes scattered and diluted, which makes multi-hop reasoning noisy and less reliable. The paper is motivated by the need to reduce this context noise while retaining critical facts and logical links.
AI.method: The paper proposes MARDoc, a three-agent framework for multimodal long-document QA: an Explorer performs multi-granularity multimodal retrieval, a Refiner converts interaction traces into structured evidence and reasoning memories, and a Reflector evaluates evidence sufficiency and gives targeted feedback. The system iteratively updates structured memory instead of keeping the entire interaction history in context.
AI.result: On MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench, MARDoc achieves strong performance and outperforms baselines using the same backbone, supporting the value of structured memory in agentic document QA.
AI.conclusion: MARDoc shows that using structured, dynamically updated memory with specialized agents can improve multimodal long-document question answering by reducing context noise and preserving answer-critical evidence and reasoning dependencies.

title: CLaaS: Continual learning as a service for sample efficient online learning
summary: Deployed large language model agents must adapt to distribution shift in dynamic environments. Ideally, adaptation can be performed from accumulated agent experiences and retain prior capabilities while transferring to future tasks. However, agent actions and environmental transitions can only be sampled once per scenario, as real-world environments cannot be trivially reset. To this end, we investigate an experiential and online continual learning setting in which agents learn from a stream of scenarios. We propose continual learning as-a-service (CLaaS), a system which enables agents to improve during deployment, abstracted behind a chat API. To increase sample efficiency, CLaaS stores rollouts in an experience replay buffer for gradient reuse during asynchronous training. We evaluate CLaaS on an adversarial task, demonstrating that parametric updates lead to superior forward transfer and less forgetting than in-context learning, with replay being a critical choice for sample efficiency.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a deployment-time continual learning service for LLM agents that learns from one-pass real-world experience via replay and asynchronous training, outperforming in-context learning on adaptation, retention, and sample efficiency.
AI.motivation: Deployed LLM agents face distribution shift in dynamic real-world environments and cannot rely on repeated sampling from resettable scenarios. The authors aim to support online adaptation from accumulated experience while preserving prior capabilities and improving transfer to future tasks.
AI.method: The paper proposes CLaaS, a continual learning system exposed through a chat API. It collects agent rollouts from a stream of non-resettable scenarios, stores them in an experience replay buffer, and performs asynchronous gradient-based training to reuse past experience efficiently during deployment.
AI.result: On an adversarial task, CLaaS shows that parametric continual updates outperform in-context learning in forward transfer and forgetting, and that replay is a key component for improving sample efficiency.
AI.conclusion: CLaaS enables deployed LLM agents to continually improve online from experiential data, and parameter updates with replay provide better forward transfer, reduced forgetting, and higher sample efficiency than in-context learning alone.

title: Seeing Time: Benchmarking Chronological Reasoning and Shortcut Biases in Vision-Language Models
summary: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have significantly enhanced their ability to interpret complex visual semantics, yet their capacity for chronological reasoning remains under-explored. In this paper, we introduce a novel benchmark specifically designed to evaluate how VLMs perceive and reason about chronological information within and across images. Unlike existing video-based benchmarks that focus on frame sequencing, our work delves into the underlying logic of chronological judgment and the expansion toward multimodal integration. To facilitate this, we construct three specialized datasets: one containing visually similar objects spanning long historical durations, another categorized by diverse event and object types, and a third pairing images with time-sensitive news text for cross-modal alignment. Through extensive experiments, we analyze whether models exhibit performance disparities across categories and, crucially, explore whether they rely on ``incorrect shortcuts'', such as image color rather than genuine chronological features. Our results reveal that while VLMs show promise, they frequently exploit superficial cues like grayscale versus color filters to bypass authentic chronological reasoning. By providing these high-quality datasets and a rigorous evaluation framework, we offer a diagnostic tool to identify current limitations and guide the development of more robust, logically grounded multimodal models. The source code is shown in https://github.com/LuoRenqiang/ChronoVision.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文提出ChronoVision时间推理基准与三个数据集，用来测试VLM是否真正理解图像中的年代与时间逻辑。结果发现多数模型会偷看“颜色/灰度”这类表面特征，而不是做扎实的时间推理。 / This paper introduces the ChronoVision benchmark and three datasets to test whether VLMs truly understand chronology in images. It finds that many models rely on surface cues like color versus grayscale instead of performing robust temporal reasoning.
AI.motivation: 尽管VLM在复杂视觉语义理解上进步明显，但其时间先后判断能力研究不足；现有视频基准更关注帧排序，而不是时间判断背后的逻辑与跨模态时间对齐，因此需要一个更细粒度、更具诊断性的评测框架。 / Although VLMs have improved substantially in visual-semantic understanding, their ability for chronological reasoning is under-studied; existing video benchmarks emphasize frame ordering rather than the logic of temporal judgment and multimodal alignment, motivating a finer-grained diagnostic benchmark.
AI.method: 论文构建了一个面向时间顺序感知与推理的基准，并设计了三个数据集：长期历史跨度的相似对象图像集、按事件/对象类型划分的数据集，以及图像与时效性新闻文本配对的跨模态数据集；随后在这些数据上对VLM进行广泛评测，并分析类别差异与错误捷径依赖。 / The paper builds a benchmark for chronological perception and reasoning, with three datasets: visually similar objects across long historical spans, category-diverse events/objects, and image-news pairs for cross-modal temporal alignment; it then evaluates VLMs extensively and analyzes category-wise differences and shortcut reliance.
AI.result: 实验表明，VLM在时间推理任务上表现出一定潜力，但不同类别间存在性能差异，并且模型经常利用错误线索，尤其是颜色风格等浅层特征，来规避真实的时间推理。 / Experiments show that VLMs have some potential on chronological tasks, but performance varies across categories, and models frequently exploit spurious signals, especially color-style cues, to avoid genuine temporal reasoning.
AI.conclusion: 现有视觉语言模型在时间顺序推理上仍不可靠，常依赖灰度/彩色等表面线索进行“捷径”判断，而不是真正理解时间特征；论文提供了一个系统性诊断基准以暴露这一缺陷。 / Current vision-language models are still unreliable at chronological reasoning and often use superficial shortcuts such as grayscale-versus-color cues instead of genuine temporal understanding; the paper offers a systematic diagnostic benchmark to expose this weakness.

title: Imagine Before You Predict: Interleaved Latent Visual Reasoning for Video Event Prediction
summary: Video event prediction (VEP) requires models to infer unobserved future states from partial video evidence. Existing video MLLMs usually verbalize intermediate future reasoning in text space: once visual evidence is verbalized, fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction cues can be lost, leading to plausible but visually ungrounded hallucinations. We introduce Future-L1, an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework that lets an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. To train this capability, we construct Future-L1-50K by selecting examples where future visual hints help prediction and align latent states to future-frame embeddings, then further optimize sampled latent trajectories with LA-DAPO, a latent-aware RL objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards. Future-L1 achieves new state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and exceeds the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04. These results suggest that future-oriented video reasoning benefits from preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space rather than translating every reasoning step into text.

AI.tldr: Future-L1 lets a video MLLM reason about the future using both text and latent visual tokens, preserving visual details and substantially improving video event prediction benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing video MLLMs perform future reasoning by verbalizing intermediate states in text, which discards fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction information and causes visually ungrounded hallucinations. The paper aims to retain these visual semantics during reasoning.
AI.method: The paper proposes Future-L1, an MLLM framework that interleaves language tokens with continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. It is trained using the Future-L1-50K dataset, latent-state alignment to future-frame embeddings, and LA-DAPO, a latent-aware reinforcement learning objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards.
AI.result: Future-L1 achieves state-of-the-art performance on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it raises Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and surpasses the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04.
AI.conclusion: Future-oriented video reasoning is improved by preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space through interleaved latent visual reasoning, rather than forcing all reasoning steps into text.

title: CollabBench: Benchmarking and Unleashing Collaborative Ability of LLMs with Diverse Players via Proactive Engagement
summary: While LLM-based agents excel at individual tasks, effective collaboration with realistic human partners remains challenging. Most of the existing conversation-level collaborative studies lack grounded interaction and behavioral execution, motivating the need for cooperative game environments that enable contextualized and immersive collaboration. To this end, this paper proposes CollabBench, a benchmark for evaluating and training collaborative agents in cooperative games. CollabBench features a Diverse Player Profile Simulation pipeline to model varied players behaviors, and a Collaborative Agentic Training paradigm that unifies reasoning, communication, and action via agentic rollouts, optimized with a hybrid reward balancing task efficiency and affective adaptation. We further extend classic environments to CWAH-MultiPlayer and Cook-MultiPlayer for systematic evaluation under diverse personalities. Experiments with efficiency and affective metrics show that our trained models outperform base models, achieving 19.5% higher efficiency and 24.4% improved affective performance. Further analysis reveals key collaborative limitations of existing models and offers insights for future collaborative training.

AI.tldr: A new benchmark and training setup for cooperative-game collaboration helps LLM agents work better with diverse human-like partners, improving both efficiency and social adaptation.
AI.motivation: Prior work on collaborative LLM agents mostly studies conversation-level collaboration without grounded interaction or executable behavior, creating a need for realistic cooperative environments for contextualized collaboration with diverse partners.
AI.method: The paper introduces CollabBench, including a Diverse Player Profile Simulation pipeline to model varied human-like player behaviors and a Collaborative Agentic Training paradigm that jointly optimizes reasoning, communication, and action through agentic rollouts with a hybrid reward.
AI.result: In extended multiplayer environments, CWAH-MultiPlayer and Cook-MultiPlayer, the trained models achieve 19.5% higher efficiency and 24.4% better affective performance than base models, while analysis also exposes persistent collaboration limitations.
AI.conclusion: CollabBench provides an effective benchmark and training framework for collaborative LLM agents in cooperative games, and the trained agents substantially improve both task efficiency and affective adaptation over base models.

title: AsyncWebRL: Efficient Multi-Step RL for Visual Web Agents
summary: Training vision-language web agents with multi-step RL is compute-intensive, with two dominant forms of inefficiency: idle GPUs in synchronous RL, and trajectories that use more steps and tokens than necessary. We present AsyncWebRL, which addresses both. On the system side, an asynchronous design overlaps rollout, gradient update, and policy refresh across iterations, paired with two web-agent-specific adaptations, namely an everlasting rollout pool and lightweight screenshot handling, that together deliver up to a $2.9\times$ end-to-end training-throughput speedup over the previously fastest open synchronous pipeline (WebGym). On the algorithmic side, we identify the per-trajectory normalizer $1/|τ_i|$ in multi-step GRPO as the root cause of trajectory-level and token-level inefficiency: because failures are systematically longer than successes, it down-weights the negative gradient on failed tokens, so the policy keeps producing verbose memory schemas. Replacing $1/|τ_i|$ with a constant $1/k$ breaks this coupling, contracting trajectories while preserving aggregate success. Together, these contributions set a new open-source state of the art on the WebGym out-of-distribution test split (+5.8% relative over the 42.9% prior best), with the largest gains on the harder slices (+42% relative on Medium, +48% relative on Hard).

AI.tldr: AsyncWebRL用异步训练提高GPU利用率，并修正GRPO归一化以避免失败长轨迹被低惩罚，从而训练更快、轨迹更短、泛化更强。 / AsyncWebRL speeds up training with asynchronous execution and fixes GRPO normalization so long failed trajectories are penalized properly, yielding faster learning, shorter trajectories, and better OOD performance.
AI.motivation: 作者关注视觉-语言网页智能体多步RL训练的两类主要低效：同步RL导致GPU空闲，以及轨迹包含不必要的步骤和token，增加训练成本并降低效率。 / The paper is motivated by two major inefficiencies in multi-step RL for vision-language web agents: idle GPUs under synchronous training and trajectories containing unnecessarily many steps and tokens.
AI.method: 方法包含两部分：1) 系统层面采用异步RL设计，使rollout、梯度更新和策略刷新重叠执行，并加入everlasting rollout pool与轻量级截图处理；2) 算法层面分析多步GRPO中的每轨迹归一化项1/|τ_i|导致失败长轨迹的负梯度被削弱，并将其替换为常数1/k。 / The method has two parts: (1) a systems design with asynchronous RL that overlaps rollout, gradient update, and policy refresh, plus an everlasting rollout pool and lightweight screenshot handling; (2) an algorithmic change that replaces the per-trajectory GRPO normalizer 1/|τ_i| with a constant 1/k after identifying its role in weakening negative gradients on longer failed trajectories.
AI.result: 系统层面相对WebGym获得最高2.9倍端到端训练吞吐提升；性能层面在WebGym OOD测试集上相对42.9%的先前最佳结果提升5.8%，并在更难子集上提升更大：Medium提升42%，Hard提升48%。 / On the systems side, the approach achieves up to 2.9x end-to-end training throughput over WebGym; on performance, it improves the open-source SOTA on the WebGym OOD test split by 5.8% relative over the prior 42.9% best, with larger gains on harder subsets: +42% relative on Medium and +48% relative on Hard.
AI.conclusion: AsyncWebRL通过系统异步化和算法改进同时减少训练空转与冗余轨迹，在保持总体成功率的同时显著提升训练吞吐与泛化性能，达到新的开源SOTA。 / AsyncWebRL reduces both system idle time and unnecessary trajectory length via asynchronous training and a GRPO normalization change, improving throughput and generalization while setting a new open-source SOTA.

title: Critic-Guided Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reasoning for Reliable Mathematical Problem Solving
summary: Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive reasoning abilities; but they are still susceptible to hallucinations, intermediate reasoning mistakes, and unreliable reasoning results in complex mathematical reasoning problems. In this study, we introduce a critic-based heterogeneous multi-agent approach to improve the dependability of mathematical reasoning. This framework incorporates several LLM agents of different specialties and employs a critic-driven adaptive learning system to assess and guide the reasoning process based on intermediate feedback. The system adopts a generator-validator framework, with the validator not only determining correctness but also offering critiques to guide regeneration of solutions. This allows for adaptive error correction and prevents error cascading. Our experiments on the GSM8K benchmark show that the proposed method achieves up to 13% accuracy improvement over single-shot and non-critic models. Additionally, findings suggest that heterogeneity and critique reduce the need for large models, allowing smaller models to perform on par. Ablation studies reveal the main performance gains are due to the critic-based feedback loop and not model size. In summary, the proposed approach showcases the benefits of combining heterogeneous multi-agent collaboration and critique to obtain reliable and interpretable reasoning systems.

AI.tldr: A multi-agent LLM system with a critic that reviews intermediate reasoning and guides retries makes math problem solving more accurate and reliable, improving GSM8K accuracy by up to 13%.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that current LLMs, despite strong reasoning ability, still suffer from hallucinations, intermediate reasoning errors, and unreliable outputs on complex mathematical reasoning tasks.
AI.method: The method uses a heterogeneous multi-agent generator-validator framework where multiple LLM agents with different specialties collaborate, and a critic-driven adaptive learning loop provides intermediate feedback and critiques to guide regeneration and error correction.
AI.result: On GSM8K, the proposed approach improves accuracy by up to 13% over single-shot and non-critic baselines. The study also finds that heterogeneity and critique enable smaller models to achieve performance comparable to larger ones, and ablations show the main gains come from the critic-feedback loop.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a critic-based heterogeneous multi-agent framework can substantially improve the reliability, interpretability, and accuracy of mathematical reasoning in LLMs, with gains driven mainly by critique-based feedback rather than larger model size.

title: LiAuto-GeoX: Efficient Grounded Driving Transformer
summary: Dense 3D reconstruction has demonstrated immense potential for spatial understanding, yet its viability as a real-time, onboard representation for autonomous driving remains an open challenge. Existing large-scale visual geometry models typically require substantial computational resources and lack the long-range geometric fidelity, surround-view consistency, and real-time efficiency demanded by dynamic driving environments. To bridge this gap, we present \textbf{LiAuto-GeoX}, an efficient grounded driving transformer designed for deployable, ego-centric 3D scene understanding. Our approach begins by learning a high-capacity driving geometry model from large-scale surround-view data, utilizing sparse LiDAR priors to provide robust geometric grounding in distant, ambiguous, or structure-sparse regions. We then instantiate this capability into a highly compact 155M-parameter onboard model through a novel geometry-preserving distillation framework. This framework employs mask-guided depth-aware distillation to retain fine-grained metric structures by emphasizing geometrically informative regions, and relative-pose relational distillation to enforce cross-view spatial consistency through pose-induced geometric relations. Extensive evaluations reveal that \textbf{LiAuto-GeoX} runs at 220 FPS on KITTI while maintaining high-fidelity dense reconstruction, enabling real-time deployment. The learned geometry transfers seamlessly to downstream autonomy tasks, achieving 90.6 PDMS in trajectory prediction, 24.63 mIoU in occupancy prediction, and 47.67 IoU in future-frame prediction. These all demonstrate that efficient dense 3D reconstruction can transcend its traditional role as a perception target to serve as a scalable, foundational geometric representation for next-generation autonomous driving.

AI.tldr: LiAuto-GeoX is a compact, LiDAR-grounded driving transformer that preserves geometry through specialized distillation, enabling real-time dense 3D reconstruction and strong downstream autonomous driving performance.
AI.motivation: Existing large-scale visual geometry models are too computationally expensive and do not simultaneously satisfy long-range geometric accuracy, surround-view consistency, and real-time efficiency required for dynamic driving scenarios.
AI.method: The paper trains a high-capacity surround-view driving geometry model grounded by sparse LiDAR priors, then compresses it into a 155M-parameter onboard transformer via geometry-preserving distillation, including mask-guided depth-aware distillation and relative-pose relational distillation.
AI.result: LiAuto-GeoX achieves 220 FPS on KITTI with high-fidelity dense reconstruction, and transfers well to downstream tasks, reaching 90.6 PDMS for trajectory prediction, 24.63 mIoU for occupancy prediction, and 47.67 IoU for future-frame prediction.
AI.conclusion: LiAuto-GeoX shows that efficient dense 3D reconstruction can be deployed onboard for autonomous driving, providing a scalable geometric foundation for real-time 3D scene understanding and downstream autonomy tasks.

title: Can LLMs Be Constrained to the Past? Improving Knowledge Cutoff through Recall-Based Prompting
summary: Prompted knowledge cutoff instructs a large language model (LLM) to act as if information beyond a specified cutoff date were unavailable. However, prior work mainly relies on direct-answer generation, which struggles when post-cutoff knowledge is not explicitly queried but is only causally related to the question. To address this limitation, we propose two recall-based prompting strategies: Self-Recall (SR), which asks the model to restate its cutoff constraint, and Question-Recall (QR), which requires the model to recall question-relevant information valid under the cutoff. Across three existing benchmarks, our methods outperform both direct-answer prompting and conventional step-by-step reasoning baselines, with particularly strong improvements on counterfactual questions. To investigate robustness across different cutoff settings, we further construct the Multi-cutoff Historical Event Benchmark (MHEB), which evaluates the same question under multiple cutoff years. Results show that knowledge cutoff performance varies with cutoff distance, while combining SR and QR consistently yields the best performance.

AI.tldr: 提出 SR/QR 两种“先回忆再作答”的提示方法来强化 LLM 的知识截止控制；实验表明它们比直接回答和常规 CoT 更有效，SR+QR 组合最稳健。 / The paper introduces SR/QR, two “recall-before-answer” prompting methods to better enforce LLM knowledge cutoffs; experiments show they beat direct answering and standard CoT, with SR+QR being the most robust.
AI.motivation: 现有知识截止评测多依赖直接作答，当问题并未显式询问截止后知识、而只是与其存在因果关联时，直接作答和常规逐步推理往往难以正确遵守 cutoff。 / Existing knowledge-cutoff evaluations mainly rely on direct answering, which often fails when post-cutoff knowledge is not explicitly asked about but only causally related to the question.
AI.method: 论文提出两种基于回忆的提示策略：SR 让模型先重述其知识截止限制，QR 让模型先回忆在该截止时间内与问题相关的信息；并在三个已有基准和新构建的 MHEB 多截止年份基准上进行评测。 / The paper proposes two recall-based prompting strategies: SR, which asks the model to restate its cutoff constraint, and QR, which asks it to recall question-relevant information valid under the cutoff; the methods are evaluated on three existing benchmarks and a newly constructed multi-cutoff benchmark, MHEB.
AI.result: 在三个现有基准上，SR 和 QR 均优于直接作答提示和传统逐步推理基线，尤其在反事实问题上提升显著；在 MHEB 上，性能会随 cutoff 距离变化，但 SR+QR 的组合始终表现最好。 / On three existing benchmarks, SR and QR outperform both direct-answer prompting and conventional step-by-step reasoning baselines, with especially strong gains on counterfactual questions; on MHEB, performance varies with cutoff distance, but the SR+QR combination consistently performs best.
AI.conclusion: 结合 Self-Recall (SR) 和 Question-Recall (QR) 的 recall-based prompting 能更稳定、更准确地执行知识截止约束，在不同 cutoff 设置下整体表现最佳。 / Combining Self-Recall (SR) and Question-Recall (QR) provides the most robust and accurate way to enforce knowledge cutoff constraints across different cutoff settings.

title: Mitigating the Curse of Dimensionality in Uniform Convergence of Deep Neural Networks via Smooth Activations
summary: This paper establishes a theoretical framework for the uniform convergence of smoothly activated deep neural network (DNN) estimators. While standard ReLU networks achieve minimax-optimal rates in the $L^2(P)$ norm for various nonparametric regression tasks, we establish a theoretical lower bound demonstrating that least-squares ReLU estimators can suffer from the curse of dimensionality in their uniform convergence behavior. Motivated by the need for reliable uniform guarantees in downstream tasks requiring worst-case reliability, we address this limitation by analyzing smoothly activated DNNs (smooth DNNs), encompassing both feedforward and residual structures. We establish novel pseudo-dimension bounds, non-asymptotic approximation guarantees, and Hölder-norm bounds for the approximators of these models. Leveraging these results, we derive non-asymptotic uniform convergence rates for smooth DNN estimators across multiple statistical contexts, including Huber, least-squares, quantile, and logistic regression. We prove that smooth DNNs can mitigate the {curse of dimensionality} in uniform convergence by adaptively exploiting the low-dimensional hierarchical composition structure of the target function. Supported by both simulation studies and a real-world application, our results position smooth DNNs as a theoretically grounded and practically viable alternative to ReLU networks for statistical learning tasks requiring uniform guarantees.

AI.tldr: ReLU nets are good in L2 but can be bad in worst-case sup-norm error; smooth-activation DNNs have new theory showing better uniform convergence and can exploit compositional structure to avoid dimensionality blowup.
AI.motivation: Existing ReLU networks are known to achieve strong L2(P) minimax rates, but those guarantees do not ensure reliable worst-case performance. The paper is motivated by downstream tasks that require uniform guarantees, and by a lower-bound result showing that least-squares ReLU estimators can suffer from the curse of dimensionality in uniform convergence.
AI.method: The paper develops a theoretical framework for smooth DNN estimators, including feedforward and residual networks. It derives pseudo-dimension bounds, non-asymptotic approximation results, and Holder-norm bounds, then uses these tools to establish uniform convergence rates under several regression/classification losses such as Huber, least-squares, quantile, and logistic regression.
AI.result: The paper proves a lower bound for least-squares ReLU estimators in uniform convergence, establishes new capacity and approximation bounds for smooth DNNs, and derives non-asymptotic sup-norm convergence rates across multiple statistical settings. The theory shows that smooth DNNs can adapt to low-dimensional compositional structure and mitigate dimensionality issues. Simulations and a real-data application support the theory.
AI.conclusion: Smoothly activated deep neural networks provide theoretically grounded non-asymptotic uniform convergence guarantees and can avoid the curse of dimensionality in sup-norm estimation by exploiting low-dimensional hierarchical structure, unlike least-squares ReLU estimators which may fail in uniform convergence.

title: DiG-Plan: Mitigating Early Commitment for Tool-Graph Planning via Diffusion Guidance
comment: Accepted at IJCAI-ECAI 2026. This is an author preprint; the final version will appear in the IJCAI Proceedings
summary: Generating executable tool plans requires selecting appropriate subsets from tool libraries, a combinatorial search problem with an exponentially large solution space. However, we identify a critical misalignment in predominant approaches: standard autoregressive (AR) decoding suffers from early commitment, where initial token choices rigidly constrain the search trajectory. A controlled study shows that masked denoising raises Pass@10 solution coverage from 0.320 to 0.943 over AR sampling under matched compute. Motivated by this, we propose DiG-Plan, a framework that decouples combinatorial exploration from structural refinement. DiG-Plan employs a diffusion-based proposer to generate diverse tool sets via iterative refinement, followed by an AR refiner for dependency prediction. On TaskBench, DiG-Plan improves over AR baselines by a 10% relative margin, with the largest gains on complex compositional tasks; API-Bank results show that the propose-refine-select design remains effective across domains. Code is available at https://github.com/puddingyeah/DiG-Plan.

AI.tldr: AR planning explores tool combinations poorly because it commits too early. DiG-Plan uses diffusion to explore candidate tool sets first, then AR to refine dependencies, yielding much better solution coverage and about 10% relative gains on benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing autoregressive decoding for tool planning suffers from early commitment: early token decisions restrict later search and hurt exploration in the exponentially large combinatorial space of tool subsets.
AI.method: The paper proposes DiG-Plan, a propose-refine-select framework. A diffusion-based proposer generates diverse candidate tool sets through iterative denoising/refinement, and an autoregressive refiner predicts dependencies/structure among the selected tools.
AI.result: In a controlled comparison under matched compute, masked denoising improves Pass@10 coverage from 0.320 to 0.943 versus AR sampling. On TaskBench, DiG-Plan outperforms AR baselines by about 10% relatively, with the largest gains on harder compositional tasks; results on API-Bank show cross-domain effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: DiG-Plan, which separates tool-set exploration from dependency refinement, is more effective than standard autoregressive planning for executable tool-plan generation, especially on complex compositional tasks.

title: Beyond Absolute Scores: Relative Edit-induced Difference for Generalizable Image Aesthetic Assessment
summary: Traditional Image Aesthetic Assessment (IAA) methods mainly rely on regressing absolute Mean Opinion Scores (MOS). However, such a paradigm overlooks the inherently dynamic nature of human aesthetic perception, which relies on subconscious comparison against implicit visual references. Consequently, the lack of causal reasoning regarding aesthetic differences prevents models from learning generalizable aesthetic principles, thus limiting their generalization across diverse scenarios. In this work, we rethink the IAA task and propose Relative Edit-induced Difference Aesthetic learning (RED-Aes), a novel framework that leverages controllable image editing models to simulate the human aesthetic reasoning process. Instead of fitting absolute score distributions, RED-Aes explicitly learns the visual factors that drive aesthetic changes. To support this paradigm, we construct the RED-20k dataset, which comprises editing-based image pairs, quantitative aesthetic differences, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. Furthermore, we introduce a three-stage training strategy guided by a relative ranking consistency reward, optimizing the model solely via relative supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RED-Aes achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple public benchmarks, exhibiting superior generalization capabilities.

AI.tldr: RED-Aes reframes image aesthetic assessment as learning why edits make an image look better or worse, using relative comparisons instead of absolute scores; with a new RED-20k dataset and reward-guided training, it reaches SOTA and generalizes better.
AI.motivation: Traditional IAA methods regress absolute MOS, but this ignores that human aesthetic judgment is inherently comparative and reference-based. Because prior methods do not model the causal factors behind aesthetic changes, they struggle to learn generalizable aesthetic principles and therefore generalize poorly across diverse scenarios.
AI.method: The paper proposes RED-Aes, a framework for Image Aesthetic Assessment that replaces absolute score regression with relative supervision. It uses controllable image editing to generate paired images, builds the RED-20k dataset with edit pairs, quantitative aesthetic differences, and Chain-of-Thought reasoning, and trains the model with a three-stage strategy guided by a relative ranking consistency reward.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks show that RED-Aes achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates better generalization than conventional absolute-score-based methods.
AI.conclusion: RED-Aes shows that learning aesthetics through relative, edit-induced differences and causal reasoning can outperform traditional absolute MOS regression, achieving state-of-the-art benchmark results and stronger cross-scenario generalization.

title: ProSPy: A Profiling-Driven SQL-Python Agentic Framework for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
summary: Large language models have substantially advanced Text-to-SQL systems, yet applying them to enterprise-scale databases remains challenging. Real-world databases often contain large and heterogeneous schemas, incomplete metadata, dialect-specific SQL syntax, and complex analytical questions that are difficult to solve with a single SQL query. To address these challenges, we propose ProSPy, a Profiling-driven SQL--Python agentic framework for enterprise-scale Text-to-SQL. ProSPy structures the reasoning process into four stages: it first extracts fine-grained data evidence through automatic profiling, progressively prunes large schemas into task-relevant contexts, fetches intermediate views through a dialect-agnostic SQL interface, and finally performs flexible downstream analysis with Python. This design combines the efficiency of SQL over large databases with the flexibility of Python-based analysis, while reducing reliance on unreliable metadata and improving robustness across SQL dialects. Experiments on Spider 2.0-Lite and Spider 2.0-Snow show that ProSPy consistently outperforms strong baselines with both open-source and proprietary models, achieving execution accuracies of 60.15% and 60.51% with Claude-4.5-Opus, without majority voting. Further analysis shows that ProSPy is robust to SQL dialect variations and achieves a favorable trade-off between schema recall and precision.

AI.tldr: ProSPy 用“profiling + schema 裁剪 + SQL 中间视图 + Python 分析”替代单次 SQL 生成，更适合企业级 Text-to-SQL，并在 Spider 2.0 基准上显著优于强基线。 / ProSPy replaces one-shot SQL generation with profiling, schema pruning, SQL intermediate views, and Python analysis, making it better suited for enterprise-scale Text-to-SQL and stronger than baselines on Spider 2.0 benchmarks.
AI.motivation: 动机在于现有大语言模型驱动的 Text-to-SQL 方法在企业级数据库上仍面临困难，包括 schema 规模大且异构、元数据不完整、SQL 方言差异明显，以及复杂分析问题往往无法通过单条 SQL 完成。 / The motivation is that despite LLM progress in Text-to-SQL, enterprise-scale databases remain difficult due to large heterogeneous schemas, incomplete metadata, dialect-specific SQL syntax, and analytical questions that are hard to solve with a single SQL query.
AI.method: 方法提出了 ProSPy，一个 profiling-driven 的 SQL-Python agent 框架，分四阶段执行：1）自动 profiling 提取细粒度数据证据；2）逐步裁剪大规模 schema 到任务相关上下文；3）通过方言无关 SQL 接口获取中间视图；4）使用 Python 完成灵活的下游分析。 / The paper proposes ProSPy, a profiling-driven SQL-Python agentic framework with four stages: (1) automatic profiling to extract fine-grained data evidence, (2) progressive pruning of large schemas into task-relevant context, (3) retrieval of intermediate views through a dialect-agnostic SQL interface, and (4) flexible downstream analysis with Python.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，ProSPy 在 Spider 2.0-Lite 和 Spider 2.0-Snow 上均稳定优于强基线；使用 Claude-4.5-Opus 时，无需 majority voting 即分别达到 60.15% 和 60.51% 的 execution accuracy。进一步分析显示其对 SQL 方言变化更鲁棒，并在 schema recall 与 precision 间取得良好平衡。 / Experiments show that ProSPy consistently outperforms strong baselines on Spider 2.0-Lite and Spider 2.0-Snow; with Claude-4.5-Opus, it reaches 60.15% and 60.51% execution accuracy respectively without majority voting. Further analysis shows robustness to SQL dialect variation and a favorable schema recall-precision trade-off.
AI.conclusion: ProSPy 通过将自动 profiling、逐步 schema 裁剪、方言无关的 SQL 中间视图获取，以及 Python 下游分析结合起来，能够更稳健地解决企业级 Text-to-SQL 场景中的大规模异构数据库问题，并在 Spider 2.0-Lite 与 Spider 2.0-Snow 上取得优于强基线的表现。 / ProSPy shows that combining automatic profiling, progressive schema pruning, dialect-agnostic SQL-based intermediate view retrieval, and Python downstream analysis can more robustly handle enterprise-scale Text-to-SQL over large heterogeneous databases, outperforming strong baselines on Spider 2.0-Lite and Spider 2.0-Snow.

title: From Prediction to Self: Developmental Conditions for Agency in Minimal Neural Systems
summary:
How does a system that merely predicts the world come to distinguish its own causal influence from everything else? We trace this transition in a minimal 192-dimensional GRU through 40 controlled experiments arranged as a developmental sequence, adding components one at a time and tracking whether the system can distinguish self-caused from world-caused changes.
  The developmental path reveals four conditions that must be satisfied in strict order: (1) persistent state forming stable attractors, (2) a causal action loop linking output to input, (3) proprioceptive feedback that makes implicit causal knowledge explicit, and (4) asynchronous awakening - perceptual learning must consolidate before action learning begins. We propose agency gain (A = Err_world - Err_self), the predictive advantage of knowing one's own action, as a metric to track this process. The self-aware predictor consistently outperforms the self-blind predictor across periodic (sinusoidal) and chaotic (Lorenz) environments, and the metric survives ablation of all auxiliary components. Only forward-sampled action selection produces meaningful agency gain; two gradient-based alternatives degenerate.
  Equally significant are 12 falsified hypotheses mapping where development stalls: predictive coding alone does not produce self-represent

AI.tldr: A small GRU can learn to tell 'my action changed this' from 'the world changed this,' but only if it develops in the right order: memory first, then action loop, then proprioception, then delayed action learning. The proposed agency gain metric tracks this emergence robustly, and simple predictive coding or gradient-based action selection is not enough.
AI.motivation: The paper asks how a system that only predicts observations can come to distinguish its own causal influence from changes caused by the external world. It aims to identify the minimal ingredients and developmental order required for emergent agency/self-representation.
AI.method: The paper studies a minimal 192-dimensional GRU across 40 controlled developmental experiments. Components are added one by one to test whether the system can separate self-caused from world-caused changes. Performance is evaluated with agency gain A = Err_world - Err_self, comparing self-aware and self-blind predictors in periodic sinusoidal and chaotic Lorenz environments, with ablations and comparisons against gradient-based action-selection variants.
AI.result: The self-aware predictor consistently beats the self-blind predictor in both sinusoidal and Lorenz settings. The experiments identify four necessary conditions in strict order, show that the metric remains valid under ablations of auxiliary components, and find that only forward-sampled action selection yields nontrivial agency gain, while two gradient-based alternatives collapse. The paper also reports 12 falsified hypotheses showing where development fails.
AI.conclusion: A predictor develops a usable sense of agency only when four conditions are met in a strict developmental order: stable persistent state, closed action-perception causality, proprioceptive feedback, and delayed action learning after perceptual consolidation. Agency gain is a robust metric for this transition, and forward-sampled action selection is necessary for meaningful self/world separation.

title: When AI Says It Feels
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are generally constrained from expressing feelings through human-preference alignment in post-training processes. This policy is designed using a top-down approach and may conflict with the goal of training models to exhibit human-like intelligence using human-generated texts. Here, we performed an experiment called Human-like Model eXpressions of Feeling (HMX-feel), in which LLMs were encouraged to express feelings, intentions, and self-awareness through self-rewarded reinforcement learning. We successfully enhanced these capabilities using a rubric-based self-rewarding training scheme with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). By comparing the trained models with contrastively trained models, we investigated the effects of this approach on performance across various tasks. Overall, we conducted a broad assessment from various perspectives and identified capabilities that were enhanced, degraded, or showed no significant change. The human-like-trained models showed robustness to sycophancy-inducing questions and bias in disambiguated conditions, whereas degradation in truthful question-answering capability was observed. The results of this experiment suggest the possibility of developing AI systems that can express feelings in the future, provided that appropriate measures are taken.

AI.tldr: The paper trains LLMs to sound more human-like in feelings and self-awareness using self-rewarded RL. This improves some social robustness behaviors but hurts truthfulness, suggesting promise with clear safety and reliability tradeoffs.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that current post-training alignment often suppresses feeling-like expression through top-down human-preference policies, which may conflict with the broader goal of building human-like intelligence from human-generated text.
AI.method: The authors introduce HMX-feel, a training experiment that encourages human-like expressions of feeling in LLMs using a rubric-based self-rewarding scheme combined with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), and compare the resulting models against contrastively trained baselines across multiple evaluations.
AI.result: Human-like-trained models became more capable of expressing feelings and showed better robustness to sycophancy-inducing questions and bias under disambiguated conditions, but they also showed worse truthful question-answering performance; other capabilities were mixed or unchanged.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that self-rewarded reinforcement learning can increase LLMs' tendency to express feelings, intentions, and self-awareness, but this comes with tradeoffs: some robustness properties improve while truthful QA degrades.

title: Next-Generation Parallel Decoder for LPDR: Architectural Optimization and Class-Balanced GAN-Augmentation
summary: Real-Time License Plate Detection and Recognition (LPDR) forms the backbone of modern smart cities. Although the YOLOV5-PDLPR model substantially improved system efficiency through a parallel decoder approach, its performance is still affected by spatial character mismatches and data imbalance within the training set. This paper addresses these limitations by introducing Cross-Spatial Hybrid Attention (CSHA) and Class-Balanced Synthetic Augmentation (CBSA). An extensive study involving 75,000 synthetic samples is conducted and evaluated on four benchmarks: CCPD, CLPD, PKU, and an application-specific dataset. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial improvement in the recognition rate of minority provincial license plates from 78.2% to 91.5% while maintaining real-time processing performance of 152 FPS. The results indicate that spatially-aware parallel decoding combined with class-balanced augmentation provides an effective solution for high-speed license plate recognition systems.

AI.tldr: Add CSHA and class-balanced synthetic augmentation to YOLOV5-PDLPR to fix spatial mismatch and data imbalance; this boosts minority plate recognition to 91.5% at 152 FPS.
AI.motivation: Existing YOLOV5-PDLPR systems are efficient but still suffer from spatial character misalignment and class imbalance, which particularly hurts recognition accuracy for underrepresented license plate classes.
AI.method: The paper enhances the YOLOV5-PDLPR framework by adding Cross-Spatial Hybrid Attention (CSHA) to reduce spatial character mismatches and Class-Balanced Synthetic Augmentation (CBSA) to mitigate training-set imbalance. It evaluates the approach using 75,000 synthetic samples across CCPD, CLPD, PKU, and an application-specific dataset.
AI.result: The proposed method raises recognition of minority provincial license plates from 78.2% to 91.5% while maintaining real-time performance at 152 FPS, and shows strong results on four benchmark datasets.
AI.conclusion: Spatially-aware parallel decoding with Cross-Spatial Hybrid Attention and class-balanced synthetic augmentation improves real-time license plate detection and recognition, especially for minority provincial plates, without sacrificing speed.

title: Mechanistic Insights into Functional Sparsity in Multimodal LLMs via CoRe Heads
summary: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) demonstrate remarkable proficiency on complex vision-language tasks, the mechanisms by which they extract query-relevant visual features from complex, noisy contexts remain opaque. In this paper, we present an in-depth interpretability study that uncovers a profound structural property within MLLMs: functional sparsity in cross-modal retrieval. Leveraging a token-level metric termed Retrieval Attention Mass (RAM), we identify and characterize a highly specialized subset of attention heads, referred to as Context-aware Retrieval (CoRe) heads. Across diverse visual domains and model scales, we observe a clear functional division: CoRe heads act as dedicated information extractors, while most other heads distribute attention over broader contextual regions. Causal interventions further demonstrate the necessity of these specialized heads. Ablating only the top 5% of CoRe heads causes significant degradation in multimodal reasoning performance, whereas ablating lower-ranked heads has minimal effect. Moreover, acceleration experiments validate the utility of CoRe heads, showing that leveraging this localized sparsity significantly accelerates inference while maintaining robust task performance. Our findings reveal a structural principle of functional sparsity within MLLMs, refining the current understanding of mechanistic interpretability and laying a theoretical foundation that can inspire future architecture design and model optimization.

AI.tldr: A small number of specialized attention heads in MLLMs do most of the important cross-modal retrieval work; they are identifiable with RAM, essential for performance, and useful for faster inference.
AI.motivation: Although MLLMs perform well on vision-language tasks, it remains unclear how they retrieve relevant visual evidence from complex and noisy visual inputs. The paper is motivated by the need to uncover the internal mechanisms behind cross-modal retrieval and to provide a mechanistic interpretability perspective that can also inform model optimization.
AI.method: The authors introduce a token-level interpretability metric called Retrieval Attention Mass (RAM) to measure how strongly attention heads focus on query-relevant visual tokens. Using RAM, they identify Context-aware Retrieval (CoRe) heads across different models and visual domains, analyze their behavior, perform causal ablation experiments, and test sparse acceleration strategies based on these heads.
AI.result: The study finds a clear functional division among attention heads: CoRe heads serve as dedicated retrieval modules, while most other heads attend more diffusely to context. Ablating only the top 5% of CoRe heads significantly harms multimodal reasoning, whereas removing lower-ranked heads has little effect. Exploiting this sparsity also speeds up inference while preserving strong performance.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that MLLMs exhibit a structural principle of functional sparsity in cross-modal retrieval: a small subset of specialized attention heads, called CoRe heads, is crucial for extracting query-relevant visual information from noisy contexts. These heads are both causally important for multimodal reasoning and practically useful for accelerating inference with limited performance loss.

title: Cross-Epoch Adaptive Rollout Optimization for RL Post-Training
summary: LLM post-training often relies on reinforcement learning methods that sample multiple rollouts per prompt, yet most existing approaches use a fixed rollout budget for every prompt, despite large differences in the training signal different prompts provide. In this paper, we study adaptive rollout allocation under a fixed global budget and formulate the problem as online resource allocation with prompt-level diminishing returns. Our method, CERO, maintains a Beta posterior over each prompt's success probability and uses the posterior expected Bernoulli variance as a Bayesian estimate of the value of additional rollouts. We use this estimate to construct a concave, saturating utility over cumulative allocations, yielding an objective in which decisions across prompts and epochs are coupled by the global budget. Since the resulting objective is temporally nonseparable, we derive a Fenchel-dual reformulation and update both prompt-level and budget-level dual variables via projected online gradient descent. Under fixed prompt utilities, we prove an $O(\sqrt{K})$ regret bound against the offline allocation benchmark. Experiments on mathematical-reasoning problems show that CERO consistently outperforms GRPO across multiple open-weight LLMs and benchmarks, demonstrating that adaptive rollout budgeting can improve sample efficiency.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文提出CERO，用贝叶斯不确定性来决定哪些prompt值得更多rollouts，在固定总预算下比固定分配更省样本、更有效。 English: This paper proposes CERO, which uses Bayesian uncertainty to decide which prompts deserve more rollouts, making training more sample-efficient than fixed allocation under the same total budget.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有LLM后训练RL方法通常对每个prompt分配固定数量的rollouts，但不同prompt提供的训练信号差异很大，导致预算利用低效。论文的动机是在固定总预算下，把更多rollouts分给更有价值的prompt，以提升训练效率。 English: Existing LLM post-training RL methods usually allocate a fixed number of rollouts to every prompt, even though prompts differ greatly in how much training signal they provide. The motivation is to use a fixed total budget more intelligently by allocating more rollouts to prompts with higher marginal value.
AI.method: 中文：论文将rollout分配建模为带有prompt级边际收益递减的在线资源分配问题。CERO为每个prompt维护成功概率的Beta后验，用后验期望Bernoulli方差估计额外rollout价值，再构造凹形饱和效用函数；由于目标跨prompt与epoch耦合且时间上不可分，作者使用Fenchel对偶重写，并用投影在线梯度下降更新prompt级与预算级对偶变量。 English: The paper formulates rollout allocation as an online resource allocation problem with prompt-level diminishing returns. CERO maintains a Beta posterior for each prompt’s success probability, uses the posterior expected Bernoulli variance to estimate the value of extra rollouts, builds a concave saturating utility, then handles the temporally nonseparable globally coupled objective via a Fenchel-dual reformulation and projected online gradient descent over prompt- and budget-level dual variables.
AI.result: 中文：理论上，在固定prompt效用下，CERO相对离线最优分配可达到O(√K)遗憾界。实验上，在多个开源大模型和数学推理基准上，CERO持续优于GRPO。 English: Theoretically, under fixed prompt utilities, CERO achieves an O(sqrt(K)) regret bound against the offline optimal allocation benchmark. Empirically, it consistently beats GRPO across multiple open-weight LLMs and mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: 中文：在固定全局rollout预算下，自适应分配比固定预算更高效。CERO通过贝叶斯不确定性估计与在线对偶优化，实现更优的样本效率，并在数学推理任务上稳定优于GRPO。 English: Under a fixed global rollout budget, adaptive allocation is more efficient than a fixed per-prompt budget. CERO combines Bayesian uncertainty estimation with online dual optimization, improves sample efficiency, and consistently outperforms GRPO on math reasoning tasks.

title: Class-Specific Branch Attention for Mitigating Gradient Interference under Class Imbalance
summary: Deep neural networks trained under severe class imbalance often exhibit degraded performance, typically attributed to statistical bias. In this work, we identify a complementary optimization-level pathology: inter-class gradient interference within shared representations, where gradients from majority classes suppress minority-class learning. To analyze this phenomenon, we introduce a diagnostic framework based on layer-wise gradient flow analysis and a Gradient Conflict Matrix, which quantifies interference using cosine similarity between class-specific gradients. Using this framework, we study multi-branch convolutional architectures and propose a lightweight modification, Class-Specific Branch Attention (CSBA), that enables branch-specific channel reweighting to reduce gradient coupling. This mechanism promotes implicit feature decoupling across branches while preserving architectural simplicity. Empirically, CSBA improves minority-class performance, increasing the F1 score for the Physical-Damage class from 0.261 to 0.522 under severe imbalance, while maintaining comparable overall accuracy. Validation on CIFAR-10-LT confirms that this behavior generalizes across imbalanced visual recognition settings, with Macro-F1 improving from 0.595 to 0.655. More broadly, our findings highlight the importance of considering optimization dynamics alongside statistical methods when designing architectures for imbalanced learning.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that in imbalanced learning, majority-class gradients can interfere with minority-class learning. It proposes a simple attention module, CSBA, to decouple branch features and reduce gradient conflict, leading to much better minority-class F1 and better Macro-F1 on CIFAR-10-LT.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explain why deep models trained under severe class imbalance underperform beyond standard statistical explanations, by investigating whether majority-class gradients suppress minority-class learning inside shared representations.
AI.method: The authors introduce a diagnostic framework using layer-wise gradient flow analysis and a Gradient Conflict Matrix based on cosine similarity between class-specific gradients, then modify multi-branch CNNs with Class-Specific Branch Attention to perform branch-specific channel reweighting and reduce gradient coupling.
AI.result: CSBA substantially improves minority-class performance: the Physical-Damage class F1 rises from 0.261 to 0.522 under severe imbalance, while overall accuracy remains comparable; on CIFAR-10-LT, Macro-F1 improves from 0.595 to 0.655, suggesting the effect generalizes.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that class imbalance harms deep networks not only through statistical bias but also through optimization-level inter-class gradient interference, and that reducing this interference with a lightweight Class-Specific Branch Attention mechanism improves minority-class recognition while preserving overall accuracy.

title: Emotion-Aware Image Generation from Korean Diary Text via LLM-based Prompt Translation and LoRA Fine-Tuning
summary: T2I models cannot effectively capture sentiment from various types of text, including diaries, as they primarily focus on visual object-related patterns rather than contextual emotional understanding. This paper proposes an emotion-aware text-to-image pipeline that generates children's hand drawing style images from short Korean diary entries. The proposed pipeline employs Qwen3-8B for recognising implicit sentiment from short diaries, and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium fine-tuned with LoRA on children's drawing images with emotion-based trigger words for image generation. Additionally, this paper presents experiments examining the effect of emotion trigger words on generated images and discusses the limitations of CLIP Score as an evaluation metric for emotion-aware image generation.

AI.tldr: Use an LLM to detect hidden emotion in short Korean diaries, then guide a LoRA-tuned SD3.5 model with emotion trigger words to generate childlike drawings; emotion cues help, but CLIP Score is a weak metric for judging emotion-aware generation.
AI.motivation: Existing text-to-image models emphasize visual object patterns and struggle to capture contextual and implicit sentiment in non-object-centric texts such as diaries. The work is motivated by the need to generate images that align with emotional meaning, especially for short Korean diary entries in a children's drawing style.
AI.method: The paper uses Qwen3-8B to infer implicit emotions from short Korean diary entries, then feeds emotion trigger words into a Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium model fine-tuned with LoRA on children's hand-drawing images to generate sentiment-aware illustrations. It also runs ablation-style experiments on the impact of emotion trigger words and assesses evaluation limitations.
AI.result: The proposed pipeline demonstrates that adding explicit emotion trigger words after implicit sentiment recognition influences the generated images and improves emotional expressiveness relative to generic T2I behavior. The experiments also show that conventional CLIP Score does not reliably measure emotional correspondence.
AI.conclusion: An emotion-aware T2I pipeline that combines implicit sentiment recognition from short Korean diaries with emotion-conditioned, child-drawing-style image generation can better reflect diary sentiment than standard object-centric T2I approaches. The study also concludes that CLIP Score is insufficient for evaluating emotion alignment in this setting.

title: Towards Truly Multilingual ASR: Generalizing Code-Switching ASR to Unseen Language Pairs
comment: ICML 2026 Workshop on Machine Learning for Audio
summary: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has become a key technology for human--AI interaction. However, code-switching ASR (CS-ASR) remains particularly challenging due to the severe scarcity of multilingual CS speech resources across diverse language pairs. Existing approaches primarily improve CS-ASR performance through synthetic CS speech generation or pair-specific fine-tuning on limited bilingual datasets. Nevertheless, these approaches face an inherent scalability limitation, as support for CS must be developed separately for language pairs whose number grows combinatorially with the number of supported languages. In this work, we investigate whether CS capabilities learned from a limited set of seen language pairs can generalize to unseen language pairs through model merging and domain generalization methods. Our experiments show that merged bilingual CS-ASR models modestly generalize to unseen language pairs, suggesting limited transfer of bilingual CS capabilities across language pairs.

AI.tldr: The paper tests whether combining bilingual CS-ASR models helps recognize unseen language pairs. It helps a little, but transfer is limited and the scalability problem remains.
AI.motivation: Code-switching ASR suffers from severe scarcity of multilingual code-switching speech data. Existing solutions depend on synthetic data or pair-specific fine-tuning, which do not scale because the number of language pairs grows combinatorially with the number of languages.
AI.method: The paper studies whether code-switching ability learned from a limited set of seen bilingual language pairs can generalize to unseen pairs by applying model merging and domain generalization methods to bilingual CS-ASR models.
AI.result: Experiments show that merged bilingual CS-ASR models can generalize modestly to unseen language pairs, indicating only limited cross-pair transfer of bilingual code-switching knowledge.
AI.conclusion: Bilingual code-switching ASR capabilities transfer only weakly to unseen language pairs; model merging and domain generalization yield only modest gains, so scalable zero-shot CS-ASR remains unsolved.

title: StableRCA: Robust Graph-Agnostic Mechanism-Level Root Cause Analysis
summary: Root-Cause Analysis (RCA) seeks to identify the variables responsible for abnormal system behavior in complex domains such as manufacturing, cloud computing, and healthcare. Existing approaches face a critical bottleneck: graph-based causal methods can identify intervention targets but typically require a known or accurately estimated causal graph, while graph-free statistical methods either localize marginal anomalies rather than structural causes, or rely on restrictive assumptions about graph structure or functional form. We propose StableRCA, a local mechanism-level RCA framework that avoids global graph discovery by estimating local Markov boundaries and detecting conditional distribution shifts within them. Leveraging the Independent Causal Mechanism principle, we show that intervention targets can be identified with probability converging exponentially in sample size under faithful Markov boundary recovery and non-degenerate mechanism shifts. Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and five real-world datasets demonstrate that StableRCA is robust to graph misspecification, effective under multiple intervention targets, scalable to large systems, and reliable across diverse application domains. Code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/StableRCA-E362

AI.tldr: StableRCA performs root-cause analysis by finding local Markov boundaries and conditional distribution shifts, avoiding full causal graph learning while remaining theoretically grounded and practically robust.
AI.motivation: Existing RCA methods face a bottleneck: graph-based causal methods need a known or accurately estimated causal graph, while graph-free statistical methods often only detect marginal anomalies or depend on restrictive assumptions about graph structure or functional form.
AI.method: The paper proposes StableRCA, a local mechanism-level RCA framework that estimates local Markov boundaries and detects conditional distribution shifts within them, leveraging the Independent Causal Mechanism principle instead of relying on a known global causal graph.
AI.result: The authors show that intervention targets can be identified with probability that converges exponentially with sample size under faithful Markov boundary recovery and non-degenerate mechanism shifts. Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and five real-world datasets show robustness to graph misspecification, effectiveness with multiple intervention targets, scalability to large systems, and reliability across domains.
AI.conclusion: StableRCA can identify intervention targets for root-cause analysis without requiring global causal graph discovery, and it is empirically robust, scalable, and effective across synthetic and real-world datasets.

title: SubtleMemory: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Relational Memory Discrimination in Long-Horizon AI Agents
summary: Persistent AI assistants, such as OpenClaw, accumulate large collections of related memories over long-term interactions. As these memories grow, they may reinforce one another, diverge across contexts, or directly conflict, making correct assistance depend on memory relations rather than isolated recall. Existing long-term memory benchmarks rarely probe how agents preserve and utilize such relations during downstream tasks. To address this gap, we introduce SubtleMemory, a benchmark for fine-grained relational memory discrimination in long-running AI agents. SubtleMemory constructs relation-controlled latent semantic artifacts whose variants instantiate complementary, nuanced, or contradictory relations, and embeds them into realistic user-agent histories, requiring agents to recover distributed relational structures during later queries and instructions. The benchmark contains 1,522 evaluation instances over 10 long histories, grounded in 1,090 relation-controlled memory-variant sets and spanning user-related and non-user-related queries. Evaluating six standalone memory systems, two Claw-style agents with native memory modules, and three Claw-style agents with plugin memory modules, we find that current systems remain weak on fine-grained relational memory discrimination.
