We further introduce diagnostic protocols that reveal distinct capability profiles across memory preservation, retrieval, and downstream reasoning stages.

AI.tldr: This paper presents SubtleMemory, a benchmark for testing whether long-term AI agents can track subtle relationships among memories across long interactions. Existing memory systems struggle significantly, and the benchmark helps pinpoint whether failures come from storing, retrieving, or reasoning over memories.
AI.motivation: Persistent AI assistants accumulate many related memories over time. As memory collections grow, relations among memories—reinforcement, divergence, and contradiction—become critical for correct behavior, but prior benchmarks mostly test isolated recall rather than relational memory use.
AI.method: The paper introduces SubtleMemory, a benchmark built from relation-controlled latent semantic artifacts with complementary, nuanced, or contradictory variants. These artifacts are embedded into realistic long user-agent interaction histories, and agents are later tested on queries/instructions that require reconstructing distributed relational memory structure.
AI.result: SubtleMemory includes 1,522 evaluation instances across 10 long histories and 1,090 relation-controlled memory-variant sets. Evaluations on six standalone memory systems, two native-memory Claw-style agents, and three plugin-memory Claw-style agents show broadly weak performance on subtle relational memory tasks. Diagnostic protocols further separate failures across preservation, retrieval, and reasoning stages.
AI.conclusion: Current long-term memory systems for AI assistants perform poorly at fine-grained relational memory discrimination, and SubtleMemory exposes distinct weaknesses in memory preservation, retrieval, and downstream reasoning.

title: Gender Artifacts from Art History to Text-to-Image Generation
summary: Artistic styles are rooted in specific socio-historical contexts that encode social hierarchies, including distinct constructions of gender. Yet in AI research, style has long been treated as a surface-level visual property: a filter of color, brushstroke, and texture applied to otherwise content-neutral scenes. We introduce the first dataset to investigate the interplay between gender representation and style in both historical and generated images. StyleGender comprises 74k images spanning 19 artistic styles, comprising art historical images with style and gender annotations, T2I-generated images under controlled style and gender prompts, and a semantically aligned set enabling direct art history-to-generation comparison. By proposing two Set Gender Artifact (SGA) metrics (PixelSGA and MaskSGA), capturing gender signals at the pixel level and in compositional structure, we show that (1) gender representation shapes visual features across artistic styles, (2) style keywords carry these patterns into T2I generation, and (3) generative models tend to amplify gender artifacts beyond what is observed in historical sources.

AI.tldr: This paper builds a new dataset and metrics to show that artistic style carries gendered visual patterns, and text-to-image models reproduce and often intensify those patterns.
AI.motivation: Prior AI research has treated artistic style as a superficial visual attribute while ignoring its socio-historical grounding and its relationship to social hierarchies such as gender. The paper aims to systematically study how gender representation and artistic style interact in both historical art and modern image generation.
AI.method: The paper introduces StyleGender, a 74k-image dataset covering 19 artistic styles, combining art historical images with style and gender annotations, controlled text-to-image generations with style and gender prompts, and a semantically aligned comparison set. It also proposes two Set Gender Artifact metrics, PixelSGA and MaskSGA, to measure gender signals in low-level pixels and compositional structure.
AI.result: The study finds that gender representation significantly shapes visual features across styles, that style prompts transfer these gendered patterns into generated images, and that generative models tend to amplify gender artifacts relative to historical sources.
AI.conclusion: Gender representation is deeply entangled with artistic style, and text-to-image models not only inherit these style-linked gender patterns from historical imagery but often exaggerate them beyond the historical record.

title: Forgive or forget: Understanding the context of hate in audio retrieval systems
summary: Handling toxic retrieval in text-to-audio systems is challenging due to contextual dependencies. Existing strategies (e.g., rephrasing, summarization) risk altering intent or omitting details. We propose a post hoc causal debiasing framework with a sentiment-controlled mediator to preserve semantic relevance while suppressing harmful speech. Our approach is model-agnostic and integrates seamlessly with existing retrieval pipelines. We introduce two variants: Forgive, which re-ranks and filters toxic audio via logit adjustment, and Forget, which generates counterfactual toxic prompts to mitigate harmful retrievals. Experiments show consistent toxicity reduction with minimal loss in retrieval accuracy, improving both safety and reliability.

AI.tldr: A model-agnostic post hoc debiasing framework for text-to-audio retrieval reduces toxic outputs using sentiment-controlled causal mediation, with two variants that improve safety while keeping retrieval performance nearly intact.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that toxic retrieval in text-to-audio systems is difficult to handle because toxicity depends on context. Existing mitigation methods such as rephrasing or summarization can distort user intent or remove important details, so a safer approach that preserves semantics is needed.
AI.method: The method introduces a post hoc causal debiasing framework for text-to-audio retrieval. It uses a sentiment-controlled mediator and proposes two variants: Forgive, which re-ranks and filters toxic audio through logit adjustment, and Forget, which generates counterfactual toxic prompts to mitigate harmful retrieval behavior.
AI.result: Experiments show that both variants consistently reduce toxicity with only minimal degradation in retrieval accuracy, improving system safety and reliability.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that post hoc causal debiasing with a sentiment-controlled mediator can reduce toxic retrieval in text-to-audio systems while largely preserving retrieval quality, offering a practical and model-agnostic safety layer.

title: Q-GNN: Query-Conditioned Graph Neural Networks with Type Awareness for Knowledge Graph Completion
summary: Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims at predicting missing triplets from incomplete knowledge graphs, which is crucial for downstream applications. Recently, Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based methods have achieved remarkable success by performing message passing over query-centered local subgraphs. However, in practice, a query is jointly defined by both the entity and the relation, with both carrying information indispensable for reasoning, yet these methods rely solely on the query relation as the guiding signal, while the information inherent in the query entity is not leveraged to guide inference - the entity serves merely as a structural anchor for subgraph extraction. To this end, we incorporate query entity information into the reasoning process from two perspectives: the first is structural context, i.e., the neighboring structure and relation patterns around the entity, which is encoded by a dedicated context encoder and used to modulate messages; the second is semantic type of the entity, inferred by a large language model, which is incorporated into attention computation and final scoring to provide type-level prior constraints. Together, these two sources of information enable the reasoning process to be guided by both the query relation and the query entity. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Q-GNN.

AI.tldr: Q-GNN为知识图谱补全引入“实体感知”推理：既利用实体周围结构上下文，也利用LLM推断的实体语义类型，从而比只看关系的GNN方法效果更好。 / Q-GNN makes KGC reasoning entity-aware by using both the entity’s local structural context and LLM-inferred semantic type, outperforming relation-only GNN baselines.
AI.motivation: 现有基于GNN的KGC方法主要以查询关系作为推理引导信号，而忽略了查询实体本身携带的关键信息，实体通常只被当作子图抽取的锚点。论文旨在弥补这一缺陷，使推理同时受关系与实体共同引导。 / Existing GNN-based KGC methods mainly use the query relation as the guiding signal and ignore the rich information in the query entity, which is often treated only as an anchor for subgraph extraction. This work aims to make reasoning jointly guided by both relation and entity.
AI.method: 论文提出Q-GNN，从两个角度引入查询实体信息：1）结构上下文：用专门的上下文编码器建模实体周围的邻域结构与关系模式，并用于调制消息传递；2）语义类型：利用大语言模型推断实体语义类型，并将其融入注意力计算和最终打分，提供类型先验约束。 / The paper proposes Q-GNN, incorporating query entity information from two aspects: (1) structural context, encoded by a dedicated context encoder to capture neighborhood structure and relation patterns and modulate message passing; (2) semantic type, inferred by an LLM and injected into attention and final scoring as type-level prior constraints.
AI.result: 在标准基准数据集上的实验表明，Q-GNN是有效的，并优于仅依赖查询关系引导的现有方法。 / Experiments on standard benchmarks show that Q-GNN is effective and outperforms methods guided only by the query relation.
AI.conclusion: Q-GNN通过同时利用查询关系与查询实体信息进行推理，能够有效提升知识图谱补全性能。 / Q-GNN improves knowledge graph completion by jointly leveraging query relation and query entity information during reasoning.

title: TAPO: Tool-Aware Policy Optimization via Credit Transfer for Multimodal Search Agents
summary: We identify and formally characterize credit misassignment as a systematic failure mode of GRPO in tool-augmented multimodal search agents: its uniform broadcast of trajectory-level advantages to all tokens causes valuable tool-use steps in failing trajectories to be penalized no differently from valueless ones. We further empirically quantify the scale of this phenomenon. Over half of failing trajectories and failing tool-use actions exhibit correctable credit misassignment, demonstrating that the wasted training signal is both substantial and structurally exploitable. Building on this insight, we propose Tool-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO), which exploits the parameter-determinism property of information-acquisition tools: similar call parameters define equivalent information-acquisition actions and should therefore share comparable action credit. TAPO constructs counterfactual witnesses within the current training batch and compensates misassigned negative credit via confidence-gated conservative advantage correction. It requires no additional annotation, models, or sampling, and introduces negligible computational overhead. Across multiple multimodal search benchmarks, TAPO delivers consistent, plug-and-play improvements over strong baselines for three mainstream RL algorithms (GRPO, GSPO, and SAPO). Our code and models will be publicly released upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that RL for tool-using multimodal agents often blames good tool calls inside bad trajectories, then fixes this with TAPO, a low-cost batch-level credit correction method that improves multiple RL algorithms.
AI.motivation: In tool-augmented multimodal search agents, trajectory-level advantage is uniformly broadcast to all tokens, so useful tool-use actions inside failed trajectories are penalized the same as useless ones. This wastes substantial training signal and harms learning.
AI.method: The paper identifies credit misassignment in GRPO-style training, then proposes Tool-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO), which uses the parameter-determinism of information-acquisition tools to find counterfactual witnesses within the same batch and apply confidence-gated conservative advantage correction to repair wrongly assigned negative credit.
AI.result: Empirically, more than half of failing trajectories and failing tool-use actions contain correctable credit misassignment. TAPO yields consistent plug-and-play gains over strong baselines across several multimodal search benchmarks and works with GRPO, GSPO, and SAPO.
AI.conclusion: TAPO effectively mitigates credit misassignment in tool-augmented multimodal search agents and consistently improves performance across multiple benchmarks and RL algorithms with minimal overhead.

title: Learning Geometric Representations from Videos for Spatial Intelligent Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at 2D semantic understanding but lack intrinsic 3D awareness, resulting in representations that fail to maintain geometric and spatial consistency across video frames. Given the scarcity of large-scale 3D data, we present GeoVR, a novel framework that learns geometric representations using purely 2D video sequences. This approach effectively restructures the semantic latent space within MLLMs to unlock spatial intelligence. Rather than employing superficial feature mixing, GeoVR reshapes the internal representations of the MLLM by distilling geometry knowledge from pre-trained 3D foundation models. This is accomplished through a multi-objective learning strategy driven by four complementary geometric targets: (1) estimating inter-frame camera poses to embed varying viewpoint dynamics, (2) regressing dense depth maps to anchor physical distances, (3) predicting a metric scale factor for real-world calibration, and (4) distilling multi-scale 3D features to align the intermediate feature space. Guided by these explicit physical and geometric constraints, the model's internal representations naturally develop strong 3D awareness. Extensive experiments on spatial reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that GeoVR achieves state-of-the-art performance, establishing a new paradigm for endowing foundation models with spatial intelligence.

AI.tldr: GeoVR teaches an MLLM 3D spatial reasoning from only 2D videos by distilling geometry signals such as pose, depth, scale, and 3D features from pretrained 3D models, leading to SOTA benchmark performance.
AI.motivation: Current MLLMs are strong at 2D semantic understanding but lack intrinsic 3D awareness, so their representations are not geometrically or spatially consistent across frames. Large-scale 3D data is scarce, motivating a method that can learn spatial intelligence from widely available 2D videos.
AI.method: The paper proposes GeoVR, a framework that distills geometric knowledge from pretrained 3D foundation models into an MLLM using 2D video sequences and a multi-objective training scheme with four targets: inter-frame camera pose estimation, dense depth regression, metric scale prediction, and multi-scale 3D feature distillation.
AI.result: GeoVR achieves state-of-the-art results on spatial reasoning benchmarks and improves the geometric and spatial consistency of internal MLLM representations.
AI.conclusion: GeoVR shows that strong 3D-aware representations can be injected into multimodal large language models using only 2D video supervision, and this yields state-of-the-art spatial reasoning performance.

title: ReverseEOL: Improving Training-free Text Embeddings via Text Reversal in Decoder-only LLMs
summary: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have opened new avenues for generating training-free text embeddings. However, the causal attention in decoder-only LLMs prevents earlier tokens from attending to future context, leading to biased contextualized representations. In this work, we propose Reverse prompting with Explicit One-word Limitation (ReverseEOL), a simple yet effective method for enhancing the representational capability of frozen LLMs. ReverseEOL augments the standard forward embedding with an additional reversed embedding derived from the reversed input text. Since reversing the input exposes each token to context inaccessible in the original order, the resulting reversed embedding effectively provides complementary information to the original one. As a result, combining the forward and reversed embeddings yields a richer final representation. Comprehensive experiments on STS and MTEB benchmarks demonstrate that ReverseEOL significantly improves the performance of existing training-free baselines across a broad range of LLMs with diverse architectures and scales. Extensive ablations and analyses further confirm the necessity of our reversal mechanism.

AI.tldr: ReverseEOL is a simple training-free embedding method for frozen decoder-only LLMs: embed the text twice, once normally and once reversed, then combine both to reduce causal-attention bias and improve representation quality.
AI.motivation: Decoder-only LLMs use causal attention, so early tokens cannot access future context and their contextual representations are biased. Reversing the input is intended to expose tokens to complementary context that is unavailable in the original order.
AI.method: The method is training-free prompt-based embedding construction: generate an embedding from the original text, generate another from the reversed text using explicit one-word limitation prompting, then fuse the forward and reversed embeddings into a final representation.
AI.result: Experiments on STS and MTEB show significant gains over existing training-free baselines across diverse LLM architectures and scales. Ablations indicate the reversal mechanism is essential to the improvement.
AI.conclusion: ReverseEOL enhances frozen LLM text embeddings by combining the standard forward embedding with a reversed-input embedding, and this consistently improves training-free embedding quality across benchmarks and model families.

title: Two-Way Is Better Than One: Bidirectional Alignment with Cycle Consistency for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning
comment: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026. 23 pages, 8 figures. Code: https://github.com/HXuSz11/BiCyc_ICLR2026
summary: Continual learning (CL) seeks models that acquire new skills without erasing prior knowledge. In exemplar-free class-incremental learning (EFCIL), this challenge is amplified because past data cannot be stored, making representation drift for old classes particularly harmful. Prototype-based EFCIL is attractive for its efficiency, yet prototypes drift as the embedding space evolves; therefore, projection-based drift compensation has become a popular remedy. We show, however, that existing one-directional projections introduce systematic bias: they either retroactively distort the current feature geometry or align past classes only locally, leaving cycle inconsistencies that accumulate across tasks. We introduce BiCyc, a bidirectional projector alignment approach with a cycle-consistency objective. BiCyc jointly optimizes two maps, old-to-new and new-to-old, with stop-gradient gating so that transport and representation co-evolve. Analytically, we show that the cycle loss contracts the singular spectrum toward unity in whitened space, and that improved transport of class means and covariances yields smaller perturbations of classification log-odds, preserving old-class decisions and mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Empirically, across standard EFCIL benchmarks, BiCyc substantially reduces forgetting and improves accuracy in from-scratch settings, while remaining competitive in the pretrained fine-grained regime.

AI.tldr: BiCyc用双向投影+循环一致性替代单向漂移补偿，在无样本类增量学习中更稳定地对齐旧新特征空间，因而减少遗忘并提升准确率。
AI.motivation: 在无样本的类增量学习中，旧数据不可保存，导致旧类原型随嵌入空间演化而漂移。现有单向投影补偿存在系统偏差，会破坏当前特征几何或仅做局部对齐，并在多任务中累积循环不一致。
AI.method: 方法提出BiCyc：同时学习old-to-new与new-to-old两个映射，并通过stop-gradient gating让特征传输与表示学习协同优化；同时加入cycle-consistency loss约束双向映射的一致性。
AI.result: 理论上，循环损失在白化空间中将奇异值谱收缩向1，并通过更好地传输类均值和协方差来减小分类log-odds扰动。实验上，BiCyc在标准EFCIL基准上显著降低遗忘、提升从头训练设置下的准确率，在预训练细粒度场景中也保持竞争力。
AI.conclusion: BiCyc通过双向投影器对齐与循环一致性约束，减少了原型漂移带来的系统性偏差，从而更好地保持旧类判别边界并缓解灾难性遗忘。

title: Can LLMs Write Correct TLA+ Specifications? Evaluating Natural-Language-to-TLA+ Generation
comment: 12 pages, 11 tables. Accepted at the 21st International Conference on Software Technologies (ICSOFT 2026); Recommended as Best Paper Award Candidate
summary: TLA+ has supported industrial verification at companies such as Amazon and Microsoft, yet writing correct TLA+ specifications from natural language still requires time and expertise, which limits adoption. LLMs show promise, but no prior study measures whether they produce semantically correct TLA+ specifications from natural language. This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of LLM-based TLA+ specification synthesis from natural language. Our study evaluates 30 LLMs across eight families on a curated dataset of 205 TLA+ specifications: 25 open-weight models across four prompting strategies (2,600 runs) and 5 proprietary models under few-shot prompting (130 runs), all validated by the SANY parser and TLC model checker. LLMs achieve up to 26.6% syntactic correctness but only 8.6% semantic correctness, with successes exclusive to progressive prompting. Results show that model size does not predict quality, e.g., DeepSeek r1:8b outperforms its 70B variant across all strategies, which suggests the importance of reasoning alignment for formal languages. Code-specialized models consistently underperform due to negative transfer from mainstream language training. We identify five recurring hallucination categories, all traceable to specific training data biases. These results suggest that current LLMs do not generate reliable TLA+ specifications without expert oversight. We release the evaluation framework, code, and dataset to support reproducibility and future research.

AI.tldr: 这是首个系统评测LLM根据自然语言合成TLA+规格的研究。作者测试了30个模型，发现即使最好的模型语义正确率也只有8.6%，说明现阶段LLM还不能可靠地自动生成TLA+规格，仍需专家把关。
AI.motivation: 尽管TLA+已在工业界用于形式化验证，但从自然语言编写正确的TLA+规格仍然耗时且依赖专家，限制了其普及；因此需要评估LLM是否能有效自动化这一过程。
AI.method: 论文构建了一个包含205个TLA+规格的评测数据集，系统评估30个LLM、8个模型家族，在多种提示策略下生成TLA+规格，并使用SANY解析器和TLC模型检查器验证语法与语义正确性。
AI.result: LLM最高仅达到26.6%的语法正确率和8.6%的语义正确率；只有渐进式提示取得语义成功。模型规模与质量不显著相关，部分小模型优于大模型；代码专用模型整体表现较差，并暴露出五类与训练偏差相关的幻觉模式。
AI.conclusion: 当前LLM从自然语言生成TLA+规格说明时，语义可靠性很低，未经专家监督不足以用于可靠工业实践。

title: Geometry-Aware Dataset Condensation for Diffusion Model Training
summary: Dataset condensation aims to construct compact datasets from real data via synthesis or selection. However, existing approaches are ill-suited for diffusion model training: synthetic data generation often yields low-fidelity samples unsuitable for authentic modeling, while real subset selection typically fails to preserve the distributional geometry required by diffusion likelihood objectives. To address this, we propose to reformulate real subset selection as a geometry-aware distribution alignment problem. By incorporating one-sided partial optimal transport, our method selectively aligns a compact subset with the full data distribution while allowing unmatched mass in low-density regions, ensuring the preserved geometric structure necessary for effective diffusion model training. To further ensure distributional fidelity, we complement geometric alignment with lightweight feature-statistics and semantic consistency regularization. An efficient two-stage discrete optimization strategy is proposed to achieve this alignment objective. Extensive experiments across diffusion variants, subset sizes, image resolutions, and training rounds show that our method achieves superior fidelity and distributional coverage in diffusion model training. Codes are available at https://github.com/2018cx/GADC.

AI.tldr: A real-data subset selection method for diffusion models that uses partial optimal transport to preserve dataset geometry, plus simple regularizers for fidelity, yielding better compact-set diffusion training than prior condensation methods.
AI.motivation: Existing dataset condensation methods do not suit diffusion model training well: synthetic condensation often creates low-fidelity samples that are poor for authentic diffusion learning, while conventional real subset selection does not preserve the distributional geometry needed by diffusion likelihood objectives. The paper is motivated by the need for compact real subsets that maintain diffusion-relevant structure.
AI.method: The method reformulates dataset condensation for diffusion training as a geometry-aware distribution alignment problem. It uses one-sided partial optimal transport to align a selected compact real subset with the full data distribution while leaving some low-density mass unmatched. It further adds lightweight feature-statistics regularization and semantic consistency regularization, and solves the objective with an efficient two-stage discrete optimization strategy.
AI.result: Across multiple diffusion variants, subset sizes, image resolutions, and training rounds, the proposed approach achieves better sample fidelity and better distributional coverage than competing methods for training diffusion models on compact subsets.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that geometry-aware real subset selection, built on one-sided partial optimal transport and supplemented with feature-statistics and semantic consistency regularization, produces compact training sets that preserve the distributional structure required by diffusion models and consistently outperforms prior dataset condensation/selection methods in fidelity and coverage.

title: TARPO: Token-Wise Latent-Explicit Reasoning via Action-Routing Policy Optimization
comment: 18 pages, 12 figures. Code available at https://github.com/NKU-LITI/TARPO-master
summary: Latent reasoning has emerged as a promising alternative to discrete Chain-of-Thought (CoT) in large language models (LLMs), enabling more expressive reasoning by operating over continuous representations. However, the inherently deterministic nature of continuous representations limits policy exploration in reinforcement learning (RL). To address this, we propose TARPO (Token-Wise Latent-Explicit Reasoning via Action-Routing Policy Optimization), a pure RL framework that adaptively switches between discrete token generation and continuous latent reasoning at each step. TARPO introduces a lightweight action head router that observes the current hidden state and samples a routing decision from a binary mode-selection space, preserving the stochasticity of discrete token sampling from the vocabulary. The LLM backbone and router are jointly optimized end-to-end with a shared group-relative advantage signal. Extensive experiments across Qwen2.5 (from 1.5B to 7B) and Llama-3.1-8B backbones demonstrate that TARPO consistently outperforms existing explicit and latent reasoning RL baselines across diverse benchmarks. Further analysis shows that TARPO learns adaptive token-wise switching behaviors while maintaining stable training dynamics. Our code is available at https://github.com/NKU-LITI/TARPO-master.

AI.tldr: TARPO is an RL framework that lets an LLM switch at each token between normal token generation and latent reasoning. This restores exploration lost in purely continuous latent reasoning and leads to better benchmark performance and stable training.
AI.motivation: Pure latent reasoning is expressive but deterministic in continuous space, which weakens policy exploration in reinforcement learning. The paper aims to restore stochastic exploration while retaining the benefits of latent reasoning by adaptively mixing latent and explicit reasoning at the token level.
AI.method: The paper proposes TARPO, a pure reinforcement learning framework with a lightweight action-head router that observes the hidden state at each step and chooses between two reasoning modes: explicit discrete token generation or continuous latent reasoning. The router and LLM backbone are trained end-to-end using a shared group-relative advantage signal.
AI.result: Across Qwen2.5 models from 1.5B to 7B and Llama-3.1-8B, TARPO consistently outperforms existing explicit-reasoning and latent-reasoning RL baselines on diverse benchmarks. It also learns adaptive token-wise switching patterns and maintains stable training dynamics.
AI.conclusion: TARPO demonstrates that combining token-level discrete generation with continuous latent reasoning through an RL-trained routing policy yields stronger reasoning performance and stable training across multiple LLM backbones and benchmarks.

title: Causal Modeling of Selection in Evolution
summary: Understanding potential selection in data is crucial for causal discovery; we argue that "selection" in common narratives takes two forms, which we term static and evolutionary selection, respectively. Static selection refers to a one-shot filtering process where observed data consist of a subset of the population of interest, as in survey volunteer bias. Evolutionary selection, in contrast, operates through repeated rounds of differential fitness in reproduction, where observed data constitute the latest generation shaped by a historical trajectory, as in immune adaptation, antibiotic resistance, and social norm emergence. Existing methods largely conflate these two forms and rely on an identical graphical model of selection. We show that this model is valid for static settings but fails to characterize data under evolution, yielding false discovery results. To address this, we introduce a new model that specifically characterizes evolutionary selection, and develop a sound and complete procedure for identifying such models from data across one or multiple environments or generations. Experimental results validate the method's ability to uncover the relevant mechanisms underlying evolution from data.

AI.tldr: This paper says not all selection bias is the same: one-shot sampling bias and multi-generation evolutionary filtering need different causal models. The usual model works only for the first case; for the second, the authors provide a new model and an identification method that is theoretically valid and empirically effective.
AI.motivation: Existing causal discovery methods often treat all selection effects with the same graphical model. However, many real-world processes such as immune adaptation, antibiotic resistance, and social norm emergence are driven by historical, generation-by-generation evolutionary dynamics rather than one-shot sampling bias. This mismatch motivates a new framework that correctly models evolutionary selection.
AI.method: The authors formalize two types of selection: static and evolutionary. They show theoretically why the conventional selection graphical model fails for evolutionary data, then introduce a new graphical/modeling framework for evolutionary selection. On top of this, they develop a sound and complete identification procedure that works with data from one or multiple environments or generations, and validate it experimentally.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates that conflating static and evolutionary selection leads to incorrect causal discovery, including false positives or false discoveries, in evolutionary settings. It proposes a new model tailored to evolutionary selection and provides a sound and complete identification algorithm. Experiments show that the method can successfully recover mechanisms underlying evolution from data.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that selection in causal discovery should be distinguished into static selection and evolutionary selection. The standard graphical selection model is appropriate only for static selection and can produce false discoveries in evolutionary settings. A new evolutionary-selection-specific model and an identification procedure are therefore necessary and effective.

title: From Risk Classification to Action Plan Remediation: A Guardrail Feedback Driven Framework for LLM Agents
summary: LLM-based guardrails typically safeguard agents by evaluating proposed actions or inputs before execution, producing safety signals such as binary allow/deny decisions, risk categories, and/or explanatory rationales about potential policy violations. However, agent risks often arise when otherwise benign tasks are contaminated by untrusted external content, unsafe instructions, or risky tool use. Existing guardrails often flag the entire task uniformly as unsafe, thereby blocking the threat but sacrificing the benign part. Moreover, existing work largely evaluates guardrails in isolation, leaving unclear whether their interventions lead to safer downstream agent behavior. To address this, we introduce TRIAD (Tripartite Response for Iterative Agent Guardrailing), a guardrail-integrated agent framework that leverages guardrail-generated verbal feedback as a guiding signal to keep the agent aligned with benign objectives at each planning step. We finetune a language model on a self-curated training dataset to output one of three decisions: proceed, refuse, or update, together with structured natural-language feedback. Rather than merely allowing or blocking execution, update guides the agent to revise its plan, avoid harmful components, and preserve the benign task where possible. TRIAD injects this feedback into the agent's context, enabling subsequent plan revision and forming a closed loop between guardrail feedback and agent planning. Extensive experiments on ASB and AgentHarm show that TRIAD reduces the average attack success rate to 10.42%, while achieving the best safety-utility trade-off among guardrail-integrated baselines. Our code is available at: https://github.com/YUHAOSUNABC/TRIAD.

AI.tldr: TRIAD turns guardrails from a binary blocker into an iterative coach: instead of only allowing or refusing, it can ask the agent to update its plan, which substantially improves safety while keeping more useful behavior.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM guardrails usually assess tasks or actions in isolation and often mark an entire mixed-risk task as unsafe, blocking both harmful and benign components. It is also unclear whether such guardrail outputs actually improve downstream agent behavior. The work is motivated by the need for finer-grained interventions that mitigate risk without unnecessarily sacrificing utility.
AI.method: The paper proposes TRIAD, a guardrail-integrated agent framework. A finetuned language model produces one of three decisions—proceed, refuse, or update—plus structured natural-language feedback at each planning step. The update option lets the agent revise its plan to remove risky components while retaining benign objectives. This feedback is injected back into the agent context, creating a closed loop between guardrail assessment and planning.
AI.result: On ASB and AgentHarm, TRIAD lowers the average attack success rate to 10.42% and achieves the best safety-utility trade-off among guardrail-integrated baselines in the reported experiments.
AI.conclusion: TRIAD demonstrates that integrating guardrail feedback directly into an agent’s iterative planning loop improves downstream safety behavior while preserving benign task completion better than simple allow/deny guardrails.

title: Resonant Minds: Closed-Loop Social Avatars with Theory of Mind
summary: Creating lifelike digital humans with genuine social intelligence requires unifying cognitive reasoning and multimodal generation within a coherent framework. Current approaches treat these as separate tasks: Large Language Models excel at dialogue but lack embodied expression, while diffusion-based talking head models achieve visual fidelity but ignore social cognition. To bridge this gap, we propose a closed-loop dual-agent framework integrating perception, social reasoning, and expression into a continuous interaction cycle. The perception module analyzes partners' multimodal behaviors from video, while the social reasoning module infers hidden mental states through Theory of Mind and selects responses via an ensemble mechanism. The expression module then generates emotion-controllable dual-agent videos synthesizing both speaker speech and expression alongside listener reactive behaviors, capturing bidirectional dynamics absent in prior work. We construct a hierarchical Persona-Scenario dataset with psychologically grounded personas and private social goals to support evaluation under information asymmetry. Experiments on this dataset demonstrate competitive or superior performance on both dialogue quality and video generation metrics. Notably, our method surpasses even the full-information Script mode on key dialogue quality dimensions, suggesting that explicit mental state inference under uncertainty can elicit more thoughtful dialogue than unrestricted information access.

AI.tldr: The paper builds a socially intelligent digital human system that watches a partner, infers their hidden intentions and emotions, and generates coordinated speaker-listener videos with controllable expression. It also introduces a new evaluation dataset, and experiments show the system matches or beats prior methods in both conversation quality and video realism, with uncertainty-aware reasoning yielding especially strong dialogue.
AI.motivation: Existing methods split cognitive dialogue reasoning and visual human generation into separate problems: LLMs support dialogue but lack embodied expression, while diffusion-based talking-head systems generate realistic visuals but neglect social cognition. The work is motivated by the need to unify reasoning, perception, and embodied expression for lifelike socially intelligent digital humans.
AI.method: The paper proposes a dual-agent closed-loop architecture with three modules: a perception module to analyze multimodal partner behavior from video, a social reasoning module that infers hidden mental states using Theory of Mind and chooses responses via an ensemble mechanism, and an expression module that generates emotion-controllable dual-agent videos with both speaker and listener behaviors. It also introduces a hierarchical Persona-Scenario dataset designed around personas, private goals, and information asymmetry.
AI.result: On the proposed Persona-Scenario dataset, the method attains competitive or better results on both dialogue quality and video generation metrics. A notable finding is that it outperforms the full-information Script mode on important dialogue quality dimensions, indicating that reasoning about hidden mental states under uncertainty can improve response quality.
AI.conclusion: A closed-loop dual-agent framework that combines perception, Theory-of-Mind-based social reasoning, and multimodal expression can produce more socially intelligent digital humans, achieving strong dialogue and video generation performance; explicit mental-state inference under uncertainty may even outperform full-information script-based dialogue on key quality dimensions.

title: Analysis of the Neglect-Zero Effect in Large Language Models
comment: 14 pages (10 pages main text), 8 figures. To appear in the Proceedings of the ACL2026 Student Research Workshop (SRW)
summary: We investigate the extent to which the language processing of LLMs resembles human cognitive processes, focusing on a human cognitive bias called the $\textit{neglect-zero effect}$. This effect refers to the human tendency to ignore $\textit{zero-models}$, which are configurations that render a proposition vacuously true by virtue of an empty set. We focus on two types of inferences driven by the neglect-zero effect, and examine how LLMs process these inferences by comparing their behavior with that in an inference that does not involve the neglect-zero effect. For this purpose, we employ a paradigm based on $\textit{structural priming}$, where recent exposure to a preceding sentence (the $\textit{prime}$) facilitates the processing of a subsequent sentence (the $\textit{target}$) due to their structural similarity. We prepare primes to force LLMs to consider the zero-model, and analyze whether they also consider it in the target. The results suggest that the neglect-zero effect may not occur in the LLMs analyzed in this study. Our code is available at https://github.com/ynklab/neglect_zero

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether LLMs share a human logical bias called the neglect-zero effect using structural priming, and finds that the tested models likely do not exhibit that bias.
AI.motivation: The paper is motivated by the broader question of whether LLM language processing resembles human cognition, specifically whether LLMs exhibit the human neglect-zero effect in logical inference.
AI.method: The authors use a structural priming paradigm to test whether recent exposure to prime sentences that force consideration of zero-models influences how LLMs process target inferences. They compare two inference types associated with the neglect-zero effect against a control inference that does not involve this effect.
AI.result: The experiments suggest that, unlike humans, the tested LLMs do not appear to systematically show the neglect-zero effect when processing the targeted inferences.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that the neglect-zero effect, a human cognitive bias involving the failure to consider zero-models, may not be present in the analyzed large language models.

title: Benchmarking Counterfactual Prediction in Epidemic Time Series with Time-Varying Interventions
summary: Deep learning has enabled significant advances in time-series causal inference, yet progress remains constrained by the lack of realistic benchmarks with observable counterfactual outcomes. Existing datasets either rely on real-world observations without ground-truth counterfactuals or on simplified simulations that fail to capture complex causal dynamics. To address this gap, we develop a large-scale benchmark for counterfactual prediction in epidemic time series under dynamic interventions. Unlike existing benchmarks, it supports static and time-varying treatments, as well as both single-policy and multi-policy intervention settings, enabling evaluation of causal inference methods across a broad range of causal inference scenarios. Leveraging a calibrated agent-based model grounded in real-world demographic, mobility, epidemiological, and policy data, we generate realistic counterfactual trajectories across more than 150 U.S. counties. Using this benchmark, we evaluate widely used and state-of-the-art causal inference methods, revealing substantial performance differences and highlighting the challenges of realistic time-series causal reasoning.

AI.tldr: This paper creates a realistic epidemic time-series benchmark with known counterfactuals for many kinds of interventions, then uses it to show that current causal inference methods still struggle and vary greatly in performance.
AI.motivation: Current time-series causal inference research lacks realistic benchmarks with ground-truth counterfactual outcomes; real-world datasets do not provide true counterfactuals, while synthetic simulations are often too simplistic to capture complex causal dynamics.
AI.method: The authors build a benchmark using a calibrated agent-based epidemic model grounded in real demographic, mobility, epidemiological, and policy data from more than 150 U.S. counties, and generate counterfactual trajectories under static, time-varying, single-policy, and multi-policy interventions to evaluate causal inference methods.
AI.result: The benchmark enables broad evaluation across multiple intervention scenarios and shows substantial performance differences among widely used and state-of-the-art causal inference methods, highlighting the ongoing difficulty of realistic time-series causal reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a realistic, large-scale benchmark with observable counterfactuals can expose meaningful gaps between current time-series causal inference methods and better reflect the difficulty of dynamic intervention reasoning in epidemic settings.

title: When Tools Fail: Benchmarking Dynamic Replanning and Anomaly Recovery in LLM Agents
summary: Existing benchmarks evaluate Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR) in LLMs on idealized ''happy paths'', largely overlooking real-world tool failures. We introduce ToolMaze, a benchmark for dynamic path discovery and error recovery in TIR agents. To separate systematic replanning from blind trial-and-error, ToolMaze adopts a two-dimensional design: DAG-based topological complexity and a $2 \times 2$ taxonomy of tool perturbations (explicit/implicit, transient/permanent). Evaluations show that perturbations degrade performance across nearly all models, with the sharpest drops under implicit semantic failures. Driven by systemic over-trust in corrupted outputs, Perturbation Recovery Rate (PRR) plummets by around 37\% in these scenarios, while complex topologies trap agents in futile trial-and-error loops. Crucially, agentic fault-tolerance improves with model scale $3.66\times$ slower than basic task execution, highlighting dynamic replanning as a distinct bottleneck unaddressed by model scaling or prompting. Data and code are available at https://github.com/Zhudongsheng75/ToolMaze.

AI.tldr: ToolMaze is a new benchmark showing that LLM agents handle real-world tool failures poorly: they over-trust bad tool outputs, recover badly from implicit failures, and scale much more slowly on fault tolerance than on normal task completion.
AI.motivation: Prior benchmarks mostly test LLM tool use on idealized happy-path settings and fail to capture how agents behave when tools return corrupted, misleading, or unavailable outputs. The paper aims to measure real-world robustness, recovery, and replanning ability under tool failures.
AI.method: The paper introduces ToolMaze, a benchmark for evaluating TIR agents under non-ideal conditions. It uses a two-dimensional design: DAG-based topological complexity for dynamic path discovery, and a 2×2 taxonomy of tool perturbations categorized as explicit vs. implicit and transient vs. permanent, to test error recovery and replanning behavior.
AI.result: Across nearly all evaluated models, tool perturbations significantly reduce performance. The worst degradation occurs under implicit semantic failures, where perturbation recovery rate drops by about 37% due to over-trust in corrupted outputs. More complex DAG topologies further induce ineffective trial-and-error loops. Improvement in fault tolerance lags behind basic task execution by a factor of about 3.66× with model scaling.
AI.conclusion: Tool-integrated reasoning agents are brittle under realistic tool failures, especially implicit semantic failures, and dynamic replanning remains a major unresolved bottleneck that is not fixed simply by scaling models or prompting better.

title: Self-Learning Expression Deformations for Data-Efficient Gaussian Avatars
summary: Modeling dynamic facial expressions using 3D Gaussian representations remains challenging due to their unstructured nature. Conventional Gaussian avatar pipelines require extensive multiview and sequential expression data, limiting scalability and accessibility. In this work, we introduce Self-Adaptive Gaussian Expression (SAGE), a framework for self-learning expression-induced Gaussian deformations that enables high-fidelity, animatable avatars from minimal input data. Our method jointly optimizes 2D Gaussian surfels and a Signed Distance Field (SDF) to enforce compact, surface-aligned Gaussian distributions, while a self-supervised expression learning phase replaces long training sequences with geometric and appearance consistency constraints. This design allows flexible deployment across multiple reconstruction regimes: in the multiview setting, only a single frame (timestep) is required instead of thousands; in the monocular setting, only head rotations are needed without expression sequences; and in the one-shot setting, no pretraining or priors are necessary. Experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves reconstruction and animation quality comparable to state-of-the-art methods, while reducing data requirements by several orders of magnitude. Our results highlight the potential of self-supervised Gaussian deformation learning as a step toward accessible, data-efficient avatar creation.

AI.tldr: SAGE is a data-efficient Gaussian avatar framework for dynamic facial expressions. It learns expression-driven deformations self-supervisedly, uses surfels plus an SDF for compact surface-aligned Gaussians, and reaches competitive quality with far less training data.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D Gaussian avatar methods for dynamic facial expressions are hard to scale because Gaussian representations are unstructured and current pipelines need extensive multiview and sequential expression data.
AI.method: The framework jointly optimizes 2D Gaussian surfels and a Signed Distance Field (SDF) to keep Gaussian distributions compact and aligned to the surface, and uses a self-supervised expression-learning phase with geometric and appearance consistency constraints instead of long expression sequences.
AI.result: The method supports three reconstruction regimes with drastically reduced input requirements: a single frame in multiview, only head rotations in monocular, and no pretraining or priors in one-shot, while matching state-of-the-art reconstruction and animation quality.
AI.conclusion: SAGE shows that self-supervised Gaussian deformation learning can produce high-fidelity, animatable avatars with far less data, making avatar creation more accessible.

title: YouZhi: Towards High-Concurrency Financial LLMs via Adaptive GQA-to-MLA Transition
summary: Large language models (LLMs) drive significant financial innovations, yet their high-concurrency deployment is severely bottlenecked by KV cache memory overhead, which inflates infrastructure costs and throttles scalability. To address this, we propose YouZhi-LLM, a highly efficient financial LLM empowered by a comprehensive structural transition and training pipeline natively built on the Huawei Ascend ecosystem. At its algorithmic core, YouZhi-LLM features a layer-adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition framework that dynamically assigns per-layer FreqFold sizes, maximizing KV-cache compression while minimizing perplexity degradation. To recover representation capacity and inject domain expertise, the Ascend-based training pipeline seamlessly integrates generalized knowledge distillation with financial-specific supervised fine-tuning. Evaluations demonstrate the superiority of this systematic approach, with the adaptive transition reducing perplexity degradation by up to 35% over uniform baselines. Crucially, when evaluated on Ascend NPUs via vLLM-Ascend, the massive KV-cache reduction translates directly into deployment efficiency. Compared to their respective base models, YouZhi-7B yields a 12.3% improvement in average financial benchmark score alongside a 2.69$\times$ increase in maximum concurrency; similarly, YouZhi-14B achieves a 7.0% accuracy gain and a 2.43$\times$ concurrency boost, establishing a new paradigm for cost-effective, high-throughput financial inference.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：论文针对金融大模型部署时KV cache过大的问题，提出YouZhi-LLM：用分层自适应GQA-to-MLA压缩KV cache，再通过蒸馏+金融微调恢复能力。结果是在Ascend上既提升金融任务表现，也把最大并发提升到约2.4到2.7倍。 / TL;DR: The paper tackles excessive KV-cache overhead in financial LLM serving by proposing YouZhi-LLM, which uses a layer-adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition for compression and a distillation plus financial fine-tuning pipeline for recovery. On Ascend, it improves both financial performance and serving concurrency by roughly 2.4x to 2.7x.
AI.motivation: 动机在于：LLM虽然正在推动金融创新，但高并发部署时KV cache占用过大，导致基础设施成本上升、系统可扩展性受限。作者希望在不明显损害模型质量的前提下，大幅降低KV cache开销，并将压缩收益真实转化为金融推理场景中的吞吐和并发提升。 / The motivation is that while LLMs enable major financial innovation, their high-concurrency deployment is heavily constrained by KV-cache memory overhead, which increases infrastructure cost and limits scalability. The authors aim to reduce this memory burden substantially without seriously harming model quality, and to convert that savings into real throughput and concurrency gains for financial inference.
AI.method: 方法上，论文首先提出分层自适应的GQA-to-MLA迁移框架，为不同层动态分配FreqFold大小，以在KV cache压缩率与困惑度退化之间取得更优平衡。随后，基于华为Ascend生态构建训练流水线，结合通用知识蒸馏与金融领域监督微调，恢复结构迁移后的表征能力并注入金融知识；最终在Ascend NPU和vLLM-Ascend上验证部署收益。 / Methodologically, the paper introduces a layer-adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition that assigns different FreqFold sizes to different layers to optimize the tradeoff between KV-cache compression and perplexity loss. It then uses an Ascend-native training pipeline combining generalized knowledge distillation with financial supervised fine-tuning to recover representation capacity and inject domain expertise, and evaluates the result on Ascend NPUs with vLLM-Ascend.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，该系统性方案优于统一配置基线：自适应迁移可将困惑度退化最多降低35%。在金融任务上，相比各自基座模型，YouZhi-7B的平均金融基准分数提升12.3%，最大并发提升2.69倍；YouZhi-14B的准确率提升7.0%，最大并发提升2.43倍。 / Results show the systematic approach outperforms uniform baselines: the adaptive transition reduces perplexity degradation by up to 35%. Relative to their respective base models, YouZhi-7B improves average financial benchmark score by 12.3% with a 2.69x increase in maximum concurrency, while YouZhi-14B gains 7.0% accuracy and 2.43x higher concurrency.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出了YouZhi-LLM，一种面向金融场景、兼顾高吞吐部署与领域能力的大语言模型方案。通过自适应的GQA到MLA结构迁移和基于Ascend生态的训练流程，模型在显著压缩KV cache的同时保持甚至提升任务性能，并在实际部署中显著提升并发能力。 / The paper concludes that YouZhi-LLM is an effective financial LLM framework that jointly improves deployment efficiency and domain performance. Its adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition plus Ascend-native training pipeline substantially compresses KV cache while preserving or improving task quality, leading to much higher serving concurrency in practice.

title: MolE-RAG: Molecular Structure-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Chemistry
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for molecular property prediction, but their ability to reason over chemical structures remains limited, as molecular representations such as SMILES differ substantially from the natural language on which LLMs are primarily trained. To bridge this semantic and chemical knowledge gap, we propose MolE-RAG, a training-free, molecule-centric retrieval-augmented generation framework for LLM-based molecular property prediction. MolE-RAG augments each prediction with three complementary sources of inference-time context: retrieved chemistry literature, molecule-specific information including compound synonyms, identifiers, functional group annotations, and physicochemical descriptors, and structurally similar molecules retrieved from the training set. We evaluate MolE-RAG across nine molecular property prediction tasks using proprietary, chemistry-specialized, and open-source LLMs. Across general-purpose LLMs, MolE-RAG improves ROC-AUC by up to 28 percentage points on classification tasks and reduces regression RMSE by up to 67% relative to a SMILES-only baseline. We further find that the utility of each context source varies across models and tasks, with different models benefiting most from textual retrieval, molecular context, or structural retrieval. These results suggest that molecule-centric retrieval can improve LLM-based molecular property prediction without model fine-tuning while providing a flexible framework for integrating heterogeneous chemical knowledge at inference time.

AI.tldr: MolE-RAG is a training-free RAG framework for molecular property prediction that combines literature, molecule metadata, and similar-structure retrieval to significantly boost LLM performance over SMILES-only prompting.
AI.motivation: LLMs struggle with molecular property prediction because chemical representations like SMILES differ markedly from natural language, creating a semantic and chemical knowledge gap that limits structure-aware reasoning.
AI.method: The paper proposes MolE-RAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework that augments each molecular prediction with three inference-time context sources: retrieved chemistry literature, molecule-specific metadata and descriptors, and structurally similar molecules retrieved from the training set.
AI.result: Across nine molecular property prediction tasks and multiple proprietary, chemistry-specialized, and open-source LLMs, MolE-RAG improves classification ROC-AUC by up to 28 percentage points and reduces regression RMSE by up to 67% versus a SMILES-only baseline; the most useful context source varies by model and task.
AI.conclusion: MolE-RAG demonstrates that training-free, molecule-centric retrieval can substantially improve LAG-based molecular property prediction without fine-tuning by injecting heterogeneous chemical knowledge at inference time.

title: Statistical Priors for Implicit Preferences: Decoupling Skill Selection as a Local Harness in Personal Agents
summary: As Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities advance, locally deployed personal agents relying on API-based remote models and external skills have emerged as a novel paradigm. With the rapid expansion of available skills, enabling personal agents to learn and adapt to implicit user preferences becomes a critical challenge. However, local deployment constraints preclude complex centralized selection algorithms, creating an urgent need for a lightweight local preference harness. This paper explores the implementation of such a harness through a novel architecture that strictly decouples statistical preference learning from semantic intent parsing. Specifically, we leverage localized statistical results to influence and modulate the selection decisions of the remote LLM. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our decoupled approach achieves the lowest cumulative regret and highest test accuracy, significantly outperforming traditional memory-augmented agents.

AI.tldr: A local lightweight preference module guides a remote LLM's skill choices, and this separation of preference learning from intent understanding works better than standard memory-based agents.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that personal agents increasingly depend on remote LLM APIs and growing external skill sets, but local deployment constraints make heavy centralized selection methods impractical; therefore, a lightweight way to capture implicit user preferences is needed.
AI.method: The method introduces a decoupled architecture: local components learn user preferences through lightweight statistical modeling, while a remote LLM handles semantic intent parsing and final selection, modulated by the local preference signals.
AI.result: Experiments show the proposed decoupled approach achieves the best performance among compared methods, including the lowest cumulative regret and the highest test accuracy, significantly outperforming traditional memory-augmented agents.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a lightweight, locally deployable preference harness can improve personal agent skill selection by decoupling statistical preference learning from semantic intent parsing, yielding lower cumulative regret and higher test accuracy than memory-augmented baselines.

title: CamFlow+: Hybrid Motion Bases for 2D Camera Motion Estimation with Stabilization Applications
summary: Estimating 2D camera motion is fundamental to computer vision and computational photography. Existing homography-based methods work well for planar scenes or pure rotation, but struggle with camera translation, depth variation, and local parallax; local homography and mesh-based models improve flexibility but still rely on piecewise planar assumptions. We introduce CamFlow+, a hybrid-basis framework that represents 2D camera motion directly in dense-flow space. CamFlow+ combines homography-derived physical bases, stochastic bases sampled from homography flows, and depth-translational bases derived from depth and camera intrinsics, relaxing the single-plane constraint while preserving camera-motion regularity. A depth-aware smoothness term further regularizes translation-induced parallax in continuous-depth regions while preserving motion changes near depth boundaries. We evaluate CamFlow+ on GHOF-Cam, a camera-motion benchmark that masks out dynamic objects and ill-posed occlusion regions in an optical-flow benchmark to isolate camera-induced motion. Experiments show that CamFlow+ improves sparse and dense camera-motion estimation. In digital video stabilization, CamFlow+ also improves global and local stability, achieving the best top-1 preference rate in a blind user study. Code and datasets will be available on the project page: https://lhaippp.github.io/CamFlow+.

AI.tldr: CamFlow+ models camera motion directly as dense optical flow using hybrid motion bases plus depth-aware regularization, outperforming prior homography-style approaches on camera-motion estimation and video stabilization.
AI.motivation: Existing homography-based, local homography, and mesh-based motion models are limited by planar or piecewise planar assumptions, making them less effective under camera translation, depth variation, and local parallax. The work is motivated by the need for a more expressive yet physically regularized model for 2D camera motion.
AI.method: The paper proposes CamFlow+, a hybrid-basis framework in dense-flow space that combines homography-derived physical bases, stochastic bases sampled from homography flows, and depth-translational bases derived from depth and camera intrinsics. It also introduces a depth-aware smoothness regularization term to handle translation-induced parallax while preserving motion discontinuities near depth boundaries.
AI.result: On the GHOF-Cam benchmark, CamFlow+ improves both sparse and dense camera-motion estimation. In digital video stabilization, it also improves global and local stability and achieves the best top-1 preference rate in a blind user study.
AI.conclusion: CamFlow+ provides a more flexible and regularized representation of 2D camera motion by modeling motion in dense-flow space with hybrid bases, leading to better camera-motion estimation and improved video stabilization performance.

title: Evaluating Stochastic Collapse and Implicit Bias in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Current evaluations for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) overwhelmingly focus on utility-driven objectives, leaving model behavior under logic-neutral scenarios largely underexplored. Stochasticity is essential in scenarios where multiple actions are equally valid, such as recommending travel itineraries or daily schedules where multiple options have similar utility. In such settings, deterministic policies may lead to repetitive behaviors and reduced coverage of valid alternatives. To bridge this gap, we propose RandomBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate whether MLLMs can maintain distributionally neutral behavior when selecting among equivalent options. We further introduce three metrics, including RI, BCI, BII, to quantify entropy and distributional bias. Experiments reveal a pervasive phenomenon termed Stochastic Collapse, where MLLMs fail to maintain uniform randomness under explicit random instructions, with top-1 probabilities reaching 97% from the ideal one quarter baseline and RI dropping to 0.068 in Claude Sonnet 4.6. Extensive ablation studies further demonstrate that these deviations persist across languages and representation formats, highlighting the robustness of distributional collapse in logic-neutral decision settings.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces RandomBench to test whether MLLMs can choose fairly among equally good options, and finds that they usually collapse to highly biased, non-random behavior even when explicitly asked to act randomly.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLM evaluations mainly emphasize utility or correctness, but they largely ignore whether models can behave neutrally and stochastically when several options are equally valid. This matters for recommendation-like settings where deterministic behavior reduces diversity and coverage.
AI.method: The authors propose RandomBench, a benchmark for logic-neutral multimodal decision scenarios with multiple equally valid options, and introduce three evaluation metrics: RI, BCI, and BII to measure entropy and distributional bias. They then evaluate MLLMs under explicit random-selection instructions and perform ablation studies across languages and representation formats.
AI.result: Experiments show severe deviation from ideal uniform randomness: some models assign up to 97% top-1 probability instead of the ideal 25%, and RI falls as low as 0.068 in Claude Sonnet 4.6. The collapse remains consistent across languages and representation formats.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that current MLLMs exhibit a strong and robust failure to produce distributionally neutral random choices in logic-neutral settings, a phenomenon the authors call Stochastic Collapse.

title: Revisiting Prototype Rehearsal for Exemplar-Free Continual Learning: Manifold-Aware Boundary Sampling with Adaptive Class-Balanced Loss
comment: Published in CVPR 2026 Findings. 10 pages, 6 figures. CVF version: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026F/html/Xu_Revisiting_Prototype_Rehearsal_for_Exemplar-Free_Continual_Learning_Manifold-Aware_Boundary_Sampling_CVPRF_2026_paper.html. Code: https://github.com/HXuSz11/ACB_CEOS_CVPR2026_Findings
summary: Exemplar-free class-incremental learning (EFCIL) aims to acquire new classes over time without storing raw data. Historically, prototype rehearsal, which samples around stored class prototypes and mixes them with current-task data, has been a popular strategy to reduce catastrophic forgetting. However, recent drift-compensation methods that explicitly realign prototypes in the evolving feature space consistently outperform prototype-based rehearsal, raising the question of whether rehearsal itself is fundamentally limited. We argue that the performance gap stems not from the idea of prototype rehearsal per se, but from how it is typically instantiated: existing approaches treat prototypes as isolated class summaries that ignore information from nearby enemy classes, and fail to correct the emerging class imbalance between a handful of synthetic old-class samples and hundreds of real instances from newly introduced classes. Building on this hypothesis, we revisit prototype rehearsal and propose a manifold-aware variant that restores its competitiveness in EFCIL. First, we introduce Constrained Expansive Over-Sampling, which interpolates each old-class prototype toward its nearest enemy features from new classes, generating boundary-aware rehearsal samples that better follow the underlying data manifold while preserving inter-class separation. Second, we design an Adaptive Class-Balanced loss that performs time-based class weighting, amplifying gradients from older prototypes when they are most informative and gradually annealing their influence as richer supervision from later tasks accumulates. Together, these components turn prototype rehearsal into a drift-resilient, imbalance-aware mechanism that closes, and often reverses, the gap to recent drift-compensation methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple EFCIL benchmarks.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：这篇论文重新审视EFCIL中的原型回放，认为其落后不是因为“回放”思想本身差，而是因为旧方法不会利用邻近异类信息且忽略类不平衡。作者提出CEOS边界感知过采样和ACB自适应类平衡损失，使原型回放对特征漂移和类别失衡更鲁棒，并在多个基准上达到SOTA。 / TL;DR: The paper revisits prototype rehearsal in EFCIL and argues that its past underperformance is due to poor instantiation, not the rehearsal idea itself. By adding CEOS boundary-aware oversampling and an ACB loss for temporal class balancing, the method becomes robust to feature drift and class imbalance, reaching SOTA on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: 论文动机：在免样本类增量学习中，近期漂移补偿方法持续优于原型回放，表面上似乎说明“回放”思路存在根本缺陷。作者认为，真正问题不在原型回放本身，而在现有做法把原型视为孤立类别摘要，忽略靠近决策边界的异类结构信息，同时没有有效处理旧类少量合成样本与新类大量真实样本之间的监督失衡。 / Motivation: In exemplar-free class-incremental learning, recent drift-compensation methods consistently outperform prototype rehearsal, seemingly suggesting a fundamental limitation of rehearsal. The authors argue instead that the issue lies in how prototype rehearsal is instantiated: prototypes are treated as isolated class summaries, boundary-relevant enemy-class structure is ignored, and the supervision imbalance between few synthetic old-class samples and many real new-class instances is not properly handled.
AI.method: 论文方法：提出一种面向EFCIL的流形感知原型回放框架。第一，Constrained Expansive Over-Sampling（CEOS）将旧类原型朝最近的新类异类特征方向进行受约束插值，生成具备边界感知能力的旧类合成样本，同时保持类间分离。第二，Adaptive Class-Balanced（ACB）损失采用基于时间的类别加权，在旧类原型最有信息量的阶段增强其梯度贡献，并随任务推进逐步退火其权重，以缓解类别不平衡。 / Method: The paper proposes a manifold-aware prototype rehearsal framework for EFCIL. First, Constrained Expansive Over-Sampling (CEOS) interpolates each old-class prototype toward its nearest enemy features from new classes to generate boundary-aware synthetic rehearsal samples while preserving inter-class separation. Second, an Adaptive Class-Balanced (ACB) loss applies time-based class weighting, boosting gradients from older prototypes when most informative and gradually annealing their influence over time to mitigate class imbalance.
AI.result: 论文结果：所提出方法弥补并经常反超近期漂移补偿方法，在多个EFCIL基准上取得SOTA性能。核心收益来自两点：更贴近数据流形、决策边界更合理的旧类合成样本，以及对跨任务类别不平衡更稳健的训练目标。 / Result: The proposed approach closes the gap to, and often outperforms, recent drift-compensation methods, achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple EFCIL benchmarks. The gains come from boundary-aware manifold-consistent synthetic old-class samples and a training objective that better handles cross-task class imbalance.
AI.conclusion: 论文结论：原型回放并非天然落后于漂移补偿方法；其性能瓶颈主要来自传统实现忽略邻近异类信息以及旧类/新类样本不平衡。通过流形感知的原型回放设计，原型回放可以变得对特征漂移更鲁棒，并在多个EFCIL基准上达到或超过最新方法。 / Conclusion: Prototype rehearsal is not fundamentally inferior to drift-compensation methods. Its weakness mainly comes from conventional instantiations that ignore nearby enemy-class information and suffer from old/new class imbalance. With a manifold-aware design, prototype rehearsal becomes more drift-resilient and can match or surpass recent methods on multiple EFCIL benchmarks.

title: Agentic Molecular Recovery via Molecule-Aware Exploration
summary: Text-guided molecular generation with LLMs often yields invalid SMILES. We argue that invalid drafts should be addressed through a shift from validity-oriented repair to identity-preserving molecular recovery: the objective is not only to restore chemical validity, but also to preserve target-relevant structural cues and recover the molecular identity implied by the description. This perspective reveals the limitations of existing correction strategies. Post-hoc repair can recover validity while distorting key structures, LLM-only correction can introduce unintended global drift, and generic agentic correction remains constrained by greedy single-candidate trajectories even when equipped with executable RDKit edit tools. To address these limitations, we propose AMREC, which couples molecule-aware mismatch tracking with expanded candidate exploration and trajectory-level selection. On invalid ChEBI-20 drafts from three backbone models, AMREC achieves the strongest overall recovery profile across structural, exact-match, and string-level metrics.

AI.tldr: AMREC fixes invalid LLM-generated SMILES by recovering the intended molecule, not just chemical validity, and outperforms prior repair strategies on ChEBI-20.
AI.motivation: Existing text-guided molecular generation methods with LLMs often produce invalid SMILES, and current correction approaches either distort important structures, cause global drift, or are limited by greedy single-path editing. The work is motivated by the need to recover validity without losing the intended molecular identity.
AI.method: The authors propose AMREC, a recovery framework that combines molecule-aware mismatch tracking, broader candidate exploration, and trajectory-level selection to recover invalid text-generated molecular drafts.
AI.result: On invalid ChEBI-20 drafts generated by three backbone models, AMREC achieves the best overall recovery performance across structural metrics, exact-match metrics, and string-level metrics.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that repairing invalid SMILES should focus on identity-preserving molecular recovery rather than validity alone. AMREC better restores chemically valid molecules while preserving target-relevant structural information and the intended molecular identity from text descriptions.

title: Unveiling the Unknown: Open Vocabulary Object Detection with Scene Graphs
summary: Open-vocabulary object detection seeks to identify novel object categories that were not part of the training data. Many knowledge distillation-based approaches have shown promising performance by transferring knowledge from pre-trained vision-language models to object detection. However, these methods often overlook structured, image-specific relationships between objects, such as interactions and spatial arrangements. This oversight can significantly restrict the effectiveness of detecting novel categories. To address this issue, we propose a Scene-guided Relational Modeling detection framework. This framework utilizes scene graphs to capture structured semantic and spatial relationships between candidate regions and their contextual objects. It explicitly models interactions among neighboring regions and incorporates a Relation Attention Module to implicitly amplify the key relational cues extracted from the scene graph. Furthermore, we present a scene-based textual alignment branch that distills category knowledge from captions to guide relational alignment. This approach facilitates a seamless integration of visual relations with semantic information for enhanced detection performance. Comprehensive experiments show that our model achieves superior performance compared to other OVOD methods, improving the AP for novel categories on COCO and LVIS datasets.

AI.tldr: A new OVOD framework uses scene graphs, relation attention, and caption-based alignment to model object relationships and improves novel-category detection on COCO and LVIS.
AI.motivation: Existing knowledge distillation approaches in open-vocabulary object detection transfer knowledge from vision-language models, but they often ignore image-specific structured relationships such as object interactions and spatial layouts. This limits detection of novel categories. The paper is motivated by the need to integrate relational scene context into OVOD.
AI.method: The method proposes a Scene-guided Relational Modeling framework for open-vocabulary object detection. It uses scene graphs to encode semantic and spatial relations between candidate regions and contextual objects, models local interactions among neighboring regions, applies a Relation Attention Module to emphasize important relational cues, and adds a scene-based textual alignment branch to distill category knowledge from captions for relational alignment.
AI.result: Comprehensive experiments show that the proposed model outperforms other open-vocabulary object detection methods and improves average precision for novel categories on both COCO and LVIS datasets.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that explicitly modeling scene-level object relationships and aligning them with caption-derived semantic knowledge improves open-vocabulary object detection, especially for novel categories, achieving better AP on COCO and LVIS than prior OVOD methods.

title: Staying with the Uncertainty: Uncertainty-Scaffolding Strategies for Artificial Moral Advisors in LLM-to-LLM Simulated Conversations
summary: LLMs are increasingly deployed as Artificial Moral Advisors (AMA) in a variety of contexts: what kind of conversational patterns should they display? In this paper, we study how AMA can help their interlocutors "stay with the uncertainty". We propose three modes of uncertainty (Perspective-Multiplying, Tension-Preserving, Process-Reflecting) and compare them against three control conditions (Baseline, Persuasive, Sycophantic). A user-agent LLM engages in a dialogue on an ethical dilemma with an AMA following a specific uncertainty strategy, and completes pre- and post-conversation questionnaires. We further examine the effect of two persona prompt formats (Declarative and Narrative). We found that (1) no single model dominates as a simulated user agent, with open models aligning with human ambiguity through between-persona divergence and closed models through within-persona hedging; (2) declarative personas better capture initial stance diversity while narrative personas show more realistic belief revision; (3) all six AMA strategies produce distinguishable conversational patterns; and (4) uncertainty strategies differ not in how much stance revision they produce, but in the quality of engagement they sustain.

AI.tldr: 本文研究LLM作为人工道德顾问时应如何处理伦理不确定性，提出三种不确定性策略并与三种对照策略比较。结论是：这些策略都会显著改变对话风格，但并不会明显改变用户改变态度的多少；真正不同的是它们维持高质量伦理参与和反思的方式。
AI.motivation: 随着LLM越来越多地被部署为人工道德顾问，关键问题是它们应采用何种对话模式，尤其是在伦理不确定性情境下，如何帮助用户“与不确定性共处”。
AI.method: 作者提出三种不确定性模式（Perspective-Multiplying、Tension-Preserving、Process-Reflecting），并与三种对照条件（Baseline、Persuasive、Sycophantic）比较。实验中，一个用户代理LLM围绕伦理困境与采用特定策略的AMA对话，并完成对话前后问卷；同时比较两种persona提示格式：Declarative与Narrative。
AI.result: 结果显示：(1) 没有单一模型在模拟用户代理上全面占优；开源模型更多通过不同persona之间的分歧贴近人类模糊性，闭源模型则更多通过同一persona内部的犹豫表达；(2) declarative persona更能捕捉初始立场多样性，而narrative persona更能表现真实的信念修正；(3) 六种AMA策略都产生了可区分的对话模式；(4) 不确定性策略之间的差异主要在于其维持的互动质量，而不是立场修正量。
AI.conclusion: 研究表明，在将大语言模型用作人工道德顾问时，不同的不确定性对话策略会形成可区分的交互模式；它们的差异主要体现在维持何种参与质量，而非促成立场改变的幅度。

title: Intercomparison of Machine Learning Algorithms for Remote Sensing-based In-season Crop Mapping
summary: In-season crop type mapping is critical for food security in the face of increasingly extreme climate-related threats to crops. Currently, the USDA Cropland Data Layer provides crop type labels at 30m resolution and is available the February after harvest, but no product exists that maps crop types before harvest with satisfactory accuracy that would allow emergency managers to respond to crop threats in near real time. Furthermore, the relative advantages of a wide range of algorithms have not been evaluated in a way that accounts for interannual variability, until this study. Here, Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel surface reflectance imagery time series and crop rotation history information are combined to map corn in Iowa and almonds in California at 30m resolution accurately by early June in unseen years, with robust quantification of uncertainty due to phenology and crop distribution. Thousands of model configurations across ten machine learning algorithms were compared using a year-wise cross-validation and a suite of metrics. Hyperparameter search revealed Support Vector Machines to be the most successful algorithm overall, with a mean F1 score of 0.74 (0.59) across five unseen validation years for almonds by early June in California (corn by early June in Iowa). Interannual variation was a large source of uncertainty, but patterns showed the potential to further improve performance with ensemble approaches or ancillary data. Future work may extend these methods to include multiclass maps of all crop types, CONUS-wide maps, and in-season crop yield forecasting.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that combining HLS imagery and crop history can map crops before harvest at 30 m resolution, with SVMs performing best overall, but year-to-year variation is still a major challenge.
AI.motivation: Existing USDA crop maps arrive only after harvest, so there is a need for accurate pre-harvest crop type maps that support near-real-time response to climate-related crop threats and that account for interannual variability in evaluation.
