AI.method: The study combined Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel surface reflectance time series with crop rotation history and compared thousands of model configurations across ten machine learning algorithms using year-wise cross-validation and multiple evaluation metrics.
AI.result: For unseen validation years, SVMs achieved the strongest mean F1 scores by early June: 0.74 for almonds in California and 0.59 for corn in Iowa, while uncertainty from phenology and crop distribution was explicitly quantified.
AI.conclusion: Support Vector Machines performed best overall for in-season crop type mapping before harvest, achieving useful early-June accuracy at 30 m resolution in unseen years, though interannual variability remains a major source of uncertainty.

title: Entropy-Based Evaluation of AI Agents: A Lightweight Framework for Measuring Behavioral Patterns
summary: AI agents are commonly evaluated using task success, reward, latency, and cost. These metrics are useful, but they often miss important aspects of agent behavior: whether an agent explores too much, repeats itself too rigidly, uses tools effectively, reduces uncertainty over time, or remains robust across repeated runs. This paper proposes Entropy-Based Evaluation of AI Agents (EEA), a lightweight framework for measuring agent behavior through entropy. Rather than treating intelligence as only final task completion, EEA studies the structure of the agents decision process. The framework introduces action entropy, trajectory entropy, tool entropy, information gain, exploration efficiency, and robustness entropy. These metrics are intended to complement, not replace, traditional evaluation methods. We also present a practical Python implementation designed to integrate with agent frameworks such as LangChain, Google ADK, custom agent loops, and stored observability traces.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes EEA, an entropy-based framework for evaluating how AI agents behave during decision-making, complementing standard metrics with measures of exploration, tool usage, information gain, and robustness.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that standard agent evaluation metrics like success, reward, latency, and cost fail to capture important behavioral properties such as over-exploration, rigid repetition, ineffective tool use, uncertainty reduction, and robustness across repeated executions.
AI.method: The method is a lightweight evaluation framework called Entropy-Based Evaluation of AI Agents (EEA) that measures agent behavior using entropy-oriented metrics such as action entropy, trajectory entropy, tool entropy, information gain, exploration efficiency, and robustness entropy, with a Python implementation for integration into existing agent systems.
AI.result: The paper introduces a set of entropy-based behavioral metrics and a practical Python implementation compatible with frameworks like LangChain, Google ADK, custom loops, and observability traces.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that entropy-based metrics provide a practical and complementary way to evaluate AI agents beyond task success by capturing structure, exploration, tool use, uncertainty reduction, and run-to-run robustness.

title: MemoryCard: Topic-Aware Multi-Modal Clue Compression for Long-Video Question Answering
summary: Long-video question answering remains challenging for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), as answer-relevant evidence is often sparse, transient, and temporally dispersed across lengthy video contexts. Existing frame-centric approaches improve efficiency through uniform sampling, query-aware frame selection, visual-token compression, and adaptive resolution strategies. However, they still rely on isolated and fragmented frames as the fundamental evidence units, limiting VLMs' ability to effectively capture coherent event-level semantics. To address this limitation, we propose MemoryCard, a video-memory-based augmentation framework that organizes long videos into self-contained Memory Cards. Specifically, MemoryCard first performs a self-reading process over videos and aligned utterances to segment the video into semantically coherent units, each corresponding to a distinct topic or event. For each unit, it generates an event-level video gist and selects representative visual moments, which are then rendered into unified Memory Cards for retrieval and question answering. Experimental results demonstrate that MemoryCard consistently improves long-video QA performance under comparable visual-token budgets, achieving up to a 21.8% relative improvement in accuracy. All code is available at https://github.com/NEUIR/MemoryCard.

AI.tldr: MemoryCard converts long videos into event-based memory cards containing a gist plus representative moments, enabling better retrieval of coherent evidence and substantially improving long-video QA accuracy.
AI.motivation: Existing long-video QA methods mostly use isolated frames as evidence, even when they improve sampling or compression efficiency. This frame-centric design struggles to capture coherent event-level semantics when relevant evidence is sparse, brief, and distributed across long temporal contexts.
AI.method: The paper proposes MemoryCard, a video-memory augmentation framework. It first performs self-reading over videos and aligned utterances to segment the video into semantically coherent event/topic units. For each unit, it generates an event-level gist and selects representative visual moments, then renders them into unified Memory Cards for retrieval and QA.
AI.result: Experiments show consistent gains on long-video QA with comparable visual-token budgets, including up to 21.8% relative accuracy improvement.
AI.conclusion: MemoryCard shows that organizing long videos into event-level memory units improves long-video question answering more effectively than frame-centric evidence selection under similar visual-token budgets.

title: EMBER: Efficient Memory via Budgeted Evidence Retention for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Long-horizon agents can archive large histories, but future answers still incur retrieval, rereading, and context costs. When retained memory misses answer-relevant evidence, the system must return to larger portions of the raw history. We study budgeted evidence survival: before the query is known, which source evidence should be retained so that it remains recoverable and usable under a fixed retained source-evidence token budget? We instantiate this setting as Budgeted Pre-Query Retention, where memory is written during ingestion and later read without access to the full raw stream. We introduce EMBER, a learned retention policy that constructs a compact, source-backed evidence state. EMBER stores evidence capsules: verbatim source excerpts paired with retrieval keys and update metadata, preserving both grounding and read-time access. Post-query outcome feedback trains the writer to preserve evidence across the ingestion-retrieval-answer chain. On LongMemEval-RR, our LongMemEval-derived retained-evidence protocol, EMBER-14B reaches 0.3017 F1 at the 8192-token retained-evidence comparison point, compared with 0.1765 for the strongest non-EMBER budgeted baseline. Across retained source-evidence budgets, EMBER improves F1, Retain-Recall, and Read-Recall, indicating that long-horizon memory depends on retaining evidence within the budget rather than rereading larger histories.

AI.tldr: EMBER通过在查询前学习性地压缩并保留带来源依据的关键证据，使长期记忆问答在有限token预算下显著优于传统预算保留方法。 / EMBER learns to preserve source-grounded key evidence before queries arrive, yielding much better long-horizon QA under tight token budgets than prior budgeted retention baselines.
AI.motivation: 长时程智能体即使能存大量历史，在回答未来问题时仍面临检索、重读和上下文窗口成本；若保留记忆遗漏关键证据，就必须回看大段原始历史。因此作者关注：在查询未知时，如何在有限预算内提前保留最有价值的源证据。 / Even if long-horizon agents can archive large histories, future question answering still suffers from retrieval, rereading, and context-window costs. If retained memory misses key evidence, the system must revisit large raw histories. The paper therefore asks how to preserve the most valuable source evidence in advance under a fixed budget before the query is known.
AI.method: 论文提出Budgeted Pre-Query Retention设定，并设计EMBER作为学习式保留策略。在摄取阶段，EMBER写入‘evidence capsules’：包含逐字源文本片段、检索键和更新元数据的紧凑证据状态；随后利用查询后的结果反馈，训练写入器优化从摄取、检索到回答的整链路证据保留。 / The paper formulates Budgeted Pre-Query Retention and introduces EMBER, a learned retention policy. During ingestion, EMBER writes evidence capsules—verbatim source excerpts plus retrieval keys and update metadata—into a compact evidence state; post-query outcome feedback then trains the writer end-to-end over ingestion, retrieval, and answering.
AI.result: 在LongMemEval-RR上，EMBER-14B在8192-token保留证据预算点达到0.3017 F1，而最强非EMBER预算基线为0.1765；并且在不同预算下，EMBER在F1、Retain-Recall和Read-Recall上均有提升。 / On LongMemEval-RR, EMBER-14B achieves 0.3017 F1 at the 8192-token retained-evidence budget, versus 0.1765 for the strongest non-EMBER budgeted baseline. It also improves F1, Retain-Recall, and Read-Recall across retained-evidence budgets.
AI.conclusion: 在固定保留证据预算下，长期记忆系统的关键不在于事后重读更长历史，而在于预先保留可恢复、可使用的源证据；EMBER在多个预算点上显著优于基线。 / Under a fixed retained-evidence budget, long-horizon memory works best by preserving recoverable and usable source evidence in advance rather than rereading larger histories later; EMBER substantially outperforms baselines across budgets.

title: Zero-Copy Semantic Contagion: An In-Memory Streaming Architecture for Evolving Attention Graphs
comment: Accepted to the 2026 ACM SIGMOD Workshop on Data Management for the Modern Financial Systems (FinDS). 10 pages, 4 figures
summary: Per-ticker forecasting models dominate financial time-series work yet remain blind to cross-company propagation: a foundry disruption in Taiwan does not register in a single-asset model until Apple's own price has already moved. To address this limitation, we introduce a heterogeneous Rust-Python streaming architecture that maps cross-company attention as a continuous-time graph driven directly from text. We show that on the ingestion side, a zero-copy Rust edge parses news records in $\sim$100 ns and scans the target equity universe in $\sim$1.2 $μ$s. On the inference end, a multivariate Neural Hawkes Process featuring per-node continuous-time LSTM states and a bilinear latent projection propagates directed excitation, while an adaptive pruning rule bounds the computational cost of dynamic neighborhood updates. Combining these stages, we demonstrate an end-to-end processing latency of $\sim$13 ms per incoming news record on a single commodity CPU. Evaluated on a one-month temporal holdout of the FNSPID corpus (638 articles across 47 tickers), the system delivers a $1.70\times$ precision lift over random at the 90th-percentile next-day return threshold, and $3.36\times$ over a same-sector baseline. Crucially, removing the graph topology collapses precision to zero, confirming that the dynamic attention network is the sole driver of cross-company signal in this architecture.

AI.tldr: A low-latency Rust-Python pipeline uses text-driven dynamic graphs and a Neural Hawkes Process to forecast cross-company stock moves, and the graph structure is essential to the observed prediction gains.
AI.motivation: Standard per-ticker forecasting models cannot represent cross-company event propagation, so important upstream disruptions are missed until the affected company’s own price already reacts.
AI.method: It builds a heterogeneous Rust-Python streaming system where a zero-copy Rust ingestion layer parses news and scans target tickers, and a multivariate Neural Hawkes Process with per-node continuous-time LSTM states, bilinear latent projection, and adaptive pruning propagates directed cross-company excitation over a dynamic graph.
AI.result: The system achieves about 13 ms end-to-end latency per news item on a single commodity CPU, and on a one-month holdout of FNSPID (638 articles, 47 tickers) it delivers 1.70x precision lift over random at the 90th-percentile next-day return threshold and 3.36x over a same-sector baseline.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that cross-company signal for financial forecasting is captured only when dynamic graph topology is modeled from text streams; without the graph, predictive precision collapses to zero.

title: QCFuse: Query-Aware Cache Fusion via Compressed View for Efficient RAG Serving
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves large language model (LLM) answer quality by grounding generation in external evidence, but processing retrieved contexts makes the prefill stage a dominant serving cost. RAG cache fusion reduces this cost by reusing precomputed key-value (KV) caches for retrieved chunks and selectively recomputing tokens under the current prompt. Existing selectors, however, face a dilemma between quality and efficiency: fast query-agnostic or final-layer query-to-context selectors can miss request-relevant evidence, whereas full-view query-aware selectors require broad context and layer visibility before recomputation and therefore stall the layer-wise cache-fusion pipeline. We present QCFuse, a compressed-view query-aware selector for RAG cache fusion. QCFuse uses chunk-anchor query probing to condition user-query states on compact per-chunk anchors and critical-layer profiling to identify recomputation tokens without all-layer inspection. We implement QCFuse in SGLang and evaluate it on four open-weight LLMs across six datasets. QCFuse reaches full-prefill-level quality. At matched quality, QCFuse achieves an average prefill-time speedup of 1.7x over full prefill and 1.5x over ProphetKV, the strongest quality-preserving baseline.

AI.tldr: QCFuse improves RAG cache fusion by using a compressed but query-aware token selector, achieving full-prefill quality with substantially lower prefill latency than prior methods.
AI.motivation: In RAG serving, prefill over retrieved contexts is expensive. Existing cache-fusion selectors either sacrifice quality because they are too shallow or query-agnostic, or sacrifice efficiency because they need broad context and deep layer visibility that break the layer-wise fusion pipeline. The work aims to resolve this quality-efficiency tradeoff.
AI.method: The paper proposes QCFuse, which combines chunk-anchor query probing to inject user-query awareness using compact per-chunk anchors, and critical-layer profiling to identify which tokens need recomputation without requiring full all-layer inspection. It is implemented in SGLang for RAG cache fusion.
AI.result: Across four open-weight LLMs and six datasets, QCFuse matches full-prefill-level quality. At the same quality level, it delivers 1.7x average prefill-time speedup over full prefill and 1.5x over ProphetKV.
AI.conclusion: QCFuse is a compressed-view, query-aware selector for RAG cache fusion that preserves full-prefill answer quality while significantly reducing prefill cost.

title: Faithful, Enriched, and Precise: Benchmarking Natural-Science Illustration Generation by T2I models
summary: Scientific illustrations are essential tools for communicating research findings, especially in natural science, where they visualize complex concepts and processes. As Text-to-Image (T2I) models become increasingly capable, researchers have started to use them for scientific illustration generation. However, existing benchmarks often assess outputs at a holistic level, overlooking fine-grained elements, while scientific reasoning ability and output conciseness remain under-quantified. We introduce FEPBench, a benchmark built from carefully selected high-quality scientific illustrations across multiple disciplines and layout types. With the assistance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and human experts, we provide fine-grained atom set annotations and systematically evaluate T2I models along three dimensions: instruction faithfulness, reasoning enrichment, and semantic precision. Our evaluation further decomposes model performance across visual, textual, relation, and layout elements. Results show that even state-of-the-art (SOTA) closed-source models, such as GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro, still suffer from text-rendering bottlenecks, limited reasoning enrichment, and difficulty balancing generation richness with precision. These findings provide practical guidance for improving and deploying T2I models in scientific illustration generation. Benchmark data, atom set annotations, and evaluation code will be released by us.

AI.tldr: FEPBench is a fine-grained benchmark for evaluating text-to-image models on scientific illustration generation, and it shows that even the best current models still struggle with accurate text, reasoning, and precision.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks for scientific illustration generation evaluate outputs too holistically and fail to quantify fine-grained element fidelity, scientific reasoning ability, and output conciseness. The authors aim to provide a more rigorous and diagnostic benchmark for this task.
AI.method: The paper introduces FEPBench, a benchmark constructed from carefully selected high-quality scientific illustrations across disciplines and layout types. It uses multimodal large language models and human experts to create fine-grained atom-set annotations, and evaluates text-to-image models across instruction faithfulness, reasoning enrichment, and semantic precision, further decomposed into visual, textual, relation, and layout elements.
AI.result: The evaluation shows that even leading closed-source models such as GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro still have major weaknesses, especially in rendering text accurately, enriching outputs with scientific reasoning, and balancing expressive richness with semantic precision.
AI.conclusion: FEPBench reveals that current state-of-the-art text-to-image models are still not reliable enough for scientific illustration generation, particularly in text rendering, scientific reasoning enrichment, and maintaining precision while producing rich outputs.

title: Representing Research Attention as Contextually Structured Flows
comment: Accepted at STi 2026 - International Conference on Science and Technology Indicators
summary: Research attention is widely used as an indicator of visibility, influence, and societal uptake, yet it is typically represented as aggregated counts that do not preserve how attention develops across contexts over time. This creates a mismatch between how attention is interpreted and how it is represented. We propose attention flows as contextually structured representations that encode the organisation of attention and its evolution over time. We evaluate whether these representations capture transferable structure by constructing a benchmark based on analogy-style reasoning across research outputs. Comparing signal, sequence, and flow-based representations, we find that flow representations more effectively support structural comparison, particularly in settings where attention is shaped by temporal progression or context distributions. We further show that learned flow representations improve robustness under partial observation and structural perturbation. Overall, these results support modelling attention as a contextually structured phenomenon and provide a basis for more informative approaches to research evaluation.

AI.tldr: 论文提出用“attention flows”来表示研究关注度，把时间和上下文结构保留下来。实验表明，这种表示比传统聚合计数或简单序列更适合做结构性比较，也更稳健，可用于更有信息量的科研评价。 / The paper proposes attention flows to represent research attention while preserving temporal and contextual structure. Experiments show they are better than aggregate counts or simple sequences for structural comparison and are more robust, supporting more informative research evaluation.
AI.motivation: 现有研究通常用聚合计数表示研究关注度，但这种表示无法保留关注度在不同情境中随时间发展的方式，导致“关注度的解释”与“关注度的表示”之间存在错配。 / Research attention is commonly represented by aggregate counts, which fail to preserve how attention develops across contexts over time, creating a mismatch between how attention is interpreted and how it is represented.
AI.method: 提出“attention flows”表征，将关注度按上下文与时间组织；构建基于类比推理的基准任务，比较signal、sequence与flow三类表征在跨研究产出结构迁移中的表现，并测试其在部分观测和结构扰动下的鲁棒性。 / The paper introduces attention-flow representations that encode attention by context and time, builds an analogy-style benchmark to test transferable structure across research outputs, compares signal-, sequence-, and flow-based representations, and evaluates robustness under partial observation and structural perturbation.
AI.result: flow表征在结构比较任务上整体优于signal和sequence表征，尤其在时间推进和上下文分布决定关注模式的场景中优势更明显；同时，学习得到的flow表征在缺失观测和结构扰动条件下表现出更强鲁棒性。 / Flow representations outperform signal and sequence representations on structural comparison tasks, especially when attention is driven by temporal progression or context distributions, and learned flow representations show stronger robustness to missing observations and structural perturbations.
AI.conclusion: 将研究关注度建模为具有上下文结构且随时间演化的“attention flows”，比简单聚合计数、单纯信号或序列表征更能支持结构性比较，并在不完整观测和结构扰动下更稳健。 / Modelling research attention as contextually structured, time-evolving attention flows better supports structural comparison than aggregated counts, signals, or sequences, and is more robust under partial observation and perturbation.

title: Beyond Soft Masks: Hard-Perturbation Mixup Explainer for Robust GNN Explainability
summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across a range of applications involving graph-structured data, particularly in high-stakes domains. However, the opaque nature of their decision-making processes limits their trustworthiness and broader adoption. Existing post-hoc explanation methods aim to improve explainability by identifying subgraphs that influence GNN predictions and adopt mixup strategies to alleviate the out-of-distribution (OOD) issue caused by using subgraphs for prediction. Yet, these approaches typically rely on soft masks, which are inherently unable to fully eliminate label-irrelevant information, allowing redundant structures to leak into the mixup process and hindering the resolution of the OOD problem, thereby degrading explanation fidelity. In this work, we propose HPME, a Hard-Perturbation Mixup Explanation framework grounded in a generalized Graph Information Bottleneck, which leverages graph pooling to extract discrete explanatory subgraphs and to yield an information-capacity bound to thoroughly compress label-irrelevant components. Furthermore, we introduce a novel mixup strategy built upon structure-level replacement, generating in-distribution explanations to effectively mitigate the distribution shift. Extensive experiments on diverse tasks demonstrate that HPME achieves state-of-the-art performance in generating robust and interpretable explanations across both synthetic and real-world datasets.

AI.tldr: HPME is a new GNN explanation method that replaces soft-mask explanations with discrete subgraphs and structure-level mixup, reducing irrelevant information and OOD shift to produce stronger explanations.
AI.motivation: Existing GNN explanation methods often use soft masks and subgraph-based mixup, which cannot fully remove label-irrelevant information. This causes redundant structures to leak into the explanation and mixup process, leading to out-of-distribution issues and reduced explanation fidelity.
AI.method: The paper proposes HPME, a Hard-Perturbation Mixup Explanation framework based on a generalized Graph Information Bottleneck. It uses graph pooling to obtain discrete explanatory subgraphs with an information-capacity bound that compresses label-irrelevant information, and introduces a structure-level replacement mixup strategy to generate more in-distribution explanations.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across diverse tasks show that HPME delivers state-of-the-art performance, producing more robust and interpretable explanations than prior methods on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
AI.conclusion: HPME improves GNN post-hoc explanations by extracting discrete explanatory subgraphs and using structure-level mixup to reduce distribution shift, achieving state-of-the-art robustness and interpretability on synthetic and real-world datasets.

title: Retry Policy Gradients in Continuous Action Spaces
summary: Retry-based objectives such as pass@K and max@K optimize the best return obtained from multiple sampled trajectories, and recent work has shown that they can promote exploration without explicit exploration bonuses. In discrete action spaces, ReMax was shown to do so by adapting to return uncertainty. In this work, we introduce pathwise derivative estimators for retry objectives and use them to extend ReMax to continuous action spaces. We study the resulting learning dynamics and show that, even with deterministic rewards, ReMax can encourage stochastic exploration by reshaping the policy-gradient landscape. In particular, it alters gradients both in direction, biasing updates toward higher policy entropy, and in magnitude, damping gradients and slowing convergence. We further show that Adam's adaptive normalization can mitigate this damping, depending on its numerical stabilization parameter. Empirically, we instantiate this objective as ReMax Actor-Critic (ReMAC), an off-policy actor--critic algorithm that optimizes the ReMax objective using a pathwise derivative estimator. Our experiments show that ReMAC can promote higher policy entropy without entropy regularization and achieves performance comparable to SAC.

AI.tldr: The paper extends ReMax to continuous control with pathwise gradients, showing that retry-based optimization itself can induce stochastic exploration and yielding an off-policy algorithm, ReMAC, that matches SAC-level performance without explicit entropy bonuses.
AI.motivation: Prior retry-based objectives like pass@K/max@K and ReMax showed exploration benefits in discrete action spaces, but a continuous-action extension and a clear understanding of the learning dynamics were missing.
AI.method: The paper derives pathwise derivative estimators for retry-based objectives and uses them to build ReMAC, an off-policy actor-critic algorithm that optimizes the ReMax objective in continuous action spaces. It also analyzes the induced policy-gradient dynamics and the interaction with Adam normalization.
AI.result: The analysis shows ReMax reshapes policy gradients by changing both direction and magnitude: it biases updates toward higher entropy and damps gradients, slowing convergence. Adam can partly offset this damping depending on its stabilization parameter. Empirically, ReMAC increases policy entropy without entropy regularization and performs comparably to SAC.
AI.conclusion: ReMax can be extended to continuous action spaces using pathwise derivative estimators, and the resulting ReMAC algorithm encourages exploration through higher policy entropy without explicit entropy regularization while achieving performance comparable to SAC.

title: T-FunS3D: Task-Driven Hierarchical Open-Vocabulary 3D Functionality Segmentation
summary: Open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation enables robots to localize functional object components in 3D scenes. It is a challenging task that requires spatial understanding and task interpretation. Current open-vocabulary 3D segmentation methods primarily focus on object-level recognition, while scene-wide part segmentation methods attempt to segment the entire scene exhaustively, making them highly resource-intensive and time consuming. Balancing segmentation performance in terms of granularity, accuracy, and speed remains a challenge. As one step towards alleviating this, we introduce T-FunS3D, a task-driven hierarchical open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation method that provides actionable perception for robotic applications. Our method takes as input the 3D point cloud and posed RGB-D images of an indoor scene. We construct an open-vocabulary scene graph by extracting instances and their visual embeddings in the environment. Given a task description, T-FunS3D identifies the most relevant instances in the scene graph and locates their functional components leveraging a vision-language model. Experiments on the SceneFun3D dataset demonstrate that T-FunS3D is comparable to state-of-the-art in open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation, while achieving faster runtime and reduced memory usage.

AI.tldr: T-FunS3D segments task-relevant functional parts in 3D indoor scenes by combining scene graphs and vision-language models, matching SOTA accuracy while running faster and using less memory.
AI.motivation: Existing open-vocabulary 3D segmentation mainly targets object-level recognition, while scene-wide part segmentation is exhaustive, slow, and resource-intensive. The work is motivated by the need to balance granularity, accuracy, and speed for robotic functional understanding in 3D scenes.
AI.method: The paper proposes T-FunS3D, a task-driven hierarchical open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation framework. It takes 3D point clouds and posed RGB-D images, builds an open-vocabulary scene graph with object instances and visual embeddings, and uses a vision-language model plus task descriptions to retrieve relevant instances and localize their functional components.
AI.result: On the SceneFun3D dataset, T-FunS3D achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods in open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation, with faster runtime and lower memory consumption.
AI.conclusion: T-FunS3D demonstrates state-of-the-art-comparable open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation while being faster and more memory-efficient, making it practical for robotic actionable perception.

title: Reducing Hallucinations in Complex Question Answering using Simple Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (long version)
summary:
Large language models (LLMs) have fundamentally transformed the landscape of Natural Language Processing. Despite these advances, LLMs and LLM-based systems remain prone to a variety of failure modes. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have emerged as a common deployment scenario seeking to both avoid the well known risk of the LLM "hallucinating" information, and to enable reasoning and question answering over proprietary information that the LLM did not have access to during training without resorting to expensive model fine-tuning.
  In this work, we explore the idea of using a lightweight graph structure with a relatively simple graph schema, to support the RAG subsystem via a dedicated toolset. We design an agentic system with a variety of vector search and graph query tools operating over a structured dataset based on a curated subset of English Wikipedia articles, and evaluate its performance on questions from MoNaCo, a challenging Wikipedia QA benchmark of complex query answering tasks.
  Our results show that the introduction of graph-based tools can significantly increase the precision and recall of factual correctness, can halve the number of hallucinated answers, and achieves the highest fine-grained truthfulness score among the three evaluated scenarios. All this with a modest increase in token usage.

AI.tldr: TL;DR: The paper adds lightweight graph querying to an agentic RAG pipeline and shows that this makes complex QA more truthful and less hallucinatory than standard retrieval approaches, at a small extra token cost.
AI.motivation: Although LLMs are powerful, they still fail in important ways, especially through hallucinations and weak access to proprietary or unseen knowledge. RAG helps, but the authors aim to further improve reliability and multi-hop reasoning by augmenting RAG with a lightweight graph structure rather than relying only on unstructured retrieval or expensive fine-tuning.
AI.method: The paper builds an agentic retrieval-augmented generation system that combines vector search tools and graph query tools over a structured dataset derived from a curated subset of English Wikipedia. The graph uses a relatively simple schema and is exposed through a dedicated toolset for retrieval and reasoning. The system is evaluated on the MoNaCo benchmark for complex Wikipedia question answering.
AI.result: Compared with the evaluated alternatives, the graph-enhanced setup significantly improves factual precision and recall, cuts hallucinated answers by roughly 50%, and delivers the highest fine-grained truthfulness score, with only a modest token-cost increase.
AI.conclusion: Using a lightweight graph structure and graph-based tools in an agentic RAG system improves factual QA performance on complex Wikipedia questions: it increases precision/recall of factual correctness, reduces hallucinations by about half, achieves the best fine-grained truthfulness among tested settings, and only modestly increases token usage.

title: Domain-Adapted Small Language Models with Hybrid Post-Processing: Achieving Cost-Efficient, Low-Latency Multi-Label Structured Prediction via LoRA Fine-Tuning on Scarce Data
summary:
Deploying frontier large language models (LLMs) for domain-specific structured evaluation tasks often incurs substantial latency, cost, and data privacy overhead. We present a hybrid framework that combines a fine-tuned small language model (LLaMA 3.1 8B, with only 2.05% trainable parameters via LoRA) and a deterministic rule-based post-processing layer. Trained on just 219 curated examples, the system is applied to multi-label compliance evaluation of conversational transcripts spanning 18 heterogeneous output fields. In blind evaluation on 53 previously unseen production transcripts, it achieves 100% JSON structural validity, 83.0% human-validated overall accuracy, and 100% accuracy on the most critical classification field. The proposed approach formalizes a hybrid neural-symbolic decomposition and introduces targeted hard-negative augmentation to improve performance on critical decision boundaries. Running on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, inference completes in approximately 2 seconds, which is 2-5x faster than frontier-model APIs. The system costs only $0.013 per evaluation compared with $0.025-$0.055 for proprietary alternatives, resulting in 46-76% cost savings. These results demonstrate that domain-adapted small language models, when combined with deterministic post-processing, can match frontier-model accuracy for structured compliance evaluation while substantially reducing operational cost, latency, and privacy risk.
  Keywords: small language models, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, LoRA, domain adaptation, hybrid inference, compliance evaluation, structured output.

AI.tldr: A LoRA-tuned 8B model plus deterministic rules matches key frontier-LLM performance for structured compliance checks, while being faster, cheaper, and better for privacy.
AI.motivation: Frontier LLMs are expensive, slower, and create data privacy concerns when used for domain-specific structured evaluation tasks. The work aims to build a cheaper, faster, and more privacy-preserving alternative without sacrificing accuracy.
AI.method: The paper fine-tunes LLaMA 3.1 8B using LoRA with only 2.05% trainable parameters on 219 curated examples, then applies a deterministic rule-based post-processing layer for 18-field multi-label structured compliance evaluation. It also introduces targeted hard-negative augmentation to strengthen critical decision boundaries.
AI.result: On 53 unseen production transcripts, the system achieved 100% JSON structural validity, 83.0% overall human-validated accuracy, and 100% accuracy on the most critical classification field. Inference took about 2 seconds on a single A100 GPU and cost $0.013 per evaluation, yielding 46-76% cost savings versus proprietary frontier-model APIs.
AI.conclusion: A hybrid system combining a LoRA-tuned small language model with deterministic rule-based post-processing can deliver frontier-level performance for domain-specific structured compliance evaluation while significantly reducing latency, cost, and privacy overhead.

title: Retrospective Harness Optimization: Improving LLM Agents via Self-Preference over Trajectory Rollouts
summary: AI agents rely on a harness of skills, tools, and workflows to solve complex problems. Continually improving this harness is essential for adapting to new tasks. However, existing optimization methods typically require ground-truth validation sets, yet such labeled data is difficult to acquire in practical deployment settings. To address this problem, we introduce Retrospective Harness Optimization (RHO), a self-supervised method that optimizes the agent harness using only past trajectories. Specifically, RHO selects a diverse coreset of challenging tasks from past trajectories and re-solves them in parallel. The agent analyzes these rollouts using self-validation and self-consistency, then generates candidate harness updates and selects the most effective one by its own pairwise self-preference. We evaluate RHO across three diverse domains, spanning software engineering, technical work, and knowledge work. Notably, a single optimization round improves the pass rate on SWE-Bench Pro from 59% to 78% without any external grading. Furthermore, our analysis demonstrates that RHO effectively targets prior failure modes. As a result, the optimized harness alters the agent's behavior patterns and sustains higher accuracy during long-horizon sessions.

AI.tldr: 中文：论文提出RHO，一种只用历史轨迹、自监督优化AI agent工作流/harness的方法；它通过重做难任务、自我评估和自我偏好选择更新，在无标注条件下显著提升性能。 English: The paper proposes RHO, a self-supervised way to optimize an AI agent’s harness using only past trajectories; by replaying hard tasks and selecting updates through self-evaluation and self-preference, it significantly improves performance without labeled data.
AI.motivation: 中文：现有agent优化方法通常依赖带标注的ground-truth验证集，但在真实部署环境中这类数据昂贵且难以获得，因此需要一种无需外部监督的自优化方法。 English: Existing agent optimization approaches usually depend on labeled ground-truth validation sets, which are hard to obtain in real deployment settings, motivating a self-supervised optimization method.
AI.method: 中文：方法核心是Retrospective Harness Optimization (RHO)。它从历史轨迹中挑选具有挑战性且多样化的任务coreset，并行重新求解；随后agent通过self-validation与self-consistency分析rollouts，提出候选harness更新，再通过pairwise self-preference选择最优更新。 English: The method is Retrospective Harness Optimization (RHO): select a diverse, challenging coreset from past trajectories, re-solve them in parallel, use self-validation and self-consistency to analyze rollouts, generate candidate harness updates, and choose the best one via pairwise self-preference.
AI.result: 中文：RHO在软件工程、技术工作和知识工作三个领域进行了评估。单轮优化便将SWE-Bench Pro的通过率从59%提升到78%，且无需外部评分；分析还表明它能够有效针对既有失败模式，并改变agent行为模式以维持更高的长期准确率。 English: RHO was evaluated across software engineering, technical work, and knowledge work. A single optimization round increased SWE-Bench Pro pass rate from 59% to 78% without external grading, and analysis showed it targets prior failure modes and sustains higher long-horizon accuracy.
AI.conclusion: 中文：RHO证明了无需外部标注或人工构建验证集，也能仅依赖历史轨迹持续优化AI agent的harness，并在长时程任务中稳定提升表现。 English: RHO shows that an AI agent harness can be improved continuously using only past trajectories, without external labels or curated validation sets, yielding sustained gains in long-horizon tasks.

title: Video-Rate Streaming Stylization on a Vision-Aware MLLM-Conditioned Edit Diffusion: Asymmetric Batched Inference on a Distilled UNet + MLLM Text Encoder
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 12 tables. Under review at IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology. Code, evaluation harness, and the released v3 Temporal LLLite adapter weights are at https://github.com/otanl/dreamlite-stream (also mirrored to Hugging Face and Zenodo)
summary: Aggressive distillation of the diffusion U-Net inverts the per-frame bottleneck of real-time text-to-image pipelines: once the denoiser is a 4-step or 1-step distilled student, the text encoder becomes the critical path. This inversion is most acute in vision-aware edit diffusion, where the encoder is a multimodal large language model (MLLM). We study the case of a 0.39B distilled edit U-Net paired with a 2.13B MLLM text encoder (Qwen3-VL) and present a streaming pipeline targeted at this regime built around three engineering mechanisms: asymmetric side-stream / main-stream CUDA pipelining with batched text-encoder amortisation (and optional static-prompt caching), a compile-friendly ControlNet-LLLite reformulation that folds the entire U-Net + adapter stack into a single fused graph, and a periodic conditioning-refresh schedule with a hook subset that amortises the per-frame conditioning cost. On a single consumer RTX 3090 Ti at 512x512 the pipeline sustains 27.4 fps over a 480-frame run at batch size B=8 and 29.6 fps at B=16, with end-to-end p50 latency of approximately 0.5 and 1.0 seconds respectively; the same operating point measures 54.9 fps on RTX 4090 and 74.1 fps on RTX 5090. We report video-rate streaming throughput rather than interactive low latency, and locate our numbers against same-stack StreamDiffusion re-runs as systems context, not as a benchmark superiority claim. For the trained oil-painting style, the released temporal adapter generalises within in-clip noise to 19 unused DAVIS-2017 sequences and 15 non-DAVIS clips from seven sources; prompt-level generalisation to unseen style families is bounded and reported separately.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：这篇论文不是单纯压缩模型，而是重新优化“蒸馏后文本编码器反成瓶颈”的实时扩散编辑系统；通过CUDA流水、文本编码摊销、融合图编译和周期性条件刷新，在消费级GPU上实现了接近或达到视频帧率的流式编辑吞吐。 / TL;DR: Rather than only compressing the model, this paper re-optimizes real-time diffusion editing for the post-distillation regime where the text encoder becomes the bottleneck; with CUDA pipelining, text-encoding amortization, fused-graph compilation, and periodic conditioning refresh, it achieves near or full video-rate streaming throughput on consumer GPUs.
AI.motivation: 动机是：传统实时扩散系统通常把U-Net视为主要瓶颈，但在4步甚至1步蒸馏后，这一假设失效，文本编码尤其是MLLM编码成为关键路径。作者希望针对这种新的系统瓶颈重新设计推理流水线，以提高视觉感知编辑任务中的视频流式吞吐。 / The motivation is that traditional real-time diffusion systems assume the U-Net is the main bottleneck, but after 4-step or 1-step distillation this assumption breaks down, and text encoding—especially with an MLLM—becomes the critical path. The paper therefore redesigns the inference pipeline for this new bottleneck to improve streaming throughput in vision-aware editing.
AI.method: 方法上，论文围绕一个0.39B蒸馏编辑U-Net和2.13B Qwen3-VL文本编码器构建流式推理管线，核心包括三点：1）非对称side-stream/main-stream CUDA流水并结合批量文本编码摊销与静态prompt缓存；2）将ControlNet-LLLite改写为更适合编译和融合的形式，把U-Net与适配器并入单一融合计算图；3）采用周期性conditioning refresh与hook子集机制，降低逐帧条件计算成本。 / Methodologically, the paper builds a streaming inference pipeline around a 0.39B distilled edit U-Net and a 2.13B Qwen3-VL text encoder, with three key mechanisms: (1) asymmetric side-stream/main-stream CUDA pipelining plus batched text-encoder amortization and optional static-prompt caching; (2) a compile-friendly reformulation of ControlNet-LLLite that folds the U-Net and adapter stack into one fused graph; and (3) a periodic conditioning-refresh schedule with a hook subset to amortize per-frame conditioning cost.
AI.result: 结果显示，在RTX 3090 Ti上、512×512分辨率、480帧序列下，该系统可在B=8时达到27.4 fps、B=16时达到29.6 fps，对应端到端p50延迟约0.5秒和1.0秒；相同设置下，RTX 4090达到54.9 fps，RTX 5090达到74.1 fps。作者还报告了训练得到的油画风格时序适配器可泛化到19个未使用的DAVIS-2017序列和15个来自7个来源的非DAVIS片段，但对未见风格族的prompt级泛化有限。 / Results show that at 512×512 on an RTX 3090 Ti over 480 frames, the system sustains 27.4 fps at B=8 and 29.6 fps at B=16, with end-to-end p50 latency of about 0.5 s and 1.0 s respectively; the same setup reaches 54.9 fps on RTX 4090 and 74.1 fps on RTX 5090. The trained oil-painting temporal adapter generalizes to 19 unused DAVIS-2017 sequences and 15 non-DAVIS clips from seven sources, though prompt-level generalization to unseen style families is limited.
AI.conclusion: 该论文的结论是：当扩散模型的U-Net经过激进蒸馏后，实时文生图/图像编辑系统的瓶颈会从逐帧去噪器转移到文本编码器，尤其是在使用MLLM作为编码器的视觉感知编辑场景中。针对这一新瓶颈，作者提出的流式系统级优化可以在单张消费级GPU上实现稳定的视频级吞吐。 / The paper concludes that once the diffusion U-Net is aggressively distilled, the bottleneck in real-time text-to-image/editing pipelines shifts from per-frame denoising to the text encoder, especially when a multimodal LLM is used. The proposed streaming-system optimizations then enable sustained video-rate throughput on a single consumer GPU.

title: ACE-SQL: Adaptive Co-Optimization via Empirical Credit Assignment for Text-to-SQL
summary: Text-to-SQL maps natural language questions to executable SQL queries. Modern databases often contain large and complex schemas, making schema linking a critical step for accurate SQL generation. Existing methods either rely on full-schema generation, which leaves schema linking implicit within a large search space, or use a separate retriever trained with static gold-column supervision, whose targets may be suboptimal for the current generator policy. To address this issue, we propose Adaptive Co-optimization via Empirical Credit Assignment for Text-to-SQL (ACE-SQL), a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that jointly optimizes schema retrieval and SQL generation under execution feedback. ACE-SQL constructs an online column-set pool from generator rollouts and derives adaptive on-policy retrieval targets from the column set most frequently associated with execution-correct rollouts. This induces bidirectional adaptation, where the retriever adapts toward column sets that the generator can execute correctly, while the generator adapts to the retriever's evolving schema selections under execution feedback. With approximately 3k synthetic Text-to-SQL question-database pairs for RL training, ACE-SQL achieves 65.3% greedy execution accuracy on BIRD Dev while using 0.93k output tokens per query. The repository is available at https://github.com/xbchen1/ACE-SQL.

AI.tldr: ACE-SQL uses RL to let the schema retriever and SQL generator adapt to each other under execution feedback, improving Text-to-SQL performance on complex schemas with relatively little synthetic training data.
AI.motivation: In large and complex database schemas, schema linking is essential for Text-to-SQL. Prior methods either search over the full schema implicitly, which is inefficient and difficult, or train a separate retriever using static gold-column labels that may not align with the generator’s current behavior. The paper aims to align retrieval with generation dynamically.
AI.method: The paper proposes ACE-SQL, an RL framework that co-optimizes a schema retriever and SQL generator. It builds an online pool of column sets from generator rollouts, assigns adaptive on-policy retrieval targets based on the column sets most often associated with execution-correct outputs, and uses execution feedback to update both components bidirectionally.
AI.result: With about 3k synthetic Text-to-SQL question-database pairs for RL training, ACE-SQL reaches 65.3% greedy execution accuracy on BIRD Dev while using 0.93k output tokens per query.
AI.conclusion: ACE-SQL demonstrates that jointly optimizing schema retrieval and SQL generation with execution-feedback-driven reinforcement learning can improve Text-to-SQL accuracy and efficiency on complex schemas.

title: Causal Longitudinal Prior-Fitted Networks for Counterfactual Outcome Prediction
summary: Longitudinal treatment decisions require predicting potential outcomes under future treatment sequences in the presence of time-varying confounding, heterogeneous patient dynamics, and limited domain-specific data. Existing longitudinal causal estimators typically train a new model for each cohort or simulator. We introduce Causal Longitudinal Prior-Fitted Networks (CausalLongPFN), a prior-fitted in-context predictor for longitudinal causal prediction. The model is pretrained entirely on synthetic episodes sampled from a broad prior over temporal structural causal models, exposing it to treatment-confounder feedback, latent heterogeneity, nonlinear state evolution, delayed effects, and cumulative treatment responses. At test time, CausalLongPFN is frozen: it conditions on support trajectories, a query history, and a proposed future treatment sequence, and returns a predictive distribution over future outcomes without gradient updates or propensity-model fitting. Multi-step predictions are obtained by recursively applying the one-step predictor under the specified treatment sequence. We evaluate on branchable cancer, HIV, and warfarin benchmarks with ground-truth counterfactual labels, and on factual-only rolling-origin prediction in MIMIC-III ICU trajectories. CausalLongPFN is competitive with domain-trained longitudinal baselines on counterfactual benchmarks and performs strongly on factual MIMIC-III prediction, suggesting that broad synthetic causal pretraining can provide a useful frozen alternative when repeated domain-specific training is costly or impractical.

AI.tldr: A frozen prior-fitted network trained on synthetic longitudinal causal data can predict outcomes under treatment sequences without retraining, matching strong baselines across several benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Longitudinal treatment decision-making requires counterfactual prediction under future treatment sequences despite time-varying confounding, heterogeneous dynamics, and scarce domain data. Existing methods usually require training a separate model for each cohort or simulator, which is costly and limits reuse.
AI.method: The paper proposes CausalLongPFN, a prior-fitted network pretrained only on synthetic episodes generated from a wide prior over temporal structural causal models. At inference, the frozen model takes support trajectories, a query history, and a planned future treatment sequence, then predicts future outcomes recursively without gradient updates or explicit propensity modeling.
AI.result: CausalLongPFN is competitive with domain-trained longitudinal causal baselines on branchable cancer, HIV, and warfarin counterfactual benchmarks, and also performs strongly on factual rolling-origin prediction on MIMIC-III ICU trajectories.
AI.conclusion: Broad synthetic causal pretraining can yield a frozen in-context predictor for longitudinal causal inference that remains competitive with domain-trained methods and is practical when repeated cohort-specific training is expensive.

title: Towards World Models in Biomedical Research
summary: A central goal of biomedicine is to understand, predict and ultimately control the dynamic mechanisms by which biological systems respond to perturbations, disease progression and therapeutic intervention. Although foundation models and large language models have accelerated biomedical data interpretation, most current systems remain focused on static pattern recognition rather than prospective simulation of biological futures. Here we propose biomedical world models as a paradigm for AI-driven discovery. These models learn latent representations of molecular, cellular, tissue and clinical states, together with intervention-conditioned dynamics that allow future trajectories to be simulated before actions are taken. We discuss how biomedical world models could function as data engines, environment simulators and scientific planning substrates across applications including virtual cells, organoids, virtual patients and surgical simulation. We outline the data infrastructure, evaluation benchmarks, safety constraints and governance frameworks required. Biomedical world models may provide a foundation for simulation-guided, closed-loop and experimentally actionable biomedical discovery.

AI.tldr: 这是一篇提出“生物医学世界模型”概念的展望文章：目标是让AI不仅看懂生物医学数据，还能在干预前模拟系统未来，从而支持实验设计、治疗决策和闭环发现。 / This perspective introduces biomedical world models: AI systems that do not just interpret biomedical data, but simulate intervention-dependent biological futures to guide experiments and decisions.
AI.motivation: 现有基础模型和大语言模型虽提升了生物医学数据解释能力，但大多停留在静态模式识别，难以预测生物系统在扰动、疾病进展和治疗干预下的动态未来，因此需要一种能够进行前瞻性仿真的模型范式。 / Current foundation models and LLMs improve biomedical data interpretation but are mostly limited to static pattern recognition, motivating a new paradigm that can prospectively simulate biological responses to perturbation, disease progression, and therapy.
AI.method: 文章为观点/展望性论文，方法上并非提出单一实验算法，而是概念性定义生物医学世界模型：学习分子、细胞、组织和临床状态的潜在表示，并学习受干预条件约束的系统动力学，以便在执行行动前模拟未来轨迹。 / This is a perspective/concept paper rather than a single experimental method; it defines biomedical world models as systems that learn latent representations of molecular, cellular, tissue, and clinical states together with intervention-conditioned dynamics to simulate future trajectories before actions are taken.
AI.result: 论文讨论了该范式在虚拟细胞、类器官、虚拟病人和手术仿真中的潜在应用，并系统梳理了实现所需的数据基础设施、评测基准、安全约束和治理框架。由于摘要看，这里更偏向框架性主张而非报告具体实验性能。 / The paper outlines applications in virtual cells, organoids, virtual patients, and surgical simulation, and identifies the required data infrastructure, evaluation benchmarks, safety constraints, and governance frameworks. From the abstract, the result is primarily a framework and research agenda rather than a concrete empirical performance report.
AI.conclusion: 该文提出“生物医学世界模型”作为AI驱动发现的新范式，认为其可通过可干预的动态仿真支持面向未来、闭环且可实验验证的生物医学研究。 / The paper concludes that biomedical world models could serve as a new paradigm for AI-driven discovery by enabling intervention-aware simulation, closed-loop experimentation, and actionable biomedical research.

title: Multimodal Sexism Identification and Characterization using Large Language Models and Gradient Boosting
summary: We present the AILS-NTUA submission to the EXIST 2026 Lab at CLEF, addressing multimodal sexism identification and characterization in memes (Task 2) and short-form videos (Task 3). Our system follows a feature-engineered late-fusion pipeline built around gradient-boosted regression models and hierarchical post-processing. For memes, we combine visual, textual, demographic, biometric, and LLM-derived semantic indicators designed to capture high-level cues such as stereotyping, objectification, irony, and misogyny. For videos, we investigate the effect of feature selection, frame-based visual representations, OCR-based textual features, acoustic descriptors, and sensor-derived metadata. Development results show that focused LLM-derived semantic cues improve meme sexism identification, while video performance is highly sensitive to feature dimensionality and cross-modal noise. For videos, development results favor compact feature selection, but official test results show that this conclusion does not fully transfer to unseen data, where the unfiltered representation generalizes better. Overall, our findings highlight the usefulness of targeted semantic feature engineering for static memes and the need for more robust temporal modeling in noisy short-form video settings.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：这是一套用于meme和短视频性别歧视检测的多模态后期融合系统。meme任务受益于LLM提供的高层语义特征；视频任务则暴露出特征选择结论不稳定、对噪声敏感的问题，未来应加强时序建模与泛化能力。 / TL;DR: This is a multimodal late-fusion system for sexism detection in memes and short videos. Memes benefit from LLM-derived high-level semantic features, while videos reveal unstable feature-selection conclusions and high sensitivity to noise, motivating stronger temporal modeling and generalization.
AI.motivation: 动机在于解决EXIST 2026中多模态性别歧视内容识别与刻画问题，并进一步理解不同模态和特征类型在meme与短视频这两类媒介中的作用差异，尤其是高级语义线索、跨模态噪声和特征维度对泛化能力的影响。 / The motivation is to address multimodal sexism identification and characterization in the EXIST 2026 shared task and to understand how different modalities and feature types behave across memes and short videos, especially the effects of high-level semantic cues, cross-modal noise, and feature dimensionality on generalization.
AI.method: 方法上，作者构建了一个基于特征工程的后期融合流水线，以梯度提升回归模型为核心，并结合层次化后处理。对meme任务，融合视觉、文本、人口统计、生物特征以及LLM生成的语义指标；对视频任务，探索帧级视觉特征、OCR文本特征、声学特征、传感器元数据以及特征选择策略。 / Methodologically, the system uses a feature-engineered late-fusion pipeline centered on gradient-boosted regression models with hierarchical post-processing. For memes, it combines visual, textual, demographic, biometric, and LLM-derived semantic indicators; for videos, it studies frame-level visual features, OCR text, acoustic descriptors, sensor metadata, and feature selection strategies.
AI.result: 结果显示：在meme上，聚焦的LLM语义特征能提升开发集上的性别歧视识别效果；在视频上，开发集实验倾向于支持紧凑特征选择，但官方测试集表明不过滤的全特征表示泛化更好，说明视频任务更容易受噪声和分布迁移影响。 / Results show that for memes, focused LLM-based semantic features improve development performance on sexism detection. For videos, compact feature selection works better on development data, but the official test set shows that the unfiltered representation generalizes better, suggesting stronger sensitivity to noise and domain shift.
AI.conclusion: 该论文结论是：针对静态meme，面向语义的定向特征工程，尤其是LLM提取的高级语义线索，能够有效提升性别歧视识别；针对短视频，性能对特征维度和跨模态噪声高度敏感，开发集上的紧凑特征选择未必能泛化到官方测试集，因此需要更稳健的时序建模。 / The paper concludes that targeted semantic feature engineering, especially LLM-derived high-level cues, is effective for sexism detection in static memes, while short-video performance is highly sensitive to feature dimensionality and cross-modal noise, indicating a need for more robust temporal modeling.

title: Better Literary Translation: A Multi-Aspect Data Generation and LLM Training Approach
summary: Literary translation poses unique challenges due to the scarcity of high-quality annotated data and the need to balance expression fluency with literary effect. We present a multi-aspect iterative refinement framework that generates high-quality translation references and preference data through specialized LLM translators, each targeting a distinct quality dimension. We leverage the generated data for supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Experiments show that our generated references outperform the original ground truth for SFT by 8.65 CEA100 points. For reinforcement learning, we find that DPO leads to performance degradation in this setting, while leveraging an explicit reward model for GRPO yields an additional 1.51 point improvement. We attribute this to the stability of two-stage training and GRPO's online exploration capability. Our resulting models, LitMT-8B and LitMT-14B, achieve 67.25 and 69.07 CEA100 respectively on the MetaphorTrans English-to-Chinese literary translation benchmark, competitive with Claude Sonnet 4.5 at 68.43, and demonstrate strong generalization to out-of-domain literary work (i.e., O. Henry).

AI.tldr: The paper builds better literary translation training data by letting multiple specialized LLM translators iteratively refine outputs from different quality angles, then trains models with SFT and GRPO. This beats using the original references, shows DPO is a poor fit here, and yields competitive English-to-Chinese literary translation models.
AI.motivation: Literary translation is difficult because annotated data is scarce and models must balance fluency with literary style and effect. Existing data and training methods are not sufficient to capture these multiple quality aspects reliably.
AI.method: The paper uses several specialized LLM-based translators, each optimized for a different translation quality dimension, to iteratively refine literary translations and create high-quality reference and preference datasets. These synthetic datasets are then used for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning, comparing DPO against GRPO with an explicit reward model.
AI.result: Generated references improve SFT performance by 8.65 CEA100 points over the original ground-truth references. DPO hurts performance in this setting, while GRPO with an explicit reward model adds 1.51 more CEA100 points. The final models, LitMT-8B and LitMT-14B, reach 67.25 and 69.07 CEA100 on MetaphorTrans En-Zh, with LitMT-14B surpassing Claude Sonnet 4.5's 68.43, and they generalize well to O. Henry out-of-domain data.
AI.conclusion: A multi-aspect iterative refinement pipeline can generate better literary translation supervision and preference data than original references, and when paired with GRPO plus an explicit reward model, it produces strong literary MT models that are competitive with top closed-source systems and generalize beyond the benchmark domain.

title: CaliDist: Calibrating Large Language Models via Behavioral Robustness to Distraction
summary: Existing calibration methods for Large Language Models (LLMs) often overlook a critical dimension of trustworthiness: a model's {\em behavioral robustness} to irrelevant or misleading information. In this paper, we argue that a model's true confidence should reflect its stability under cognitive pressure. We introduce \textsc{CaliDist}, a novel post-hoc calibration approach that directly measures and penalizes a model's susceptibility to distraction. \textsc{CaliDist} quantifies how an LLM's predictions and uncertainty change when its input prompt is perturbed with semantic \textit{distractors}. This stability (or lack thereof) signal is then used to adaptively scale the model's initial confidence score. Our extensive experiments on seven Natural Language Understanding classification benchmarks using six distinct LLMs show that \textsc{CaliDist} consistently achieves lower Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier Score compared with strong baselines. Remarkably, our method reduces the ECE from 23\% to 7\% on average--a relative improvement of 70\%--demonstrating that behavioral stability is a powerful signal for calibration. We make our code and datasets available at github.com/m-anas-j/CaliDist.

AI.tldr: CaliDist calibrates LLM confidence by checking how much predictions shift when prompts include semantic distractors; more unstable models get lower confidence, which greatly improves calibration.
AI.motivation: Prior LLM calibration methods mainly focus on aligning confidence with accuracy but ignore behavioral robustness to irrelevant or misleading information. The authors argue that true confidence should also reflect stability under cognitive pressure.
AI.method: The paper proposes CaliDist, a post-hoc calibration method that perturbs prompts with semantic distractors, measures changes in predictions and uncertainty, and then adaptively rescales the model's original confidence based on this distraction sensitivity.
AI.result: Across seven NLU classification benchmarks and six LLMs, CaliDist consistently outperforms strong baselines on ECE and Brier Score, reducing average ECE from 23% to 7%, a relative improvement of 70%.
AI.conclusion: CaliDist shows that behavioral stability under semantic distractors is a strong post-hoc calibration signal for LLMs, substantially improving trustworthiness by reducing miscalibrated confidence.

title: A Pre-Registered Causal Partition of Self-Consistency Elicitation and Reward Design in RLVR
summary: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves reasoning even when the reward signal is spurious -- assigning credit to the group-plurality answer rather than a ground-truth verifier. Practitioners commonly interpret naive = acc(TRUE) - acc(RANDOM) as the reward-design effect. We prove this estimand is systematically biased: it conflates self-consistency elicitation (sharpening the policy toward its modal answer via majority pseudo-reward) with genuine reward-design signal. Using a controlled tabular-GRPO simulator we derive an exact telescoping decomposition total = null + elicit + rd and measure each term across five prior-strength levels. The reward-design fraction of the naive estimator ranges from 0.139 at weak prior (ps=0.20) to 0.05 at strong prior (ps=0.80), with the elicitation term flipping sign at the self-consistency crossover. A pre-registered 2x2x2 factorial confirms non-additivity (interaction ratio 0.385; AxC effect -0.089). A points-vs-bounds pilot gate shows strong-prior regimes are point-identified while near-crossover regimes are only bounded. Re-audits of two named published results yield ELICITATION DOMINATED (elicitation share 0.98) and REWARD DESIGN DOMINATED (rd share 1.18) verdicts respectively, demonstrating the diagnostic value of the partition. We pre-commit to submit regardless of flip outcome; a non-flip is a finding of equal standing. We release a reusable one-command harness for any alignment paper to run the same audit.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that common RLVR estimates overstate reward-design benefits because they confound them with self-consistency effects. It introduces an exact decomposition, validates it in simulation and factorial experiments, and provides an audit harness to reassess prior alignment results.
AI.motivation: Prior RLVR practice often treats acc(TRUE)-acc(RANDOM) as the effect of reward design, but spurious majority-based rewards may improve reasoning through self-consistency sharpening rather than genuine verifier quality. The paper aims to disentangle these mechanisms.
AI.method: The paper proves a telescoping decomposition of the naive estimator into null, elicitation, and reward-design terms, validates it in a controlled tabular-GRPO simulator across five prior-strength settings, runs a pre-registered 2x2x2 factorial study for interactions, uses a points-vs-bounds identification pilot, and re-audits two published results with a one-command harness.
AI.result: The reward-design share of the naive estimator is small, from 0.139 at weak prior to 0.05 at strong prior; the elicitation term can flip sign near a self-consistency crossover; factorial experiments show non-additivity with interaction ratio 0.385 and AxC effect -0.089; audits of prior work classify one result as elicitation-dominated and another as reward-design-dominated.
AI.conclusion: Naive reward-design estimates in RLVR are systematically biased because they mix self-consistency elicitation with true reward-design effects; the proposed decomposition separates these components and better diagnoses prior results.

title: Deep Learning-based 3D Oral Cavity Reconstruction Using 2D Intraoral Images
comment: 4 pages, 5 figures. English version of a paper presented at the Korea Multimedia Society Conference, November 2025
summary: Oral 3D modelling is one of the most essential stages in dentistry, and many different approaches, such as impression taking and intraoral scanning, are commonly used for this phase, each with notable limitations. Impression taking, which involves placing alginate or silicone material in a tray and inserting it into the patient's oral cavity to form a negative mold, suffers from significant patient discomfort, material deformation errors, and difficulties in storage and transportation. Intraoral scanners, which directly scan oral structures in real time using structured light or laser technology, produce state-of-the-art results but are associated with substantially high equipment costs. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a software-based approach that reconstructs a 3D oral model using only ten 2D intraoral images captured from different angles, requiring no dedicated hardware devices. The proposed method reduces cost, eliminates the need for physical scanning equipment, minimises patient discomfort, and enables automated 3D reconstruction. The model is trained on the publicly available Dental3DS dataset, comprising 950 upper jaw samples, and employs MobileNetV2 as the image encoder combined with Multi-head Attention for multi-view feature fusion. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 77.49%, measured by nearest-neighbor matching with a distance threshold of 0.035. However, predicted vertices tend to concentrate in high-density regions of the ground truth, resulting in uneven point distribution across the reconstructed model.

AI.tldr: A software-only model reconstructs 3D dental shapes from just ten 2D mouth images, reducing cost and discomfort compared with impressions or scanners, but current reconstruction quality is limited by uneven vertex distribution.
AI.motivation: Traditional impression taking causes patient discomfort and suffers from deformation, storage, and transport issues, while intraoral scanners provide strong performance but are expensive. The work is motivated by the need for a cheaper, hardware-free, and more comfortable alternative for 3D oral modeling.
AI.method: The method uses ten intraoral images captured from different viewpoints as input, encodes each image with MobileNetV2, fuses multi-view features through Multi-head Attention, and reconstructs the 3D oral model. Training is performed on the public Dental3DS dataset with 950 upper-jaw samples.
AI.result: On the Dental3DS dataset, the model achieves 77.49% accuracy under nearest-neighbor matching with a distance threshold of 0.035. A key limitation is that predicted vertices cluster in dense ground-truth areas, leading to non-uniform point coverage in the reconstructed model.
AI.conclusion: The paper shows that a low-cost, software-only pipeline can reconstruct a 3D oral model from ten 2D intraoral images using MobileNetV2 and multi-head attention, but the reconstructed point distribution remains uneven and limits reconstruction quality.

title: To Be Multimodal or Not to Be: Query-Adaptive Audio-Visual Person Retrieval via Active Modality Detection
summary: When retrieving a person from a video archive by voice and face, should the system be multimodal or not? In real-world broadcast archives, unlike curated benchmarks, a target may be heard but unseen, seen but unheard, or both. Fusing scores from an absent modality injects noise, degrading precision below the best unimodal system. We propose a query-adaptive framework that detects active modalities via cross-modal score consistency: when both modalities are active, files retrieved by one also score highly on the other; this agreement breaks down when a modality is absent. Classifiers driven by these cross-modal features achieve 89% detection accuracy. On the BBC Rewind corpus (with over 12,000 broadcast videos) the adaptive system attains 94.2% P@1, outperforming speaker-only (82.9%), face-only (93.4%), and fixed fusion (90.0%), recovering 64% of the gap to an oracle with ground-truth modality labels (96.6%).

AI.tldr: Real-world person retrieval from video should use multimodal evidence only when it is actually present. The paper detects active voice/face modalities using cross-modal score agreement and adaptively chooses how to retrieve, improving P@1 to 94.2% over unimodal and fixed-fusion baselines.
AI.motivation: In real-world broadcast archives, unlike curated benchmarks, a target person may be visible but silent, audible but off-screen, or both visible and audible. Applying fixed multimodal fusion when a modality is absent introduces noise and can reduce retrieval precision below the best single-modality system. The work is motivated by the need for a retrieval strategy that adapts to modality availability rather than assuming both modalities are always informative.
AI.method: The paper proposes a query-adaptive framework for person retrieval in broadcast video archives. It uses cross-modal score consistency features to detect whether voice and face modalities are active for a target query. The intuition is that when both modalities are present, items retrieved by one modality should also receive high scores from the other; when one modality is absent, this agreement weakens. Classifiers built on these cross-modal features predict active modalities and guide adaptive fusion or modality selection.
AI.result: The modality-activity classifiers achieve 89% detection accuracy. On the BBC Rewind dataset with more than 12,000 broadcast videos, the adaptive system reaches 94.2% P@1, outperforming speaker-only retrieval (82.9%), face-only retrieval (93.4%), and fixed fusion (90.0%). It also recovers 64% of the performance gap to an oracle system with ground-truth modality labels, which achieves 96.6% P@1.
AI.conclusion: A query-adaptive multimodal retrieval system should not always fuse voice and face signals; instead, it should first detect which modalities are actually present and then adapt retrieval accordingly, yielding better precision than unimodal or fixed-fusion approaches in real-world archives.

title: SALT: When More Rollouts Don't Help in Group-Based Policy Optimization and How to Make Them Matter
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) often adopts GRPO-style group-relative updates, sampling multiple rollouts per prompt to construct normalized learning signals. However, merely increasing the number of rollouts does not reliably strengthen learning: under GRPO-style group normalization, per-rollout policy-gradient features can concentrate into a low-rank, signed geometry, causing substantial cancellation during aggregation and weakening the effective update. We address this failure mode with SALT, a Subspace-Adaptive geometry pLug-in componenT that uses sample-wise gradient geometry to reweight the coefficients of group-relative updates. SALT estimates a dominant shared subspace from the mini-batch Gram geometry, decomposes group-relative coefficients into shared and residual channels, and adaptively amplifies the residual channel when signed cancellation is severe. Across diverse reasoning-oriented RLVR benchmarks and model scales, SALT improves effective update geometry and performance without modifying the reward model or the rollout sampling procedure

title: Edit-R2: Context-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Image Editing
summary: Text-guided image editing has advanced rapidly with diffusion models and unified multimodal foundation models. However, most existing methods remain confined to single-turn settings, overlooking the more realistic scenario of multi-turn in-context editing, where users iteratively refine an image through a sequence of instructions. In this setting, a model must follow each new instruction while preserving accumulated session-level constraints, challenged by two coupled failure modes: long-context dilution, where sparse textual constraints become difficult to recover from growing interleaved image-text histories, and state contamination, where earlier editing mistakes degrade subsequent generations. We introduce Edit-R2, a novel reinforcement learning post-training framework for unified multimodal models. Edit-R2 reconstructs the operative session intent, which effectively consolidates scattered historical constraints into an explicit reasoning trace before each editing turn. It further enables multi-turn RL over both reasoning and generation through a unified objective that jointly optimizes intent reconstruction generation in discrete text space and flow-matching image generation in continuous latent space, while a trajectory filtering mechanism suppresses corrupted rollouts to stabilize training under state contamination. To support systematic evaluation, we introduce MICE-Bench, a large-scale benchmark for multi-turn in-context editing with automated metrics for instruction following (IF), content consistency (CC), and global awareness (GA) over accumulated session constraints. Experiments show that Edit-R2 substantially improves multi-turn in-context editing and achieves competitive performance compared against strong baselines.
