title: ATT-CR: Adaptive Triangular Transformer for Cloud Removal
summary: Cloud removal aims to accurately reconstruct the ground objects obscured by clouds in remote sensing images. Existing Transformer-based methods utilizing self-attention have shown impressive results by effectively modeling long-range dependencies in cloudy images. However, they suffer from the following issues: 1) the high computational complexity of self-attention limits scalability; 2) treating both cloudy and clean pixels as valid within the attention computation brings disturbances in subsequent layers, leading to suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Triangular Transformer for Cloud Removal (ATT-CR), a model that effectively reduces computational costs and mitigates interference from cloudy pixels. Specifically, it consists of two core components: Triangular Attention (TAN) and Feature Selected Gating Module (FSGM). TAN employs lower and upper triangular matrices to approximate Softmax attention with O(N) computational complexity, significantly reducing the computational costs. The FSGM, on the other hand, integrates with TAN to adaptively distinguish between cloudy and clean features, which minimizes the introduction of invalid information into subsequent layers. Extensive experiments on cloud removal benchmarks demonstrate that ATT-CR delivers superior performance compared to existing methods.

AI.tldr: ATT-CR is a more efficient Transformer for cloud removal that replaces costly self-attention with linear-complexity triangular attention and uses gating to suppress cloudy-feature interference, leading to better benchmark results.
AI.motivation: Existing Transformer-based cloud removal methods model long-range dependencies well, but standard self-attention is computationally expensive and incorrectly treats cloudy pixels as equally valid as clean pixels, which propagates noise and harms reconstruction quality.
AI.method: The paper proposes Adaptive Triangular Transformer for Cloud Removal (ATT-CR), built on two components: Triangular Attention (TAN), which uses lower and upper triangular matrices to approximate Softmax attention with O(N) complexity, and a Feature Selected Gating Module (FSGM), which adaptively filters cloudy versus clean features before passing them to later layers.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on cloud removal benchmarks show that ATT-CR outperforms existing methods while being more computationally efficient.
AI.conclusion: ATT-CR effectively improves remote sensing cloud removal by reducing attention complexity to linear time and suppressing interference from cloudy pixels, achieving better benchmark performance than prior methods.

title: Epistemic Injustice in Language Models: An Audit of Pretraining Filters and Guardrails
summary: Modern language models rely on pretraining filters to remove undesirable content from training corpora and inference-time guardrails to suppress undesirable outputs during deployment. In this paper, we examine how these filtering and moderation decisions produce forms of epistemic erasure and reveal tensions both across automated systems and between these systems and human judgment. We audit four pretraining filters and three inference-time guardrails on Common Crawl sentences containing gender and regional-origin mentions, together with a manually annotated subset of 500 sentences. Our analysis shows that filtering and guardrail decisions are strongly associated with blocklist-based lexical cues, while frequently failing to flag content containing private information or explicit hate speech. At the same time, marginalized groups, particularly transgender people, women, and Central Americans, are significantly over-flagged across systems. Human annotators, by contrast, would retain 88.5\% of filter-flagged and 91.3\% of guardrail-flagged content, often recognizing representational harms arising from tensions of content removal that current systems fail to capture. Taken together, our findings document a form of epistemic erasure in which mentions of marginalized groups are disproportionately removed before pretraining and additionally suppressed again at inference time.

AI.tldr: LLM safety filters often over-remove content mentioning marginalized groups, miss some truly harmful content, and disagree sharply with human judgments, producing epistemic erasure at both training and inference time.
AI.motivation: The study is motivated by concern that content filtering and moderation in modern language models may not only remove undesirable content but also systematically erase knowledge about marginalized groups and diverge from human judgment.
AI.method: The paper audits four pretraining filters and three inference-time guardrails on Common Crawl sentences containing gender and regional-origin mentions, and compares system decisions against a manually annotated subset of 500 sentences.
AI.result: Filtering and guardrail decisions are heavily driven by blocklist-style lexical cues, frequently fail to flag private information and explicit hate speech, and significantly over-flag transgender people, women, and Central Americans. Human annotators would retain most flagged content: 88.5% of filter-flagged and 91.3% of guardrail-flagged content.
AI.conclusion: Pretraining filters and inference-time guardrails jointly create epistemic erasure by disproportionately removing mentions of marginalized groups while missing genuinely harmful content such as private information and explicit hate speech.

title: Robust and sparse support vector machine via hybrid truncated loss for supervised classification
summary: The support vector machine (SVM) is a widely used classifier, but choosing an appropriate loss function remains difficult. Convex losses such as the hinge loss and least-squares loss are sensitive to outliers, while bounded non-convex losses often lead to high computational cost. To address this, we propose a hybrid truncated loss function ($L_{\mathrm{ht}}$) that is both sparse and bounded, and build the $L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM model for single-view classification. We introduce the P-stationary point and use it to establish the first-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions. Based on these conditions, we design an alternating direction method of multipliers with a working-set strategy that reduces computational cost and achieves global convergence. We further extend $L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM to multi-view learning by adding structural information and view weights, resulting in Mv$L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM, which follows both the consensus and complementarity principles. Experiments on synthetic, real-world, and image datasets show that $L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM achieves higher accuracy with fewer support vectors and better noise robustness than five single-view methods, while Mv$L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM outperforms six multi-view methods in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

AI.tldr: A new sparse, bounded truncated loss makes SVMs more robust and efficient; with an ADMM-based solver and a multi-view extension, the method outperforms standard single-view and multi-view baselines.
AI.motivation: Standard convex SVM losses such as hinge and least-squares are sensitive to outliers, whereas bounded non-convex losses are often computationally expensive. The work aims to design a loss that is simultaneously robust, sparse, bounded, and more efficient to optimize.
AI.method: The paper proposes a hybrid truncated loss function (L_ht) and builds an L_ht-SVM for single-view classification. It defines P-stationary points to derive first-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions, then develops an ADMM algorithm with a working-set strategy and proves global convergence. The method is extended to multi-view learning as MvL_ht-SVM by incorporating structural information and adaptive view weights.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic, real-world, and image datasets show that L_ht-SVM achieves higher accuracy, fewer support vectors, and stronger noise robustness than five single-view baselines. The multi-view MvL_ht-SVM also surpasses six multi-view methods on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hybrid truncated loss enables SVMs to achieve stronger robustness to noise and outliers while keeping sparsity and computational tractability; its multi-view extension further improves classification performance by leveraging consensus and complementarity across views.

title: Bidirectional Search for Longest Paths: Case for Front-to-Front Heuristics
summary: Bidirectional heuristic search can potentially reduce search effort for problems amenable to backward search. Therein, it is well-known that front-to-front heuristics can reduce the number of node expansions, but their overhead is so high that overall runtime almost always increases. We propose BiXDFBnB, a bidirectional depth-first branch-and-bound algorithm that adapts the Single-Frontier Bidirectional Search (SFBDS) framework - originally developed for shortest-path (MIN) problems - to the Generalized Longest Simple Path (GLSP) setting. Because SFBDS inherently operates on paired states, front-to-front (F2F) heuristic evaluation arises naturally and avoids the overhead typically associated with bidirectional frontier management. We show that this adaptation can be successfully applied to maximization (MAX) problems while efficiently handling overlapping constraints. BiXDFBnB is applied to several types of longest-path problems: Longest Simple Path (LSP), Snakes, and Coil-in-the-Box (CIB). Empirical evaluation shows that the new algorithm frequently reduces the number of node expansions and, in some cases, also improves overall runtime.

AI.tldr: BiXDFBnB is a bidirectional branch-and-bound method for longest-path maximization problems that uses paired-state front-to-front heuristics efficiently; it usually expands fewer nodes and can sometimes run faster than prior approaches.
AI.motivation: Existing bidirectional front-to-front heuristics can reduce node expansions, but their computational overhead usually negates runtime benefits. The paper aims to retain the search-efficiency advantages of bidirectional heuristic search while avoiding the typical overhead, and to extend these ideas from MIN shortest-path problems to MAX longest-path problems.
AI.method: The paper proposes BiXDFBnB, a bidirectional depth-first branch-and-bound algorithm based on Single-Frontier Bidirectional Search (SFBDS). It operates on paired states, enabling efficient front-to-front heuristic evaluation while handling overlapping constraints in generalized longest simple path settings.
AI.result: Empirical results show that BiXDFBnB often reduces the number of node expansions and, in some instances, also lowers total runtime on several longest-path problem classes, including LSP, Snakes, and CIB.
AI.conclusion: BiXDFBnB successfully adapts the SFBDS bidirectional framework from shortest-path minimization to generalized longest simple path maximization problems, leveraging natural front-to-front heuristic evaluation to reduce node expansions and sometimes improve runtime across LSP, Snakes, and Coil-in-the-Box tasks.

title: Global-Local Monte Carlo Tree Search in Vision-Language Models for Text-to-3D Indoor Scene Generation
summary: Large Vision-Language Models have achieved significant reasoning performance in various tasks.However, there are few studies on text-to-3D indoor scene generation with LVLMs. The main challenge is that prevailing LVLM-based methods employ chain-of-thought sequential decision mechanisms that cannot revise earlier decisions, causing error propagation.In this paper, we consider the task as a planning problem constrained by spatial and layout commonsense.To solve this problem, we model it as a tree search problem with global and local trees, which differs from existing sequential decision-making approaches.In the global tree, we place each object iteratively and explore multiple attempts like humans furnishing a room, where the problem space is represented as a tree.To effectively search the tree, we propose a hierarchical scene representation and a PRM-guided MCTS method.The hierarchical representation abstracts a scene into room level, region level, floor object level, and supported object level.The PRM-guided MCTS method uses the PRM to prune unnecessary branches and the MCTS algorithm to balance exploration and exploitation to get an optimal solution with fewer attempts.In the local tree, it further decomposes the placement of each object into finer sub-steps, including the specific placement parameters.To make the whole appearance of the scene consistent, we leverage pre-trained diffusion image generative models to predict textures for all the objects in the scene.As existing benchmarks for text-to-3D indoor scene generation remain limited in scale and diversity, we collect a new large-scale diverse dataset that contains 65 scene types and 3,250 instructions with diverse sizes, layouts, and styles, named 3DTindo-bench, to better assess the capability of the state-of-the-art models. Our experiments show that our method generates more realistic 3D scenes than state-of-the-art approaches.

AI.tldr: Treat text-to-3D indoor scene generation as a revisable planning/tree-search problem rather than a fixed sequential reasoning process. Use hierarchical scene abstraction plus PRM-guided MCTS for efficient object placement, refine placements locally, and apply diffusion models for texture consistency. The method outperforms prior work and is evaluated on a new large-scale benchmark, 3DTindo-bench.
AI.motivation: Existing LVLM-based text-to-3D indoor scene generation methods rely on sequential chain-of-thought decisions that cannot revise earlier choices, which leads to error propagation. The paper is motivated by the need for a planning framework that can revise decisions, incorporate spatial and layout commonsense, and better handle the combinatorial complexity of realistic indoor scene generation.
AI.method: The method formulates scene generation as a global-local tree search problem instead of sequential chain-of-thought decision making. A global tree iteratively places objects with multiple candidate attempts, using a hierarchical scene representation across room, region, floor-object, and supported-object levels, and a PRM-guided MCTS strategy for pruning and efficient search. A local tree further decomposes each object placement into finer sub-steps and placement parameters. Pre-trained diffusion image generation models are used to infer consistent object textures.
AI.result: Experiments show that the proposed approach generates more realistic 3D indoor scenes than existing state-of-the-art methods. The paper also contributes a new benchmark, 3DTindo-bench, with 65 scene types and 3,250 instructions covering diverse sizes, layouts, and styles, enabling broader evaluation.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that modeling text-to-3D indoor scene generation as a tree-search planning problem, combined with hierarchical scene representation, PRM-guided MCTS, local object-placement decomposition, and diffusion-based texture prediction, produces more realistic 3D indoor scenes than prior state-of-the-art methods. It also introduces 3DTindo-bench to better evaluate such systems at scale.

title: Large Language Models are Perplexed by some Political Parties
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used, including in political applications, but their political fairness has been little studied. We assess it using perplexity, posing that a fair model should give equal probability to all political groups. However, we find, across ten LLMs and three datasets covering 37 languages, that LLMs are more perplexed by the texts of far right and nationalist parties than of social-democratic parties. We find this to be consistent with previous work on translation fairness, to the point that perplexity correlates with downstream translation metrics. Our method is applicable to both base LLMs as well as their instruction-tuned counterpart, and we find that both are highly correlated, suggesting that the political fairness of LLMs stems from their pretraining, and is hardly affected by instruction-tuning.

title: Consistency Training Along the Transformer Stack
summary: Consistency training encourages models to behave similarly across different contexts, and has shown promise for reducing misalignment. We broaden the scope of consistency training in two ways. First, we introduce two new internal consistency targets: MLP Consistency Training (MLPCT), which matches post-activation MLP states, and Attention Consistency Training (AttCT), which matches per-head attention distributions. Second, we apply consistency training to four additional safety threats: persona in-context learning attacks, adversarial frustration, prefill attacks, and conditional misalignment. Across several models and threat settings, we find that consistency training reduces misalignment well beyond the sycophancy and jailbreak settings studied in prior work. We also find cases of cross-threat generalization, where training against one failure mode improves robustness to another, and identify a shared residual-stream mechanism underlying ACT, MLPCT, and AttCT, while distinguishing BCT as mechanistically distinct. Our results suggest that consistency training is a flexible and extensible framework for alignment, capable of unifying defenses against a broader class of model pathologies.

AI.tldr: The paper extends consistency training by matching internal MLP and attention states and testing it on more attack/misalignment settings. It shows stronger, broader robustness and suggests consistency training may unify defenses across multiple model failure modes.
AI.motivation: Prior consistency training work showed promise mainly for sycophancy and jailbreak mitigation, but its scope was narrow in both training targets and evaluated failure modes. The paper aims to test whether consistency training can be generalized to richer internal targets and a broader set of alignment and safety threats.
AI.method: The paper expands consistency training in two directions: it introduces MLP Consistency Training (MLPCT), which aligns post-activation MLP states, and Attention Consistency Training (AttCT), which aligns per-head attention distributions; and it evaluates consistency training against four additional safety threats: persona in-context learning attacks, adversarial frustration, prefill attacks, and conditional misalignment, across multiple models and threat settings.
AI.result: Across several models and threat settings, consistency training substantially reduces misalignment beyond prior benchmark settings. The study also finds cross-threat generalization, where training on one failure mode can improve robustness to another, and identifies a shared residual-stream mechanism for ACT, MLPCT, and AttCT, in contrast to BCT.
AI.conclusion: Consistency training is a flexible and extensible alignment framework that can mitigate multiple safety threats beyond previously studied sycophancy and jailbreak settings. Internal-state consistency targets such as MLPCT and AttCT are effective, some defenses generalize across threats, and ACT/MLPCT/AttCT appear to share a residual-stream mechanism while BCT is mechanistically distinct.

title: The Self-Correction Illusion: LLMs Correct Others but Not Themselves
summary: Recent work shows that LLM agents struggle to correct errors in their own reasoning traces yet show markedly higher correction rates when identical claims appear under external sources. We ask whether this asymmetry reflects a capability deficit or a role-label artifact: does an agent's willingness to correct a wrong claim depend causally on the chat-template role that carries it, rather than on the claim's content? Our setup keeps the erroneous claim byte-identical across all conditions (SHA-256 verified) and varies only its wrapping role: the agent's own \role{<thought>}, a \role{user} message, a \role{tool} response, or a \role{system <memory>} block. Across 13 model-domain cells covering seven model families and three domains ($n{=}30$ paired tasks per cell), relabeling the claim from \role{<thought>} to an external role lifts the explicit-correction rate by 23 to 93 percentage points, with 10 of 13 cells reaching $p{<}0.001$. Further experiments confirm that the effect is asymmetric, mechanistically decomposable, and robust across domains. The failure to self-correct is not a cognitive deficit; it is a chat-template artifact. We exploit this artifact by designing a prompt-structure-only intervention that requires no training and no model modification, with its strongest role label being domain-dependent: \role{<memory>} dominates on math, while a plain \role{user} message dominates on logical deduction.

AI.tldr: Same error, different role label: LLMs correct it far more often when it looks external rather than self-generated, showing that failed self-correction is mostly a chat-template artifact and can be improved with prompt-structure changes alone.
AI.motivation: Prior work showed that LLM agents often fail to correct mistakes in their own reasoning traces but correct the same mistakes more readily when those claims appear from external sources. The paper is motivated by determining whether this difference comes from a genuine capability limitation or from superficial role-label effects introduced by the chat template.
AI.method: The authors keep an erroneous claim byte-identical across conditions and verify identity with SHA-256, while varying only the chat-template role that contains it: the model's own thought, a user message, a tool response, or a system-memory block. They evaluate 13 model-domain cells spanning seven model families and three domains, using 30 paired tasks per cell, and then run additional experiments to test asymmetry, mechanism decomposition, and cross-domain robustness.
AI.result: Relabeling the same wrong claim from an internal thought role to an external role raises explicit correction rates by 23 to 93 percentage points, with 10 of 13 model-domain cells achieving p<0.001. The best external role varies by domain: memory-style system blocks work best for math, while plain user messages work best for logical deduction.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that LLMs' weak self-correction is primarily caused by a chat-template role-label artifact rather than a true reasoning-capability deficit. Simply changing the role wrapper of the same erroneous claim can substantially increase explicit correction rates, and this can be exploited through prompt-structure-only interventions without retraining or modifying the model.

title: ReSAGE-PAR: Representational Similarity Assessment for Generative Expansion in Pedestrian Attribute Recognition
comment: Under review at IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (TCSVT)
summary: To address the limited diversity and data scarcity in Pedestrian Attribute Recognition (PAR), we explore image synthesis using diffusion models guided by attribute-based prompts. While this enables the controlled generation of pedestrian images, it faces two critical challenges: (i) the domain gap between high-quality pre-training data and low-resolution, non-standard surveillance crops, and (ii) the need for reliable attribute verification to prevent generative hallucinations. In this paper, we introduce a robust generate-score-autolabel pipeline called ReSAGE-PAR (REpresentational Similarity Assessment for Generative Expansion in PAR) that bridges this domain gap and enables scalable, high-fidelity dataset expansion. First, we adapt pre-trained diffusion models to native PAR resolutions using a tailored LoRA-based Image-to-Image approach. Second, we extract vision-language alignment scores between the generated images and their conditioning prompts, utilizing a comprehensive prompting strategy that includes label-consistent and inconsistent complements. Finally, we formulate a Bayesian classifier that converts these continuous scores into reliable binary pseudo-labels. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of ReSAGE-PAR in preserving spatial priors and verifying attributes. When integrated into PAR training, ReSAGE-PAR consistently yields significant improvements-achieving gains of up to 8.7% on standard backbones and pushing state-of-the-art frameworks to new performance levels. This proves its value as an architecture-agnostic solution for scalable PAR enhancement. The complete codebase for ReSAGE-PAR is publicly available at http://www-vpu.eps.uam.es/publications/ReSAGE-PAR.

AI.tldr: ReSAGE-PAR uses adapted diffusion generation plus score-based pseudo-label verification to create reliable synthetic pedestrian-attribute data, substantially improving PAR performance.
AI.motivation: Pedestrian Attribute Recognition suffers from limited data diversity and scarcity. Although diffusion-based synthesis can generate controllable pedestrian images, it is hindered by a domain gap between high-quality pretraining data and low-resolution surveillance crops, as well as the lack of reliable attribute verification to avoid hallucinated labels.
AI.method: The paper proposes a generate-score-autolabel pipeline. It first adapts pre-trained diffusion models to native PAR image resolutions using a LoRA-based image-to-image method, then computes vision-language alignment scores between generated images and attribute prompts using both label-consistent and inconsistent complementary prompts, and finally maps these continuous scores to binary pseudo-labels with a Bayesian classifier.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that ReSAGE-PAR preserves spatial priors, verifies attributes effectively, and improves PAR training performance consistently, with gains of up to 8.7% on standard backbones while further improving strong existing frameworks.
AI.conclusion: ReSAGE-PAR is an architecture-agnostic pipeline that reliably expands PAR datasets by adapting diffusion models to surveillance-like pedestrian crops and auto-verifying attributes, leading to consistent performance gains up to 8.7% and stronger state-of-the-art PAR results.

title: Measuring the sensitivity of LLM-based structured extraction to prompt, model, and schema choices in clinical discharge summaries
comment: 69 pages, 5 main figures, supplementary material included
summary: Large language models are increasingly used for structured extraction from clinical free-text notes, but the sensitivity of their output to upstream configuration choices is less understood than their accuracy on fixed benchmarks. This work measures that sensitivity without human-annotated ground truth, by holding the extraction task fixed and varying one choice at a time. The fixed schema comprises 17 clinical documentation flags on a three-way yes/no/not_documented value set and a 47-tag vocabulary for the primary admission reason. Three prompt variants expressing this schema were each run at two model sizes on MIMIC-IV v3.1 discharge summaries. Cross-prompt agreement was measured by Cohen's kappa on ICD-stratified subsets. A paired same-note comparison isolated the effect of model choice, and a post-hoc collapse of the three-way flags to binary tested the schema's contribution to disagreement. On the three-way flags, the two models reach the same pooled cross-prompt agreement (median kappa 0.69 and 0.68); the larger model raises agreement on some fields and lowers it on others, a redistribution rather than the absence of an effect. Collapsing the schema to binary dissolves most of the cross-prompt disagreement, locating it on the absence-versus-silence distinction rather than on whether the finding is present. On the multi-class admission categorization, changing the model reassigns the dominant tag on close to half of all notes while changing the prompt phrasing reassigns it on roughly one in eight, and the larger model places far less mass on residual catch-all categories (44% to 26%). These patterns indicate a schema-imposed source of disagreement concentrated on the absence-versus-silence axis and a dominance of model over prompt phrasing on multi-class categorization, identified by a reusable methodology for auditing extraction reproducibility on a population-scale deployment.

AI.tldr: This paper audits how stable LLM-based clinical extraction is under prompt, model, and schema changes. It finds that prompt disagreement on three-way clinical flags mostly comes from the schema’s distinction between explicit absence and not documented, while model choice has the larger impact on multi-class admission-reason labeling.
AI.motivation: Although LLMs are widely used for structured extraction from clinical free text, their robustness to configuration choices such as prompt wording, model size, and output schema is not well understood. The paper aims to measure this sensitivity without relying on human-annotated ground truth, focusing on reproducibility in large-scale deployment settings.
AI.method: The paper fixes a clinical extraction task on MIMIC-IV v3.1 discharge summaries and varies one upstream factor at a time. It uses three prompt formulations, two model sizes, 17 three-way clinical documentation flags, and a 47-tag admission-reason vocabulary; evaluates cross-prompt agreement with Cohen’s kappa on ICD-stratified subsets; performs paired same-note comparisons to isolate model effects; and post-hoc collapses three-way flags to binary to test whether the schema drives disagreement.
AI.result: For the three-way flags, the two models show similar pooled cross-prompt agreement (median kappa 0.69 vs 0.68), but the larger model improves some fields and worsens others. When the three-way labels are collapsed to binary, most disagreement disappears, showing that instability mainly lies in the absence-versus-silence distinction. For admission-reason categorization, changing the model alters the dominant tag for nearly half of notes, while changing prompt phrasing alters it for about one in eight; the larger model also reduces use of residual catch-all categories from 44% to 26%.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that reproducibility of LLM-based clinical information extraction is strongly shaped by schema design and model choice. For three-way clinical flags, most disagreement comes from distinguishing explicit absence from non-documentation, while for multi-class admission-reason tagging, model choice affects outputs more than prompt phrasing.

title: GenAutoML: An Agentic Framework for Dynamic Architecture Generation and Optimization in Time-Series Analysis
summary: Designing neural architectures for time-series forecasting and anomaly detection remains a resource-intensive task that often requires substantial domain expertise. Traditional Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) systems typically rely on static, predefined search spaces, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse data characteristics. We present GenAutoML, an agentic framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) as neural architects to bridge natural-language requirements and executable PyTorch implementations. The framework incorporates a Sandboxed Reflection Loop for autonomous code refinement and a Signature-Aware Runtime that enforces architectural consistency and execution safety. To improve robustness under non-stationary conditions, we further introduce a Dynamic Reversible Instance Normalization (Dyn-RevIN) wrapper. Experiments on the ETTh1, ETTm1, and Weather benchmarks demonstrate that GenAutoML can dynamically generate task-specific neural architectures tailored to dataset characteristics. Among the generated models, WaveInterferenceNet achieves inference latency below 0.01 ms per sample while maintaining competitive predictive performance. By emphasizing computational efficiency, architectural adaptability, and stable optimization behavior, GenAutoML enables the creation of ultra-lightweight neural networks suitable for resource-constrained and latency-sensitive Edge AI deployments.

AI.tldr: An LLM-based AutoML system for time-series tasks that writes and refines PyTorch models automatically, stays safe and architecturally consistent, and produces ultra-lightweight networks with competitive accuracy and very low latency.
AI.motivation: Manual neural architecture design for time-series tasks is expensive and requires domain expertise, while conventional AutoML relies on static search spaces that adapt poorly to different datasets and task requirements.
AI.method: The paper proposes GenAutoML, which uses LLMs as neural architects to translate natural-language requirements into executable PyTorch models. It includes a Sandboxed Reflection Loop for iterative autonomous code refinement, a Signature-Aware Runtime for consistency and execution safety, and a Dynamic Reversible Instance Normalization (Dyn-RevIN) wrapper to improve robustness under non-stationary conditions.
AI.result: On ETTh1, ETTm1, and Weather benchmarks, GenAutoML generates dataset-tailored architectures. One generated model, WaveInterferenceNet, achieves inference latency below 0.01 ms per sample while retaining competitive predictive performance, indicating strong suitability for resource-constrained Edge AI settings.
AI.conclusion: GenAutoML demonstrates that an agentic LLM-driven AutoML framework can automatically generate lightweight, task-specific neural architectures for time-series forecasting and anomaly detection, achieving strong efficiency and competitive accuracy for edge deployment.

title: Framing, Judging, Steering: An Assessable Competency Model for Teach-ing Students to Reason With Generative AI
summary: Generative AI makes answers easy and understanding hard, and uncritical use invites cognitive offloading. Schools still measure unaided performance, yet the real task is to produce good work with AI: framing an ill-defined task, judging the output, and steering the model toward a better result. This ability is rarely assessed in its own right; where measured, it collapses into one "prompting" score that cannot diagnose why AI use succeeds or fails. We propose CoRe-3 (Co-Reasoning), a competency model factoring productive AI use into three assessable skills we abbreviate FJS: Framing (specifying an ill-defined task before invoking AI), Judging (evaluating output for errors and unstated assumptions), and Steering (iteratively redirecting the model). Its distinguishing claim is the separation of pre-generation Framing from post-generation Steering, with Judging as the gate between. We ground the skills in theory, state five testable propositions, and instantiate them in CoReasoningLab, an open platform that presents flawed AI output and scores them independently. Over simulated learners (generated and graded by different models), the skills dissociate: each tracks its own manipulated competence while staying flat in the others, and grades become correlated when one competence is shared across all three (convergent and discriminant validity), across grader backends from two providers. Human-rater agreement and outcomes are next; we release the instrument, data, and protocol.

AI.tldr: 论文提出CoRe-3，把“会用AI”拆成任务界定（Framing）、结果判断（Judging）和迭代引导（Steering）三项能力，并用CoReasoningLab进行独立测评；模拟实验表明这三项能力能被区分开来，比单一prompting分数更有诊断价值。 The paper proposes CoRe-3, which decomposes “using AI well” into Framing, Judging, and Steering, and assesses them independently in CoReasoningLab; simulations suggest these skills can be distinguished, making the framework more diagnostically useful than a single prompting score.
AI.motivation: 现有教育评估仍主要考察无AI辅助表现，但现实任务越来越要求人与AI协作完成工作。现有相关测量往往把能力压缩为单一“prompting”分数，无法诊断AI使用成功或失败的具体原因，因此需要更细粒度、可评估的能力框架。 Existing educational assessment still emphasizes unaided performance, while real-world work increasingly requires productive human-AI collaboration. Current measurements often collapse this ability into a single “prompting” score, which cannot diagnose why AI use succeeds or fails, creating a need for a more fine-grained and assessable framework.
AI.method: 作者提出CoRe-3能力模型，基于理论定义FJS三项技能，提出五个可检验命题，并在开放平台CoReasoningLab中实现测评：给受试者呈现有缺陷的AI输出，分别对三项技能独立评分。验证上使用由不同模型生成并由不同模型评分的模拟学习者，并跨两家提供商的评分后端检查结果一致性。 The authors introduce the CoRe-3 competency model, theoretically define the three FJS skills, state five testable propositions, and implement the assessment in the open platform CoReasoningLab: participants are shown flawed AI outputs and scored independently on each skill. Validation uses simulated learners generated and graded by different models, with consistency checked across grader backends from two providers.
AI.result: 在模拟学习者实验中，FJS三项技能表现出可分离性：每项分数主要随其对应的被操控能力变化，而其他两项基本保持稳定；当三项共享同一底层能力时，评分之间相关性上升。这一模式在两家提供商的评分后端上都出现，支持其区分效度与收敛效度。 In simulated learner experiments, the three FJS skills dissociate: each score mainly tracks its own manipulated competence while the other two remain largely flat; when a shared underlying competence is introduced, correlations across scores increase. This pattern holds across grader backends from two providers, supporting discriminant and convergent validity.
AI.conclusion: CoRe-3将高质量AI协作能力拆分为Framing、Judging、Steering三项可独立评估的技能，而不是单一的prompting分数；初步模拟结果支持该三分结构具有区分效度与收敛效度。 CoRe-3 separates productive AI use into three independently assessable skills—Framing, Judging, and Steering—rather than a single prompting score; initial simulation evidence supports both discriminant and convergent validity of this structure.

title: Texture-preserving implicit neural representation for Cone beam CT truncated reconstruction
summary: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) frequently suffers from data truncation, which introduces severe artifacts and limits the effective field of view (FOV). Existing deep learning methods for truncated cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) reconstruction suffer from serious limitations, including a strict reliance on supervised ground truth and a failure to account for continuous 3D spatial truncation variations. To address these challenges, we introduce a self-supervised 3D reconstruction framework based on neural scene representations. By directly mapping spatial coordinates to radiodensity under projection supervision, our approach inherently bypasses traditional filtering and backprojection operations, thereby fundamentally eliminating truncation-induced ring artifacts while enabling robust continuous 3D data extrapolation. However, coordinate networks are susceptible to an inherent spectral bias, which leads to a severe loss of clinically vital high-frequency textures. To resolve this bottleneck, we further incorporate a physics-based iterative refinement module into the neural scene representation architecture. Leveraging the artifact-free, extrapolated volume from the coordinate network as an optimal initialization, this module progressively re-extracts and injects high-frequency structural information from the original projections back into the volume. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method successfully unifies the exceptional artifact suppression and extrapolation capabilities of neural networks with the high-fidelity detail preservation of iterative algorithms.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a self-supervised neural-scene-based CBCT reconstruction method for truncated data, then refines it with a physics-guided iterative module to recover fine details. It removes truncation artifacts, extrapolates missing volume, and performs well on both synthetic and real scans.
AI.motivation: Truncated CBCT reconstruction is difficult because existing deep learning methods depend on supervised ground truth and do not model continuous 3D spatial truncation well. In addition, coordinate networks alone lose high-frequency texture due to spectral bias.
AI.method: The method first learns a coordinate-based neural scene representation that maps 3D spatial coordinates directly to radiodensity under projection supervision, enabling continuous 3D extrapolation and avoiding FBP-style reconstruction artifacts. It then applies a physics-based iterative refinement stage that uses the network output as initialization and re-injects high-frequency information from the original projections.
AI.result: Experiments on simulated and real datasets show strong artifact suppression, robust extrapolation beyond the truncated FOV, and improved preservation of clinically important structural details by combining neural and iterative reconstruction strengths.
AI.conclusion: A self-supervised 3D CBCT reconstruction framework using neural scene representations plus physics-based iterative refinement can reduce truncation artifacts, extend the effective FOV, and recover high-frequency details without supervised ground truth.

title: Beyond Alignment: Value Diversity as a Collective Property in Multicultural Agent Systems
summary: Multicultural multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed in globally diverse settings, where different agents are grounded in different cultural backgrounds. Existing cultural evaluation focuses on value alignment: how closely a single agent matches a target culture. Yet alignment is a per-agent property and cannot reveal whether a system, taken as a whole, preserves the cultural plurality it is meant to represent. We propose value diversity as a system-level evaluation axis for multicultural agent systems, defined through the dissimilarity between culturally conditioned agents' responses on a shared value survey. Using the World Values Survey, we evaluate 19 cultures and 18 backbone models across a wide range of system configurations. We find that diversity is largely uncorrelated with alignment, indicating that the two capture complementary system properties, and that current multicultural agent systems fall substantially below human societies in value diversity. Mixed-backbone systems narrow this gap but do not close it, and the gap persists across culture compositions and agent scales. Social interaction further erodes diversity by driving agents toward consensus, and a participatory budgeting case study shows that this homogenization narrows the breadth of collective decision-making. Together, our results establish value diversity as a distinct evaluation axis for multicultural multi-agent systems and reveal a persistent homogenization tendency in current LLM-based societies. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/iNLP-Lab/MultiAgent-Diversity.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that evaluating multicultural multi-agent systems requires more than checking if each agent matches a culture. It introduces value diversity, measures it with World Values Survey responses, and shows that today’s LLM-based agent societies are too homogeneous compared with real human societies, especially after interaction.
AI.motivation: Prior evaluation of cultural agents mainly measures alignment of an individual agent to a target culture, but this misses whether a whole multi-agent system preserves the cultural plurality it is intended to represent. The paper aims to introduce and validate a system-level metric for multicultural representation.
AI.method: The paper defines value diversity as the dissimilarity among culturally conditioned agents’ responses to a shared value survey. Using the World Values Survey, it evaluates 19 cultures and 18 backbone models across varied system configurations, including mixed-backbone setups, different culture compositions, different agent scales, social interaction settings, and a participatory budgeting case study.
AI.result: Value diversity is largely uncorrelated with alignment, showing they measure complementary properties. Existing multicultural agent systems have substantially lower value diversity than human societies. Mixed-backbone systems reduce but do not eliminate this gap. The deficit persists across culture mixes and scales. Social interaction decreases diversity by pushing agents toward consensus, and this homogenization reduces the breadth of collective choices in participatory budgeting.
AI.conclusion: Value diversity is a necessary system-level evaluation axis for multicultural multi-agent systems, distinct from cultural alignment. Current LLM-based multicultural societies exhibit persistent homogenization: they underrepresent human-level value diversity, and social interaction further drives consensus and narrows collective decisions.

title: Deciphering Two Training Clocks in Grokking via Deep Linear Network Theory with Conditional ReLU Reduction
summary: Grokking suggests that fitting the training data and learning a simple underlying rule may occur on different time scales. We formalize this phenomenon by separating the fast decay of the classification loss from the slower simplification of the learned representation, and we call the resulting pair of stopping times two training clocks. For deep linear networks, we show that a post-margin gap-growth or one-step tail-contraction condition reduces the cross-entropy loss to level epsilon on a logarithmic time scale. In contrast, when layerwise weight decay is present, the induced regularization on the end-to-end map can be expressed as a Schatten-type penalty; under a sharp late-time Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz tail, this structural energy closes on a polynomial time scale. The two clocks, therefore, separate fitting from representation simplification. We then explain how the same mechanism can appear in ReLU MLPs. In regions where the activation patterns on the training set remain fixed, the network reduces to a linear model in the active coordinates. In a two-layer ReLU embedding model, chain-rule estimates further show that the classifier head can receive larger effective gradients than the embedding block under controlled downstream norms. This supports a two-stage mechanism in which the classifier fits first, while the representation continues to simplify later. We use modular addition as the main experimental setting. The deep linear theory provides the rigorous core of the analysis. But the ReLU results are formulated as conditional reductions that account for empirical behavior without claiming a global proof for nonlinear training dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper explains grokking as a mismatch between two learning speeds: networks fit labels quickly, but simplify their internal representation much more slowly. It proves this separation for deep linear nets and gives conditional evidence that ReLU MLPs behave similarly, especially in modular addition.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explain why neural networks can fit training data early while only much later appear to learn a simple underlying rule, as observed in grokking. The paper aims to separate and quantify these two processes theoretically.
AI.method: The authors formalize grokking with two stopping times, one for cross-entropy loss reduction and one for representation simplification. They analyze deep linear networks using margin/tail conditions to prove logarithmic-time fitting and layerwise weight decay plus a Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz tail condition to prove polynomial-time structural energy decay. They then extend the mechanism to ReLU MLPs through fixed activation-region linearization and gradient-chain estimates in a two-layer ReLU embedding model.
AI.result: For deep linear networks, the paper shows cross-entropy can drop to epsilon on a logarithmic time scale, while representation simplification driven by induced Schatten-type regularization occurs on a polynomial time scale, creating a clear separation between the two clocks. For ReLU MLPs, it provides conditional arguments showing a similar two-stage dynamic: the classifier can fit first while the embedding/representation continues simplifying later. Experiments on modular addition are consistent with this view.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that grokking can be understood as two distinct training clocks: a fast clock for fitting the training data via rapid loss decay, and a slower clock for simplifying the learned representation under implicit/explicit structural regularization. This separation is rigorous for deep linear networks and conditionally extends to ReLU MLPs.

title: Beyond Vector Similarity: A Structural Analysis of Graph-Augmented Retrieval for Industrial Knowledge Graphs
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) fails systematically on queries requiring structural reasoning over interconnected entities. We compare eight retrieval architectures for aerospace supply chain intelligence, progressing from text retrieval through graph traversal to graph computation. Using a 46-node knowledge graph with 64 typed edges, we evaluate 23 queries across 10 intent categories and demonstrate that five query classes are structurally unreachable for vector retrieval. Our central finding is the operator vocabulary thesis: the barrier to LLM-based graph reasoning is not model intelligence but the computational operators available as tools. An LLM Query Planner with 9 typed traversal primitives outperforms bespoke handlers (F1 = 0.632 vs. 0.472) while generalizing to unseen queries. Adding 6 graph computation tools, the LLM selectively adopts them for exactly the query categories where traversal fails. We also identify a measurement gap: entity-level F1 systematically underscores structural queries where comprehensive answers are correct.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文说明：RAG在结构化图查询上不行，核心问题不是模型不够聪明，而是缺少可调用的图遍历与图计算操作符；给LLM配上这些工具后，性能和泛化都明显提升。English: This paper shows that RAG is weak on structural graph queries, and the core issue is not that the model is not smart enough, but that it lacks callable graph traversal and computation operators; equipping an LLM with these tools substantially improves both performance and generalization.
AI.motivation: 中文：研究动机是传统RAG和向量检索在涉及多实体关系、路径、连接性和结构约束的查询中表现不足，作者希望找出失败的根因，并验证通过显式图操作工具是否能显著提升LLM在此类任务中的表现。English: The motivation is that standard RAG and vector retrieval perform poorly on queries involving multi-entity relations, paths, connectivity, and structural constraints. The paper seeks to identify the root cause of these failures and test whether explicit graph operators can substantially improve LLM performance.
AI.method: 中文：作者在航空航天供应链情报场景下，对8种检索架构进行比较，这些架构从纯文本检索、图遍历到图计算逐步增强；基于一个包含46个节点、64条类型化边的知识图谱，在23个查询和10类意图上评估，并测试带有9种类型化遍历原语和额外6种图计算工具的LLM Query Planner。English: The authors compare eight retrieval architectures for aerospace supply chain intelligence, ranging from text retrieval to graph traversal and graph computation. They evaluate them on a 46-node knowledge graph with 64 typed edges, across 23 queries in 10 intent categories, including an LLM Query Planner equipped with 9 typed traversal primitives and 6 graph computation tools.
AI.result: 中文：结果表明，23个查询中有5类查询对向量检索在结构上不可达；配备9种遍历原语的LLM Query Planner优于定制处理器（F1=0.632 vs. 0.472），且能泛化到未见查询；再加入6种图计算工具后，LLM会在遍历失效的查询类别上有选择地使用它们。同时，作者发现实体级F1会系统性低估结构型查询中其实正确且完整的答案。English: The results show that five query classes are structurally unreachable for vector retrieval. The LLM Query Planner with 9 traversal primitives outperforms bespoke handlers (F1=0.632 vs. 0.472) and generalizes to unseen queries. After adding 6 graph computation tools, the LLM selectively uses them exactly where traversal fails. The paper also finds that entity-level F1 systematically undervalues correct, comprehensive answers on structural queries.
AI.conclusion: 中文：本文结论是，RAG在需要对互联实体进行结构化推理的查询上存在系统性失效；关键瓶颈不在于LLM本身的智能，而在于它可调用的图操作符工具集。English: The paper concludes that RAG systematically fails on structurally reasoning queries over interconnected entities, and the main bottleneck is not LLM intelligence itself but the set of graph operators available as tools.

title: LoomVideo: Unifying Multimodal Inputs into Video Generation and Editing
summary: Developing unified video generation and editing models capable of interpreting interleaved multimodal inputs is a promising yet challenging frontier field. Existing unified frameworks predominantly rely on massive models (typically 13B parameters or more) and incorporate source video conditions for editing by concatenating sequence tokens. This concatenation inevitably doubles the sequence length, quadrupling the computational complexity of the self-attention mechanism and introducing prohibitive overhead. To address these bottlenecks, we present LoomVideo, a highly efficient 5B-parameter unified architecture for both video generation and editing. LoomVideo replaces the standard text encoder with a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) and employs Deepstack injection mechanism to align multi-layer MLLM features with the Diffusion Transformer (DiT). Crucially, we introduce a zero-overhead Scale-and-Add conditioning approach for video editing. By scaling and directly adding the clean source video latent to the noised target latent, this elegant design eliminates the need for token concatenation, drastically reducing computational cost while maintaining robust capabilities for complex, non-rigid edits. Furthermore, a Negative Temporal RoPE strategy is seamlessly integrated to handle multiple reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our compact 5B model achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance across comprehensive benchmarks, exhibiting exceptional superiority in e-commerce and fashion generation scenarios. Benefiting from the zero-overhead conditioning mechanism, LoomVideo achieves at least a 5.41x acceleration in inference speed compared to models of similar capabilities, paving the way for highly practical and efficient video foundation models.

AI.tldr: LoomVideo是一种面向视频生成与编辑的高效5B统一模型：用MLLM+Deepstack做多模态理解，用Scale-and-Add替代token拼接做编辑条件注入，在保持复杂编辑能力的同时显著降低计算，取得强性能和5.41x+加速。 / LoomVideo is an efficient 5B unified model for video generation and editing: it uses MLLM+Deepstack for multimodal understanding and replaces token concatenation with Scale-and-Add conditioning, preserving strong editing ability while sharply reducing compute and delivering strong results plus 5.41x+ speedup.
AI.motivation: 动机在于现有统一视频生成/编辑框架通常依赖13B以上大模型，并通过token拼接注入源视频条件，导致序列长度翻倍、自注意力复杂度升至4倍、推理成本过高，限制了实际应用。 / The motivation is that existing unified video generation/editing frameworks typically depend on 13B+ models and incorporate source-video conditions via token concatenation, which doubles sequence length, increases self-attention cost roughly fourfold, and makes inference prohibitively expensive for practical deployment.
AI.method: 方法上，论文以MLLM替代标准文本编码器，并通过Deepstack injection将多层MLLM特征对齐注入DiT；在视频编辑中提出Scale-and-Add机制，将干净源视频latent按比例直接加到加噪目标latent上，避免token拼接；同时引入Negative Temporal RoPE以支持多参考图像。 / Methodologically, the paper replaces the standard text encoder with an MLLM, aligns multi-layer MLLM features with the DiT via Deepstack injection, introduces a Scale-and-Add conditioning scheme that directly adds the scaled clean source-video latent to the noised target latent instead of concatenating tokens, and integrates Negative Temporal RoPE to support multiple reference images.
AI.result: 实验表明，LoomVideo在综合基准上达到SOTA或高度竞争的结果，尤其在电商与时尚视频生成场景中表现突出；由于零开销条件机制，其推理速度相比同能力模型至少提升5.41倍。 / Experiments show that LoomVideo achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across comprehensive benchmarks, with especially strong performance in e-commerce and fashion generation, while its zero-overhead conditioning yields at least a 5.41x inference speedup over similarly capable models.
AI.conclusion: LoomVideo通过5B参数统一架构、零额外开销的视频编辑条件注入和多模态对齐设计，在视频生成与编辑上实现了高效且强竞争力的性能，证明小于主流13B+模型的统一视频基础模型也能达到实用级SOTA/接近SOTA效果。 / LoomVideo shows that a compact 5B unified architecture, combined with zero-overhead editing conditioning and multimodal alignment, can deliver efficient and highly competitive video generation/editing performance, demonstrating that practical near-SOTA or SOTA-level unified video foundation models do not require 13B+ scale.

title: The Generator-Eraser Paradox: Community Guidelines for Responsible LLM-Assisted Dialect Resource Creation
summary: Dialect resources occupy a unique position at the intersection of scientific description, cultural preservation, and computational infrastructure. Large language models offer powerful capabilities for accelerating dialect resource development through retrieval-grounded drafting, corpus navigation, metadata enrichment, and annotation workflow support. However, the same systems pose substantial risks: they can contribute to dialect erasure by privileging prestige varieties, homogenizing orthography, and enabling synthetic feedback loops that reduce linguistic diversity over time. These risks are particularly acute for language varieties characterized by diglossia, limited written standardization, or marginalized speaker communities. This paper makes three contributions. First, we integrate insights from variationist sociolinguistics and corpus linguistics to formalize the generator-eraser paradox as a theoretical framework for understanding the dual nature of LLM-assisted dialect work. Second, we derive 12 community guidelines that operationalize this framework into implementable design requirements for dialect resource creation and documentation. Third, we provide an in-depth case study of Arabic dialects, including a structured comparison of widely used resources, to demonstrate how these guidelines address language-specific challenges including diglossia, orthographic variability, and community governance. The contribution is conceptual and operational rather than experimental, with the goal of enabling dialect communities and resource builders across languages to adopt LLMs without sacrificing authenticity, variation, or sovereignty.

AI.tldr: LLMs can help build dialect resources, but they can also erase dialect diversity. The paper defines this tension as the generator-eraser paradox, proposes 12 community guidelines, and shows through Arabic dialects how to use LLMs without losing authenticity or community control.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that dialect resources are important for scientific, cultural, and computational purposes, while LLMs both accelerate resource development and create serious risks such as dialect erasure, orthographic homogenization, and loss of diversity, especially for marginalized or weakly standardized varieties.
AI.method: The paper uses a conceptual and operational approach: it integrates variationist sociolinguistics with corpus linguistics to define the generator-eraser paradox, derives 12 actionable community guidelines from that framework, and applies them in a detailed case study on Arabic dialect resources.
AI.result: The main result is a theoretical framework for understanding the dual role of LLMs in dialect work, a set of 12 implementable guidelines for responsible dialect resource development, and an Arabic dialect case study showing how these guidelines can address diglossia, orthographic variability, and governance issues.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that LLMs can support dialect resource creation only if their use is governed by explicit community-centered safeguards that preserve authenticity, variation, and linguistic sovereignty, rather than pushing dialects toward homogenization or prestige norms.

title: TS-ICL: A Flexible Time-Indexed Foundation Model for Time Series via In-Context Learning
summary: Foundation models mark a profound paradigm shift in time series modeling, with task-specific models being superseded by general-purpose zero-shot models. Yet, current approaches primarily focus on forecasting, while real-world time series are often irregularly and partially observed, requiring models that can jointly forecast, impute missing values, and handle degraded sampling conditions. To address these challenges, we introduce TS-ICL, a novel probabilistic In-Context Learning encoder--regressor Transformer that unifies forecasting and imputation. TS-ICL formulates time series tasks as timestamp-aligned regression and naturally incorporates covariates by training on synthetic dependency structures generated from a novel causal data prior. Empirically, TS-ICL achieves a new state-of-the-art in imputation, while remaining competitive with leading forecasting foundation models across both univariate and covariate-aware benchmarks. It shows particularly strong performance in forecasting with partially observed look-back windows.

AI.tldr: TS-ICL is a unified probabilistic Transformer for time-series forecasting and imputation. By casting tasks as timestamp-aligned regression and training with a causal synthetic data prior, it achieves SOTA imputation and strong forecasting, especially under missing or irregular observations.
AI.motivation: Existing time-series foundation models mainly emphasize forecasting, but many real-world series are irregularly sampled and partially observed. A more general model is needed to jointly perform forecasting, imputation, and remain robust under degraded sampling conditions.
AI.method: The paper proposes TS-ICL, a probabilistic in-context learning encoder-regressor Transformer. It reformulates time-series tasks as timestamp-aligned regression, supports covariates naturally, and is trained on synthetic dependency structures generated from a novel causal data prior.
AI.result: Empirically, TS-ICL sets a new state of the art for imputation and remains competitive with strong forecasting foundation models on both univariate and covariate-aware benchmarks. It performs particularly well when the look-back window is only partially observed.
AI.conclusion: TS-ICL provides a unified probabilistic foundation model for time series that handles both forecasting and imputation, and it is especially effective when observations are irregular or partially missing.

title: PLAN-S: Bridging Planning with Latent Style Dynamics for Autonomous Driving World Models
summary: Latent world models (LWMs) have strengthened end-to-end autonomous driving by forecasting compact scene dynamics for downstream planning. However, existing LWM-based planners usually generate trajectories directly from entangled latent representations. This compact latent-to-planner pathway lacks explicit modeling of risk, drivability, and diverse style preferences, making driving-style dynamics difficult to supervise, inspect, or modulate before a final trajectory is selected. We propose PLAN-S (PLANning with latent Style dynamics), a planner-facing bridge that addresses this compactness-controllability dilemma by decoding a style-conditioned, four-channel semantic cost map from the latent representation. The cost map is conditioned on ego state and driving style and is consumed up-stream of the planning decision through two host-side interfaces: attention-level fusion for regression planners and reward-level fusion for anchor-score planners. We validate PLAN-S on two architecturally distinct hosts, ResWorld on nuScenes and WoTE on NAVSIM, while keeping the host backbones frozen to isolate the contribution of the proposed bridge. On nuScenes, PLAN-S reduces L2 at every horizon over the baseline, with 0.55 m average L2 and a 42% relative reduction in the 3 s collision rate. On NAVSIM, the rule-cost variant reaches 89.4 Predictive Driver Model Score (PDMS), while the learned cost variant provides complementary gains on baseline-challenging scenes. Ablations show that the cost pathway contributes most directly to safer trajectory selection. Qualitative results further show that PLAN-S can produce diverse cost maps, with spatially consistent variations aligned to different driving styles.

AI.tldr: PLAN-S turns latent world model features into an explicit style-aware semantic cost map before planning, making autonomous driving decisions safer, more controllable, and more interpretable, with strong gains on nuScenes and NAVSIM.
AI.motivation: Existing latent world model planners map compact latent representations directly to trajectories, but this entangled latent-to-planner path lacks explicit modeling of risk, drivability, and driving style. As a result, style dynamics are hard to supervise, inspect, and control before trajectory selection. PLAN-S is motivated by the need to resolve the tradeoff between compact latent representations and controllable, interpretable planning.
AI.method: The method decodes a style-conditioned four-channel semantic cost map from latent world model representations, conditioned on ego state and driving style. This cost map is injected upstream into planning through two interfaces: attention-level fusion for regression planners and reward-level fusion for anchor-score planners. The framework is evaluated on two different frozen host planners, ResWorld and WoTE, to isolate the effect of the bridge.
AI.result: On nuScenes, PLAN-S reduces L2 error at every prediction horizon, achieving 0.55 m average L2 and a 42% relative reduction in 3-second collision rate versus the baseline. On NAVSIM, the rule-cost variant achieves 89.4 PDMS, and the learned-cost variant shows complementary improvements on challenging scenes. Ablation studies indicate that the cost pathway is the main contributor to safer trajectory selection, and qualitative results show style-consistent, spatially diverse cost maps.
AI.conclusion: PLAN-S introduces a planner-facing bridge for latent world model based autonomous driving, converting entangled latent features into a style-conditioned four-channel semantic cost map that improves controllability, safety, and interpretability while keeping host planners frozen. It consistently improves trajectory quality and safety on both nuScenes and NAVSIM.

title: LLM-Conditioned Synthesis of Pathological Gaits via Structured Gait-Language Representations
comment: Accepted at CVPR MOMA Workshop 2026 and selected for spotlight presentation at the workshop
summary: Pathological gait datasets remain scarce due to privacy, recruitment, cost, and movement variability. Our work presents a multimodal LLM-guided framework for pathology-aware 3D gait data synthesis from structured textual descriptions. The proposed method generates fixed-length synthetic skeleton-based gait sequences for pathological gait classification tasks. The framework combines motion tokenisation, pathology-aware language conditioning, LLM-based semantic augmentation, and language-to-gait generation. A key contribution is the proposed pathological tokeniser, which is designed to preserve pathology-specific motion characteristics during discrete representation learning. Experiments suggest that the proposed synthetic sequences improve downstream classification for recurrent classifiers when combined with real data. The best result is obtained using a GRU classifier trained with real and synthetic samples, achieving 92.77\% accuracy under a leave-one-subject-out protocol.

AI.tldr: The paper uses an LLM-guided text-to-gait pipeline to generate pathology-aware synthetic 3D gait skeleton sequences, and these synthetic samples improve pathological gait classification, with the best GRU model reaching 92.77% accuracy.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that pathological gait datasets are limited because of privacy constraints, recruitment difficulty, cost, and high movement variability. These limitations hinder data-hungry learning methods, so the paper seeks to synthesize realistic, pathology-aware 3D gait data to support classification tasks.
AI.method: The method is a multimodal framework for generating fixed-length synthetic pathological gait sequences from structured text. It combines motion tokenization, pathology-aware language conditioning, LLM-based semantic augmentation, and language-to-gait generation. A key component is a pathological tokenizer that aims to retain pathology-specific movement characteristics during discrete representation learning.
AI.result: Experiments indicate that adding the proposed synthetic sequences to real data improves downstream classification performance for recurrent models. The strongest result is 92.77% accuracy with a GRU classifier under a leave-one-subject-out protocol.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that multimodal, LLM-guided synthesis of pathology-aware 3D gait sequences can generate useful synthetic skeleton data that preserves clinically relevant motion patterns and improves downstream pathological gait classification when combined with real samples. The best reported setup is a GRU classifier trained on both real and synthetic data, reaching 92.77% accuracy under leave-one-subject-out evaluation.

title: Contextualized Prompting For Stance Detection On Social Media
summary: Stance detection on social media is challenging due to short, noisy, and context-dependent language. While large language models (LLMs) show zero-shot generalization, they are typically prompted without contextual information, which limits their ability to interpret ambiguous posts. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of incorporating real-world (e.g., user biographies), derived (e.g., political party), and LLM-generated (e.g., target descriptions) contextual features into zero-shot prompting for stance detection on Twitter. Our evaluation spans four benchmark datasets, including a new high-quality German Twitter stance dataset. Across multiple LLMs, we find that integrating contextual information improves performance, but only under specific conditions. LLM-generated target descriptions consistently enhance accuracy, while other user metadata has mixed or even detrimental effects. Notably, we show that the inclusion of other tweets by the same user, often beneficial in supervised learning, can impair performance due to input noise. Our qualitative analysis reveals that LLMs struggle to distinguish task-specific useful information from irrelevant context. Our findings highlight both the promise and challenges of prompting with context information in noisy real-world settings. We publish code and data at this \href{https://github.com/tilmanbeck/stance-context-twitter}{page}.

title: When Denser Credit Is Not Enough: Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Training
summary: Long-horizon LLM agents require reinforcement learning methods that can assign credit to intermediate decisions under sparse and delayed rewards. Recent group-based methods such as GiGPO improve over GRPO by constructing step-level advantages at repeated anchor states. However, we show that such dense credit can be statistically unreliable: under limited rollouts, rare but lucky actions may receive overly large advantages, producing divergent anchor bias and late-stage training oscillation. We propose Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization (ECPO), a critic-free policy optimization algorithm that calibrates step-level credit before policy updates. ECPO combines Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage, which groups rollouts by canonical actions and shrinks low-count estimates, with Variance-Gated Credit Weighting, which suppresses anchor states dominated by within-action noise. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B show that ECPO consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving GiGPO by +5.2/+7.3 success points on ALFWorld/WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B while adding only 0.1% additional advantage-computation overhead.

AI.tldr: 中文：这篇论文提出 ECPO，用证据收缩和方差门控来修正长时程 LLM agent RL 中不可靠的步骤级信用分配，比 GiGPO 更稳、更强、几乎不增加计算成本。 English: This paper proposes ECPO, which fixes unreliable step-level credit assignment in long-horizon LLM-agent RL via evidence shrinkage and variance gating, making training more stable and more effective than GiGPO at almost no extra cost.
AI.motivation: 中文：作者指出现有基于组的方法如 GiGPO 虽然通过 anchor state 构造稠密步骤级优势，但在 rollout 数有限时，罕见但偶然成功的动作会被高估，导致 anchor bias 发散和训练后期震荡，因此需要更可靠的信用分配。 English: The motivation is that existing group-based methods such as GiGPO create dense step-level credit at anchor states, but with limited rollouts they can over-credit rare but lucky actions, causing divergent anchor bias and late-stage training oscillation; therefore, more reliable credit assignment is needed.
AI.method: 中文：方法是一个无 critic 的策略优化框架 ECPO，包含两部分：1）Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage：按规范化动作对 rollout 分组，并对低样本动作优势做收缩估计；2）Variance-Gated Credit Weighting：对受动作内噪声主导的 anchor state 降低权重。 English: The method is a critic-free policy optimization algorithm, ECPO, with two components: (1) Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage, which groups rollouts by canonical actions and shrinks low-count action-advantage estimates; and (2) Variance-Gated Credit Weighting, which downweights anchor states dominated by within-action noise.
AI.result: 中文：在 ALFWorld 和 WebShop 上，使用 Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B，ECPO 持续优于强基线；其中在 Qwen2.5-1.5B 上，相比 GiGPO 分别提升 ALFWorld 5.2 个成功率点、WebShop 7.3 个成功率点，且额外优势计算开销仅 0.1%。 English: On ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B, ECPO consistently outperforms strong baselines; with Qwen2.5-1.5B it improves over GiGPO by 5.2 success points on ALFWorld and 7.3 on WebShop, with only 0.1% additional advantage-computation overhead.
AI.conclusion: 中文：ECPO 通过在策略更新前对步骤级信用进行证据校准，能够更稳定地处理稀疏延迟奖励下的长时程 LLM agent 强化学习，并以极低额外开销稳定优于 GiGPO 等强基线。 English: ECPO shows that calibrating step-level credit before policy updates yields more stable and effective RL for long-horizon LLM agents under sparse, delayed rewards, outperforming strong baselines like GiGPO with negligible overhead.

title: RedditPersona: A Modular Framework for Community-Conditioned LLM Adaptation from Reddit
summary: Community-conditioned language model adaptation requires choices about data collection, community definition, and evaluation that are currently made independently in each study, making it hard to compare assumptions or reuse artifacts. We present RedditPersona, a modular framework that standardizes these choices: it collects Reddit posts and comments, profiles active users, partitions them under five grouping strategies (subreddit-based, graph-structural, semantic, hybrid, and interaction-based), trains a parameter-efficient adapter per strategy via QLoRA, and evaluates them under a shared metric suite spanning fluency, fidelity, distributional alignment, and community identifiability. Applied to 112 subreddits in the urban well-being domain (301,429 user profiles, 16M+ comments), we find that adapters' behavioral identifiability tracks each strategy's intrinsic agreement with the subreddit baseline, and that a consistent trade-off between identifiability and distributional similarity to real text holds across all five strategies. The code and configuration files are available at: https://github.com/Ahghaffari/redditpersona.

AI.tldr: RedditPersona is a reusable benchmark/framework for adapting language models to Reddit communities. It standardizes data, grouping, training, and evaluation, and shows that making community-specific behavior more identifiable generally makes generated text less similar to real community text.
AI.motivation: Prior work on community-conditioned LM adaptation makes inconsistent choices about data collection, community definition, and evaluation, which prevents fair comparison across studies and limits artifact reuse. The authors aim to standardize these choices in one reusable framework.
AI.method: The paper builds a pipeline that collects Reddit posts/comments, creates active-user profiles, partitions users with five grouping strategies (subreddit-based, graph-structural, semantic, hybrid, interaction-based), trains parameter-efficient adapters for each strategy using QLoRA, and evaluates them with shared metrics covering fluency, fidelity, distributional alignment, and community identifiability.
AI.result: On data from 112 urban well-being subreddits, 301,429 user profiles, and over 16 million comments, the authors find that adapter identifiability correlates with how much each grouping strategy agrees with the subreddit baseline, and they observe a consistent identifiability-versus-distributional-similarity trade-off across all five strategies.
AI.conclusion: RedditPersona provides a standardized, modular framework for community-conditioned language model adaptation, and experiments show a robust trade-off: higher community identifiability tends to come with lower distributional similarity to real text across all grouping strategies.

title: ReCache: Learning Budget-Aware Caching Schedules for Diffusion Models via REINFORCE
summary: Modern diffusion models generate high-quality images and videos, but their iterative denoising process makes inference expensive. Feature caching accelerates sampling by reusing or predicting intermediate activations across neighboring denoising steps, exploiting the redundancy of computations along the reverse trajectory. In this work, we focus on the caching schedule: selecting which denoising steps should be fully recomputed. Existing schedules are either fixed (e.g. uniform) or chosen adaptively from per-step error heuristics; in both cases, the actual compute cost is a side-effect of hand-tuned thresholds rather than a quantity the user can specify. We propose ReCache, which inverts this: given a target budget k, it learns the recomputation schedule that maximizes generation quality, turning compute into a directly controllable input. ReCache trains via policy gradients, sidestepping backpropagation through full diffusion inference, and uses no labelled data. Generations from uncached inference serve as matching targets, paired with a reward for generation quality. ReCache is compatible with any caching mechanism, including feature reuse and feature forecasting; for each mechanism, a single trained policy adapts across computational budgets at inference time. ReCache consistently outperforms scheduling baselines: under a $\times5.04$ FLOPs reduction on FLUX, it reduces LPIPS by 31% (from 0.456 to 0.316) compared to DiCache; on Wan 2.1 at a $\sim \times2.6$ speedup, it drops LPIPS by 65% (from 0.480 to 0.169) and boosts the VBench score by 7% (5.6 points, from 70.4 to 76.0) over uniform HiCache. Code is available at https://github.com/thecrazymage/ReCache.

AI.tldr: ReCache is a reinforcement-learning-based cache scheduler for diffusion models that takes a target compute budget as input and learns which denoising steps to recompute, delivering better quality-speed tradeoffs than fixed or heuristic schedules.
AI.motivation: Diffusion sampling is expensive, and feature caching can reduce cost by skipping redundant computation across denoising steps. However, existing schedules are fixed or heuristic-driven, so users cannot directly control compute budget. The paper aims to make compute an explicit, user-controllable input while maximizing output quality.
AI.method: The paper formulates cache scheduling as a budget-conditioned policy learning problem. Given a target recomputation budget k, ReCache trains a policy with policy gradients to choose which denoising steps are fully recomputed, using uncached generations as matching targets and generation quality as reward. It is mechanism-agnostic and works with both feature reuse and feature forecasting.
AI.result: ReCache outperforms prior scheduling baselines. On FLUX with 5.04x FLOPs reduction, it lowers LPIPS by 31% versus DiCache (0.456 to 0.316). On Wan 2.1 with about 2.6x speedup, it reduces LPIPS by 65% (0.480 to 0.169) and improves VBench by 7% or 5.6 points (70.4 to 76.0) over uniform HiCache.
AI.conclusion: ReCache learns a recomputation schedule conditioned on a user-specified compute budget and consistently improves generation quality over fixed or heuristic caching schedules across image and video diffusion models.

title: EGTR-Review: Efficient Evidence-Grounded Scientific Peer Review Generation via Multi-Agent Teacher Distillation
