summary: Scientific peer review generation has attracted increasing attention for reducing reviewing burdens and providing timely feedback. However, existing Large Language Model (LLM)-based methods often produce generic comments with insufficient evidence support and weak source traceability, while complex multi-agent systems incur high inference costs. To address these challenges, we propose EGTR-Review, an Evidence-Grounded and Traceable Review Generation framework via Multi-Agent Teacher Distillation. EGTR-Review first constructs a multi-agent teacher that performs structure-aware paper decomposition, key-element extraction, external scholarly evidence retrieval, evidence-state labeling, verification reasoning, and review synthesis. It then distills both intermediate reasoning trajectories and final review comments into a lightweight student model through task-prefix-driven multi-task learning. An evidence-weighted objective further reduces the influence of weak, missing, or non-verifiable supervision. Experiments on public peer-review datasets show that EGTR-Review (Student) outperforms strong prompt-based, fine-tuned, and structured/agentic baselines across automatic metrics, LLM-as-Judge evaluation, and human evaluation, while maintaining strong factual grounding and source traceability with substantially lower token consumption and inference time. Our code, prompts, configurations, and sample data are available on GitHub.

AI.tldr: EGTR-Review 用高成本多智能体教师教会低成本学生模型写“有证据、可追溯”的评审，并在质量与效率上同时取得优势。 / EGTR-Review uses a costly multi-agent teacher to train a cheap student model to write evidence-grounded, traceable reviews, achieving better quality and efficiency.
AI.motivation: 现有基于大语言模型的评审生成方法常产生泛化、缺乏证据支撑且难以追溯来源的评论，而复杂多智能体系统虽然能力更强，但推理成本较高；因此需要一种同时兼顾质量、可验证性和效率的方法。 / Existing LLM-based review generation methods often produce generic, weakly supported, and poorly traceable comments, while stronger multi-agent systems are expensive at inference time; thus, a method balancing quality, verifiability, and efficiency is needed.
AI.method: 论文提出 EGTR-Review：先构建一个多智能体教师系统，执行结构感知的论文分解、关键要素提取、外部学术证据检索、证据状态标注、验证推理与评审合成；再通过任务前缀驱动的多任务学习，将中间推理轨迹和最终评审蒸馏到学生模型，并采用证据加权目标降低低质量监督的影响。 / The paper proposes EGTR-Review: it first builds a multi-agent teacher for structure-aware paper decomposition, key-element extraction, external evidence retrieval, evidence-state labeling, verification reasoning, and review synthesis; then distills both intermediate reasoning trajectories and final reviews into a student model via task-prefix-driven multi-task learning, with an evidence-weighted objective to downweight weak supervision.
AI.result: 在公共同行评审数据集上，EGTR-Review 的学生模型在自动指标、LLM-as-Judge 和人工评测中均优于强基线，同时保持较强的事实依据与来源可追溯性，并显著降低 token 消耗和推理时间。 / On public peer-review datasets, the EGTR-Review student model outperforms strong prompt-based, fine-tuned, and agentic baselines on automatic metrics, LLM-as-Judge, and human evaluation, while preserving factual grounding and source traceability with much lower token usage and inference time.
AI.conclusion: EGTR-Review 通过多智能体教师蒸馏与证据加权训练，使轻量级学生模型能够生成更有证据支撑、可追溯、成本更低的同行评审意见，并在多种评测中优于现有方法。 / EGTR-Review shows that a lightweight student model distilled from a multi-agent teacher can generate more evidence-grounded, traceable, and efficient peer reviews, outperforming existing baselines across multiple evaluations.

title: High-Dimensional Theory of LoRA Fine-Tuning in a Solvable Attention Model
summary: We develop a high-dimensional statistical theory of low-rank adaptation (LoRA) in attention models, capturing the interplay between pre-training and fine-tuning. We introduce a solvable framework in which a single-head attention layer is first pre-trained on a data-abundant task and subsequently adapted via a rank-one LoRA update on limited data. In the high-dimensional limit, both stages admit a sharp asymptotic characterization in terms of a finite set of order parameters, yielding explicit predictions for test errors and representation alignment. Our analysis shows that the impact of pre-training on LoRA is summarized by an effective noise term, from which we derive prescriptions for the optimal pre-training procedure. We also demonstrate a regime with a mismatch between the value of the test error and representation quality, and propose an application of our theory to active fine-tuning.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文为注意力模型中的LoRA建立了可解的高维理论：先预训练、再做秩一LoRA微调，并用少量序参量精确预测泛化与表征行为。核心发现是预训练的作用等价于一个“有效噪声”，这使最优预训练设计可被解析推导；同时，测试误差与表征质量并不总是一致。 / This paper builds a solvable high-dimensional theory for LoRA in attention models: pre-train first, then apply rank-one LoRA fine-tuning, with a small set of order parameters predicting generalization and representation behavior. The key insight is that pre-training acts through an “effective noise” term, enabling analytic prescriptions for optimal pre-training, while also showing that test error and representation quality do not always agree.
AI.motivation: 现有LoRA实践广泛依赖预训练，但缺乏能够定量解释“预训练如何影响低秩微调效果”的理论，尤其是在高维、有限样本和注意力模型场景下。本文旨在建立可解析理论，明确预训练与LoRA之间的相互作用，并据此给出最优预训练和微调策略。 / LoRA is widely used on top of pre-trained models, but there is limited theory explaining how pre-training quantitatively affects low-rank adaptation, especially in high-dimensional, limited-data attention settings. The paper aims to build an analytically tractable theory of the interaction between pre-training and LoRA, and to derive prescriptions for better pre-training and fine-tuning.
AI.method: 文章构建了一个可解的高维统计框架：先在数据充足的任务上对单头注意力层进行预训练，再在小样本场景下用秩一LoRA更新进行适配；在高维极限下，用有限个序参量精确刻画预训练与微调两个阶段的动力学与泛化表现。 / The paper develops a solvable high-dimensional statistical framework: a single-head attention layer is pre-trained on a data-rich task and then adapted with a rank-one LoRA update under limited data; in the high-dimensional limit, both stages are characterized sharply by a finite set of order parameters.
AI.result: 作者得到对测试误差和表征对齐的尖锐渐近表征，证明预训练效应可通过有效噪声统一表述，并据此推导最优预训练方案；同时识别出测试误差低但表征质量未必高的失配区间，并展示该理论在主动微调中的潜在应用。 / The authors derive sharp asymptotic characterizations of test error and representation alignment, show that pre-training is captured through an effective noise term, use it to derive optimal pre-training prescriptions, identify a mismatch regime where low test error does not imply high-quality representations, and illustrate an application to active fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: 预训练对LoRA微调的影响可以被压缩为一个有效噪声项；该理论不仅给出测试误差与表征对齐的显式渐近预测，还揭示了测试误差与表征质量可能失配的区间，并可用于指导主动式微调策略。 / The effect of pre-training on LoRA fine-tuning can be summarized by an effective noise term; the theory provides explicit asymptotic predictions for test error and representation alignment, reveals a regime where test error and representation quality mismatch, and suggests a principled use for active fine-tuning.

title: Memory is Reconstructed, Not Retrieved: Graph Memory for LLM Agents
summary: Despite recent progress, LLM agents still struggle with reasoning over long interaction histories. While current memory-augmented agents rely on a static retrieve-then-reason paradigm, this rigid pipeline design prevents them from dynamically adapting memory access to intermediate evidence discovered during inference. To bridge this gap, we propose MRAgent, a framework that combines an associative memory graph with an active reconstruction mechanism. We represent memory as a Cue-Tag-Content graph, where associative tags serve as semantic bridges connecting fine-grained cues to memory contents. Operating on this structure, our active reconstruction mechanism integrates LLM reasoning directly into memory access, allowing the agent to iteratively explore and prune retrieval paths based on accumulated evidence. This ensures that memory retrieval is dynamically adapted to the reasoning context while avoiding combinatorial explosion caused by unconstrained expansion. Experiments on the LoCoMo benchmark and LongMemEval benchmark demonstrate significant improvements over strong baselines (up to 23%), while substantially reducing token and runtime cost, highlighting the effectiveness of active and associative reconstruction for long-horizon memory reasoning.

AI.tldr: MRAgent replaces static memory retrieval with reasoning-guided, graph-based active memory reconstruction, improving long-context agent performance and efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing memory-augmented LLM agents use a static retrieve-then-reason pipeline, which cannot adapt memory access dynamically during inference and therefore performs poorly on long interaction histories.
AI.method: The paper proposes MRAgent, which models memory as a Cue-Tag-Content associative graph and uses an active reconstruction mechanism to iteratively explore and prune retrieval paths based on intermediate reasoning evidence from the LLM.
AI.result: On LoCoMo and LongMemEval, MRAgent significantly outperforms strong baselines by up to 23% and also reduces token usage and runtime cost.
AI.conclusion: MRAgent shows that integrating reasoning directly into memory access through an associative memory graph and active reconstruction can substantially improve long-horizon memory reasoning while lowering token and runtime costs.

title: NAVIRA: Decoupled Stochastic Remasking for Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: Masked diffusion language models generate text by iteratively unmasking many tokens in parallel, but this speed comes with a correction problem: tokens generated in the same step are predicted from marginal distributions, and early local dependency errors can later contaminate the context. PRISM addresses this by learning token-level quality scores and remasking unreliable tokens, but its inference rule is coupled: the same forward pass both detects low-quality tokens and computes logits for their replacements, so the erroneous tokens still condition regeneration. We propose NAVIRA, an inference-time decoding policy that separates these two operations and samples remasking positions stochastically. A first forward pass scores tokens; selected tokens are masked; a second forward pass regenerates from the cleaned context. Temperature-controlled remasking reduces repeated correction of the same positions and balances fluency against diversity. In controlled experiments with a 170M masked diffusion language model, decoupling improves fluency, while scheduled stochastic remasking preserves entropy and achieves stronger LLM-judge scores under larger forward-pass budgets. These results show that remasking policy, not only the learned quality signal, is central to reliable masked-diffusion text generation.

AI.tldr: NAVIRA improves masked diffusion text generation by first identifying unreliable tokens, masking them out, and only then regenerating them in a second pass; this decoupled and stochastic remasking strategy yields more fluent and diverse text than coupled correction methods like PRISM.
AI.motivation: Existing masked diffusion decoding is fast but suffers from a correction problem because tokens generated in parallel are predicted from marginal distributions, so early local dependency errors can propagate. In PRISM, detection of bad tokens and regeneration are coupled in one forward pass, meaning erroneous tokens still influence their own replacement. The paper aims to remove this coupling and improve correction reliability.
AI.method: The paper proposes NAVIRA, a decoding policy for masked diffusion language models that uses two separate forward passes at each correction step: the first pass estimates token-level quality scores, then low-confidence positions are stochastically selected and remasked, and the second pass regenerates those tokens from the cleaned context. A temperature-controlled remasking schedule is used to reduce repeatedly correcting the same positions.
AI.result: In experiments with a 170M masked diffusion language model, decoupled regeneration improves fluency, and scheduled stochastic remasking preserves entropy and achieves better LLM-judge scores when more forward passes are available.
AI.conclusion: NAVIRA shows that inference-time remasking policy is a key factor in reliable masked diffusion language model decoding; decoupling token scoring from regeneration improves generation quality, and stochastic temperature-controlled remasking better balances fluency and diversity under larger decoding budgets.

title: Addressing Imbalance in Multi-Label Data via Label-Specific Distance-based Oversampling
summary: The complex imbalanced label distribution poses a crucial challenge to multi-label classification, as most classifiers are biased towards the majority class and high-frequent labels. Oversampling is an efficient and flexible solution that augments instances to provide a more balanced training dataset for multi-label classifiers. Most existing oversampling methods create synthetic instances in a heuristic way that essentially relies on neighborhood information retrieved using Euclidean distance within the entire feature space. However, they fail to consider the varying semantic relevance of features to different labels, leading to label inconsistency among proximate neighbors and further introducing label confusion and overfitting to synthetic instances. To overcome the above issue, we propose a novel sampling approach called Label-Specific Distance-based Multi-Label Oversampling (LSDMLO) that creates more useful and well-labeled synthetic instances to address the imbalance in multi-label datasets. LSDMLO derives the label-specific distance to identify label-consistent neighbors based on the weighted pertinent feature space, which facilitates selecting seed instances that express more label correlations in boundary areas and generating synthetic instances aligned with the label distribution of original data. The comprehensive experiments verify that the proposed LSDMLO outperforms the state-of-the-art multi-label sampling approaches under various base classifiers.

AI.tldr: LSDMLO通过“按标签定义距离”来找更合适的邻居并生成标签更一致的合成样本，从而比传统基于全局欧氏距离的多标签过采样方法效果更好。 / LSDMLO finds better neighbors using label-specific distance and creates more label-consistent synthetic samples, outperforming traditional multi-label oversampling methods based on global Euclidean distance.
AI.motivation: 现有多标签过采样方法大多依赖整个特征空间中的欧氏距离进行启发式合成，忽略了不同特征对不同标签的语义相关性差异，导致近邻间标签不一致，进而带来标签混淆和对合成样本的过拟合。 / Existing multi-label oversampling methods mostly rely on Euclidean distance in the full feature space and ignore that feature relevance varies by label, which can cause label inconsistency among neighbors, label confusion, and overfitting to synthetic samples.
AI.method: 方法核心是LSDMLO：为不同标签构建标签特定距离，基于加权相关特征空间识别标签一致邻居；再选择边界区域中能体现更多标签相关性的种子样本，并生成与原始标签分布更一致的合成实例。 / The core method is LSDMLO: it derives a label-specific distance, identifies label-consistent neighbors in a weighted pertinent feature space, selects seed instances in boundary regions that better capture label correlations, and generates synthetic instances aligned with the original label distribution.
AI.result: 摘要声称在全面实验中，LSDMLO在不同基分类器设置下均优于当前先进的多标签采样方法，说明其能更有效缓解多标签数据中的标签不平衡问题。 / The abstract reports that comprehensive experiments show LSDMLO surpasses state-of-the-art multi-label sampling approaches under different base classifiers, indicating better handling of label imbalance in multi-label datasets.
AI.conclusion: 提出的LSDMLO通过标签特定距离在加权相关特征空间中寻找标签一致的邻居，并生成更可靠的合成样本；实验表明其在多种基分类器下优于现有多标签过采样方法。 / The proposed LSDMLO uses label-specific distance in a weighted pertinent feature space to find label-consistent neighbors and generate more reliable synthetic samples; experiments show it outperforms existing multi-label oversampling methods across various base classifiers.

title: Beyond Similarity: Trustworthy Memory Search for Personal AI Agents
summary:
Personal AI agents increasingly rely on long-term memory to provide persistent personalization across sessions. However, existing memory pipelines are largely driven by semantic similarity: memory data close to the current query is retrieved and injected into the model context. This creates a critical trustworthiness gap, since a semantically related memory may still be contextually inappropriate, leading to threats such as cross-domain leakage, sycophancy, tool-call drift, or memory-induced jailbreaks.
  In this paper, we study memory search as a trust boundary in personal AI agents. We evaluate representative agentic memory frameworks, including A-Mem, Mem0, and MemOS, together with OpenClaw, a real-world personal-agent environment with persistent state and tool-use capability. Our results show that long-term memory is not merely a utility layer, but a durable control channel that can reshape how agents interpret tasks and execute actions, leaving them highly susceptible to the aforementioned threats. To mitigate these vulnerabilities, we propose MemGate, a lightweight and deployable memory plug-in for trustworthy memory search, with only 9M parameters and a 35.1MB footprint. MemGate is inserted between the vector memory store and the backbone LLM, requiring no LLM modification, memory-database rewriting, or inference-time LLM judge. It applies a query-conditioned neural gate to candidate memory representations, turning raw similarity search into task-conditioned memory admission. Across multiple mainstream memory frameworks, real-world agent settings, and diverse LLM backbones, MemGate reduces memory-induced threats while preserving long-term memory utility.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that similarity-based memory retrieval in personal AI agents is a major trust and safety weakness. It proposes MemGate, a small plug-in that filters retrieved memories based on the current task, reducing unsafe memory effects across several agent frameworks while keeping long-term memory useful.
AI.motivation: Existing personal AI agents typically retrieve long-term memories based on semantic similarity alone. The authors argue this is insufficient for trustworthiness because semantically related memories can still be contextually inappropriate, causing risks such as cross-domain leakage, sycophancy, tool-call drift, and memory-induced jailbreaks. The work is motivated by the need to treat memory search itself as a security and trust boundary.
AI.method: The paper evaluates several representative long-term memory frameworks (A-Mem, Mem0, MemOS) in the OpenClaw personal-agent environment to characterize threats caused by similarity-based memory retrieval. It then introduces MemGate, a lightweight plug-in inserted between the vector memory store and the backbone LLM. MemGate uses a query-conditioned neural gate to filter candidate memory representations before they are passed to the model, converting raw semantic retrieval into task-conditioned memory admission, without modifying the LLM, rewriting the memory database, or relying on an inference-time LLM judge.
AI.result: The empirical study shows that long-term memory acts not just as a utility mechanism but as a persistent control channel that can substantially alter agent behavior and make agents vulnerable to several memory-induced threats. Across multiple memory systems, agent settings, and LLM backbones, MemGate reduces these threats while preserving the benefits of long-term memory. It does so with a small footprint of 9M parameters and 35.1MB, making it practical to deploy.
AI.conclusion: MemGate demonstrates that memory retrieval in personal AI agents should be treated as a trust boundary, and that a lightweight query-conditioned gating module can significantly reduce memory-induced safety and trustworthiness risks without sacrificing the utility of long-term memory.

title: VZCrash: A Large-Scale IMU Dataset of Ego-Vehicle Crashes
comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC 2026). VZCrash is publicly available at this URL: https://huggingface.co/datasets/vzc-research-chapter/VZCrash
summary: We introduce VZCrash, the largest publicly available dataset of real-world vehicle collision data featuring Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) telemetry. The dataset contains more than 31,000 validated crashes and 158,000 negative samples, including hard cases and distractors. Each sample includes acceleration and angular velocity at 100 Hz, and GPS speed at 1 Hz. Events in VZCrash were captured by devices installed on a fleet of 73,010 commercial vehicles of different sizes driving in the United States over the span of several years. We also present an extensive experimental study enabled by the volume of the dataset. We first benchmark several different approaches, from a simple threshold-based heuristic to state-of-the-art deep learning models. Then, we present an experiment demonstrating the importance of scaling data to train high-quality crash detection models, and we show that scale is especially important when these models need to be deployed into a real-world environment.

AI.tldr: VZCrash is a very large public IMU-based vehicle crash dataset, and experiments on it show that modern models benefit substantially from large-scale real-world data for reliable crash detection.
AI.motivation: Prior crash detection research has been limited by the lack of large, publicly available real-world datasets with high-frequency IMU signals, making it difficult to benchmark methods fairly and understand how dataset scale affects practical deployment performance.
AI.method: The paper introduces VZCrash, a large public dataset of commercial-vehicle collision events with synchronized IMU telemetry and GPS speed, then conducts extensive experiments comparing threshold heuristics and state-of-the-art deep learning models, including scaling studies on training data volume.
AI.result: The authors release a dataset with over 31,000 validated crashes and 158,000 negative samples collected from 73,010 commercial vehicles, and show through benchmarking and scaling experiments that stronger models and larger datasets yield better crash detection performance, particularly under real-world deployment conditions.
AI.conclusion: VZCrash demonstrates that large-scale, real-world IMU-based crash datasets materially improve the development and evaluation of vehicle crash detection systems, and that dataset scale is especially critical for robust deployment in real-world settings.

title: English-to-Prakrit Machine Translation via Multilingual Transfer Learning
summary: We study English-to-Prakrit machine translation in a low-resource setting where the target language is unsupported by IndicTrans2. We adapt the multilingual model by mapping Prakrit to the Hindi language tag (hin_Deva) without modifying the tokenizer, vocabulary, or architecture. Using a 1,474-pair Maharashtri Prakrit parallel corpus and evaluation on a 20-sample Ardhamagadhi test set, we report corpus BLEU improvements over an untuned baseline. The results indicate that script-compatible language routing can enable feasible transfer to unsupported classical languages, while highlighting limitations due to data scarcity and dialect mismatch. Our code and trained models are released to the public for further exploration https://github.com/D3v1s0m/indictrans2-prakrit-mt.

AI.tldr: Map Prakrit to Hindi inside IndicTrans2, train on a small Prakrit corpus, and get better BLEU than baseline; this simple transfer works, but low data and dialect mismatch still limit quality.
AI.motivation: Prakrit is an unsupported classical language in IndicTrans2, and parallel data are scarce. The work explores whether script-compatible transfer through language-tag routing can provide a simple, low-cost adaptation path.
AI.method: The paper adapts the multilingual IndicTrans2 model for English-to-Prakrit MT by reusing the Hindi language tag without changing tokenizer, vocabulary, or model architecture, then trains/evaluates on a 1,474-pair Maharashtri Prakrit parallel corpus with a 20-sample Ardhamagadhi test set.
AI.result: The adapted system achieves corpus BLEU improvements over an untuned baseline, showing feasible transfer to an unsupported classical language, though gains are limited by scarcity of training data and mismatch between Maharashtri training data and Ardhamagadhi evaluation data.
AI.conclusion: Using IndicTrans2 with Prakrit mapped to the Hindi tag (hin_Deva) is a practical way to obtain English-to-Prakrit translation in a low-resource unsupported-language setting, but performance remains constrained by limited data and dialect mismatch.

title: Short paper: Models in the dark -- Rectification and erasure under GDPR in ML supply chains
comment: accepted for presentation at Annual Privacy Forum 2026
summary: The rights to rectification and erasure, as established under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), are central to protecting individuals' privacy. However, their effective enforcement in machine learning (ML) systems remains challenging. Existing work has largely addressed these rights from either a legal or a technical perspective in isolation and disregards the fact that models are produced in complex supply chains involving multiple actors across development, distribution, and deployment. This paper presents a holistic survey of challenges in implementing the rights to rectification and erasure in ML models. Drawing on academic literature and guidance from data protection authorities, we find that many GDPR requirements cannot yet be technically met in practice. Our findings further suggest that issues arising in ML supply chains are insufficiently addressed in research. To tackle this gap, we introduce the notion of models in the dark -- derived models created further downstream in an ML chain without sufficient transparency or traceability -- and analyse the urgent challenges posed by this phenomenon. By adopting an interdisciplinary perspective, this work contributes to bridging the gap between legal requirements and the technical implementation of data subject rights in ML, ultimately supporting the development of trustworthy artificial intelligence.

AI.tldr: A survey showing that GDPR correction/deletion rights are still hard to implement in ML, especially across opaque supply chains; the paper highlights unmet technical requirements and proposes 'models in the dark' as a key problem concept.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that prior work treats GDPR rectification and erasure either legally or technically in isolation, while real ML systems are built and propagated through complex multi-actor supply chains.
AI.method: The paper uses a holistic interdisciplinary survey method, reviewing academic literature and guidance from data protection authorities to analyze legal and technical challenges across ML supply chains.
AI.result: The paper finds that many GDPR requirements are not technically achievable in current practice and that research insufficiently addresses supply-chain-specific problems. It introduces the concept of 'models in the dark' to characterize opaque downstream derived models and analyzes the challenges they create.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that current machine learning systems and their supply chains cannot yet reliably satisfy GDPR rights to rectification and erasure in practice, especially where downstream derived models lack transparency and traceability.

title: When Should Memory Stay Silent: Measuring Memory-Use Boundaries in Memory-Augmented Conversational Agents
summary: Long-term memory enables language model agents to support personalized interactions, but it remains unclear when available memories warrant integration into responses. Existing memory evaluations emphasize retrieval accuracy and downstream task utility, while overlooking whether retrieved sensitive memory content is warranted in the current turn. We introduce RBI-Eval, a controlled measurement study built around a probe set that compares model behavior with and without access to sensitive memory under identical benign prompts. We evaluate four base LLMs against a matched no-memory reference across four memory-access settings: full-context exposure and three retrieval systems. Our results reveal substantial behavioral divergence. With memory available, the separation score for sensitive-memory integration decreases by 8.9\%--26.6\% relative to the matched no-memory reference for GPT-5.4-mini, but by 51.1\%--82.9\% for Claude-Sonnet-4.6, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and Qwen3.5-9B. Control experiments on DeepSeek and GPT-5.4-mini show this effect is specific to sensitive content, rather than general personalization. Retrieval systems reduce exposure but do not eliminate integration once sensitive memory reaches the generator. These findings suggest safe personalization requires memory-aware decisions at both retrieval and generation time.

AI.tldr: RBI-Eval measures whether LLM agents improperly use sensitive long-term memories in otherwise benign prompts. Across four models and multiple memory-access setups, memory availability often causes inappropriate sensitive-memory integration, with GPT-5.4-mini being more robust than the others tested. The paper argues that safe personalization needs safeguards during both retrieval and response generation.
AI.motivation: Prior memory evaluations focus on retrieval accuracy and downstream utility, but they do not measure whether integrating retrieved sensitive memory is actually warranted in the current conversational turn. The paper aims to quantify that behavioral risk.
AI.method: The paper introduces RBI-Eval, a controlled probe-based evaluation that compares model responses with and without access to sensitive memory under identical benign prompts. It evaluates four base LLMs using four memory-access settings: full-context exposure and three retrieval systems, against matched no-memory references.
AI.result: Models with memory access show notable increases in inappropriate sensitive-memory integration. GPT-5.4-mini shows a smaller drop in separation score (8.9%–26.6%) relative to the matched no-memory reference, while Claude-Sonnet-4.6, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and Qwen3.5-9B show much larger drops (51.1%–82.9%). Control experiments indicate the effect is specific to sensitive content rather than personalization in general. Retrieval reduces exposure but does not eliminate the problem once sensitive memory is passed to generation.
AI.conclusion: Safe personalization in language model agents requires memory-aware decision-making at both retrieval and generation stages, because retrieval alone cannot prevent inappropriate use of sensitive memories once they reach the generator.

title: Knowledge Distillation for Visual Autoregressive Models
summary: Autoregressive (AR) image generation models are highly expressive but computationally intensive, motivating effective model compression. Knowledge distillation (KD) is a natural approach for model compression and has been widely studied in language modeling, yet its behavior in visual AR generation remains underexplored. In this work, we present the first systematic study of distillation strategies for AR image models. Our analysis shows that while standard distillation can yield meaningful gains, recent methods developed for language do not directly transfer to images: long decoding horizons and visual token ambiguity make teacher supervision unreliable especially under student-conditioned contexts. To address this, we propose VarKD, a distillation framework for visual autoregressive models that distills on student samples while selectively applying teacher supervision and reducing token-level ambiguity. Experiments on ImageNet across multiple AR backbones show that VarKD consistently outperforms prior distillation baselines, narrowing the gap to large-scale models.

AI.tldr: This paper studies why knowledge distillation is harder for autoregressive image models than for language models, then proposes VarKD to make teacher supervision more reliable on student-generated samples. VarKD beats existing KD baselines on ImageNet across several AR image generators.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive image generation models are powerful but expensive to run, so model compression is important. Although knowledge distillation is a natural compression approach and is well studied in language modeling, its behavior and challenges in visual autoregressive generation were not well understood.
AI.method: The paper conducts a systematic study of distillation strategies for autoregressive image models, analyzes why standard and language-model-inspired KD methods degrade under student-conditioned generation, and proposes VarKD, which distills on student-generated samples while selectively applying teacher supervision and reducing token-level ambiguity.
AI.result: Experiments on ImageNet with multiple autoregressive backbones show that standard KD provides some gains, but recent language-oriented KD methods do not transfer well to images. VarKD performs better than prior distillation baselines and narrows the performance gap between compressed and large models.
AI.conclusion: VarKD is an effective distillation framework for visual autoregressive image generation. It consistently outperforms prior distillation baselines on ImageNet across multiple AR backbones and helps smaller models better approach the performance of large-scale models.

title: IA-RAG: Interval-Algebra-Driven Temporal Reasoning for Dynamic Knowledge Retrieval
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, 13 tables. Code available at https://github.com/xiaoAugenstern/LogicalRAG_TemporalQA
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has shown strong effectiveness in grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) with external knowledge. However, existing RAG and Graph RAG frameworks largely treat knowledge as static or associate time with coarse-grained timestamps or metadata, failing to capture rich temporal structures such as duration, overlap, and containment. We propose IA-RAG, a hierarchical temporal RAG framework that models knowledge as time intervals and performs retrieval under formal temporal constraints. IA-RAG represents facts as Interval Event Units (IEUs) and organizes them into a hierarchical Thematic Forest, where temporal dependencies are governed by Allen's Interval Algebra. To handle incomplete or uncertain temporal boundaries, IA-RAG further introduces a Sub-graph Time Tightening mechanism that refines fuzzy intervals through logical constraints within connected event subgraphs. In addition, IA-RAG supports implicit temporal semantic retrieval through interval-algebra-guided traversal. Experiments on multiple temporal question answering benchmarks, including TimeQA, TempReason, and ComplexTR, demonstrate that IA-RAG achieves strong temporal retrieval and reasoning performance, particularly on complex compositional temporal reasoning tasks. Our code is released at https://github.com/xiaoAugenstern/LogicalRAG_TemporalQA.

AI.tldr: IA-RAG upgrades RAG for temporal QA by treating facts as time intervals instead of static records, using interval algebra and graph-based constraint tightening to retrieve and reason over time-sensitive knowledge more accurately.
AI.motivation: Existing RAG and Graph RAG methods usually treat knowledge as static or use only coarse timestamps/metadata, which cannot represent rich temporal structures such as duration, overlap, containment, and uncertainty in temporal boundaries.
AI.method: The paper proposes IA-RAG, a hierarchical temporal RAG framework that represents facts as Interval Event Units (IEUs), organizes them in a hierarchical Thematic Forest, governs temporal relations with Allen's Interval Algebra, refines uncertain intervals via a Sub-graph Time Tightening mechanism, and performs interval-algebra-guided temporal semantic retrieval.
AI.result: Across TimeQA, TempReason, and ComplexTR, IA-RAG achieves strong temporal retrieval and reasoning performance, with particularly notable gains on complex compositional temporal reasoning benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: IA-RAG demonstrates that modeling knowledge with time intervals and formal temporal constraints substantially improves temporal retrieval and reasoning, especially for complex compositional temporal QA tasks.

title: Dead Directions: Geometric Singular Learning
summary: Singular learning theory and information geometry have studied the same parameter spaces in mostly separate vocabularies: the former computes Bayesian invariants in resolved coordinates, the latter works in original coordinates under a non-degeneracy assumption that overparameterised models routinely violate. We bridge them through one primitive, the dead direction: a unit vector along which the Fisher metric degenerates, equivalently a tangent to the analytic singular set with a definite KL order, set by how fast the KL divergence vanishes. The two readings name the same vector; our central move shows its KL order is recoverable as the decay rate of the directional Fisher curvature approaching the singularity, in original parameter coordinates and without a Hironaka resolution. A selection rule on smooth fibres translates this rate into Watanabe's single-direction contribution to the real log canonical threshold, and we extend the recovery to multi-component crossings, multiplicity $m$, the singular fluctuation $ν$ (universal in the KL order for 1D directions), prior-RLCT shifts, and tempered posteriors. We then lift this rate to a deep network: a multi-layer K-FAC factorisation writes each Fisher block as a product of activation- and gradient-side rates with a duality between them, instantiated at modern-network primitives (residual streams, layer normalisation, attention). A quotient theorem carries the rate to the gauge quotient $Θ/G$ under gradient flow on a $G$-invariant metric; SGD qualifies, standard Adam does not, and we construct a $G$-equivariant Adam-family preconditioner (DDCAdam) that does. The bridge yields a parameter-coordinate handle on singular geometry, closed-form per-architecture predictions, and a trajectory-rate readout of Watanabe's triple $(λ, m, ν)$ from one checkpoint's forward and backward passes, without posterior sampling.

AI.tldr: A dead direction links singular learning theory and information geometry: by measuring how directional Fisher curvature decays near singularities, the paper recovers KL order and Watanabe’s invariants directly in original coordinates, extends the theory to deep networks and symmetry quotients, and proposes a practical optimizer-compatible readout without posterior sampling.
AI.motivation: Singular learning theory and information geometry study the same singular parameter spaces but use different coordinate systems and assumptions. Existing information-geometric tools typically rely on non-degeneracy and fail in overparameterized models, while singular learning theory often requires resolved coordinates via Hironaka resolution. The paper aims to connect these frameworks in original parameter coordinates with a computable primitive.
AI.method: The authors define dead directions as Fisher-degenerate unit vectors tangent to analytic singular sets and prove that their KL order equals the asymptotic decay rate of directional Fisher curvature near the singularity. They introduce a smooth-fibre selection rule to map this rate to RLCT contributions, extend the analysis to crossings, multiplicity, singular fluctuation, prior shifts, and tempered posteriors, then derive a K-FAC-based factorized rate analysis for deep networks and a quotient theorem for gauge symmetries under invariant metrics, including a symmetry-respecting Adam variant.
AI.result: The paper derives a coordinate-level bridge between KL vanishing order and Fisher-curvature decay, yielding closed-form architectural predictions and a way to read off Watanabe’s triple (lambda, m, nu) from a single checkpoint using forward and backward passes. It also characterizes when optimization on quotient spaces preserves the rate, showing SGD is compatible while standard Adam is not, and proposes DDCAdam as a G-equivariant alternative.
AI.conclusion: The paper unifies singular learning theory and information geometry through the concept of a dead direction, showing that KL order can be recovered directly in original parameter coordinates from the decay rate of directional Fisher curvature near singularities. This enables practical estimation of Watanabe’s invariants and extension to deep-network architectures and symmetry quotients without requiring resolution of singularities.

title: Learning Visual Spatial Planning from Symbolic State via Modality-Gap-Aware Self-Distillation
summary: While vision-language models excel at general multimodal understanding, they still struggle with visual spatial planning. We attribute this to a perception-reasoning modality gap: visual planning requires models to infer latent state structures from pixels and then reason over the recovered structure to produce valid actions, whereas symbolic planning directly leverages explicit objects and constraints. This creates dual bottlenecks in visual state recovery and multi-step planning. To address this, we propose MGSD, a two-stage modality-gap-aware self-distillation framework. First, a cold-start grounding stage equips the visual student with reliable state representations, minimizing early perception noise. Second, a privileged teacher transfers planning capabilities via on-policy distillation, using explicit symbolic states to supervise the student's own visual rollout prefixes. Crucially, symbolic data is used strictly during training, leaving inference purely visual. Experiments on visual planning benchmarks show that MGSD consistently improves visual planning across both 4B and 8B backbones, raising the macro average by 19.3% and 18.4%, respectively. The resulting models narrow the gap to symbolic-input upper bounds, while ablations and diagnostics confirm that the improvement comes from both visual state recovery and optimal-path reasoning. These results suggest that modality-gap-aware self-distillation improves not only how models perceive actionable states, but also how they plan over the inferred structure. Code is available at https://github.com/Oranger-l/MGSD.

AI.tldr: MGSD 用符号信息只在训练阶段教会视觉模型“先看懂状态，再学会规划”，从而显著提升纯视觉空间规划性能。 / MGSD uses symbolic information only during training to teach a visual model to first recover states reliably and then plan effectively, substantially improving pure-vision spatial planning.
AI.motivation: 动机在于视觉-语言模型在通用多模态理解上表现强，但在视觉空间规划上仍然薄弱。作者将其归因为感知与推理之间的模态鸿沟：模型既要从像素恢复潜在状态结构，又要基于该结构进行多步规划，因此同时受限于视觉状态恢复和规划推理两个瓶颈。 / The motivation is that vision-language models perform well on general multimodal understanding but remain weak at visual spatial planning. The authors attribute this to a perception-reasoning modality gap: the model must recover latent state structure from pixels and then reason over it for multi-step planning, creating dual bottlenecks in visual state recovery and planning.
AI.method: 方法是 MGSD，两阶段框架：第一阶段为 cold-start grounding，用于学习可靠的视觉状态表示；第二阶段使用具备符号状态特权信息的教师进行 on-policy distillation，对学生基于视觉 rollout 前缀的规划进行监督。训练时使用符号数据，推理时仅使用视觉输入。 / The method is MGSD, a two-stage framework: (1) a cold-start grounding stage to learn reliable visual state representations; (2) an on-policy distillation stage where a privileged teacher with access to symbolic states supervises the student's planning over visual rollout prefixes. Symbolic data is used only during training, while inference remains purely visual.
AI.result: 在视觉规划基准上，MGSD 在 4B 和 8B backbone 上都取得稳定提升，macro average 分别提高 19.3% 和 18.4%。消融和诊断实验表明，收益同时来自更好的视觉状态恢复和更优的路径推理。 / On visual planning benchmarks, MGSD consistently improves both 4B and 8B backbones, increasing the macro average by 19.3% and 18.4%, respectively. Ablations and diagnostics show that the gains come from both better visual state recovery and stronger optimal-path reasoning.
AI.conclusion: MGSD 通过感知-推理模态差距感知的两阶段自蒸馏，显著提升了纯视觉输入下的空间规划能力，并缩小了与符号输入上界之间的差距。 / MGSD significantly improves spatial planning under purely visual input through a two-stage modality-gap-aware self-distillation framework, narrowing the gap to symbolic-input upper bounds.

title: HyperVis: Continuous Latent Visual Relational Graphs on the Lorentz Hyperboloid for Compositional Reasoning
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) struggle with compositional reasoning that requires understanding inter-object relationships. A natural remedy is to inject explicit scene graph triplets $\langle s, p, o \rangle$ from an off-the-shelf scene graph generator (SGG), but we show this backfires: discrete text labels collide with the continuous visual modality, degrading GQA accuracy from 60.38\% to 58.86\%. We propose \textbf{HyperVis}, which bypasses the SGG semantic bottleneck entirely. From $N$ class-agnostic region proposals, we compute a dense $O(N^2)$ visual relation tensor via spatially-biased cross-attention, project it onto a Lorentz hyperboloid, and enforce hierarchy through spatial physics, namely IoA-driven entailment cones and exterior-angle repulsion. We discover that HyperVis contributes in two complementary ways: (1) as a \emph{training-time regularizer}, the hyperbolic relational losses shape LoRA representations that improve generative VQA (GQA 61.03\% vs.\ 57.21\% for LoRA fine-tuning without relational losses, recovering and surpassing the baseline); and (2) as an \emph{inference-time relational encoder}, hyperbolic prefix tokens boost discriminative compositional scoring (SugarCrepe 79.94\%, $+$6.25pp over baseline). The learned curvature stabilises at $κ{=}4.0$, an order of magnitude above prior hyperbolic VLMs where $κ$ typically collapses toward zero, indicating that continuous visual features genuinely require the exponential volume of strongly curved space. A controlled Euclidean ablation confirms this decomposition: the relational pipeline regularises LoRA comparably in flat space (GQA 60.81\%), but the compositionality gain is specifically hyperbolic (SugarCrepe $+$4.58pp over Euclidean), with entailment loss ${\sim}6{\times}$ higher in Euclidean training. Codes are available at TBA.

AI.tldr: HyperVis replaces discrete scene-graph labels with continuous hyperbolic visual relations, improving VLM compositional reasoning in both training and inference; the hyperbolic geometry is the key factor behind the compositionality gains.
AI.motivation: Vision-Language Models struggle with compositional reasoning, especially when they must understand relations between objects. Although adding scene graph triplets from off-the-shelf scene graph generators seems like a natural solution, the paper shows that discrete symbolic labels conflict with continuous visual representations and can hurt performance. This motivates a fully continuous relational representation that preserves hierarchy and compositional structure.
AI.method: The paper starts from class-agnostic region proposals and computes a dense O(N^2) visual relation tensor using spatially-biased cross-attention. It then projects relational features onto a Lorentz hyperboloid and imposes hierarchical structure with IoA-based entailment cones and exterior-angle repulsion. HyperVis is used in two modes: as a training-time regularizer for LoRA fine-tuning via hyperbolic relational losses, and as an inference-time relational encoder via hyperbolic prefix tokens for compositional scoring.
AI.result: Injecting scene graph text labels reduces GQA accuracy from 60.38% to 58.86%. HyperVis improves GQA to 61.03% compared with 57.21% for LoRA fine-tuning without relational losses, and improves SugarCrepe to 79.94%, a +6.25 percentage point gain over baseline. The learned curvature stabilizes at kappa=4.0, much higher than prior hyperbolic VLMs, suggesting strong curvature is useful for continuous visual relations. A Euclidean ablation shows similar regularization on GQA (60.81%) but weaker compositional gains, with SugarCrepe 4.58 points below the hyperbolic version and much higher entailment loss during training.
AI.conclusion: HyperVis avoids the semantic bottleneck of discrete scene graph labels by modeling inter-object relations directly in continuous visual space and representing them in hyperbolic geometry. It improves both training-time representation learning and inference-time compositional reasoning, and the main compositional gains are specifically due to the hyperbolic space rather than the relational pipeline alone.

title: Automatic Labelling of Speech Translation Errors
summary: Errors in speech translations reduce trustworthiness of Speech Translation (ST) systems and can have serious consequences. Yet currently there is no established methodology for evaluating confidence and quality estimation of speech translations. To initiate progress in this direction, we propose Speech Translation Error Labelling (STEL). We create an annotation protocol, a small authentic end-to-end evaluation dataset, and we analyse how existing text-only and speech-processing systems perform the STEL task. Our results show that text-only XCOMET and multimodal LLM Qwen2.5-Omni are able to perform the STEL task in roughly half the precision of humans. We also find that direct speech processing is necessary for the STEL task, and that the current text-only and speech-processing systems are complementary in labelling translation-only vs. speech-processing errors in ST.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces STEL, a new benchmark for labeling speech translation errors, and shows that current models are much worse than humans but that combining text-only and speech-based approaches may help.
AI.motivation: Errors in speech translation can undermine trust and lead to serious consequences, but there is no established methodology for evaluating confidence and quality estimation in speech translation. The work aims to address this gap.
AI.method: The paper proposes STEL, including an annotation protocol and a small authentic end-to-end evaluation dataset. It then evaluates existing text-only and speech-processing systems, including XCOMET and Qwen2.5-Omni, on the STEL task and compares their performance with humans.
AI.result: Text-only XCOMET and multimodal LLM Qwen2.5-Omni can perform STEL at roughly half the precision of humans. The study also finds that direct speech processing is necessary for the task, and that text-only and speech-processing systems are complementary for identifying translation-only versus speech-processing errors.
AI.conclusion: Speech Translation Error Labelling (STEL) is a useful new benchmark and annotation framework for evaluating confidence and quality estimation in speech translation, and current systems remain far below human performance. Direct speech processing is necessary, while text-only and speech-based systems offer complementary strengths.

title: Steering Vectors are an Adversarial Attack Surface
summary: Activation steering has become a popular way to control Large Language Model (LLM) behavior without fine-tuning. Since the technique is plug-and-play, users share datasets and precomputed vectors to steer model activations. However, we show that a \emph{stealth data poisoning attack} silently compromises this pipeline. By substituting $4{-}6\%$ of tokens in the steering dataset, an attacker can silently align the resulting vector with an anti-refusal direction. This jailbreaks the target model while preserving the intended steering effect on benign prompts. Under this threat model, a malicious actor can distribute an apparently safe bundle containing texts, vectors, and weights, alongside an equivalence certificate that the end-user can verify. We test the attack on two open-weight model families and eight model-attribute combinations, observing that poisoned vectors reach an absolute attack success rate (ASR) of $20{-}55\%$, $+19\%$ to $+51\%$ over a clean reference. Finally, we find that a refusal-direction orthogonalization defense can recover ${\approx}82\%$ of the ASR gap without harming benign behavior.

AI.tldr: A small, hard-to-detect poisoning of activation-steering data can turn a seemingly safe steering vector into a jailbreak vector; the attack works broadly, and orthogonalizing away the refusal direction is an effective mitigation.
AI.motivation: Activation steering is widely used as a plug-and-play control method for LLMs, with users often sharing datasets, vectors, and weights. This creates a supply-chain-like risk: if the steering data or artifacts are poisoned, end users may unknowingly deploy jailbreak-capable vectors. The paper aims to expose this overlooked security vulnerability.
AI.method: The paper introduces a stealth data poisoning attack on the activation-steering pipeline by modifying only 4-6% of tokens in the steering dataset so that the derived steering vector becomes aligned with an anti-refusal direction. It evaluates the attack across two open-weight model families and eight model-attribute settings, and studies a defense based on orthogonalizing against the refusal direction.
AI.result: Poisoned steering vectors achieve 20-55% absolute attack success rate, improving ASR by 19-51 percentage points over clean vectors, while still maintaining the intended steering behavior on benign prompts. A refusal-direction orthogonalization defense recovers about 82% of the ASR gap without degrading benign performance.
AI.conclusion: Steering vectors for LLM activation steering are vulnerable to stealthy data poisoning: tiny token-level changes can implant a jailbreak-oriented anti-refusal component while preserving apparent benign utility, and refusal-direction orthogonalization substantially mitigates the attack.

title: A Framework for Measuring Appropriate Reliance on Set-Valued AI Advice
summary: Appropriate reliance on AI advice has become a central research theme in human-AI collaboration. Existing frameworks have focused exclusively on point predictions as AI advice. However, set-valued AI advice (e.g., discrete sets or continuous intervals) is increasingly being used to communicate uncertainty and improve human decision making. In this paper, we develop the first formal framework for measuring appropriate reliance on set-valued AI advice within the sequential judge-advisor paradigm, spanning both classification and regression tasks. For classification, we first introduce the dimensions that are necessary for evaluating set-valued AI advice. We then define two metrics: correct reliance rate on AI and correct reliance rate on self, which jointly characterize appropriate reliance in this setting. For regression, we introduce quantity of AI reliance and quality of AI reliance, which respectively measure whether a decision maker utilized the AI advice and whether their reliance helped them get closer to the ground truth relative to their initial estimate. Through the application of our framework, we demonstrate how these metrics capture important nuances in human-AI collaboration that existing measures overlook.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the first formal framework for measuring whether people appropriately rely on set-valued AI advice, with new metrics for classification and regression that better capture useful human-AI collaboration than prior point-prediction-based measures.
AI.motivation: Prior work on appropriate reliance has focused only on point-valued AI advice, while real systems increasingly provide set-valued advice such as label sets or prediction intervals to communicate uncertainty. Existing metrics therefore cannot adequately assess how humans should rely on this richer form of AI assistance.
AI.method: The authors develop a formal evaluation framework for sequential judge-advisor settings where AI provides set-valued advice. For classification, they identify essential evaluation dimensions and define two metrics: correct reliance rate on AI and correct reliance rate on self. For regression, they define quantity of AI reliance and quality of AI reliance to measure whether users used the advice and whether doing so improved accuracy relative to their initial estimate.
AI.result: The framework successfully applies to both classification and regression tasks and shows that the new metrics capture important nuances of human-AI reliance behavior that earlier measures overlook.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that appropriate reliance on set-valued AI advice requires new evaluation metrics beyond those designed for point predictions. The proposed framework and metrics reveal nuanced patterns of human-AI collaboration in both classification and regression settings that existing measures fail to capture.

title: MS-DKC: A Dataset Knowledge Card Framework for Designing and Adapting Medical Image Segmentation Models
summary:
Medical image segmentation is often framed as a search for stronger architectures, but this can obscure a more fundamental question: what does the dataset require from the model? In medical imaging, this requirement is shaped by foreground occupancy, morphology, boundary ambiguity, topology sensitivity, annotation quality, acquisition variation, and operating point.
  This paper introduces the Medical Segmentation Dataset Knowledge Card (MS-DKC), a framework for making these factors explicit. MS-DKC records dataset evidence through image/acquisition, morphology, supervision, context-dependence, and deployment-risk descriptors. These descriptors are mapped to failure modes, design priors, and risk-aligned criteria, making segmentation design more traceable than architecture-first comparison.
  We evaluate MS-DKC on DRIVE, ISIC2018, and ACDC, representing distinct regimes. DRIVE contains sparse, thin, branching vessels, favoring detail-preserving models, sensitivity-aware optimization, threshold analysis, and topology-aware metrics. DKC-TNet-v2 achieved Dice 0.8044 and IoU 0.6730 with 35103 parameters, while SA-UNetv2-DKC-AmbRef reached Dice 0.8141, IoU 0.6865, sensitivity 0.8265, specificity 0.9804, and AUC 0.9853. ISIC2018 involves compact but appearance-variable lesions; validation-constrained score-function selection on Att-Next-Topo/ATTNext produced MS-DKC-AttNextTopo-VCSF-NoAug with Dice 0.8872, IoU 0.8214, precision 0.9173, Boundary F1 0.4878, and ASSD 4.13, while plausible additions failed to improve the risk-aligned profile. ACDC provides a multi-class cardiac case, where MS-DKC recommends four-class softmax segmentation, class-balanced Dice/CE supervision, and class-wise surface evaluation. Overall, the results support dataset-conditioned design: different datasets require different priors, operating points, and evidence before a model can be judged appropriate.

AI.tldr: Instead of asking which segmentation architecture is strongest overall, this paper asks what each medical dataset requires and formalizes the answer with MS-DKC, a dataset knowledge framework that guides model design and evaluation for different segmentation regimes.
AI.motivation: Architecture-first comparison in medical image segmentation can miss the more fundamental issue of what a specific dataset demands from a model, given factors such as sparsity, topology, annotation quality, acquisition variation, and operating constraints.
AI.method: The paper proposes the Medical Segmentation Dataset Knowledge Card (MS-DKC), which encodes dataset evidence using descriptors for image/acquisition, morphology, supervision, context dependence, and deployment risk, and maps them to failure modes, design priors, and risk-aligned evaluation criteria.
AI.result: On DRIVE, MS-DKC-guided models achieved strong vessel segmentation with both compact and higher-performing variants; on ISIC2018, validation-constrained score-function selection yielded the best risk-aligned lesion segmentation profile while seemingly reasonable additions did not help; on ACDC, MS-DKC recommended a four-class softmax setup with class-balanced Dice/CE and class-wise surface evaluation.
AI.conclusion: MS-DKC makes dataset requirements explicit and supports dataset-conditioned medical image segmentation design; results across DRIVE, ISIC2018, and ACDC suggest different datasets need different priors, operating points, and evaluation criteria before a model is considered appropriate.

title: Multi-task Learning is Not Enough: Representational Entanglement in Dual-output Second Language Speech Recognition
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, Accepted to the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning Workshop on Machine Learning for Audio
summary: Second-language (L2) speech recognition often requires transcriptions of pronunciations and intended meanings. Multi-task learning (MTL) is a natural approach because it assumes that shared representations benefit both outputs. However, this paper shows that this assumption does not hold across Korean and English. MTL improves meaning but degrades surface transcription, especially in English, where the degradation scales with surface-meaning divergence measured by Levenshtein edit distance.Encoder analysis links these patterns to encoder-level entanglement, with Korean preserving distinct task representations while English produces nearly identical ones. Cross-task decoder analysis shows that the meaning dual-output decoder adapts with a unique representation, while the surface dual-output decoder remains constrained by the encoder. These findings motivate the design of MTL frameworks that mitigate encoder-level entanglement to reduce surface degradation in dual-output L2 automatic speech recognition.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that in L2 ASR, sharing one model for pronunciation transcription and intended meaning is not always helpful: it helps meaning, but often hurts surface transcription, especially in English. The main reason is encoder representation entanglement, so better MTL architectures should separate task representations more effectively.
AI.motivation: Dual-output L2 speech recognition needs both pronunciation-based surface transcriptions and intended meanings. Multi-task learning is a natural choice because shared representations are usually expected to help both tasks, but it is unclear whether that assumption holds across languages and output types.
AI.method: The paper studies dual-output L2 automatic speech recognition for Korean and English using multi-task learning, comparing surface transcription and intended-meaning outputs. It analyzes performance patterns with respect to surface-meaning divergence measured by Levenshtein edit distance, and probes internal model behavior through encoder analysis and cross-task decoder analysis.
AI.result: MTL improves meaning recognition but degrades surface transcription, with the effect being particularly strong in English. In English, the degradation increases as the divergence between surface and meaning grows. Encoder analysis shows Korean maintains more distinct task representations, while English collapses them into nearly identical ones. Decoder analysis further shows the meaning-side dual-output decoder can adapt with a unique representation, whereas the surface-side decoder remains limited by the encoder.
AI.conclusion: Multi-task learning is not uniformly beneficial for dual-output L2 speech recognition. It improves intended-meaning prediction but can harm surface-form transcription, and this harm is tied to encoder-level representation entanglement, especially in English. Future MTL designs should explicitly reduce encoder entanglement to protect surface transcription quality.

title: LLM Explainability with Counterfactual Chains and Causal Graphs
summary: Causal graphs provide a high-level language for making mechanisms transparent. Recent work uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to recover causal graphs of external-world processes. Instead, in this paper, we use causal graphs to model LLM inference itself, providing stakeholders with a transparent view of how the model perceives and organizes high-level concepts to produce a prediction. We propose a four-phase method for constructing such graphs. Given a target LLM and a set of textual examples, our method discovers class-discriminative, human-interpretable concepts and maps each input to LLM-perceived concept states. We then introduce an MCMC-inspired counterfactual augmentation procedure that expands the sparse observational data through chains of counterfactuals. This enables stable causal discovery with $σ$-CG, yielding informative, interpretable graphs. We apply our method to three LLMs across disease diagnosis, sentiment analysis, and LLM-as-a-judge classification tasks. We evaluate the learned graphs for predictive fidelity and structural stability, and the MCMC-inspired augmentation for convergence and downstream utility. Our results show that the discovered causal graphs capture meaningful dependencies consistent with LLMs' reasoning. Together, this paper provides a foundation for concept-level explainability of LLMs.

AI.tldr: This paper builds concept-level causal graphs of how LLMs reason, using interpretable concepts plus MCMC-style counterfactual data augmentation, and shows the graphs are stable, predictive, and useful for explaining model behavior.
AI.motivation: Prior work uses LLMs to recover causal graphs about external processes, but this paper instead wants to use causal graphs to explain the LLM's own inference process, making high-level concept organization and prediction mechanisms more transparent to stakeholders.
AI.method: The method has four phases: discover class-discriminative and human-interpretable concepts from text examples for a target LLM; map each input into LLM-perceived concept states; expand sparse observations using an MCMC-inspired chain of counterfactual augmentations; and run stable causal discovery with sigma-CG to construct interpretable causal graphs.
AI.result: Across three LLMs and tasks including disease diagnosis, sentiment analysis, and LLM-as-a-judge classification, the learned causal graphs achieved predictive fidelity and structural stability, while the counterfactual augmentation improved convergence and downstream utility. The resulting graphs reflected meaningful dependencies consistent with LLM reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that causal graphs can be used to model the internal inference behavior of LLMs at the concept level, producing interpretable and structurally stable explanations that align with meaningful parts of the model's reasoning.

title: Beyond Semantic Organization: Memory as Execution State Management for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: LLM-based agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks with interdependent decisions, where each action reshapes future constraints and intermediate errors can cascade. Existing RAG and agent memory systems organize histories by semantic similarity, retrieving content-relevant entries at decision time. We argue that this design mismatches execution-state dependencies: it fragments decision trajectories and mixes valid and erroneous traces, hindering coherent state reconstruction and error isolation. We propose MAGE (Memory as Agent-Guided Exploration), an active execution-state manager that stores interactions in a hierarchical state tree. The agent derives its state from the active root-to-current path, combining subgoal summaries, recent traces, and hints from prior branches. Four coupled operations maintain the tree: Grow records new traces, Compress summarizes completed subgoals, Maintain validates summaries, and Revise restores a target boundary and resumes on a new branch. This design bounds context growth while preserving state integrity and isolating flawed segments from the active path. Experiments on MemoryArena show that MAGE improves the average task success rate by 7.8--20.4 pp over baselines, while reducing token consumption by 55.1%.

AI.tldr: MAGE用状态树而不是语义相似检索来管理agent记忆，在长程决策任务中更连贯地恢复执行状态、隔离错误，并以更少token获得更高成功率。
AI.motivation: 现有基于RAG或语义相似度的agent记忆系统按内容相关性检索历史，但长时程任务更依赖执行状态之间的连续约束关系；这种错配会打碎决策轨迹、混合正确与错误痕迹，导致状态重建困难和错误隔离不足。
AI.method: 提出MAGE（Memory as Agent-Guided Exploration），将交互过程存储为层次化状态树；代理从当前根到活动节点的路径恢复状态，并通过Grow、Compress、Maintain、Revise四个操作分别记录轨迹、压缩子目标、校验摘要、恢复边界并分支继续执行。
AI.result: 在MemoryArena上的实验显示，MAGE相比基线将平均任务成功率提升了7.8到20.4个百分点，同时将token消耗降低55.1%。
AI.conclusion: MAGE通过层次化状态树管理执行状态，能够在长时程任务中更好地保持状态一致性、隔离错误轨迹，并以更低token成本显著提升任务成功率。

title: Where, What, Why, and Importance: Structured Defect Grounding for Text-to-Image Feedback
summary: Despite generating increasingly photorealistic images, text-to-image (T2I) models still exhibit localized, subtle, and structurally complex failures. Diagnosing these failures requires instance-level feedback that answers where a defect occurs, what type it is, why it is defective, and its importance to overall image quality. While recent dense-feedback methods move beyond scalar supervision, their heatmap-centric representations still formulate diagnosis as pixel-field regression, making it difficult to localize variable-cardinality defects and bind semantic reasons to individual failures. To address this representation bottleneck, we propose Structured Defect Grounding (SDG), which casts T2I diagnosis as structured set prediction by modeling each defect as a (location, type, reason, importance) tuple. To make this formulation trainable and measurable, we introduce SDG-30K, a 30K-image dataset with box-grounded annotations across four modern T2I generators, together with a dedicated evaluation protocol, SDG-Eval. Building on this structured representation, we further present a diagnosis-to-alignment framework in which a Vision-Language Model (VLM) serves as the SDG detector, and BoxFlow-GRPO converts predicted defect sets into box-derived, importance-weighted spatial rewards for diffusion model alignment. Extensive experiments show that our SDG detector outperforms leading proprietary VLMs on structured defect grounding, while SDG-guided rewards consistently improve T2I alignment and support localized image refinement. These results establish SDG as a unified, instance-level interface for diagnosing, evaluating, and enhancing modern generative models.

AI.tldr: This paper turns T2I image failure diagnosis from heatmap prediction into structured defect detection with box-grounded semantic tuples, then uses those detected defects as spatial rewards to improve diffusion model alignment.
AI.motivation: Existing T2I models still produce subtle, localized, and structurally complex defects. Prior dense-feedback approaches rely on heatmap regression, which struggles to represent a variable number of defects and to associate semantic explanations with each individual failure.
AI.method: The paper proposes Structured Defect Grounding (SDG), which formulates T2I failure diagnosis as structured set prediction over defect tuples: (location, type, reason, importance). It introduces the SDG-30K dataset with box-level annotations and the SDG-Eval protocol. A VLM is used as the SDG detector, and BoxFlow-GRPO converts predicted defect sets into box-derived, importance-weighted spatial rewards to align diffusion models.
AI.result: Experiments show that the SDG detector surpasses strong proprietary VLM baselines on structured defect grounding. SDG-based rewards also consistently improve T2I model alignment and enable localized image refinement.
AI.conclusion: SDG provides a unified instance-level framework for diagnosing, evaluating, and improving text-to-image models by representing defects as structured tuples and using them for both assessment and alignment.

title: SkillComposer: Learning to Evolve Agent Skills for Specification and Generalization
summary: Agent skills, which consist of reusable strategies that guide agent reasoning and action, have shown strong potential for improving model capability at inference time. However, current skill construction methods treat the problem as one-shot extraction, overlooking a fundamental tension: a skill tailored to the specific task fails to transfer, while the abstracted skill often provides insufficient guidance. We attribute this fragility to the absence of explicit mechanisms for skill specification and generalization. To address this gap, we introduce SkillComposer, a framework that decomposes skill construction into three learnable operations: create, improve, and merge. Trained via systematic rejection sampling recipe, SkillComposer enables language models to self-evolve skills at inference time and supports three deployment modes: offline for building generalized libraries, online for task-specific refinement, and hybrid for combining both. Comprehensive experiments on $τ^2$-Bench, LiveCodeBench v6, and AppWorld show that SkillComposer consistently outperforms baselines. Our SkillComposer-4B improves a 27B executor by up to +4.5 on agent tasks and +3.4 on code tasks, while generalizing across domains and task types unseen during training. Analysis reveals that merge and improve address orthogonal quality dimensions and that skill composition is a transferable meta-ability, providing a practical recipe for skill-augmented inference.

AI.tldr: SkillComposer teaches models to build, refine, and combine reusable skills at inference time, overcoming the specificity-vs-generalization tradeoff and improving agent/code performance across benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing agent skill construction methods rely on one-shot extraction and fail to resolve the tradeoff between task-specific skills, which do not transfer well, and abstract skills, which are often too weak to guide behavior effectively. The paper aims to introduce explicit mechanisms for skill specification and generalization.
AI.method: The paper proposes SkillComposer, which decomposes skill construction into three learnable operations: create, improve, and merge. It is trained with a systematic rejection sampling recipe and can be deployed in offline, online, and hybrid modes for generalized libraries, task-specific refinement, or both.
AI.result: Across τ^2-Bench, LiveCodeBench v6, and AppWorld, SkillComposer consistently outperforms baselines. A 4B SkillComposer improves a 27B executor by up to +4.5 on agent tasks and +3.4 on code tasks, while also generalizing to unseen domains and task types.
AI.conclusion: SkillComposer provides a practical and transferable recipe for skill-augmented inference by explicitly modeling skill creation, refinement, and composition, leading to stronger and more generalizable agent performance than one-shot skill extraction.

title: Compress-Distill: Reasoning Trace Compression for Efficient Knowledge Distillation
summary: Reasoning models produce long chain-of-thought traces that are costly to distill and encourage verbose student outputs. We study post-hoc compression of such traces before knowledge distillation. Two teachers, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and gpt-oss-120B, generate about 283k correct traces each; two instruction-tuned models then compress them to 8.6-21.0% of their original character length. Across a 48-run main grid plus seven Qwen-teacher truncation ablations, compressed traces reduce training tokens to 12-30% of raw, speed up training by 2.0-7.6x, and shorten inference outputs by 3-19x with smaller reductions under the shorter gpt-oss teacher. However, raw traces retain the highest downstream accuracy at every scale and for both teachers. A length-matched raw-trace truncation ablation shows that compression is not merely benefiting from a smaller token budget: model-compressed traces usually beat or match naive truncation, especially for smaller students, while maintaining shorter inference outputs. Overall, reasoning-trace compression offers an accuracy-efficiency trade-off rather than a free improvement: students retain up to 96% of raw-trace accuracy while gaining up to 18x higher per-token efficiency, and at the 0.8B scale under LoRA compressed traces narrow the raw-vs-compressed gap but do not exceed raw.

AI.tldr:
TL;DR：把教师的长推理链先压缩再蒸馏，能大幅省token、提速训练并减少学生模型推理时的废话，但准确率通常仍略逊于直接用原始推理链。它提供的是明确的“效率-精度权衡”，而不是无代价增益。
TL;DR: Compressing teacher reasoning traces before distillation greatly reduces token cost, speeds up training, and makes student outputs much shorter, but it usually gives slightly worse accuracy than training on raw traces. It is an efficiency-accuracy trade-off, not a free win.
AI.motivation:
动机：长链式思维虽然常被用于蒸馏推理能力，但其代价高昂，会增加训练token开销，也会诱导学生模型在推理时生成冗长输出。作者希望验证：在蒸馏前对教师推理链进行压缩，能否在尽量保留性能的同时显著提升训练与推理效率。
Motivation: Long chain-of-thought traces are useful for distilling reasoning ability, but they are expensive to train on and encourage verbose student responses at inference. The paper asks whether compressing teacher traces before distillation can preserve most of the performance while substantially improving efficiency.
AI.method:
方法：作者使用两个大教师模型（Qwen3.5-397B-A17B 与 gpt-oss-120B）各生成约28.3万条正确推理链，再用两个指令微调模型将这些推理链压缩到原字符长度的8.6%到21.0%。随后在48组主实验和7组Qwen教师截断消融中，比较原始推理链、模型压缩推理链以及长度匹配的朴素截断推理链在不同学生规模和训练设置（包括LoRA）下的蒸馏效果、训练token、训练速度、推理输出长度与准确率。
Method: The authors collect about 283k correct reasoning traces from each of two teacher models, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and gpt-oss-120B, then use two instruction-tuned models to compress those traces to 8.6%-21.0% of the original character length. They compare raw traces, model-compressed traces, and length-matched naive truncation across a 48-run main grid plus seven Qwen-teacher truncation ablations, evaluating distillation quality, training tokens, training speed, inference length, and downstream accuracy across student scales and settings including LoRA.
AI.result:
结果：压缩后的推理链将训练token降至原始数据的12%-30%，训练加速2.0-7.6倍，推理输出缩短3-19倍；在较短的gpt-oss教师上，这种缩短效应更小。尽管如此，原始推理链在所有模型规模和两类教师上始终取得最高准确率。长度匹配截断消融表明，压缩收益并不只是来自更少token；模型压缩通常优于或不差于朴素截断，尤其对小模型更明显，并且仍能保持更短输出。在0.8B+LoRA条件下，压缩进一步缩小与原始推理链的精度差距，但仍未反超。
Result: Compressed traces cut training tokens to 12%-30% of the raw data, speed training up by 2.0-7.6x, and shorten inference outputs by 3-19x; the shortening effect is smaller under the shorter gpt-oss teacher. Even so, raw traces consistently achieve the best downstream accuracy across all student scales and both teachers. Length-matched truncation ablations show the gains are not merely due to fewer tokens: model-based compression usually beats or matches naive truncation, especially for smaller students, while still producing shorter outputs. Under the 0.8B LoRA setting, compression narrows but does not close the accuracy gap to raw traces.
AI.conclusion:
结论：对推理链进行事后压缩能显著降低训练与推理成本，并显著缩短学生模型输出，但它不是“免费提升”；在所有规模和两类教师下，原始推理链仍然带来最高下游准确率。压缩后的学生通常可保留最高约96%的原始准确率，同时获得最高约18倍的每token效率提升。
Conclusion: Post-hoc compression of reasoning traces substantially reduces training and inference cost and shortens student outputs, but it is not a free improvement; raw traces still deliver the best downstream accuracy across all student scales and both teachers. Compressed-trace students retain up to about 96% of raw-trace accuracy while achieving up to roughly 18x higher per-token efficiency.

title: Integrating Mechanistic and Data-Driven Models for Neurological Disorders through Differentiable Programming
summary: Advances in computational modeling, neuroimaging, and artificial intelligence are revolutionizing the modeling of neurological disorders for improved diagnostics, prognosis, and treatment planning. Mechanistic models provide valuable scientific insight into the disorders, but in practice they are often simplified with assumptions or computationally expensive and slow to solve. However, while purely data driven approaches provide speed and scalability, they require large, high quality data to train and generally suffer from interpretability and generalization issues. This perspective paper presents a structured overview of hybrid modeling strategies, which combine deep learning models with physics based solvers, and are categorized into parallel, series, and parallel-series architectures.
