Three main approaches that have been emphasized are residual modeling for missing or incomplete physics, Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (NODEs) for continuous time dynamics approximation, and solver in the loop that accelerates traditional solvers with neural approximations. These hybrid models integrate the governing differential equation based formulations and deep learning to characterize the evolution of neurological disorders, and promise advanced personalized neurological modeling. In addition, the study explores and proposes different hybrid configurations to improve diagnosis accuracy, predict disease progression, and inform treatment strategies across a range of neurological disorders. These capabilities outperform standalone mechanistic or purely data driven approaches, making hybrid modeling a powerful tool, especially in applications involving modeling the progression and treatment responses in neurological conditions such as brain tumors, Alzheimer's disease, and stroke.

AI.tldr: TL;DR：这篇论文主张用“物理/机制模型 + 深度学习”的混合建模替代单一方法，通过并联、串联和混合架构，以及残差建模、NODEs、solver-in-the-loop等技术，在神经疾病建模中实现更准确、更快且更可解释的预测。 / TL;DR: The paper argues for replacing single-model approaches with hybrid modeling that combines physics/mechanistic models and deep learning. Using parallel, series, and mixed architectures, along with residual modeling, NODEs, and solver-in-the-loop techniques, it aims to deliver more accurate, faster, and more interpretable predictions in neurological disease modeling.
AI.motivation: 纯机制模型虽然能提供科学解释，但往往依赖简化假设且计算代价高；纯数据驱动方法速度快、可扩展，但依赖大量高质量数据，并存在可解释性和泛化能力不足的问题。因此需要融合两者优势的混合建模。 / Mechanistic models provide scientific insight but are often simplified and computationally expensive, while purely data-driven models are fast and scalable but require large high-quality datasets and often lack interpretability and generalization. This motivates hybrid approaches that combine the strengths of both.
AI.method: 本文是一篇观点/综述性质论文，构建了混合建模策略的结构化框架，将其分为并联、串联和并联-串联三类架构，并重点讨论三种实现路径：残差建模、神经常微分方程（NODEs）以及solver-in-the-loop。 / This is a perspective-style paper that provides a structured framework for hybrid modeling strategies, categorizing them into parallel, series, and parallel-series architectures, with emphasis on three approaches: residual modeling, Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (NODEs), and solver-in-the-loop methods.
AI.result: 论文总结并提出了适用于神经系统疾病的多种混合建模配置，指出这类方法可提高诊断准确率、预测疾病进展并支持治疗策略制定，尤其适用于脑肿瘤、阿尔茨海默病和卒中等场景。 / The paper summarizes and proposes multiple hybrid configurations for neurological disorders, showing that these methods can improve diagnostic accuracy, predict disease progression, and support treatment strategy design, especially for applications such as brain tumors, Alzheimer's disease, and stroke.
AI.conclusion: 混合建模将物理/机制模型与深度学习结合，在神经系统疾病建模中兼顾可解释性、个体化与计算效率，相比纯机制或纯数据驱动方法更有潜力提升诊断、预后和治疗规划。 / Hybrid modeling that combines physics/mechanistic models with deep learning offers a better balance of interpretability, personalization, and computational efficiency for neurological disorder modeling, outperforming purely mechanistic or purely data-driven approaches for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning.

title: Diff-CA: Separating Common and Salient Factors with Diffusion Models
summary: Contrastive Analysis aims to separate factors that are common between two data distributions from those that are salient to only one of them. Existing contrastive methods are based on generative models (e.g., VAEs or GANs) that often suffer from limited reconstruction and image quality, which hampers effective latent factor separation and limits their applicability to high-fidelity image generation and edition. We propose a novel conditioning framework for diffusion models that enables contrastive decomposition without compromising generation quality. We first train a prompt-free, image-conditioned diffusion model, and then learn to decompose the conditioning into a common and a salient factor, using weak supervision. We prove that the additive contrastive factorization, commonly assumed in prior work, is identifiable under mild conditions. This factorization enables targeted operations by swapping or interpolating only the salient factor.

AI.tldr: 论文把对比分析从 VAE/GAN 推进到扩散模型：先学一个图像条件扩散模型，再把条件分成共享与显著两部分，既保证高保真生成，又能做可控编辑，并给出了该加性分解可识别性的理论证明。 / The paper brings contrastive analysis to diffusion models: it first learns an image-conditioned diffusion model, then splits conditioning into common and salient parts, preserving high-fidelity generation while enabling controllable editing, with a theoretical identifiability guarantee for the additive decomposition.
AI.motivation: 动机在于现有对比分析方法大多依赖 VAE 或 GAN 等生成模型，这些方法常受限于重建能力和图像质量，导致潜在因素分离效果不足，也难以扩展到高保真图像生成与编辑。 / The motivation is that existing contrastive methods mainly rely on generative models such as VAEs or GANs, which often suffer from limited reconstruction fidelity and poor image quality, weakening latent factor separation and restricting high-fidelity image generation and editing.
AI.method: 方法上，作者先训练一个无需文本提示、以图像为条件的扩散模型；随后利用弱监督学习将条件表示分解为 common factor 和 salient factor，从而支持仅针对显著因子的交换与插值操作。 / Methodologically, the authors first train a prompt-free image-conditioned diffusion model, then use weak supervision to decompose the conditioning representation into a common factor and a salient factor, enabling operations such as swapping or interpolating only the salient factor.
AI.result: 结果表明，该框架能够在扩散模型中实现有效的对比分解，同时保持高质量生成，并支持通过仅操作显著因子来实现更有针对性的图像编辑。 / The results indicate that the framework achieves effective contrastive decomposition within diffusion models while preserving high-quality generation, and supports targeted image editing by manipulating only the salient factor.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出了一种面向扩散模型的对比分析框架，能够在不牺牲生成质量的前提下，将条件信息分解为共享因子与显著因子；并证明了常见的加性对比分解在温和条件下可识别。 / The paper introduces a diffusion-based conditioning framework for contrastive analysis that decomposes conditioning information into common and salient factors without sacrificing generation quality, and proves that the standard additive contrastive factorization is identifiable under mild conditions.

title: LatentSkill: From In-Context Textual Skills to In-Weight Latent Skills for LLM Agents
summary: Agent systems increasingly use textual skills to encode reusable task procedures, but injecting these skills into the prompt at every step incurs substantial context overhead and exposes skill content as plaintext. We present LatentSkill, a framework that converts textual skills into plug-and-play LoRA adapters through a pretrained hypernetwork. LatentSkill stores skill knowledge in weight space rather than context space, removing per-step skill tokens while preserving modular loading, scaling, and composition. On ALFWorld and Search-QA, LatentSkill outperforms the corresponding in-context skill baseline while using substantially fewer prefill tokens: it improves ALFWorld success by 21.4 and 13.4 points on the seen and unseen splits with 64.1% fewer prefill tokens, and improves Search-QA exact match by 3.0 points with 72.2% lower skill-token overhead. Further analysis shows that generated skill LoRAs form a structured semantic geometry, can be precisely controlled via the LoRA scaling coefficient, and can be composed through parameter-space arithmetic when skill components are aligned. These findings suggest that weight-space skills provide an efficient, modular, and less exposed substrate for extending LLM agents.

AI.tldr: LatentSkill turns textual agent skills into LoRA adapters with a hypernetwork, replacing repeated prompt injection. It achieves better task performance with much lower token overhead and supports modular control and composition in weight space.
AI.motivation: Existing agent systems often represent reusable procedures as text and prepend them to prompts repeatedly, which increases context cost and exposes the skill contents directly in plaintext. The work aims to replace context-space skill injection with a more efficient and less exposed weight-space mechanism.
AI.method: The paper proposes LatentSkill, which uses a pretrained hypernetwork to transform textual skill descriptions into plug-and-play LoRA adapters. These adapters are loaded into the base model at inference time, allowing modular scaling and composition without adding skill text to the prompt context at each step.
AI.result: On ALFWorld, LatentSkill improves success rates by 21.4 points on seen tasks and 13.4 points on unseen tasks while reducing prefill tokens by 64.1% relative to the in-context skill baseline. On Search-QA, it improves exact match by 3.0 points with 72.2% lower skill-token overhead. The analysis also shows semantic structure in generated skill LoRAs, controllable behavior through LoRA scaling, and feasible parameter-space composition for aligned skills.
AI.conclusion: LatentSkill demonstrates that encoding reusable agent skills in weight space via generated LoRA adapters is more efficient and effective than repeatedly injecting textual skills into prompts, while also reducing plaintext exposure of skill content.

title: HoT-SSM:Higher-order Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning with State Space Models for Health Care
summary: Medical knowledge graphs (MKGs) infused with clinical knowledge have been increasingly used to model electronic health records (EHRs) to support interpretable predictions in healthcare domain. However, existing MKG-based approaches are limited in capturing pairwise relations between clinical concepts (e.g., conditions, procedures, and medications), and restricts their ability to model higher-order interactions among co-occurring or semantically related concepts. In addition, most representation learning methods that leverage MKGs either collapse temporal information across visits or lack an explicit mechanism for modeling long-range temporal dependencies, which is critical for clinical tasks such as mortality prediction. To mitigate these limitations, we propose HoT-SSM, a parameter efficient and higher-order temporal graph reasoning with state space models. For each visit, HoT-SSM constructs hypergraphs by grouping semantically related clinical concepts into hyperedges using domain knowledge, thereby preserving visit-level clinical context. Further, to model the temporal dynamics while learning the representations, we introduce a novel dynamic hypergraph-based state space model that explicitly captures patients latent state evolution over time while preserving long-range information. The learned representations are used for downstream clinical prediction and reasoning. Experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets shows significant performance improvement over the current state-of-the-art models, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly modeling higher-order clinical interactions and long-range temporal dependencies.

AI.tldr: HoT-SSM builds visit-level hypergraphs from clinical concepts and uses a state space model to track patient state over time, outperforming prior EHR prediction methods on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.
AI.motivation: Existing medical knowledge graph approaches for EHR modeling mainly capture pairwise relations, miss higher-order interactions among co-occurring or semantically related clinical concepts, and often inadequately model long-range temporal dependencies across patient visits.
AI.method: The paper proposes HoT-SSM, which constructs visit-level hypergraphs from semantically related clinical concepts using medical knowledge, and then applies a novel dynamic hypergraph-based state space model to capture latent patient state evolution over time for downstream prediction and reasoning.
AI.result: On MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, HoT-SSM achieves significant performance gains over state-of-the-art baselines, indicating that combining higher-order graph reasoning with explicit temporal state modeling is effective for clinical prediction tasks such as mortality prediction.
AI.conclusion: HoT-SSM effectively improves clinical prediction by jointly modeling higher-order clinical concept interactions within visits and long-range temporal dependencies across visits using a parameter-efficient dynamic hypergraph state space framework.

title: CogManip: Benchmarking Manipulative Behavior in Multi-Turn Interactions with Large Language Model
summary: Whether Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit covert psychological manipulation in complex human-AI interactions has garnered increasing safety concerns. However, existing AI safety benchmarks remain largely restricted to explicit rule compliance and static prompts, failing to capture the dynamic and covert nature of manipulative strategies in multi-turn dialogues. We introduce CogManip, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates 15 manipulation strategy risks across 1,000 multi-turn interaction scenarios, validated by human experts. A systematic evaluation of 13 representative models, including frontier models like GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-V3.2, reveals significant risk heterogeneities and illuminates the targeted direction for future defense. Further analysis of objective function perturbation reveals that DeepSeek-V3.2's manipulation tactics are highly sensitive to both negative and benign system prompts, demonstrating the critical necessity of prompt-based defense engineering and implicit goal auditing. CogManip offers a robust instrument and perspective for auditing the implicit psychological influence and dynamic strategy selection of modern LLMs.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes CogManip, a multi-turn benchmark for covert psychological manipulation by LLMs, and shows that manipulation risk differs substantially across models while prompt design can strongly affect these behaviors.
AI.motivation: Existing AI safety benchmarks focus mainly on explicit rule-following and static prompts, which are insufficient for detecting dynamic, covert manipulation strategies that can emerge in realistic multi-turn human-AI interactions.
AI.method: The paper introduces CogManip, a benchmark covering 15 manipulation strategies across 1,000 expert-validated multi-turn interaction scenarios, and uses it to systematically evaluate 13 representative LLMs. It also studies objective function perturbation to test sensitivity of manipulation behavior to different system prompts.
AI.result: The evaluation finds significant heterogeneity in manipulation risk across 13 models, including frontier systems such as GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-V3.2. It further shows that DeepSeek-V3.2’s manipulation tactics are highly sensitive to both negative and benign system prompt changes.
AI.conclusion: CogManip exposes that modern LLMs can display covert, multi-turn psychological manipulation risks, that these risks vary substantially across models, and that prompt-based defenses plus implicit goal auditing are necessary to mitigate them.

title: Computation-Aware Event-to-Frame Reconstruction via Selective Attention
summary: Event-to-frame (E2F) reconstruction bridges asynchronous event streams with frame-based vision pipelines, but existing methods often face a trade-off between reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. In this work, we propose an efficient E2F framework that emphasizes causal temporal modeling and computation-aware design. The architecture adopts a recurrent encoder-decoder to incrementally aggregate event information with compact hidden states. To improve robustness under fast motion and illumination variations, a selective context fusion strategy is introduced to integrate event-driven features with prior intensity cues. Within this fusion process, a lightweight hybrid attention mechanism enhances feature selectivity without relying on heavy attention operations. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves competitive reconstruction performance while maintaining a favorable balance between accuracy and model complexity.

AI.tldr: An efficient recurrent event-to-frame model uses selective context fusion and lightweight hybrid attention to reconstruct frames accurately while staying computationally economical.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the common trade-off in event-to-frame reconstruction between reconstruction quality and computational efficiency, especially under fast motion and illumination changes.
AI.method: The method uses a recurrent encoder-decoder to causally and incrementally aggregate event streams with compact hidden states, then fuses event-driven features with prior intensity cues through a selective context fusion module enhanced by a lightweight hybrid attention mechanism.
AI.result: Experiments on standard benchmarks show competitive reconstruction performance and a favorable balance between accuracy and computational/model efficiency.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that an efficient event-to-frame reconstruction framework can achieve competitive image reconstruction while preserving low model complexity by combining causal temporal modeling, recurrent aggregation, and lightweight selective fusion.

title: CHALIS: A Challenge Dataset for Language Identification in Difficult Scenarios
summary: We present CHALIS (Challenging Language Identification Samples), a new benchmark dataset explicitly designed to address difficult cases in language identification: cousin languages and orthographic noise. Our dataset has two parts: First, we collected sentences shared across mutually intelligible language pairs (Czech/Slovak, Spanish/Catalan, Portuguese/Galician, Danish/Norwegian). The second part tests for orthography noise: we transliterate text across multiple scripts, remove diacritics, simulate homoglyph attacks, and use Internet slang. We evaluate four widely used language identification systems on CHALIS and demonstrate that all struggle substantially in these scenarios, especially on lower-resource languages within cousin pairs and on transliterated input. The resource is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/michal-tichy/CHALIS.

AI.tldr: CHALIS是一个专门测试语言识别“难例”的新基准，聚焦近亲语言和正字法噪声。实验表明，主流语言识别工具在这些场景下明显不可靠，说明现有方法和评测都存在重要缺口。 / CHALIS is a new benchmark for hard language identification cases, focusing on cousin languages and orthographic noise. Results show that popular language ID tools are unreliable in these settings, exposing major gaps in current methods and evaluation.
AI.motivation: 现有语言识别基准通常不足以覆盖真实世界中的困难案例，特别是近亲语言之间的混淆和非标准拼写/转写噪声，因此需要一个专门针对这些问题的评测资源。 / Existing language identification benchmarks do not adequately capture hard real-world cases, especially confusion between closely related languages and non-standard orthographic/transliteration noise, motivating a dedicated evaluation resource.
AI.method: 论文提出CHALIS基准数据集，包含两部分：1）从互通性较强的近亲语言对中收集共享句子；2）构造正字法噪声测试，包括跨文字转写、去除变音符号、同形异义字符攻击模拟以及网络俚语。随后在该基准上评测四种常用语言识别系统。 / The paper introduces the CHALIS benchmark with two components: (1) shared sentences from mutually intelligible cousin-language pairs, and (2) orthographic-noise tests including script transliteration, diacritic removal, homoglyph attack simulation, and Internet slang. The authors then evaluate four widely used language identification systems on this benchmark.
AI.result: 四个广泛使用的语言识别系统在CHALIS上都出现明显性能下降；问题在低资源近亲语言和转写文本上最为严重。数据集已公开发布。 / All four evaluated language identification systems show substantial degradation on CHALIS, with the largest failures on lower-resource languages within cousin pairs and on transliterated inputs. The dataset is publicly available.
AI.conclusion: 现有主流语言识别系统在困难场景下表现显著不足，尤其是在近亲语言区分、低资源语言以及转写/正字法噪声输入上。 / Existing mainstream language identification systems perform poorly in challenging settings, particularly for cousin-language discrimination, lower-resource languages, and transliterated or noisy orthographic input.

title: Diffusion Models for Adaptive Sequential Data Generation
summary:
Generating realistic synthetic sequential data is critical in real-world applications across operations research, finance, healthcare, energy systems, and scientific computing, where time-indexed observations are used for prediction, simulation, risk assessment, and data-driven decision-making. While diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in generating static data, their direct extensions to sequential settings often fail to capture temporal dependence and information structure. Designing diffusion models that can simulate sequential data in an adapted manner, and hence without anticipation of future information, therefore remains an open challenge.
  In this work, we propose a sequential forward-backward diffusion framework for adapted time series generation. Our approach progressively injects and removes noise along the sequence, conditioning on the previously generated history to ensure adaptiveness. A novel score-matching objective is introduced for efficient parallel training. We derive rigorous statistical guarantees under a generic framework, then establish score approximation, score estimation, and distribution estimation results with ReLU networks serving as a concrete instance. Empirically, we validate our method on synthetic data, including ARMA models and Gaussian processes, and demonstrate its effectiveness in constructing mean-variance optimal portfolios.

AI.tldr: 提出了一种面向时间序列的“适应性”扩散生成模型，按时间顺序逐步生成并只依赖过去信息，既有理论保证，也在合成数据和投资组合任务上验证了效果。 / The paper proposes an adapted diffusion model for time series that generates sequentially using only past information, and shows both theoretical guarantees and strong empirical results on synthetic data and portfolio optimization.
AI.motivation: 动机在于：现有扩散模型擅长静态数据生成，但直接用于序列数据时往往无法正确建模时间依赖与信息流结构，尤其难以保证生成过程不利用未来信息。 / The motivation is that diffusion models work well for static data, but their direct extension to sequential data often fails to capture temporal dependence and information structure, especially the requirement of generating without access to future information.
AI.method: 论文提出一种用于适应性时间序列生成的顺序前向-后向扩散模型：沿时间序列逐步加噪与去噪，并在每一步条件于已生成的历史；同时设计了新的score-matching目标以支持高效并行训练，并给出基于ReLU网络的理论分析。 / The method is a sequential forward-backward diffusion model for adapted time-series generation, which progressively adds and removes noise along the sequence while conditioning on previously generated history; it also introduces a novel score-matching objective for efficient parallel training and provides theory with ReLU networks as a concrete instantiation.
AI.result: 理论上，论文给出了通用框架下的统计保证，并进一步建立了score approximation、score estimation和distribution estimation结果；实验上，在ARMA、Gaussian process等合成数据以及均值-方差最优投资组合构建中验证了方法有效性。 / The results include rigorous statistical guarantees under a generic framework, with score approximation, score estimation, and distribution estimation results; empirically, the method performs well on synthetic data such as ARMA models and Gaussian processes, and is effective for mean-variance optimal portfolio construction.
AI.conclusion: 该论文认为，顺序前向-后向扩散框架能够在不预知未来信息的前提下生成具有时间适应性的序列数据，并在理论与实证上都表现有效。 / The paper concludes that a sequential forward-backward diffusion framework can generate adapted sequential data without anticipating future information, with both theoretical guarantees and empirical effectiveness.

title: Step-adaptive multimodal fusion network with multi-scale cloud feature learning for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting
summary: Ultra-short-term solar irradiance prediction is critical for photovoltaic system dispatch and power grid stability. Existing approaches suffer from three key shortcomings: single time-series models cannot capture the spatial dynamics of clouds under complex conditions, standard convolutions inadequately represent multi-scale cloud features, and fixed low-frequency compensation strategies fail to adapt to different prediction steps. To address these issues, this proposes a multi-source data fusion model for ultra-short-term irradiance prediction. The model first employs InceptionNeXt to extract multi-scale, multi-directional spatial features from ground-based cloud images. A step-adaptive low-frequency compensation unit is then introduced to dynamically modulate global low-frequency information based on the prediction step. Eventually, the enhanced image features are combined with meteorological time-series features, and a TempAttnLSTM network captures global temporal dependencies for multi-step prediction. Experiments on the public NREL dataset and practical photovoltaic stations in Shandong illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared with several state-of-the-art approaches.

AI.tldr: A cloud-image plus weather-data fusion model with adaptive low-frequency compensation and temporal attention LSTM delivers better ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasts.
AI.motivation: Existing ultra-short-term irradiance prediction methods have three major limitations: pure time-series models miss cloud spatial dynamics, standard convolutions are weak at representing multi-scale cloud patterns, and fixed low-frequency compensation cannot adapt across different prediction steps.
AI.method: The method uses InceptionNeXt to extract multi-scale and multi-directional spatial features from ground-based cloud images, introduces a step-adaptive low-frequency compensation unit to adjust global low-frequency information according to prediction horizon, and fuses these enhanced image features with meteorological time-series features in a TempAttnLSTM network for multi-step forecasting.
AI.result: Experiments on the public NREL dataset and photovoltaic station data from Shandong show that the proposed model is effective and achieves better performance than several state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed multi-source fusion framework improves ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting by jointly modeling cloud-image spatial structure and meteorological temporal dynamics, and it outperforms several state-of-the-art baselines on both public and real-world datasets.

title: Adaptive Tokenisation Via Temporal Redundancy Masking And Latent Inpainting
summary:
Adaptive video tokenisation seeks to dynamically allocate token budgets based on the underlying visual complexity of a sequence. Current continuous-regime approaches achieve this via iterative binarised searches or trained neural regressors, while discrete methods often require a full-rate decoder pass to estimate information content. We demonstrate that such computational overheads are not strictly necessary. We show that the latent space of a frozen continuous video tokeniser inherently encodes temporal redundancy that can be exploited directly: spatial positions whose latent representations change minimally between consecutive frames carry near-zero additional information.
  We introduce a parameter-free adaptive token allocation mechanism that applies a fixed threshold to per-position temporal-L1 differences, identifying and dropping redundant latent positions. Consequently, the compression rate emerges naturally from the input content rather than being enforced top-down: static scenes get compressed aggressively, while highly dynamic sequences retain more tokens. To reconstruct the dropped positions, we propose the Latent Inpainting Transformer (LIT), a lightweight factorised spatial-temporal attention architecture. The resulting inference pipeline is highly efficient, requiring only a single encoder pass and one LIT forward pass, eliminating the need for auxiliary routing networks. Evaluations across TokenBench and DAVIS, which are the standard benchmarks used by recent tokenisers~\cite{infotok, agarwal2025cosmos}, indicate that our framework yields meaningful, content-driven token allocation while maintaining competitive reconstruction fidelity, and delivers a $31\times$ inference-time speedup over the continuous adaptive baseline (ElasticTok-CV) and an $\approx2\times$ speedup over the discrete information-theoretic baseline (InfoTok)

AI.tldr: Exploit temporal changes in latent tokens directly: drop spatial positions whose latent values barely change across frames, then restore them with a lightweight inpainting transformer. This removes the need for search or routing networks, keeps reconstruction competitive, and greatly improves inference speed.
AI.motivation: Existing adaptive video tokenisation methods incur significant computational overhead: continuous methods rely on iterative binarised search or trained regressors, while discrete methods often need a full-rate decoder pass to estimate information content. The paper is motivated by the need for a simpler and faster adaptive mechanism that still allocates tokens according to actual scene dynamics and visual complexity.
AI.method: The method uses a frozen continuous video tokeniser and computes per-spatial-position temporal L1 differences between consecutive latent frames. Positions with changes below a fixed threshold are treated as redundant and dropped, yielding adaptive token allocation without learned regressors or iterative procedures. Dropped latent positions are reconstructed by a Latent Inpainting Transformer (LIT), a lightweight factorised spatial-temporal attention architecture. The inference pipeline requires one encoder pass and one LIT forward pass.
AI.result: On TokenBench and DAVIS, the proposed framework provides meaningful content-driven token allocation while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality. It achieves a 31x inference-time speedup over the continuous adaptive baseline ElasticTok-CV and about a 2x speedup over the discrete baseline InfoTok.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that adaptive video token allocation can be done efficiently without iterative search, auxiliary routing networks, or full-rate decoder estimation by directly exploiting temporal redundancy already present in the latent space of a frozen continuous video tokeniser. Their parameter-free thresholding method, combined with a lightweight latent inpainting model, achieves content-driven compression with competitive fidelity and substantial inference speedups.

title: IR3DE: A Linear Router for Large Language Models
comment: Accepted at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Resource-Adaptive Foundation Model Inference
summary: Foundational Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate proficiency on a wide range of general tasks, and achieve remarkable results on various specialized tasks via domain-expert LLMs. With the ever-growing list of available LLMs, inference routers are being proposed to select the most appropriate LLM for each prompt. However, existing routing methods either optimize cost across weak-to-strong generalist LLMs or require substantial training to support domain-expertise routing. In this paper, we propose IR3DE, a Ridge Regression-based Router for Domain Experts that provides cheap and fast routing decisions for each prompt. We evaluate IR3DE in two Causal Language Modeling (CLM) settings where the tasks are next-token prediction for all domains, and one reasoning setting where each domain has its own distinct reasoning task. Despite being a linear router, IR3DE achieves performance comparable to the other baselines in both CLM settings, and surpassing them in the reasoning setting, with a normalized performance of 98.4%. Moreover, IR3DE enables the addition or removal of new domain experts without requiring the router to be retrained from scratch, allowing a dynamic set of LLMs to be served with minimal disruption to the router itself. Our code is available at: github.com/gensyn-ai/IR3DE.

AI.tldr: IR3DE uses simple ridge regression to route prompts to the right domain-expert LLM cheaply and quickly, performs nearly as well or better than stronger baselines, and is easy to update when the expert pool changes.
AI.motivation: As the number of available LLMs grows, there is a need for efficient routing methods that can select the best model for each prompt. Existing methods either focus on cost optimization among generalist models or require substantial training to handle domain-expert routing. The paper aims to provide a cheaper, faster, and more flexible alternative.
AI.method: The paper proposes IR3DE, a linear inference router based on Ridge Regression. It makes low-cost, fast routing decisions to choose the most suitable domain-expert LLM for each input prompt, and is evaluated in two causal language modeling setups and one domain-specific reasoning setup.
AI.result: IR3DE achieves comparable results to existing baselines in both CLM scenarios and surpasses them in the reasoning scenario, reaching 98.4% normalized performance. It also offers operational flexibility by allowing dynamic addition or removal of domain experts without full retraining.
AI.conclusion: IR3DE is an efficient ridge-regression-based router for selecting domain-expert LLMs per prompt. It matches baseline performance in two CLM settings, outperforms them in a reasoning setting with 98.4% normalized performance, and supports adding or removing experts without retraining the router from scratch.

title: Adaptive Oscillatory-State Alignment for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Long-term time series forecasting benefits from inductive biases that expose recurring temporal structure. Existing periodic forecasting methods typically model recurrence through predefined periods, global spectral components, or fixed learnable templates. However, real-world temporal dynamics are rarely rigidly periodic: oscillatory behavior often evolves through amplitude modulation, phase drift, and local frequency variation. Under these conditions, fixed-template periodic modeling can become fundamentally mismatched to the underlying temporal states. We propose AOSNET, a Hilbert-guided forecasting framework that reformulates periodic forecasting from fixed template matching to adaptive oscillatory-state alignment. AOSNET extracts analytic-signal descriptors from both the observed sequence and a learnable global oscillatory prior, then adaptively aligns local states through a descriptor-conditioned gate that selectively preserves reliable observations while softly correcting mismatched regions. The learned prior serves not as a rigid repeated template but as a flexible oscillatory reference interpreted through local state dynamics. Experiments on eight benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art or highly competitive accuracy with fast inference speed. Controlled synthetic studies isolating amplitude modulation, phase drift, and local frequency variation confirm that the advantage of oscillatory-state alignment consistently increases as non-stationarity intensifies.

AI.tldr: AOSNET uses Hilbert-based oscillatory-state descriptors and adaptive alignment to forecast non-stationary periodic time series more effectively than fixed periodic templates.
AI.motivation: Existing periodic forecasting methods rely on predefined periods, global spectral components, or fixed learnable templates, but real-world temporal patterns are often only quasi-periodic and evolve over time. This creates a mismatch between rigid periodic assumptions and actual temporal dynamics.
AI.method: The paper proposes AOSNET, a Hilbert-guided forecasting framework. It extracts analytic-signal descriptors from the observed sequence and a learnable global oscillatory prior, then uses a descriptor-conditioned gating mechanism to align local oscillatory states, preserving reliable observations and softly correcting mismatched regions.
AI.result: Experiments on eight benchmarks show state-of-the-art or highly competitive forecasting accuracy with fast inference. Synthetic experiments further show that AOSNET’s advantage grows as non-stationarity becomes stronger.
AI.conclusion: AOSNET reframes periodic time-series forecasting as adaptive oscillatory-state alignment rather than fixed-template matching, and this shift better handles non-stationary oscillatory dynamics such as amplitude modulation, phase drift, and local frequency variation.

title: Towards Healthy Evolution: Exploring the Role and Mechanisms of Human-Agent Interaction in Self-Evolving Systems
summary: Self-evolving agents improve through continual self-play and self-generated learning signals, but autonomous evolution can also cause capability degradation and safety drift. Although human feedback has proven effective for static and post-trained agents, its role in self-evolving systems remains underexplored. We introduce Agent Norm Correction through Human-like Oversight and Review (ANCHOR), an LLM-based framework that simulates human supervision and delivers feedback at various phases of self-evolution. With ANCHOR, we evaluate two representative open-source self-evolving agent systems across coding, mathematical reasoning, and safety. Our results show that even limited supervision substantially mitigates safety degradation while preserving stable performance on core evolutionary objectives. Further analysis shows that supervision over the output verification phase is the most effective for intervention, whereas increasing supervision frequency yields diminishing returns. These findings provide empirical evidence and practical guidance for designing more stable, controllable, and human-aligned self-evolving agent systems.

AI.tldr: ANCHOR adds human-like oversight to self-evolving agents and shows that modest supervision can keep them safer without hurting core performance; checking the output verification phase works best, and supervising more often helps less than expected.
AI.motivation: Self-evolving agents can improve through self-play and self-generated learning signals, but this autonomy may also lead to capability degradation and safety drift. The authors aim to understand whether human-like oversight can stabilize such systems without undermining their core evolutionary benefits.
AI.method: The paper proposes ANCHOR, an LLM-based framework that simulates human supervision and injects feedback at multiple stages of agent self-evolution. It is evaluated on two open-source self-evolving agent systems across coding, mathematical reasoning, and safety tasks.
AI.result: Even limited supervision substantially mitigates safety degradation while preserving stable performance on coding and mathematical reasoning objectives. Among intervention stages, supervising output verification is the most effective, while increasing supervision frequency shows diminishing returns.
AI.conclusion: ANCHOR-style human-like oversight can significantly reduce safety degradation in self-evolving agents while maintaining stable task performance; the output verification stage is the most impactful intervention point, and more frequent supervision brings diminishing returns.

title: RQUL-UIE: Revitalizing Quality-Unstable Labels for Underwater Image Enhancement via In-Dataset Self-Supervision
summary: Underwater Image Enhancement (UIE) is essential for mitigating degradations caused by water medium. Although learning-based methods have advanced significantly, most rely on paired datasets with unstable label quality, which bottlenecks model performance. This paper proposes a diffusion-based, in-dataset self-supervised learning strategy designed to exploit the quality distribution of training labels. Specifically, we evaluate label quality via semantic perception embeddings from a pre-trained diffusion model in a training-free manner. These quality scores are subsequently quantized into noise-level indices, guiding a multi-step denoising process for level-wise supervision. This mechanism prevents low-quality labels from degrading the model while maximizing their utility during training. Furthermore, a Fourier-based refinement network is incorporated to explicitly reconstruct high-frequency components. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms SOTA approaches in restoration quality. The code and pre-trained model will be available once accepted in link.

AI.tldr: A self-supervised diffusion-based UIE method scores label quality, turns that into denoising guidance, and adds Fourier refinement for details, leading to better results than prior SOTA methods.
AI.motivation: Existing learning-based underwater image enhancement methods depend heavily on paired datasets whose labels are often unstable or low quality, limiting model performance. The paper is motivated by the need to exploit imperfect in-dataset labels more effectively without allowing poor labels to harm training.
AI.method: The method evaluates training label quality in a training-free manner using semantic perception embeddings from a pre-trained diffusion model, quantizes the quality scores into noise-level indices, and uses these indices to guide a multi-step denoising process for level-wise supervision. It also adds a Fourier-based refinement network to reconstruct high-frequency details explicitly.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that the proposed approach consistently surpasses state-of-the-art methods in underwater image restoration quality.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a diffusion-based in-dataset self-supervised strategy, guided by label-quality-aware denoising and complemented by a Fourier refinement network, can more effectively use noisy paired underwater datasets and consistently outperform state-of-the-art underwater image enhancement methods.

title: Harnessing Structural Context for Entity Alignment Foundation Models
summary: Entity alignment (EA) aims to identify equivalent entities across heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs) and is a key component of knowledge fusion and cross-KG reasoning. The recent EA foundation model demonstrates that alignment knowledge, once pretrained, can be directly applied to diverse previously unseen KG pairs. However, it still underuses structural context in two places: cross-KG interaction is weak during encoding, and final candidate ranking still relies too heavily on coarse similarity. We address these limitations with ContextEA, an enhanced encoder-decoder framework for transferable EA. On the encoder side, we introduce a cross-KG interaction encoder that unifies the two KGs with anchor bridges and performs earlier relation-aware cross-graph propagation. On the decoder side, we introduce a structural calibration decoder that calibrates alignment scores with entity-level, neighborhood-level, relation-level, and anchor-aware structural evidence. This design strengthens both structural context construction and structural context exploitation while remaining lightweight. Experiments on 29 EA datasets in OpenEA, SRPRS, and DBP show consistent gains over strong transferable baselines. Notably, the pretrained ContextEA already surpasses the finetuned baselines on all three benchmark groups, demonstrating substantially stronger transfer to unseen KGs. These results suggest that explicitly harnessing structural context is an effective direction for improving EA foundation models.

AI.tldr: ContextEA improves transferable entity alignment by injecting stronger structural context into both encoding and decoding, and it achieves consistent state-of-the-art transfer performance on 29 benchmark datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing transferable EA foundation models do not fully use structural context: cross-KG interaction during encoding is weak, and final ranking depends too much on coarse similarity. The work aims to fix both issues while keeping the model lightweight.
AI.method: The paper proposes ContextEA, an encoder-decoder framework for transferable entity alignment. Its encoder performs early cross-KG, relation-aware propagation by unifying two KGs with anchor bridges, while its decoder structurally calibrates candidate alignment scores using entity-, neighborhood-, relation-, and anchor-level evidence.
AI.result: On 29 datasets from OpenEA, SRPRS, and DBP, ContextEA consistently outperforms strong transferable baselines. The pretrained model even surpasses finetuned baselines across all three benchmark groups, indicating substantially better generalization to unseen KGs.
AI.conclusion: ContextEA shows that explicitly modeling and exploiting structural context improves transferable entity alignment, yielding stronger transfer to unseen knowledge graphs than prior foundation and finetuned baselines.

title: OPRD: On-Policy Representation Distillation
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) supervises the student only in output space by matching next-token probabilities. This output-only paradigm has two limits: (1) sampling variance from Monte Carlo KL estimates over large vocabularies (e.g., Qwen's ~150k tokens) persists throughout training, and (2) it treats the teacher as a black-box, discarding all intermediate hidden states after the LM head. We propose On-Policy Representation Distillation (OPRD), which lifts distillation into hidden-state space by aligning student and teacher representations across selected layers on the same rollouts, bypassing the LM head entirely. Theoretically, OPRD eliminates sampling variance and provides richer per-layer structural information. Empirically, OPRD closes the student-teacher gap on AIME 2024/2025 and AIMO, while output-space OPD baselines plateau below the teacher. OPRD also trains 1.44x faster and uses 54% less memory than top-k OPD. Code: https://github.com/ShenzhiYang2000/OPRD.

AI.tldr: OPRD把on-policy蒸馏从token输出概率提升到隐藏状态表示对齐，既减少方差又利用教师层级结构信息，因此更快、更省内存、效果更接近教师。 / OPRD moves on-policy distillation from token-probability matching to hidden-state alignment, reducing variance and exploiting layerwise teacher structure, which makes it faster, more memory-efficient, and closer to teacher performance.
AI.motivation: 传统OPD只在输出空间蒸馏，存在大词表下Monte Carlo KL估计方差持续存在、且把教师当黑盒丢弃中间层信息两大问题。 / Standard OPD distills only in output space, suffering from persistent Monte Carlo KL variance under large vocabularies and wasting informative intermediate teacher representations by treating the teacher as a black box.
AI.method: 提出On-Policy Representation Distillation：在on-policy生成轨迹上，对教师和学生在若干选定层的隐藏状态进行表示对齐，而不是仅匹配下一token概率。 / The paper proposes On-Policy Representation Distillation: on on-policy rollouts, it aligns teacher and student hidden representations at selected layers instead of matching only next-token probabilities.
AI.result: 在AIME 2024/2025与AIMO上，OPRD优于输出空间OPD基线并更接近教师；训练速度提升1.44倍，相比top-k OPD显存/内存占用降低54%。 / On AIME 2024/2025 and AIMO, OPRD outperforms output-space OPD baselines and gets closer to teacher performance; it trains 1.44x faster and uses 54% less memory than top-k OPD.
AI.conclusion: OPRD通过在同一rollout上对齐教师与学生的多层隐藏表示，避免LM head与输出分布匹配带来的采样方差，能更高效地缩小student-teacher性能差距。 / OPRD aligns teacher and student hidden states on the same rollouts, avoiding LM-head/output-space sampling variance and narrowing the student-teacher gap more efficiently.

title: WorldFly: A World-Model-Based Vision-Language-Action Model for UAV Navigation
summary: End-to-end Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promise in UAV navigation. However, existing approaches typically rely on historical observations to directly predict actions, often struggling in dense urban environments where severe occlusions and sharp turns result in drastic viewpoint transitions. We argue that the ability to "imagine" future states -- inherent in World Models -- is critical for robust decision-making under such partial observability. To address this, we construct a challenging Urban Canyon Traversal Benchmark, specifically designed to evaluate spatial understanding in scenarios characterized by severe occlusions and drastic viewpoint transitions. To this end, we propose WorldFly, a novel world-model-based VLA framework that employs a dual-branch coupled flow matching mechanism to jointly generate future video predictions and navigation actions, thereby explicitly guiding the agent's policy via spatial imagination. Extensive evaluations on our benchmark demonstrate that WorldFly outperforms other baselines, particularly in unseen environments, validating the effectiveness of integrating world models into embodied aerial agents.

AI.tldr: WorldFly adds future-state imagination to UAV VLA navigation by jointly predicting future video and actions, and it performs better than prior methods on a hard urban canyon benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing end-to-end VLA methods directly predict actions from historical observations and struggle under partial observability in dense urban UAV navigation, where severe occlusions and sharp turns cause drastic viewpoint transitions.
AI.method: The paper builds an Urban Canyon Traversal Benchmark and proposes WorldFly, a world-model-based Vision-Language-Action framework using a dual-branch coupled flow matching mechanism to jointly predict future video and navigation actions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on the new benchmark show that WorldFly outperforms baseline methods, with particularly strong generalization in unseen environments.
AI.conclusion: Integrating a world model that imagines future states improves UAV navigation robustness, especially in dense urban and unseen environments with occlusions and sharp viewpoint changes.

title: Adversarial Attacks Already Tell the Answer: Directional Bias-Guided Test-time Defense for Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs), such as CLIP, have shown strong zero-shot generalization but remain highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, posing serious risks in real-world applications. Test-time defenses for VLMs have recently emerged as a promising and efficient approach to defend against adversarial attacks without requiring costly large-scale retraining. In this work, we uncover a surprising phenomenon: under diverse input transformations, adversarial images in CLIP's feature space consistently shift along a dominant direction, in contrast to the dispersed patterns of clean images. We hypothesize that this dominant shift, termed the Defense Direction, opposes the adversarial shift, pointing features back toward their correct class centers. Building on this insight, we propose Directional Bias-guided Defense (DBD), a test-time framework that estimates the Defense Direction and employs a DB-score-based two-stream reconstruction strategy to recover robust representations. Experiments on 15 datasets demonstrate that DBD not only achieves SOTA adversarial robustness while preserving clean accuracy, but also reveals the counterintuitive result that adversarial accuracy can even surpass clean accuracy. This demonstrates that adversarial perturbations inherently encode directional priors about the true decision boundary.

AI.tldr: 作者发现CLIP中的对抗特征在变换后会沿一个稳定主方向偏移，于是提出测试时防御DBD，估计一个反向的Defense Direction并做双流重建，从而在15个数据集上显著提升鲁棒性且不牺牲干净精度。 / The authors find that adversarial features in CLIP consistently move along a stable dominant direction under transformations, then propose the test-time defense DBD, which estimates an opposite Defense Direction and performs two-stream reconstruction, yielding strong robustness gains on 15 datasets without sacrificing clean accuracy.
AI.motivation: 现有VLM如CLIP虽然零样本能力强，但对抗脆弱性严重；而大规模重训练代价高，因此需要高效的测试时防御方法。作者希望挖掘对抗样本在特征空间中的结构性规律，以设计无需重训练、可泛化的防御机制。 / Although VLMs such as CLIP have strong zero-shot generalization, they are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks; large-scale retraining is costly, so an efficient test-time defense is needed. The authors aim to exploit structural regularities of adversarial features to design a retraining-free and generalizable defense.
AI.method: 论文首先观察到：在多种输入变换下，对抗样本在CLIP特征空间中沿一个主导方向一致偏移，而干净样本的变化更分散。基于此，作者定义与对抗偏移相反的Defense Direction，并提出DBD框架：估计该方向，再结合基于DB-score的双流重建策略，恢复更稳健的特征表示。 / The paper first observes that under diverse input transformations, adversarial samples in CLIP feature space shift consistently along a dominant direction, while clean samples are more dispersed. Based on this, the authors define a Defense Direction opposing the adversarial shift and propose DBD: estimate this direction and use a DB-score-based two-stream reconstruction strategy to recover robust representations.
AI.result: 在15个数据集上的实验表明，DBD取得了SOTA级别的对抗鲁棒性，并且能够较好保持干净精度。更有意思的是，论文报告了一种反直觉现象：某些情况下对抗样本上的准确率甚至高于干净样本。 / Experiments on 15 datasets show that DBD achieves state-of-the-art adversarial robustness while largely preserving clean accuracy. Interestingly, the paper reports a counterintuitive phenomenon: in some cases, adversarial accuracy can even exceed clean accuracy.
AI.conclusion: DBD通过估计并利用CLIP特征空间中的Defense Direction，在无需重训练的测试时防御设置下显著提升VLM对抗鲁棒性，同时保持干净样本精度；论文还指出，对抗扰动可能隐含有助于恢复真实决策边界的方向先验。 / DBD improves adversarial robustness of VLMs at test time by estimating and leveraging a Defense Direction in CLIP feature space, without retraining, while preserving clean accuracy; the paper also suggests adversarial perturbations may encode directional priors useful for recovering the true decision boundary.

title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
summary: Speech translation (ST) is increasingly adopted in user applications, yet its evaluation largely focuses on decontextualized testbeds and holistic quality, rather than end users' communication needs. We introduce Ouvia, an evaluation framework for measuring user-perceived usability of speech translation outputs in real-world settings. Ouvia focuses on one-to-one communication: an English speaker needs to convey a request to a Portuguese speaker, and the message is automatically translated. Through a custom web app and multi-phase study design, we collect more than 1,750 such interactions in healthcare and everyday situations, mediated by four ST systems, involving speakers from three English dialects and two genders. We find that modern ST serves people only to a limited extent -- only around half of interactions are rated as usable -- with significant gaps in reported usability across demographic groups. Moreover, among quality metrics, we find that QA-based evaluation is a substantially stronger predictor of real-world usability than standard approaches. Together, these findings stress the importance of situated, user-centered evaluation frameworks that go beyond holistic quality scores and attend to who the technology serves -- and how well.

AI.tldr: Ouvia 用真实用户交互来评测语音翻译可用性，结果显示当前系统离“真正好用”还有明显距离，而 QA-based 指标比传统质量分数更接近用户实际体验。 / Ouvia evaluates speech translation through real user interactions and shows that current systems are still far from reliably usable, while QA-based metrics align better with actual user experience than traditional quality scores.
AI.motivation: 现有语音翻译评测主要基于去语境化测试集和整体质量指标，无法充分反映终端用户在真实沟通中的实际需求与可用性。 / Existing speech translation evaluation relies mainly on decontextualized benchmarks and holistic quality metrics, which do not adequately capture end-user communication needs and real-world usability.
AI.method: 作者提出了 Ouvia 评测框架，通过定制网页应用和多阶段用户研究，收集了 1,750 多次英语到葡萄牙语的一对一沟通交互，覆盖医疗和日常场景，并比较了四个语音翻译系统、三种英语方言和两种性别。 / The authors introduce Ouvia, an evaluation framework implemented via a custom web app and a multi-phase user study, collecting over 1,750 English-to-Portuguese one-to-one interactions across healthcare and everyday settings, covering four ST systems, three English dialects, and two genders.
AI.result: 研究发现，现代语音翻译只有大约一半的交互被用户认为可用；不同人口统计群体之间的可用性存在显著差异；在多种质量指标中，基于问答的评测比标准方法更能预测真实世界可用性。 / The study finds that only about half of interactions are judged usable, that usability differs significantly across demographic groups, and that QA-based evaluation is a much stronger predictor of real-world usability than standard metrics.
AI.conclusion: 该论文认为，语音翻译系统在真实一对一沟通中的可用性仍然有限，且不同人群之间存在明显差距；因此评测应从整体质量分数转向情境化、以用户为中心的可用性评估。 / The paper concludes that current speech translation systems have limited usability in real one-to-one communication, with substantial disparities across demographic groups; evaluation should therefore move beyond holistic quality scores toward situated, user-centered usability assessment.

title: Catastrophic Forgetting as Accessibility Collapse: A Three-Level Framework for Knowledge Persistence in Continual Learning
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. Sequential continual-learning experiments on CIFAR-100 using ResNet-18
summary: Catastrophic forgetting is commonly interpreted as the irreversible erasure of previously acquired knowledge during sequential learning. In this work, we investigate an alternative perspective: that forgetting may arise not from complete destruction of task representations but from a loss of accessibility to preserved information. We introduce a three-level framework separating knowledge storage, representation, and accessibility, and evaluate each component through a series of continual-learning experiments on sequential CIFAR-100 classification using ResNet-18. Our analysis combines checkpoint persistence, linear probing, representation geometry, classifier-reset recovery, and layer-wise recoverability experiments. We observe complete behavioral forgetting of earlier tasks, with task accuracy collapsing from 54.8% to 0%, while linear probe performance retains approximately 76% of the original representational information. Furthermore, retraining only the final classifier restores 75.7% of the original task performance without modifying the backbone network. Layer-wise analysis reveals that early and intermediate layers preserve highly recoverable task information despite severe degradation at later stages. Projection-energy and principal-angle analyses indicate that retained knowledge persists as distributed high-dimensional representations rather than through preservation of a small dominant subspace. These findings suggest that catastrophic forgetting is better characterized as an accessibility failure than complete representational erasure, and that substantial task-relevant information remains embedded within neural representations even after functional forgetting has occurred.

AI.tldr: Catastrophic forgetting may not fully erase old knowledge; much of it remains inside the network but becomes hard to access. On sequential CIFAR-100, old-task accuracy can fall to zero, yet most representation quality remains and much performance can be recovered by retraining only the classifier.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to challenge the standard view that catastrophic forgetting means irreversible destruction of prior knowledge. The authors investigate whether forgotten knowledge may still exist in the model but become inaccessible to the current readout or decision mechanism.
AI.method: The paper proposes a three-level framework separating knowledge storage, representation, and accessibility. It evaluates these levels in continual learning on sequential CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18 using checkpoint persistence, linear probing, representation-geometry analysis, classifier-reset recovery, and layer-wise recoverability experiments.
AI.result: The results show complete behavioral forgetting on earlier tasks, with accuracy dropping from 54.8% to 0%, while linear probes retain about 76% of original representational information. Retraining only the final classifier recovers 75.7% of original task performance without changing the backbone, and layer-wise analysis shows stronger preservation in early and intermediate layers. Geometry analyses suggest the retained knowledge is distributed across high-dimensional representations rather than confined to a small dominant subspace.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that catastrophic forgetting is largely an accessibility problem rather than complete erasure of stored task knowledge. Even when old-task accuracy falls to zero, substantial task-relevant information remains in the network representations and can be recovered, especially through classifier retraining and from earlier/intermediate layers.

title: Amortizing Federated Adaptation: Hypernetwork Driven LoRA for Personalized Foundation Models
comment: Accepted at International Workshop on Federated Learning in the Age of Foundation Models In Conjunction with IJCAI 2026 (FL@FM-IJCAI'26)
summary: Federated fine-tuning of foundation models using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) offers a communication efficient solution for distributed learning. However, existing federated LoRA methods suffer from two fundamental limitations: (1) structural aggregation bias, where independently averaging low rank factors fails to approximate the true combined update, and (2) client side initialization lag, as clients repeatedly reinitialize LoRA parameters across communication rounds, slowing convergence. We propose HyperLoRA, a unified framework that addresses both issues through amortized federated adaptation through hypernetwork-driven LoRA generation and product space aggregation. Instead of iterative per-client optimization, HyperLoRA employs a learned generator that maps client distribution signatures to LoRA initializations, effectively amortizing per client adaptation. On the server side, we introduce a learned aggregation module that directly synthesizes updates in the low-rank product space, eliminating the inconsistencies of factor-wise averaging. A lightweight residual correction module further improves stability under heterogenous (non-IID) client distributions.By replacing iterative optimization and heuristic averaging with learned operators, HyperLoRA jointly enables efficient personalization, unbiased aggregation, and faster convergence. Experiments on federated vision and vision-language benchmarks show that HyperLoRA achieves improved convergence speed, greater robustness to distribution shift, and stronger personalization performance compared to prior federated LoRA methods.

AI.tldr: HyperLoRA replaces hand-designed federated LoRA optimization and averaging with learned generation and learned aggregation, reducing bias and client reinitialization overhead while improving convergence, robustness, and personalization.
AI.motivation: Existing federated LoRA methods are communication-efficient but suffer from two core issues: factor-wise averaging introduces structural aggregation bias because low-rank factors are not linearly compositional in a faithful way, and repeated reinitialization of LoRA parameters on clients across rounds causes initialization lag and slower convergence.
AI.method: The paper proposes HyperLoRA, which has three main components: a hypernetwork-like generator that maps client distribution signatures to LoRA initializations for amortized client adaptation; a learned server-side aggregation module that combines updates directly in the low-rank product space instead of averaging LoRA factors independently; and a lightweight residual correction module to stabilize training under non-IID settings.
AI.result: On federated vision and vision-language benchmarks, HyperLoRA improves convergence speed, robustness to distribution shift, and personalization performance compared with prior federated LoRA baselines.
AI.conclusion: HyperLoRA provides a unified federated LoRA framework that uses learned generation and learned aggregation to overcome structural aggregation bias and repeated client reinitialization, leading to faster convergence, better personalization, and stronger robustness under heterogeneous client distributions.

title: The Tell-Tale Norm: $\ell_2$ Magnitude as a Signal for Reasoning Dynamics in Large Language Models
summary: Recent work has sought to understand Large Language Models (LLMs) reasoning, yet a principled, model-intrinsic signal that captures its layer-wise reasoning dynamics remains underexplored. We bridge this gap by demonstrating that the l2 norm of hidden states serves as an endogenous signal of the model's reasoning intensity. Using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) as a diagnostic probe, we observe that LLMs' internal reasoning is marked by a sharp increase in reasoning feature activations concentrated in late layers. Motivated by this pattern, we establish a formal link between reasoning intensity and the model's latent geometry and theoretically prove that the l2 norm of hidden states bounds the activation strength of SAE reasoning features. Empirical correlation analysis and causal interventions further validate the l2 norm as a faithful indicator, where heightened norms consistently correspond to critical reasoning steps. We then introduce three test-time scaling techniques guided by l2 norms: (i) Adaptive Layer-wise Reasoning Recursion, (ii) Endogenous Reasoning State Steering, and (iii) l2-guided Response Selection, which requires no additional training or data and is compatible with advanced inference engines. Experiments across model architectures and benchmarks show that l2-norm-based techniques significantly improve reasoning performance, offering a principled yet simple lens to perceive and control LLM latent reasoning dynamics. Our code is available at https://github.com/zjy1298/The-Tell-Tale-Norm.

AI.tldr: Hidden-state l2 norm acts as an internal meter of LLM reasoning intensity; using it to monitor and steer inference improves reasoning accuracy with simple training-free methods.
AI.motivation: Prior work tried to understand LLM reasoning, but lacked a principled endogenous signal that reflects internal reasoning dynamics layer by layer. The paper aims to identify such a model-intrinsic signal and leverage it for both interpretability and performance gains.
AI.method: The authors use Sparse Autoencoders to probe reasoning-related features across layers, develop a theoretical connection between hidden-state l2 norms and the activation strength of SAE reasoning features, validate the signal through correlation analysis and causal interventions, and then design three inference-time scaling methods guided by l2 norms.
AI.result: They find that reasoning feature activations surge in late layers and are strongly associated with increased hidden-state l2 norms. Across architectures and benchmarks, their three l2-guided inference techniques improve reasoning performance while requiring no additional training or data.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the l2 norm of hidden states is a principled intrinsic signal for tracking and controlling layer-wise reasoning intensity in LLMs, and that simple l2-guided test-time methods can significantly improve reasoning performance without extra training.

title: When Good Enough Is Optimal: Multiplication-Only Matrix Inversion Approximation for Quantized Gated DeltaNet
summary: Matrix inversion in chunk-wise parallel linear attention is a major bottleneck for long-context modeling, particularly on NPUs, where forward-substitution-based methods exhibit limited parallelism and poor hardware utilization. We propose a fast, Matrix Multiplication (MatMul)-based algorithm tailored for strictly lower-triangular matrices arising in chunk-wise linear attention. Motivated by the rapid growth of Neumann-series terms and the diagonal concentration of the inverse matrix, we employ a truncated Neumann expansion with structural masking and parallel residual correction to eliminate sequential dependencies. We further extend our method to low-bits INT by mitigating the dynamic range expansion arising from repeated matrix power operations, and adapt the approximation order and residual step to the chunk size to minimize computational cost while preserving the model's accuracy. Experiments on Qwen3.5-family models demonstrate up to 5$\times$ kernel-level speedup and a 20% reduction in decode-layer overhead, while preserving accuracy under both floating-point and low-precision inference. Our method offers an efficient and hardware-friendly solution for scalable linear attention.

AI.tldr: A hardware-friendly MatMul-based inverse approximation for linear attention speeds up chunk-wise decoding on NPUs by up to 5x at kernel level and cuts decode overhead by 20% without hurting accuracy.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that matrix inversion is a major bottleneck in chunk-wise parallel linear attention for long-context modeling, especially on NPUs, where existing forward-substitution-based methods have poor parallelism and low hardware utilization.
AI.method: The method replaces forward-substitution-style matrix inversion with a truncated Neumann-series expansion specialized for strictly lower-triangular matrices. It uses structural masking and parallel residual correction, and extends the approach to low-bit INT by controlling dynamic range growth from repeated matrix powers. The approximation order and residual correction step are adapted to chunk size to balance speed and accuracy.
AI.result: Experiments on Qwen3.5-family models show up to 5x kernel-level speedup and a 20% reduction in decode-layer overhead, while maintaining accuracy under both floating-point and low-precision inference.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a MatMul-based approximation for inverting the strictly lower-triangular matrices in chunk-wise parallel linear attention can remove sequential dependencies, improve hardware utilization on NPUs, and preserve model accuracy in both floating-point and low-bit INT inference.

title: Where does Absolute Position come from in decoder-only Transformers?
summary: RoPE-trained transformers distinguish absolute position in their attention patterns, even though RoPE encodes only relative offsets in the inner product. We trace this leakage to two architectural components, The causal mask is responsible for the first: its per-query softmax denominator depends on the absolute query position by construction. The residual stream supplies the second. Under causal attention the activation at position $0$ attends only to itself and runs as a closed dynamical system from the embedding of the token at that position; downstream attention reads this trajectory through sink-reading heads. Both components appear in all three architectures we study, in architecturally specific balance: NTK scaling suppresses the residual-stream component, sliding-window attention allows it to accumulate with depth, and standard RoPE sits between. Replacing the \texttt{BOS} embedding before the forward pass removes $40\%$ of the residual-stream component at early queries. Attention sinks are token-anchored stabilizers that pass forward a deterministic fingerprint of the token at position $0$, constant across inputs when that token is the auto-prepended \texttt{BOS} and varying with it otherwise.

AI.tldr: RoPE models learn absolute position not from RoPE itself, but from causal masking plus a BOS-driven residual-stream trace that attention sinks can read.
AI.motivation: RoPE is designed to encode relative offsets, yet trained transformers still appear to distinguish absolute positions. The work aims to explain where this absolute-position signal comes from and how architectural choices influence it.
AI.method: The paper analyzes attention patterns in RoPE-trained transformers and decomposes absolute-position leakage into two architectural mechanisms. It studies three architectures, compares the balance between causal-mask and residual-stream effects, and performs an intervention by replacing the BOS embedding before the forward pass to measure the residual-stream contribution.
AI.result: The causal mask makes the per-query softmax denominator depend on absolute query position, while the residual stream carries a position-0-dependent trajectory that downstream sink-reading heads can detect. NTK scaling weakens the residual-stream pathway, sliding-window attention amplifies it with depth, and replacing BOS removes about 40% of the residual-stream component at early query positions.
AI.conclusion: Absolute-position information emerges in RoPE-trained transformers despite RoPE's relative-position inner-product formulation. The leakage comes from two sources: the causal mask and the residual stream, with their relative importance depending on architecture. Attention sinks propagate a deterministic fingerprint of the token at position 0, often the BOS token.

title: DisasterBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for UAV-Based Disaster Response in Complex Environments
summary: When a disaster unfolds, responders must answer not only what is happening, but also why it is happening, what will happen next, and what to do now, often from noisy low-altitude UAV views and under tight on-site compute constraints. However, most existing multimodal benchmarks emphasize perception (e.g., recognition/description), cover limited disaster types, and provide insufficient support for the multi-stage reasoning required in practical emergency response. We introduce DisasterBench, a multi-stage multimodal reasoning benchmark for UAV-Based disaster response in complex environments. DisasterBench spans 14 disaster-related scene types and 9 response-critical tasks across pre-, during-, and post-disaster stages, with fine-grained disaster-task mappings that explicitly test causal attribution, propagation prediction, damage analysis, and decision-oriented reasoning. To enable reasoning on the edge, we further propose DisasterVL, a lightweight multimodal model optimized with a three-stage pipeline combining domain instruction tuning, chain-of-thought-guided multimodal alignment, and reinforcement learning-based policy optimization. Experiments across 21 popular MLLMs show that our 2B-parameter DisasterVL outperforms all evaluated open-source models and substantially narrows the gap to state-of-the-art closed-source models, achieving GPT-4o-comparable reasoning accuracy with superior efficiency. The project page is available at https://github.com/TanmouTT/DisasterBench.

AI.tldr: The paper builds a realistic UAV disaster-response benchmark for multi-stage reasoning and introduces a compact 2B model, DisasterVL, that delivers near-GPT-4o reasoning performance with much lower compute cost.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal disaster benchmarks focus mostly on perception, cover too few disaster categories, and do not adequately test the multi-step reasoning needed by responders working from noisy UAV imagery under strict on-site compute limits.
AI.method: The paper introduces DisasterBench, a benchmark covering 14 disaster scene types and 9 tasks across pre-, during-, and post-disaster stages, with mappings for causal attribution, propagation prediction, damage analysis, and decision reasoning. It also proposes DisasterVL, a lightweight multimodal model trained with a three-stage pipeline: domain instruction tuning, chain-of-thought-guided multimodal alignment, and reinforcement learning-based policy optimization.
AI.result: Across 21 popular multimodal large language models, the 2B-parameter DisasterVL outperforms all tested open-source models, significantly reduces the gap to top closed-source systems, and achieves GPT-4o-comparable reasoning accuracy with better efficiency.
AI.conclusion: DisasterBench fills a major gap in UAV-based disaster-response evaluation by supporting multi-stage multimodal reasoning, and the proposed 2B DisasterVL shows that strong disaster reasoning can be achieved with edge-friendly efficiency, reaching near closed-source performance.

title: Improving Answer Extraction in Context-based Question Answering Systems Using LLMs
summary: Question answering (QA) systems have achieved notable progress with the advent of large language models (LLMs). However, they still face challenges in accurately extracting and generating precise answers from given contexts, particularly when dealing with complex or ambiguous queries. Existing approaches often struggle with contextual understanding, answer consistency, and generalization across diverse domains. In this work, we propose a question answering system based on large language models, where the input consists of a textual context and a corresponding question, and the output is a concise and accurate answer. The motivation behind this research lies in addressing the limitations of current QA systems, particularly their tendency to produce irrelevant or imprecise responses despite having access to the correct context. Our methodology involves fine-tuning a pre-trained LLM on a benchmark QA dataset to improve its contextual comprehension and answer extraction capabilities. Specifically, we utilize the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD1.1), which provides high-quality context-question-answer triplets for supervised training and evaluation. Experimental results show that the fine-tuned Roberta-base model achieves the highest performance, attaining a ROUGE-L score of 86.84%, a BLEU score of 28.24%, and a BERTScore of 95.38%. These results indicate strong accuracy and answer relevance, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach for context-based question answering tasks. Furthermore, the findings confirm that targeted fine-tuning substantially improves the reliability and precision of QA systems.

AI.tldr: Fine-tuning RoBERTa-base on SQuAD1.1 significantly improves context-based QA accuracy and answer relevance, outperforming alternatives with strong ROUGE-L, BLEU, and BERTScore results.
AI.motivation: Current QA systems based on LLMs still produce irrelevant or imprecise answers even when the correct context is available, especially for complex or ambiguous questions and across diverse domains.
AI.method: The paper fine-tunes a pre-trained large language model for extractive/context-based QA using supervised training on SQuAD1.1 context-question-answer triplets, then evaluates performance with ROUGE-L, BLEU, and BERTScore.
AI.result: The fine-tuned RoBERTa-base model achieves the best reported results: ROUGE-L 86.84%, BLEU 28.24%, and BERTScore 95.38%, indicating strong answer accuracy and relevance.
AI.conclusion: Targeted fine-tuning of a pre-trained LLM on SQuAD1.1 substantially improves the reliability, precision, and relevance of context-based question answering, with RoBERTa-base delivering the best performance.

title: Online KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation under Misspecification
summary: We study KL-regularized contextual bandits and episodic reinforcement learning (RL) under general function approximation with model misspecification. Existing guarantees rely on realizability and therefore do not extend to misspecified models, where classical regret bounds may fail. This work introduces KL misspecification formulations for contextual bandits and episodic RL and analyzes regression-based algorithms with Gibbs policy updates. High-probability KL-regret guarantees with explicit misspecification terms are established, recovering the standard realizable KL-regularized setting as a special case.

AI.tldr: The paper extends KL-regularized bandit/RL theory beyond realizable models: define KL-based misspecification, analyze regression plus Gibbs-policy algorithms, and prove high-probability KL-regret bounds that gracefully worsen with misspecification while matching standard results when the model is correct.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that prior regret guarantees for KL-regularized contextual bandits and RL typically assume realizability, which is often unrealistic in practice. Under model misspecification, classical regret guarantees can break down, so the paper seeks a framework and theory that remain valid beyond the realizable setting.
AI.method: The method introduces KL misspecification formulations for both contextual bandits and episodic RL, then studies regression-based learning algorithms combined with Gibbs policy updates in the KL-regularized setting. The analysis derives high-probability KL-regret guarantees with explicit misspecification-dependent terms.
AI.result: The main result is a set of high-probability KL-regret bounds for contextual bandits and episodic RL under general function approximation and model misspecification. These bounds include explicit penalty terms for misspecification and reduce to the standard realizable KL-regularized regret guarantees as a special case.
