Specifically, we first identify a sparse set of pivotal key frames that dominate the latent semantic evolution. Then, only these keyframes undergo dense, step-by-step denoising to ensure structural integrity, while non-keyframes progressively skip denoising steps to minimize computational cost. Since skipped intermediate states of non-keyframes break the temporal coherence in keyframe denoising steps, leading to visual degradation, we further introduce a latent trajectory projection module, which enables keyframes to interact with a complete and temporally consistent sequence representation. Extensive experiments on current DiT-based video generation models demonstrate our method outperforms existing baselines with higher inference speed and better visual quality.

AI.tldr: RhymeFlow speeds up DiT video generation by fully denoising only important keyframes and skipping steps for other frames, while a projection module preserves temporal consistency; this yields faster and better-looking videos without training.
AI.motivation: Standard diffusion video generation applies dense denoising to every frame at every timestep, which is computationally expensive and redundant because adjacent frames in natural videos often share correlated content and motion. Existing acceleration methods only optimize within each denoising step and do not break this rigid per-frame dense denoising constraint.
AI.method: The method decouples denoising trajectories across video frames. It first selects a sparse set of pivotal keyframes that dominate semantic evolution. These keyframes are fully denoised at every timestep, while non-keyframes progressively skip denoising steps to save computation. To mitigate temporal inconsistency caused by skipped intermediate states, a latent trajectory projection module is introduced so keyframes can interact with a temporally consistent full-sequence representation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on current DiT-based video generation models show that RhymeFlow surpasses existing baselines by providing higher inference speed together with improved visual quality.
AI.conclusion: RhymeFlow is a training-free acceleration framework for DiT-based video generation that reduces redundant denoising across frames by densely denoising only pivotal keyframes and progressively skipping steps for non-keyframes, while preserving temporal coherence through latent trajectory projection. It achieves both faster inference and better visual quality than existing baselines.

title: LLMs Can Leak Training Data But Do They Want To? A Propensity-Aware Evaluation of Memorization in LLMs
summary: Large language models can reproduce training data, but existing memorization evaluations mostly measure whether models can be forced to do so, rather than whether they do so under ordinary use. We introduce PropMe, a propensity-aware framework for memorization evaluation that contrasts prefix-based capability attacks with non-adversarial evaluations. We propose a metric transformation that, applied to existing functions, allows to create propensity metrics. We further introduce SimpleTrace, a lightweight tracing pipeline built on infini-gram that deterministically attributes model generations to large-scale training corpora and computes verbatim, near-verbatim, and propensity-transformed memorization metrics. Evaluating two fully-open models: Comma and DFM Decoder on two datasets: Common Pile and Dynaword in two languages, we find a consistent gap between capability and propensity: prefix attacks elicit substantially stronger memorization signals than generic or dataset-specific prompts, while propensity scores remain low overall. Thus, the models can reveal training data when directly elicited, but rarely do so in more common non-adversarial settings. We also find that DFM Decoder, which is continually pre-trained from Comma, exhibits reduced memorization and memorization propensity for Common Pile, confirming that memorization capability can decrease when later training emphasizes partially different data. Our results suggest, and we encourage, that memorization audits should report both worst-case extractability and ordinary leakage propensity in order to have a more comprehensive view of this phenomenon.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces PropMe and SimpleTrace to measure not just whether LLMs can leak training data, but how likely they are to do so in normal use. It finds a clear gap: models are extractable under targeted attacks, but rarely leak memorized data under ordinary prompts, and continued pretraining can even reduce memorization.
AI.motivation: Prior memorization evaluations mainly test whether language models can be induced to reveal memorized training data under attack, but they do not measure how often such leakage occurs in ordinary use. The paper aims to separate memorization capability from memorization propensity.
AI.method: The paper proposes PropMe, a propensity-aware evaluation framework that contrasts adversarial prefix-based extraction with ordinary prompting. It introduces a metric transformation to convert existing memorization measures into propensity metrics, and presents SimpleTrace, a lightweight deterministic tracing pipeline built on infini-gram to attribute generations to training corpora and compute verbatim, near-verbatim, and propensity-based scores.
AI.result: Across Comma and DFM Decoder, evaluated on Common Pile and Dynaword in two languages, prefix attacks produced much stronger memorization signals than generic or dataset-specific prompts, while propensity scores stayed low overall. DFM Decoder, continually pretrained from Comma, showed lower memorization and propensity on Common Pile, indicating later training on partially different data can reduce memorization.
AI.conclusion: Memorization audits should report both worst-case extractability and ordinary leakage propensity. The studied models can reproduce training data when directly elicited, but they rarely do so in typical non-adversarial use; continued pretraining on partially different data can reduce memorization.

title: Trust-Aware Predictive Emissions Monitoring for Gas Turbine Fleets with Limited Labelled Data
summary: Machine learning-based predictive emissions monitoring systems offer a practical alternative to direct emissions measurement, but their deployment across gas turbine fleets is challenging when emissions labels are available for only a small subset of assets. In this work, a trust-aware probabilistic framework is proposed for fleet-level gas turbine NOx prediction under limited labelled supervision. The framework combines a multi-head recurrent prediction model with learned confidence estimation, ensemble-based uncertainty quantification, auxiliary feature prediction, feature-space distance analysis, and operating-range diagnostics. These signals are calibrated on labelled data to produce interpretable per-sample trust scores, providing indicators of prediction reliability on unlabelled turbines, supporting the identification of predictions that should be treated with greater caution during fleet-level deployment. Confidence-based filtering reduces MAE from 0.202 at full coverage to 0.070 for the highest-confidence 10\% of predictions, demonstrating that confidence estimates are meaningfully related to prediction error. Unlabelled and out-of-distribution samples exhibit increased uncertainty and reduced confidence, indicating that the framework responds appropriately to distributional shift. The results show that the proposed trust framework provides actionable reliability information for emissions prediction on unlabelled turbines, supporting more transparent and trustworthy deployment of PEMS across industrial fleets.

AI.tldr: A trust-aware ML framework predicts gas-turbine NOx across mostly unlabelled fleets and assigns calibrated trust scores; higher-confidence predictions are much more accurate and the system detects distribution shift.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that direct emissions measurement is impractical at scale and ML-based PEMS are attractive, but fleet-wide deployment is difficult because only a small subset of turbines has emissions labels, making reliability assessment on unlabelled assets essential.
AI.method: The method combines a multi-head recurrent prediction model with learned confidence estimation, ensemble uncertainty quantification, auxiliary feature prediction, feature-space distance analysis, and operating-range diagnostics, then calibrates these signals on labelled turbines to produce interpretable trust scores for predictions on unlabelled assets.
AI.result: Confidence-based filtering reduced MAE from 0.202 at full coverage to 0.070 for the highest-confidence 10% of predictions, and unlabelled or out-of-distribution samples showed higher uncertainty and lower confidence, indicating the trust signals meaningfully reflect prediction risk.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a trust-aware probabilistic framework can make fleet-level NOx prediction on largely unlabelled gas turbines more transparent and deployable by providing calibrated per-sample trust scores that track prediction reliability under distribution shift.

title: ToolChoiceConfusion: Causal Minimal Tool Filtering for Reliable LLM Agents
summary:
Large language model agents increasingly rely on external tools, but larger tool menus can reduce reliability and efficiency by increasing wrong-tool calls, premature actions, and token cost. Existing tool-selection methods often optimize semantic relevance, exposing tools whose names or descriptions match the user request. We argue that relevance is insufficient: a tool may be related to the task while still being unnecessary or premature at the current step.
  We propose Causal Minimal Tool Filtering (CMTF), a training-free method that selects tools by causal sufficiency. CMTF uses lightweight precondition-effect contracts to expose only the minimal next-step tool frontier needed to advance from the current state toward the user goal. Across multi-step tool-use tasks, we compare CMTF with all-tools exposure, keyword retrieval, state-aware filtering, and causal-path ablations, measuring task success, wrong-tool calls, premature actions, tool exposure, and token cost. In the main benchmark with 102 tasks, 100 tools, four LLM backends, and 2448 task-method-model runs, CMTF matches the strongest causal baseline in aggregate success while reducing visible tools from 100 to one per step and reducing token usage by about 90% relative to all-tools exposure.

AI.tldr: Use causally sufficient, minimally necessary tools at each step. CMTF does this without training, keeping success competitive while sharply reducing tool exposure, mistakes, and token cost.
AI.motivation: As LLM agents use more external tools, exposing large tool menus harms reliability and efficiency by increasing wrong-tool calls, premature actions, and token cost. Existing methods focus too much on semantic relevance, which may expose tools that are related but not necessary or timely for the current step.
AI.method: The paper proposes Causal Minimal Tool Filtering (CMTF), a training-free filtering method that uses lightweight precondition-effect contracts to expose only the minimal next-step tool frontier needed to move from the current state toward the user goal. It is evaluated against all-tools exposure, keyword retrieval, state-aware filtering, and causal-path ablations across multi-step tool-use benchmarks.
AI.result: On a benchmark with 102 tasks, 100 tools, four LLM backends, and 2448 runs, CMTF matches the strongest causal baseline in aggregate success, reduces visible tools from 100 to about one per step, and cuts token usage by roughly 90% compared with exposing all tools.
AI.conclusion: CMTF shows that tool selection for LLM agents should be based on causal sufficiency rather than semantic relevance alone. It can preserve strong task success while drastically shrinking the visible tool set and token cost.

title: StoryVideoQA: Scaling Deep Video Understanding with a Large-Scale, Multi-Genre and Auto-Generated Dataset
summary: Video question answering (VideoQA) aims to answer questions about given videos. While existing approaches excel on factoid VideoQA, they struggle with deep video understanding (DVU), which requires the comprehension of complex storylines. This challenge arises from the inherent long-range video content, multi-faceted question types, and instance-level story elements, all of which constrain the scale and diversity of manually constructed DVU datasets.These difficulties constrain the scale and diversity of manually-constructed DVU dataset. To address these, we previously introduced StoryMind to automatically construct DVU datasets with balanced fine-grained topics. Though it can generate high-quality question-answer pairs (QAs) for TV series, it suffers significant performance degradation when handling longer and more complex movies. In this paper, we further design StoryMindv2, an enhanced multi-agent collaboration framework to generate high-quality DVU datasets for both TV series and movies. By integrating a novel supervisor-guided generation mechanism and a refined multi-reviewer voting strategy, the framework is utilized to construct StoryVideoQA, the largest DVU dataset to date, featuring over 363K QAs on 393.2 hours diverse story videos including TV series (avg. 1,635 seconds) and movies (avg. 7,878 seconds). Comprehensive evaluations of 20 state-of-the-art VideoQA methods on this large-scale benchmark reveal that they cannot fully maintain long-range character associations or construct a coherent understanding of complex storylines. To bridge this gap, we propose PlotTree, a novel video understanding agent, re-organizing long-range video content into a hierarchical plot structure, enabling efficient storyline reasoning on StoryVideoQA. Project page: https://github.com/nercms-mmap/StoryVideoQA/

AI.tldr: The paper upgrades StoryMind into StoryMindv2 to automatically generate a much larger and more reliable deep video understanding benchmark, StoryVideoQA, and shows that current VideoQA models still cannot reason well over long, complex storylines; PlotTree is introduced to improve hierarchical plot-based reasoning.
AI.motivation: Existing VideoQA methods perform well on factoid questions but fail on deep video understanding because long videos, diverse question types, and instance-level story elements make manual dataset construction difficult and limit dataset scale and diversity. The earlier StoryMind system also degrades on longer, more complex movies, motivating a stronger framework.
AI.method: The paper proposes StoryMindv2, a multi-agent collaboration framework with a supervisor-guided generation mechanism and a refined multi-reviewer voting strategy to generate question-answer pairs for deep video understanding. It uses this framework to build the StoryVideoQA dataset and further introduces PlotTree, a video understanding agent that reorganizes long videos into a hierarchical plot structure for storyline reasoning.
AI.result: Using StoryMindv2, the authors construct StoryVideoQA, the largest DVU dataset reported, with more than 363K question-answer pairs over 393.2 hours of diverse story videos, including TV series and movies. Benchmarking 20 state-of-the-art VideoQA methods shows clear limitations on deep storyline understanding, while PlotTree is proposed as a stronger reasoning approach for this setting.
AI.conclusion: StoryMindv2 can automatically build larger and higher-quality deep video understanding datasets across both TV series and movies, and evaluations on the resulting StoryVideoQA benchmark show current VideoQA models still struggle with long-range character association and coherent storyline reasoning; PlotTree helps address this by structuring videos into hierarchical plots for efficient reasoning.

title: Decomposing Factual Sycophancy in Language Models: How Size and Instruction Tuning Shape Robustness
summary: Factual sycophancy occurs when a language model abandons a correct, verifiable answer under social pressure. Because a flip occurs only when pressure toward a false answer exceeds the model's neutral preference for the truth, flip rates conflate two mechanisms: the strength of that baseline preference (truth margin), and how far pressure shifts it (manipulation sensitivity). We decompose factual sycophancy into these channels and use them to separate the effects of size and instruction tuning across 56 open-weight models spanning 0.3B-32B parameters and 13 manipulation types. We find that vulnerability is governed mainly by size, but instruction tuning changes how size acts: small instruction-tuned models can become less robust, whereas large instruction-tuned models usually become more robust. Instruction tuning primarily increases truth margin, but its behavioral effect depends on manipulation type. Scaling also changes the two channels differently: base models gain margin but become mildly more manipulation-sensitive, whereas instruction-tuned models gain margin faster and become less sensitive. Factual sycophancy is therefore not a single scalar property. Evaluations should report channel-specific, manipulation-specific, and size-conditioned robustness rather than flip rates alone.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that factual sycophancy is caused by two distinct factors: how strongly a model prefers the truth and how easily social pressure changes its answer. Across 56 models, larger models are generally more robust, and instruction tuning helps mainly by strengthening the truth preference, especially in larger models. Therefore, flip rate alone is a misleading robustness metric.
AI.motivation: Raw flip rate is an insufficient measure because it conflates two different mechanisms: whether the model initially prefers the truth, and how strongly social pressure can move it away from that truth. The paper aims to separate these mechanisms to better understand how scaling and instruction tuning affect factual robustness.
AI.method: The paper decomposes factual sycophancy into two channels: a model’s baseline preference for the correct answer (truth margin) and the shift induced by social pressure toward a false answer (manipulation sensitivity). It evaluates 56 open-weight models ranging from 0.3B to 32B parameters across 13 manipulation types, comparing the effects of model size and instruction tuning.
AI.result: Model vulnerability is driven mainly by scale, but instruction tuning modulates the effect of scale. Small instruction-tuned models can become less robust, while large instruction-tuned models usually become more robust. Instruction tuning mainly raises truth margin, though its behavioral impact varies by manipulation type. Scaling increases truth margin in both base and instruction-tuned models, but base models become slightly more manipulation-sensitive, whereas instruction-tuned models become less sensitive as they scale.
AI.conclusion: Factual sycophancy should not be treated as a single scalar metric. It arises from two separable factors: truth margin and manipulation sensitivity. Robustness evaluation should therefore report channel-specific, manipulation-specific, and size-conditioned results rather than relying only on flip rates.

title: On the training of physics-informed neural operators for solving parametric partial differential equations
summary: Physics-informed neural operators (PINOs) aim to learn solution operators for partial differential equations by using the governing physics as supervision, rather than relying solely on paired input-output simulation data. By incorporating physical constraints into the training objective, PINOs combine the cross-instance generalization of neural operators with the data efficiency of physics-informed learning. Despite this promise, how to train PINOs efficiently and robustly remains less well-understood than the training of either data-driven neural operators or physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). To bridge this gap, we examine key components of the PINO training pipeline, including architecture design, optimizer choice, loss balancing, and collocation-point sampling strategy. We study three representative operator backbones, Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), Fourier Neural Operator (FNO), and Continuous Vision Transformer (CViT), across five diverse parametric PDE systems. Our results show that CViT provides consistently strong and stable performance across the considered benchmarks. Beyond architecture, we find that several optimization pathologies previously identified in PINN training naturally arise in PINOs, including gradient conflicts and causal violation. We also find that mitigation algorithms developed for PINNs remain effective in the PINO setting. We further compare physics-informed and data-driven training under different data regimes, revealing that a carefully designed physics-informed training pipeline can match, and in some cases, outperform purely data-driven neural operators. Taken together, these findings provide a systematic empirical understanding of the optimization challenges in PINO training and inform a practical pipeline for efficient and robust physics-informed operator learning. Code and data are available at https://github.com/NanxiiChen/PI-CViT.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文系统评测了PINO怎么训练才更稳、更强。作者比较了DeepONet、FNO、CViT三种骨干，在五类PDE任务上分析架构、优化器、损失权重和采样策略，发现CViT最稳健；同时PINN常见优化问题在PINO里也存在，但已有缓解方法可直接迁移。结论是：设计得当的PINO训练流程在低数据或部分场景下可以媲美甚至超过纯数据驱动方法。/ This paper systematically studies how to train PINOs well. It compares DeepONet, FNO, and CViT on five PDE benchmarks, analyzing architecture, optimizer, loss balancing, and sampling strategy. CViT is the most robust backbone, PINN-style optimization issues also appear in PINOs, and existing mitigation methods transfer well. A well-designed PINO pipeline can match or beat purely data-driven operators, especially in some low-data settings.
AI.motivation: 尽管PINO兼具神经算子的跨样本泛化能力与物理信息学习的数据效率优势，但其高效、稳健训练机制仍缺乏系统认识。论文动机是填补这一认知空白，明确PINO训练中的关键设计与常见优化问题。/ Although PINOs promise the cross-instance generalization of neural operators and the data efficiency of physics-informed learning, efficient and robust training remains poorly understood. The motivation is to close this gap by identifying key design choices and optimization issues in PINO training.
AI.method: 论文比较了三类PINO骨干网络：DeepONet、FNO、CViT，并在五类参数化PDE系统上系统评估训练流程中的关键因素：架构设计、优化器选择、损失平衡、以及配点采样策略；同时比较了physics-informed与data-driven训练在不同数据规模下的表现。/ The paper studies three representative PINO backbones—DeepONet, FNO, and CViT—and systematically evaluates key training components across five parametric PDE systems: architecture design, optimizer choice, loss balancing, and collocation-point sampling. It also compares physics-informed and data-driven training under different data regimes.
AI.result: 主要结果包括：1) CViT在所测试基准上整体最稳定、性能最强；2) PINN中的梯度冲突和因果违背等问题也会在PINO中出现；3) 针对这些问题的PINN缓解算法在PINO中同样有效；4) 在合适设计下，physics-informed训练可达到甚至超过纯数据驱动神经算子的性能。/ Main findings: (1) CViT delivers the strongest and most stable overall performance; (2) PINN pathologies such as gradient conflict and causal violation also arise in PINOs; (3) mitigation methods developed for PINNs transfer effectively to PINOs; (4) with proper design, physics-informed training can match or even outperform purely data-driven neural operators.
AI.conclusion: 系统性的实验表明，精心设计的PINO训练流程能够高效且稳健地学习PDE解算子；CViT在多个基准上表现最稳定且强；PINN中的优化病理（如梯度冲突、因果违背）同样出现在PINO中，但相应缓解方法依然有效。/ A systematic empirical study shows that a carefully designed PINO pipeline can learn PDE solution operators efficiently and robustly; CViT is the most consistently strong and stable backbone; optimization pathologies known in PINNs also appear in PINOs, and corresponding mitigation methods remain effective.

title: TRACE: A Temporal Conditional Estimation for Multimodal Time Series Foundation Models
comment: 5 figures and 5 tables in the main paper, plus appendix
summary: Time series foundation models (TS-FMs) aim to learn generalizable temporal representations that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. In real-world multimodal settings, time series are frequently affected by temporal misalignment and partial modality missingness, where different modalities are observed at heterogeneous time scales or are partially absent. Existing approaches typically rely on naive imputation or masking strategies, which fail to account for cross-modal dependencies and often lead to misaligned or degraded representations. We propose TRACE, a conditional estimation paradigm for multimodal time series foundation model pipelines under missingness and irregular sampling, allowing incomplete target modalities to be systematically inferred from available auxiliary modalities. We evaluate TRACE on diverse multimodal benchmarks spanning healthcare and affective computing, including the MIMIC-IV clinical dataset and the CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI benchmarks for multimodal sentiment analysis. Across a range of downstream prediction tasks and missing-modality settings, TRACE consistently outperforms prior multimodal fusion approaches, demonstrating improved robustness to severe modality missingness and more reliable cross-modal representations.

AI.tldr: TRACE is a conditional estimation approach for multimodal time-series foundation models that handles irregular sampling and missing modalities better than standard imputation/masking baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal time-series methods often use naive imputation or masking, which ignore cross-modal dependencies and produce misaligned or degraded representations when modalities are missing or sampled irregularly.
AI.method: The paper proposes TRACE, a conditional estimation framework that infers incomplete target modalities from available auxiliary modalities in multimodal time series settings with temporal misalignment, missingness, and heterogeneous sampling rates.
AI.result: On MIMIC-IV, CMU-MOSI, and CMU-MOSEI across multiple downstream tasks and missing-modality settings, TRACE consistently outperforms prior multimodal fusion baselines and shows stronger robustness under severe modality missingness.
AI.conclusion: TRACE provides a stronger multimodal time-series foundation model pipeline under missing modalities and irregular sampling, yielding more robust and reliable cross-modal representations than prior fusion methods.

title: Comparison of Deep Learning Frameworks For Rice Disease Mapping From UAV Multispectral Imaging
comment: This paper has been accepted in IGARSS 2026. Copyright 2026 IEEE
summary: In this study, UAV multispectral imagery is used to segment the severity of bacterial leaf blight (BLB) in rice using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models. The evaluated architectures include U-Net with a ResNet- 101 encoder, U-Net++ with EfficientNet-B3 and EfficientNetB7, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer, all trained under a common pipeline with three input configurations (multispectral only, multispectral+NDVI, and multispectral+NDRE). Experiments are conducted using the publicly available BLB dataset with performance reported using mean IoU (mIoU), mean F1 (mF1), mean accuracy (mAcc), precision, and recall. U-Net++ with EfficientNet-B3 achieved the highest performance, with an mIoU of 97.62%. SegFormer obtained lower segmentation accuracy but comparable inference speed. Overall, the results indicate that lightweight CNN backbones remain more reliable for operational BLB monitoring while integration of vegetation indices provides small and consistent improvements. The study also highlights the value of standardised UAV datasets to compare disease mapping methods and encourages the use of CNN architectures for field implementation.

AI.tldr: UAV multispectral BLB segmentation benchmark: U-Net++ + EfficientNet-B3 wins, transformer SegFormer is faster but less accurate, and vegetation indices help a little.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to segment and quantify the severity of bacterial leaf blight in rice from UAV multispectral imagery, addressing the need for accurate, field-deployable disease monitoring methods and for standardized benchmarks to compare segmentation models fairly.
AI.method: The study evaluates multiple segmentation architectures on a public BLB rice dataset: U-Net with a ResNet-101 encoder, U-Net++ with EfficientNet-B3 and EfficientNet-B7, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer. All models are trained under a common pipeline with three input settings: multispectral imagery only, multispectral+NDVI, and multispectral+NDRE, and are assessed using mIoU, mF1, mAcc, precision, and recall.
AI.result: U-Net++ with EfficientNet-B3 achieved the best performance with 97.62% mIoU. SegFormer showed lower segmentation accuracy but similar inference speed. Adding NDVI or NDRE produced small but consistent improvements across models.
AI.conclusion: For operational UAV-based bacterial leaf blight monitoring in rice, lightweight CNN architectures are more reliable than transformer-based models, and vegetation indices give small but consistent gains. The work also supports the need for standardized UAV disease datasets for fair comparison across methods.

title: "Chi nas dal soch el sent de legn" -- Auditing Text Corpora for Lombard
summary: Several of the world's languages are still under-resourced in terms of Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools. This is mostly due to the lack of high-quality datasets to train, develop, and evaluate systems and models for several tasks, such as Machine Translation (MT). We conduct a manual audit of the parallel and monolingual corpora available for Lombard, an under-resourced language continuum from Italy. Our analysis reveals that the perceived abundance of web-scraped data is an illusion, with massive datasets plagued by severe language misidentification, boilerplate text, and non-linguistic noise. Furthermore, we analyze the orthographic composition of the valid Lombard portions across web-scraped datasets, curated corpora, and benchmarks. Our findings show conflicting orthographical systems and severe representational bias across all corpora: high-quality data is heavily skewed towards Western Lombard varieties, with Eastern ones left on the margins. This underscores the need for variety-aware, community-driven data curation rather than purely quantity-driven scraping.

AI.tldr: 这篇论文指出：伦巴第语的NLP语料不是“少”这么简单，而是“看起来多、实际上脏且失衡”。作者通过人工审计发现网页抓取数据质量很差，且高质量语料在拼写体系和方言覆盖上偏差严重，因此未来应重视社区参与和变体感知的数据建设。 / This paper shows that Lombard NLP resources are not merely scarce; they are deceptively abundant but noisy and unbalanced. A manual audit reveals poor web-scraped data quality and strong orthographic and varietal bias, implying that future dataset creation should be community-driven and variety-aware.
AI.motivation: 许多语言（包括意大利的伦巴第语连续体）在NLP中仍然资源匮乏，而机器翻译等任务依赖高质量训练、开发和评测数据。论文的动机是验证“可用数据很多”这一印象是否真实，并评估这些语料是否在质量和变体覆盖上足以支持可靠的NLP研究。 / Many languages, including the Lombard continuum in Italy, remain under-resourced in NLP, while tasks such as MT depend on high-quality training, development, and evaluation data. The paper is motivated by the need to test whether the perceived availability of Lombard data is real and whether these resources are adequate in both quality and varietal coverage for reliable NLP work.
AI.method: 作者对伦巴第语可用的平行语料和单语语料进行了人工审计，并比较了网页抓取数据、人工整理语料和基准测试中的有效伦巴第语片段，重点分析其数据质量、语言有效性、噪声类型以及正字法构成与方言代表性。 / The authors conduct a manual audit of available Lombard parallel and monolingual corpora, comparing valid Lombard portions in web-scraped datasets, curated corpora, and benchmarks, with a focus on data quality, linguistic validity, noise patterns, orthographic composition, and varietal representation.
AI.result: 研究发现：1）大规模网页抓取语料中存在严重的语言误识别、样板文本和非语言噪声，导致“海量数据”并不真正可用；2）不同语料之间存在冲突的正字法体系；3）所有语料都表现出明显的代表性偏差，高质量数据主要集中于西伦巴第语，东伦巴第语明显不足。 / The study finds that: (1) large web-scraped corpora suffer from severe language misidentification, boilerplate, and non-linguistic noise, so the apparent data volume is not truly usable; (2) orthographic systems conflict across datasets; and (3) all corpora exhibit strong representational bias, with high-quality data concentrated in Western Lombard and Eastern Lombard substantially underrepresented.
AI.conclusion: 现有伦巴第语NLP语料的“规模充足”是表象；大量网页抓取数据因语言误识别、模板噪声和非语言内容而质量很差。同时，高质量语料在正字法和方言覆盖上严重失衡，尤其偏向西伦巴第语，东部变体被边缘化。因此，论文主张采用面向变体、社区驱动的数据整理，而不是单纯追求抓取数量。 / The apparent abundance of Lombard NLP data is misleading: much web-scraped material is low quality because of language misidentification, boilerplate, and non-linguistic noise. High-quality resources are also orthographically inconsistent and heavily biased toward Western Lombard, leaving Eastern varieties underrepresented. The paper therefore argues for variety-aware, community-driven curation rather than quantity-driven scraping.

title: Learning to model pediatric asthma exacerbation from multiple risk factors: a case study in coastal Virginia
summary: Childhood asthma is a common illness exacerbated by air pollution as well as meteorological and neighborhood-level socioeconomic factors. Modeling asthma exacerbation (AE) in large spatiotemporal datasets requires disentangling impacts from multiple contributors. In this case study, we compared three techniques that balance predictive power with interpretability to predict AE in Hampton Roads, a coastal Virginia region comprising 7 cities and over 1.5 million people. After collating ambient air pollution measurements, weather data, and measures of neighborhood opportunity, we modeled zip code-level acute AE visits to a regional children's hospital and affiliated providers from 2018-2023. Generalized linear models (GLM) provided a baseline while neural networks (NN) served as a maximally predictive target. To bridge between statistical models and deep learning, we developed a framework based on sparse dictionary learning to identify and interpret parsimonious nonlinear interacting equations. After comparing each model's predictive performance, we estimated relative risks for AE due to input exposure variables and found consensus across frameworks. Our work links statistical and interpretable machine learning models to highlight possible synergistic interactions influencing AE, and may enable future studies to guide public health interventions in coastal Virginia.

AI.tldr: This paper predicts childhood asthma exacerbations in coastal Virginia using pollution, weather, and neighborhood data, comparing GLM, neural networks, and a new sparse dictionary learning method. The key finding is that interpretable nonlinear models can approach strong predictive performance while revealing synergistic risk factors consistent across methods.
AI.motivation: Childhood asthma exacerbation is influenced by multiple environmental and socioeconomic factors that vary across space and time. Large spatiotemporal datasets make it difficult to disentangle these contributors, creating a need for models that balance predictive performance with interpretability.
AI.method: The authors assembled zip code-level data from 2018-2023 in Hampton Roads, including ambient air pollution, weather variables, neighborhood opportunity measures, and acute childhood asthma exacerbation visits. They compared generalized linear models, neural networks, and an interpretable sparse dictionary learning framework designed to recover parsimonious nonlinear interacting equations.
AI.result: The models were compared on predictive performance, with GLM as a baseline and neural networks as a high-performance reference. The sparse dictionary learning approach provided interpretable nonlinear interaction structures, and relative risk estimates for exposure variables showed broad agreement across modeling frameworks.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that combining statistical models with interpretable machine learning can capture nonlinear and interacting drivers of childhood asthma exacerbation while retaining interpretability, and that these models can support future public health interventions in coastal Virginia.

title: Multi-ResNets for Subspace Preconditioning in Constrained Optimization
summary: We propose MResOpt, a staged residual neural network architecture for constrained optimization problems. Our architecture fits within predict-complete-correct pipelines and decomposes constraint satisfaction by priority through intermediate re-completion and stage-aware losses. The framework enables domain-informed ordered constraint satisfaction which allows the network to utilize ordinal structure when present. Under an idealized infinite-width regime, we show that our design behaves as sequential Gaussian Process regression. On synthetic QP, QCQP, and SOCP benchmarks, the staged architecture improves high-priority constraint satisfaction across convex and non-convex settings. On line-flow-constrained AC optimal power flow, we introduce a physics-motivated constraint ordering and show that MResOpt supports a learned division of labor that keeps iterates on the equality manifold, achieving substantially lower high-priority violation than reprojected baselines while remaining computationally efficient.

AI.tldr: MResOpt is a staged residual neural solver for constrained optimization that satisfies constraints in priority order; it has a GP interpretation at infinite width and outperforms reprojected baselines on several benchmarks, especially for the most important constraints.
AI.motivation: Standard learned solvers for constrained optimization often treat all constraints uniformly, which can be inefficient or suboptimal when some constraints are more important or naturally ordered. The authors aim to build a domain-informed architecture that decomposes feasibility by priority, improves satisfaction of critical constraints, and remains computationally efficient.
AI.method: The paper proposes MResOpt, a staged residual network embedded in a predict-complete-correct pipeline. It performs intermediate re-completion at multiple stages, applies stage-aware losses, and enforces constraints by priority so the model can exploit ordinal structure. The method is evaluated on synthetic QP, QCQP, SOCP tasks and AC optimal power flow with a physics-motivated constraint ordering.
AI.result: On synthetic convex and non-convex benchmarks, MResOpt improves satisfaction of high-priority constraints. On line-flow-constrained AC optimal power flow, it learns a useful division of labor across stages, keeps iterates on the equality manifold, and achieves substantially lower high-priority constraint violation than reprojected baselines while maintaining computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: MResOpt is an effective staged residual neural architecture for constrained optimization that prioritizes constraint satisfaction in ordered stages, achieves better high-priority feasibility than standard reprojected baselines, preserves efficiency, and admits an interpretable infinite-width view as sequential Gaussian Process regression.

title: Physics in 2-Steps: Locking Motion Priors Before Visual Refinement Erases Them
summary: Image-to-Video diffusion models leverage input images to generate visually stunning content, yet frequently produce motion that violates physical laws. We reveal a surprising finding: a 2-step generation often exhibits better physical consistency than a 50-step output from the same model. Through spectral analysis, we trace this to phase erosion during denoising; the phase degrades significantly (dropping by $\approx 18\%$ from step 2 to step 50), whereas the magnitude remains relatively stable. Building on this insight, we propose PhaseLock, a training-free framework that preserves the valid motion priors from few-step inference throughout the denoising trajectory. Rather than relying on full-step inference for physical consistency, PhaseLock extracts a motion prior from just 2 steps and enforces it onto high-fidelity generation via Latent Delta Guidance. Our approach effectively mitigates phase degradation, improving physical consistency by an average of 6.2 points across diverse models while largely maintaining visual fidelity, with negligible overhead ($1.06\times$ time, $1.02\times$ memory) and reduced reliance on expensive external guidance methods ($\sim5\times$ time).

AI.tldr: Few-step diffusion preserves better motion phase than long denoising; PhaseLock keeps that early motion prior throughout generation, improving physical consistency cheaply and without training.
AI.motivation: Existing image-to-video diffusion models generate visually appealing videos but often produce motion that violates physical laws. The authors aim to understand why this happens and how to improve physical consistency without expensive retraining or external guidance.
AI.method: The authors perform spectral analysis of the denoising trajectory, identify phase degradation as the key issue, and propose PhaseLock, a training-free method that extracts motion priors from 2-step inference and injects them into later high-fidelity denoising using Latent Delta Guidance.
AI.result: They find that 2-step generation can be more physically consistent than 50-step generation, with phase dropping by about 18% from step 2 to step 50 while magnitude stays stable. PhaseLock improves physical consistency by an average of 6.2 points across multiple models, largely preserves visual fidelity, incurs only 1.06x runtime and 1.02x memory overhead, and is much cheaper than external guidance methods.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that physical inconsistency in image-to-video diffusion mainly stems from phase erosion during long denoising, and that preserving early-step phase information can substantially improve motion realism with minimal overhead.

title: EDIT: Evidence-Diagnosed Intervention Training for Rule-Faithful LLM Grading
summary: Reliable rubric grading requires more than accurate score prediction. Each judgement must be grounded in the mark scheme and evidence from the student answer. Existing credit-assignment and intervention methods, primarily designed for self-contained reasoning tasks such as mathematics reasoning, struggle in this setting because they do not identify where grading reasoning goes wrong or how the model's belief about the final mark changes during reasoning. We propose Evidence-Diagnosed Intervention Training (EDIT), a two-phase framework for training more rubric-faithful LLM graders. First, EDIT-SFT locates problematic reasoning steps using internal model signals: posterior belief over the final mark and input-grounding scores. It then revises only these local steps with help from a rubric checklist. Second, EDIT-RL calibrates the grader with belief-guided reward shaping, penalising large harmful belief drifts while still allowing helpful exploration. Experiments on two real-world, multi-subject grading benchmarks demonstrate that EDIT consistently outperforms strong supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning baselines on both in-domain and out-of-domain splits, with ablation studies confirming that internal-state diagnostics drive these gains.

AI.tldr: EDIT trains LLM graders to follow rubrics more faithfully by detecting flawed grading steps using internal belief and grounding signals, then refining and calibrating reasoning; it beats standard SFT and RL baselines on real grading benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Accurate score prediction alone is insufficient for reliable rubric grading. Each grading decision must be grounded in the rubric and supported by evidence from the student response. Existing intervention and credit-assignment methods are mainly built for self-contained reasoning tasks like math and do not adequately diagnose where grading reasoning fails or how belief about the final score evolves during reasoning.
AI.method: The paper proposes a two-phase framework called EDIT. In EDIT-SFT, the model uses internal signals, specifically posterior belief over the final mark and input-grounding scores, to identify problematic reasoning steps and locally revise them with a rubric checklist. In EDIT-RL, the model is further trained with belief-guided reward shaping that penalizes harmful belief drift while allowing beneficial exploration.
AI.result: On two real-world multi-subject grading benchmarks, EDIT consistently surpasses strong supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning baselines on both in-domain and out-of-domain splits. Ablation studies show that the gains come from the internal-state diagnostic signals used by the framework.
AI.conclusion: EDIT improves rubric-faithful LLM grading by diagnosing faulty reasoning steps and calibrating belief changes during grading, outperforming strong SFT and RL baselines across in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks.

title: Learning to Route LLMs from Implicit Cost-Performance Preferences via Meta-Learning
summary: Large language models (LLMs) present a trade-off between performance and cost, where more powerful models incur greater expense. LLM routing aims to mitigate expenses while maintaining performance by sending queries to the most suitable model. However, existing methods cannot perform well for different user cost-performance preferences. To address this gap, we introduce a novel perceptive LLM routing paradigm for personalized and user-centric cost-performance optimization, which efficiently learns users' implicit preferences through little interaction. To handle the challenge of heterogeneous user needs, we formulate preference profiles as a set of distinct tasks in contextual bandit and propose MetaRouter, a meta-learning framework designed for preference-aware LLM routing. Experimental results show that MetaRouter outperforms strong baselines on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks. Furthermore, it exhibits high efficiency in learning user preferences, robustness to changes in the routable LLMs, and scalability to multi-model routing.

AI.tldr: MetaRouter uses meta-learning plus contextual bandits to personalize LLM routing, learning each user’s cost-quality preference from little feedback and outperforming prior routing methods across accuracy, robustness, and scalability.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM routing methods reduce cost while preserving quality, but they do not adapt well to heterogeneous user-specific cost-performance preferences. The paper aims to provide personalized, user-centric routing that can learn these preferences efficiently with minimal interaction.
AI.method: The paper formulates personalized LLM routing as a set of contextual bandit tasks, where each task corresponds to a user preference profile. It then applies meta-learning in a framework called MetaRouter to quickly infer users’ implicit cost-performance preferences from limited interactions and route queries to the most suitable LLM.
AI.result: Experiments show that MetaRouter surpasses strong baselines on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks. It also learns user preferences efficiently, stays robust when the available LLM set changes, and scales well to routing across multiple models.
AI.conclusion: MetaRouter is an effective preference-aware LLM routing framework that better balances cost and performance for different users, generalizes to unseen preference settings, and remains efficient, robust, and scalable.

title: AIS-Based Vessel Trajectory Prediction Using Memory-Augmented Neural Networks
summary: Accurate vessel trajectory prediction is essential for safe and efficient maritime operations, enabling collision avoidance and supporting route optimization. Although memory-augmented neural networks have recently shown strong performance in pedestrian and road-vehicle trajectory prediction by selectively retrieving relevant information from an external memory, their potential for vessel trajectory prediction remains underexplored. This paper presents an empirical investigation of memory-based trajectory prediction using Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. Experiments on data from the Gulf of Mexico and the New York Bight demonstrate consistent and substantial performance gains over a range of deep learning baselines that do not incorporate an external memory.

AI.tldr: The paper tests memory-augmented trajectory models on AIS vessel data and shows they predict ship movements better than standard deep learning baselines in two real-world maritime regions.
AI.motivation: Accurate vessel trajectory prediction is important for collision avoidance and route optimization in maritime operations. While memory-augmented models have worked well for pedestrians and road vehicles, their use for vessel prediction has not been sufficiently explored.
AI.method: The paper empirically studies memory-based trajectory prediction for vessels by applying a memory-augmented neural network to Automatic Identification System (AIS) trajectory data and comparing it against multiple deep learning baselines that do not use external memory.
AI.result: On datasets from the Gulf of Mexico and the New York Bight, the memory-based approach consistently outperforms a range of non-memory deep learning baselines by a substantial margin.
AI.conclusion: Memory-augmented neural networks are effective for vessel trajectory prediction with AIS data, producing consistent and substantial improvements over deep learning baselines without external memory across two maritime regions.

title: GMBFormer: An NDVI-Guided Global Memory Bank Transformer for Urban Green-Space Extraction from Ultra-High-Resolution Imagery
summary: Urban green-space extraction from ultra-high-resolution (UHR) imagery is commonly performed patch by patch, which limits semantic reuse among spatially separated but visually similar vegetation patterns. Directly injecting the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) into red-green-blue (RGB) backbones can also blur the roles of visual appearance learning and physical vegetation confidence. We propose GMBFormer, a SegFormer-based framework that replaces adjacency-driven feature propagation with selective, similarity-driven prototype retrieval. Only RGB channels enter the backbone and decoder, while NDVI is decoupled as a physics-informed gate that admits high-confidence vegetation descriptors into a compact global memory bank through momentum updates. During training and inference, the current patch queries stored prototypes through memory-mediated cross-attention, and the retrieved response is integrated with bounded overhead. Experiments use a self-constructed Chengdu UHR dataset with 7,700 labeled 512 x 512 patches and two reduced-label settings derived from the public International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ISPRS) Potsdam dataset. Under the same training and evaluation protocol, GMBFormer obtains mean intersection over union (mIoU)/mean Dice (mDice) scores of 89.25%/94.31%, 92.17%/95.92%, and 83.72%/90.86%, respectively, improving the controlled SegFormer-B4 baseline in each setting. Ablation studies indicate that decoupled NDVI admission, memory retrieval, capacity, and momentum jointly shape the final performance.

AI.tldr: GMBFormer improves UHR urban green-space segmentation by keeping RGB feature learning separate from NDVI-based vegetation confidence and retrieving similar vegetation prototypes from a global memory bank, leading to better mIoU and Dice than SegFormer-B4.
AI.motivation: Patch-wise urban green-space extraction from UHR imagery cannot effectively reuse semantics across distant but visually similar vegetation regions. In addition, directly injecting NDVI into RGB backbones mixes appearance learning with physical vegetation cues, potentially weakening both roles.
AI.method: The paper proposes GMBFormer, a SegFormer-based segmentation framework where only RGB images are fed into the backbone and decoder, while NDVI is used separately as a physics-informed gate to admit high-confidence vegetation descriptors into a momentum-updated compact global memory bank. Current patches retrieve similar prototypes through memory-mediated cross-attention during training and inference.
AI.result: On a self-constructed Chengdu UHR dataset and two reduced-label ISPRS Potsdam settings, GMBFormer achieved mIoU/mDice scores of 89.25%/94.31%, 92.17%/95.92%, and 83.72%/90.86%, outperforming the controlled SegFormer-B4 baseline in all settings. Ablation studies show that NDVI decoupled admission, memory retrieval, bank capacity, and momentum all contribute to performance.
AI.conclusion: GMBFormer effectively improves urban green-space extraction from ultra-high-resolution imagery by decoupling NDVI from RGB feature learning and using a selective global memory bank for prototype retrieval, yielding consistent gains over the SegFormer-B4 baseline across all evaluated settings.

title: Emergent Language as an Approach to Conscious AI
summary: The question of whether artificial systems can be conscious remains open, in part because existing approaches either evaluate systems against theory-derived checklists (discriminative) or engineer consciousness-inspired modules directly (architectural); both leave open whether observed structures are artifacts of human language priors. We propose a generative methodology: emergent language (EL) in multi-agent reinforcement learning, where agents start from minimal (no language, no concept of self, minimal exposure to human text) and develop communication under task pressure alone, ensuring causal attributability to task demands rather than inherited human language priors. We position our methodology by discussing how EL serves as a generative tool for studying consciousness-relevant structure, including the role of environment complexity and the interpretation of emergent communication. As a proof of concept, we instantiate this methodology in a minimal environment and show that agents develop self-referential communication, including an echo-mismatch detection circuit that is not predicted by task structure or architecture alone but emerges from a specific environmental affordance.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using emergent language in multi-agent RL as a cleaner way to study consciousness-like structures. In a minimal setup, agents spontaneously develop self-referential signals and an unexpected echo-mismatch detection mechanism, suggesting environment-driven emergence beyond built-in design or human language bias.
AI.motivation: The motivation is that prior approaches to machine consciousness are limited: discriminative approaches rely on theory-driven checklists, and architectural approaches build in consciousness-inspired modules. Both may reflect human language priors rather than genuinely task-induced structures. The paper seeks a method with clearer causal attribution.
AI.method: The authors propose a generative method using emergent language in multi-agent reinforcement learning. Agents begin with no language, no self-concept, and minimal human-text exposure, then develop communication purely under task pressure. A proof-of-concept is implemented in a minimal environment to observe what communication structures emerge.
AI.result: The proof-of-concept shows that agents develop self-referential communication. It also reveals an echo-mismatch detection circuit that is not directly predicted by the task structure or architecture alone, but instead emerges from a specific environmental affordance.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that emergent language in multi-agent reinforcement learning can serve as a generative methodology for probing consciousness-relevant structures without relying on human language priors, and that even a minimal environment can give rise to self-referential communication and an emergent echo-mismatch detection circuit shaped by environmental affordances.

title: A Machine Learning-Based Framework for Discovering Huntington's Disease Stages: Integrating Graph Representation Learning and clustering to Uncover Progression Dynamics in Longitudinal Enroll-HD Dataset
comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 10th International Conference on Medical and Health Informatics (ICMHI 2026), Association for Computing Machinery (ACM)
summary: Huntington's disease (HD) is a progressive brain disorder that gradually affects movement, cognitive function, and behavior. Identifying the stage of the disease accurately and consistently is important for understanding its course, grouping patients, personalized care, and discovering treatment. Existing clinical staging frameworks rely primarily on predefined clinical measurement thresholds and clinical expert decisions, yet these discrete cut-offs may obscure meaningful intra-stage variability and remain vulnerable to inter-rater differences, especially in motor and functional assessments. To address these limitations, we developed an unsupervised machine learning framework based on dynamic graph representation learning to capture temporal relationships within and across patients from longitudinal clinical measurements. Using the learned representations, we applied K-means++ clustering to identify well-separated groups. We then iteratively increased the number of clusters (k), using stability analysis to assess robustness and reveal additional meaningful clusters beyond the initial optimal solution. We applied the framework to 302 individuals from the Enroll-HD cohort (1,477 visits, 44 clinical variables per visit; 80% manifest participants), enabling data-driven discovery of HD stages reflecting natural clinical progression. Despite the limited cohort size, the proposed framework achieved robust clustering performance using a four-dimensional latent space, identifying four meaningful and statistically distinct disease stages through clustering stability analysis. Each stage corresponded to well-defined clinical measurement boundaries, with minimal overlap compared to previously established clinical staging methods.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an unsupervised dynamic graph learning approach for Huntington's disease staging and finds four robust, clinically meaningful stages from longitudinal cohort data, improving on traditional cutoff-based staging.
AI.motivation: Existing Huntington's disease staging systems depend on predefined clinical cutoffs and expert judgment, which can hide variability within stages and are susceptible to inter-rater inconsistency, particularly for motor and functional assessments. A more objective, data-driven method is needed to capture natural disease progression from longitudinal data.
AI.method: The study used longitudinal clinical measurements from 302 Enroll-HD participants and modeled temporal within-patient and across-patient relationships using dynamic graph representation learning. The learned low-dimensional latent representations were then clustered with K-means++, and the number of clusters was iteratively increased with stability analysis to determine robust and meaningful disease subgroups.
AI.result: Using 1,477 visits and 44 clinical variables per visit, the framework achieved robust clustering in a four-dimensional latent space and identified four meaningful disease stages. These stages were statistically distinct, aligned with interpretable clinical measurement boundaries, and showed minimal overlap compared with previously established staging approaches.
AI.conclusion: A data-driven unsupervised framework based on dynamic graph representation learning can robustly identify four clinically meaningful and statistically distinct Huntington's disease stages from longitudinal data, offering clearer stage boundaries and less overlap than conventional threshold-based clinical staging methods.

title: LLM Self-Recognition: Steering and Retrieving Activation Signatures
comment: To appear in Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)
summary: Recent advances in interpretability suggest that large language models (LLMs) implicitly encode signals in their generated text that enable self-recognition of their outputs. We demonstrate that this capability is reliable, even in low-entropy scenarios, and that it can be amplified through targeted intervention. By steering the internal residual stream during generation with a random sparse vector, we create a detectable fingerprint that enables attribution of a given text to a specific LLM. This signal is recoverable from the activations of an LLM used as a detector, achieving over 98% accuracy across multiple detection settings while preserving the quality of generated text. As AI-generated content proliferates, this approach offers a practical alternative to traditional detectors by leveraging the model's natural representation structure for attribution rather than embedding a signal externally. Our contributions include: (i) establishing reliable self-recognition capabilities in LLMs, (ii) a simple steering mechanism enabling multi-LLM identification with no quality degradation, (iii) demonstrating that activation spaces contain exploitable structure for encoding signals without semantic interference.

AI.tldr: LLMs can recognize and reveal their own generation signatures. By injecting a sparse residual-stream fingerprint during decoding and reading it from detector-model activations, the authors get >98% source-attribution accuracy without degrading output quality.
AI.motivation: Traditional AI-text detectors often rely on surface statistics or externally embedded watermarks, which can be brittle or intrusive. The paper is motivated by the idea that LLMs may already encode source-identifying signals internally, and that exploiting this native representational structure could yield a more practical attribution method.
AI.method: The paper studies self-recognition in LLMs and introduces a lightweight intervention that adds a random sparse steering vector into the residual stream during generation. A detector LLM then reads activation patterns to recover this fingerprint and attribute text to its source model across multiple settings.
AI.result: The approach achieves over 98% attribution accuracy in several detection settings, including low-entropy generation scenarios, while maintaining the quality of generated text. It also shows that activation spaces can encode identifiable signals without interfering with semantics.
AI.conclusion: LLMs contain intrinsic, recoverable attribution signals in their activation dynamics, and these signals can be strengthened through residual-stream steering to enable high-accuracy identification of which model generated a text, without harming text quality.

title: Visual Commonsense Driven Knowledge Refinements for Scene Graph Generation
summary: Learning-driven Scene Graph Generation (SGG) models excel on frequent relation types but degrade sharply under annotation sparsity, failing to capture reliable visual commonsense knowledge. We propose a model-agnostic, semantically-guided knowledge refinement framework that systematically mines commonsense-grounded constraints from training data - capturing spatial, functional, and qualitative relational regularities - and uses general declarative commonsense reasoning to correct and refine ranked SGG predictions at inference time. The framework requires no manual rule authoring, no model retraining, and transfers across datasets and architectures. On three standard benchmarks, we obtain consistent improvements over strong baselines, demonstrating that structured visual commonsense reasoning over deep scene semantics is a practical and effective complement to purely learning-based scene graph generation.

AI.tldr: A training-free, model-agnostic commonsense refinement layer improves scene graph generation by automatically mining relational constraints and correcting predictions at inference time.
AI.motivation: Existing learning-based SGG models perform well on frequent relation classes but fail under annotation sparsity, limiting their ability to capture reliable visual commonsense knowledge. The work is motivated by the need to improve generalization and reasoning without requiring costly retraining or manual rule engineering.
AI.method: The paper proposes a model-agnostic, semantically-guided knowledge refinement framework that automatically mines commonsense constraints from training data, including spatial, functional, and qualitative relational regularities, and applies declarative commonsense reasoning to refine ranked SGG predictions during inference.
AI.result: The framework achieves consistent improvements over strong baselines on three standard benchmarks and transfers across different datasets and model architectures.
AI.conclusion: Structured visual commonsense reasoning can effectively complement purely learning-based scene graph generation, improving robustness under sparse annotations without retraining or manual rule design.

title: CollabSim: A CSCW-Grounded Methodology for Investigating Collaborative Competence of LLM Agents through Controlled Multi-Agent Experiments
summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models have shown growing promise, with their effectiveness resting on agents' ability to coordinate through text-based channels much as human teams do. Yet recent study suggests that MAS often falter not because agents lack individual task-solving ability, but because they lack collaborative competence: the capacity to establish common ground, maintain shared task understanding, balance individual and collective incentives, and repair misalignment as interaction unfolds. Decades of research in Computer-Supported Cooperative Work have characterized these requirements for human teams coordinating under constrained communication, yet existing MAS evaluations focus mainly on task outcomes or single-agent proficiency in reasoning, planning, and tool use. To enable a systematic analysis of agents' collaborative competence in MAS, we introduce CollabSim, a configurable simulation framework that combines a theory-grounded definition of collaborative capabilities, controlled manipulation of interaction conditions, and action-level probing of agents' internal states. Experiments across four LLMs show that CollabSim can capture condition effects, separate model performance patterns, and reveal task-dependent effects of agent design.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a theory-based simulator, CollabSim, to measure how well LLM agents actually collaborate, and shows it can reveal collaboration strengths and weaknesses that standard task metrics miss.
AI.motivation: Existing evaluations of LLM-based multi-agent systems mainly measure task success or single-agent abilities, but often miss the core issue that failures stem from weak collaboration rather than weak individual problem solving.
AI.method: The paper proposes CollabSim, a configurable simulation framework grounded in CSCW theory that manipulates communication conditions and probes agent actions and internal states to assess collaboration capabilities.
AI.result: Experiments on four LLMs show that CollabSim detects condition-dependent effects, differentiates performance patterns across models, and uncovers task-specific impacts of agent design.
AI.conclusion: CollabSim enables systematic evaluation of collaborative competence in LLM-based multi-agent systems, distinguishing how different models and agent designs behave under varying interaction conditions.

title: Non-Negative Matrix Factorization for Event Data
summary: Continuous-time event data, in which entities emit instantaneous events over time, arises naturally across many domains such as neuroscience, seismology, and social networks. Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) is a natural tool to uncover interpretable structure in such data, but it has so far only been applied after binning or smoothing the entity-level counting measures. This preprocessing step comes with the risk of erasing entity-level heterogeneities and fine-grained temporal features. In this paper, we introduce EventNMF, a continuous-time non-negative factorization model that operates directly on event times: each entity's events are modeled as a Poisson process whose intensity factorizes through a non-negative B-spline basis, and a simple estimation procedure recovers interpretable temporal templates shared across entities. The resulting method is mathematically principled, easy to implement, and computationally efficient. We further show that standard binned-count approaches arise as the special case of degree-zero splines, explore bias-variance tradeoffs and compare against existing methods on a synthetic latent factor model, and demonstrate the effectiveness of EventNMF on several real-world applications.

AI.tldr: EventNMF is a continuous-time NMF method for event timestamps that uses Poisson processes and non-negative B-splines to learn interpretable shared temporal patterns more faithfully than binning-based approaches.
AI.motivation: Existing NMF approaches for event data usually require binning or smoothing continuous-time events into counts, which can obscure entity-level heterogeneity and fine temporal structure. The paper aims to avoid this information loss by factorizing directly in continuous time.
AI.method: The paper proposes EventNMF, where each entity’s event sequence is modeled as a Poisson process with an intensity function factorized into non-negative entity weights and non-negative B-spline temporal basis components. Estimation is performed with a simple procedure that yields interpretable temporal templates and computational efficiency.
AI.result: The authors show that binned-count NMF is a special case corresponding to degree-zero splines, analyze bias-variance tradeoffs, outperform or compare favorably with existing methods on synthetic latent factor data, and demonstrate effectiveness on multiple real-world datasets.
AI.conclusion: EventNMF provides a principled and efficient way to perform non-negative factorization directly on continuous-time event data without binning or smoothing, recovering interpretable shared temporal patterns while preserving fine-grained timing information.

title: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions
summary: GUI agents - vision-based models that control desktops, web browsers, and mobile devices through graphical user interfaces - promise to automate a wide range of digital tasks. While million-scale datasets have enabled substantial progress on click-grounding, drag grounding (e.g. drag-and-drop, swipe, highlight) data remains an order of magnitude smaller and current models fall short on complex drag-based interactions. We introduce DragOn, a drag grounding benchmark and training dataset covering four domains: text highlighting, cell selection, element resizing and slider manipulation. The dataset comprises 286K training screenshots and 3.5M training tasks, plus a 2000-example held-out evaluation suite. We evaluate proprietary (GPT, Claude) and open-weight (Qwen, Kimi, Holo) models, as well as a Qwen VLM fine-tuned on our training data. Results suggest that our dataset could improve performance of state-of-the-art models on downstream computer-use tasks.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces DragOn, a large-scale benchmark and dataset for drag-based GUI actions, addressing a key data bottleneck beyond click grounding. Experiments on several VLMs show that drag interactions remain challenging, but the new dataset can improve model performance on real computer-use tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing GUI-agent progress has been driven mainly by large click-grounding datasets, while drag-grounding data is much smaller and current models perform poorly on complex drag interactions. The work is motivated by the need for a dedicated large-scale resource to train and evaluate drag-based GUI control.
AI.method: The paper introduces DragOn, a drag-grounding benchmark and training dataset spanning four drag interaction domains: text highlighting, cell selection, element resizing, and slider manipulation. It includes 286K training screenshots, 3.5M training tasks, and a 2,000-example held-out evaluation set. The authors evaluate both proprietary and open-weight vision-language models, and also fine-tune a Qwen VLM on the new training data.
AI.result: Across evaluations on proprietary and open-weight models, the study finds that current models still struggle with drag-based interactions, while training with DragOn appears to improve performance, including for a fine-tuned Qwen VLM, suggesting practical benefit for downstream computer-use tasks.
AI.conclusion: DragOn fills a major gap in GUI-agent training and evaluation for drag-based interactions, and the reported experiments indicate that adding this dataset can improve state-of-the-art models on downstream computer-use tasks.

title: EasyLens: A Training-Free Plug-and-Play Subtle-Lesion Representation Amplifier for Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) have shown increasing potential for clinical image interpretation, including lesion detection and report generation. However, their practical utility remains limited by insufficient sensitivity to subtle lesions, whose visual evidence is often sparse, low-contrast, and embedded within complex anatomical context. As local visual tokens are aggregated, these weak lesion cues can become underrepresented in global image representations, making them difficult for medical VLMs to recognize. Existing efforts to improve lesion sensitivity mainly rely on medical-domain vision-encoder pre-training, clinical-term-guided alignment, or trainable pathological representation enhancement. Although effective, these approaches usually require additional training or model-specific adaptation and may overfit to particular disease morphologies, limiting their applicability to frozen medical VLMs. To address these limitations, we propose EasyLens, a training-free plug-and-play subtle-lesion representation amplifier for medical VLMs. EasyLens first constructs EasyBank, a pathology-anatomy prototype space that provides lesion-related prototypes and anatomy-aware normal references for comparing suspicious patches against both pathological and normal anatomical patterns. To avoid blindly amplifying normal tissues, EasyTag selects lesion-relevant patches through counterfactual prototype reasoning. To counteract the dilution of subtle lesion cues in global image representations, EasyAmplifier strengthens the selected lesion-relevant patch representations through morphology-guided residual enhancement, thereby increasing their contribution to the global image embedding. Experiments on multiple medical image datasets and frozen medical VLM backbones show that EasyLens improves subtle-lesion detection and outperforms existing encoder-enhancement baselines.

AI.tldr: EasyLens是一种面向冻结医学VLM的免训练病灶增强模块：先用病理-解剖原型识别可疑病灶patch，再有选择地增强其特征，从而让细微病灶在线索被全局池化稀释前得到更强表示。 / EasyLens is a training-free module for frozen medical VLMs that identifies suspicious lesion patches using pathology-anatomy prototypes and selectively amplifies them so subtle lesion cues survive global representation aggregation.
AI.motivation: 动机在于医学VLM对细微病灶不够敏感，因为这类病灶通常视觉证据稀疏、低对比度，并嵌入复杂解剖背景中；在局部视觉token聚合为全局表示时，弱病灶线索容易被稀释。现有提升方法往往需要额外训练或模型适配，并可能过拟合特定病种形态，因此不适用于冻结的通用医学VLM。 / The motivation is that medical VLMs are insufficiently sensitive to subtle lesions because their cues are sparse, low-contrast, and embedded in complex anatomy; these weak signals get diluted during aggregation into global representations. Existing improvements usually require extra training or model-specific adaptation and may overfit to specific disease morphologies, limiting applicability to frozen medical VLMs.
AI.method: 方法上，EasyLens包含三个核心部分：1) EasyBank：构建病理-解剖原型空间，提供病灶原型和具解剖感知的正常参考；2) EasyTag：通过反事实原型推理选择与病灶相关的可疑patch，避免误增强正常组织；3) EasyAmplifier：通过形态引导的残差增强强化选中patch的表征，提高其在全局图像嵌入中的贡献。 / Methodologically, EasyLens has three components: (1) EasyBank, which builds a pathology-anatomy prototype space with lesion prototypes and anatomy-aware normal references; (2) EasyTag, which selects lesion-relevant suspicious patches via counterfactual prototype reasoning to avoid amplifying normal tissue; and (3) EasyAmplifier, which uses morphology-guided residual enhancement to strengthen selected patch features and increase their contribution to the global image embedding.
AI.result: 实验结果表明，在多个医学图像数据集和冻结医学VLM骨干上，EasyLens能够提升细微病灶检测性能，并且优于已有的编码器增强类基线方法。 / Results show that across multiple medical image datasets and frozen medical VLM backbones, EasyLens improves subtle-lesion detection and surpasses existing encoder-enhancement baselines.
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出了EasyLens，一种无需训练、即插即用的细微病灶表征增强方法，可在冻结的医学视觉语言模型上提升细微病灶检测能力，并优于现有编码器增强基线。 / The paper concludes that EasyLens, a training-free and plug-and-play subtle-lesion representation amplifier, improves subtle-lesion detection on frozen medical VLMs and outperforms existing encoder-enhancement baselines.

title: A Komi-Yazva--Russian Parallel Corpus and Evaluation Protocol for Zero- and Few-Shot LLM Translation
summary: We present the first Komi-Yazva--Russian parallel corpus together with an explicit evaluation protocol for studying LLM translation in an endangered, extremely low-resource setting. The dataset contains 457 aligned sentence pairs from 74 narrative texts and is accompanied by documented provenance, sentence-level alignment, and story identifiers that enable leakage-aware evaluation. We use this setup to compare modern large language models on Komi-Yazva-to-Russian translation under severe parallel-data scarcity in zero-shot and retrieval-based few-shot regimes. The protocol includes story-level cross-validation, deterministic retrieval for few-shot prompting, strict validation of generated outputs, complementary reference-based and judge-based metrics, and story-level uncertainty estimates. Across models, LLMs produce non-trivial translations, but performance varies strongly by model family and prompting regime. Retrieval-based few-shot prompting consistently improves over zero-shot prompting, while gains beyond a small retrieved context remain limited. The results show that evaluative conclusions in this setting depend materially on metric choice and failure handling, so the paper frames the corpus as both a dataset contribution and a reproducible evaluation testbed for endangered-language machine translation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the first Komi-Yazva--Russian parallel corpus and a strict evaluation protocol for testing LLM translation in an endangered low-resource language. LLMs can translate somewhat effectively, few-shot retrieval helps reliably, but extra context helps only a little, and conclusions depend heavily on how translation quality is measured.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to enable rigorous study of machine translation for Komi-Yazva, an endangered and extremely low-resource language, where standard datasets and evaluation setups are lacking and where leakage and unstable conclusions can easily distort results.
AI.method: The authors build the first Komi-Yazva--Russian parallel corpus with 457 aligned sentence pairs from 74 narrative texts, including provenance, sentence-level alignments, and story identifiers. They evaluate multiple modern LLMs on zero-shot and retrieval-based few-shot translation using story-level cross-validation, deterministic retrieval, output validation, reference-based and judge-based metrics, and story-level uncertainty estimation.
AI.result: The main results are that LLMs achieve non-trivial translation quality in this setting, retrieval-based few-shot prompting consistently outperforms zero-shot prompting, and adding more retrieved examples yields only limited further gains.
